All at GMS would like to wish readers a Happy Chinese / Lunar New Year!

headline: FIRM BUT FAR!
body_text:
Several specialist, non-ferrous units (stainless steel tankers and Russian fish factories) have made their way to Alang this year, especially as prices improve closer to the USD 600/LDT mark over the course of January.

However, Indian Buyers are still unable to compete on competitive market tonnage, which is largely ending up in competing Pakistani or Bangladeshi hands. Even previously favoured passenger units are reportedly finding their way onto Pakistani shores.

On the local fundamentals front, the Indian Rupee is trading at a steady level in the high Rs. 74s against the U.S. Dollar, whilst local steel plate prices have improved by nearly USD 16/Ton over the course of the week, leaving the Indian market positively poised as we enter into February.

headline: COMING UP!
highlights: Raising game. | Market dynamics.
body_text:
Having missed out on a number of market and even geographically positioned units, Gadani Buyers knew they had to raise the level of their game if they were to secure their share of any of the dwindling number of market / private vessels.

The holiday season in the East is now upon us and this is likely to lead to an even greater dearth in the availability of units for hungry Recyclers.

It will therefore be interesting to see how market dynamics resume post holidays, given that many end Buyers have plots cleared and are ready to buy and compete aggressively on any available units.

headline: LETHARGY?
body_text:
The Turkish market seems to be going through a lethargic phase with virtually no news being reported on the SNP front. While reports of a trickle of tonnage arriving the waterfront do make it from time to time, there is little market tonnage to negotiate at present.

Fundamentals too remain relatively stable as both import & local steel plate prices remain steady and the Turkish Lira buoys around the mid TRY 13s against the U.S. Dollar.

As reported last year, most local Buyers are eager to get tonnage basis late Q1 delivery and as such, we can only hope this market stays steady (or even firms further) when the time comes.

headline: TIGERISH LEVELS!
highlights: Roaring back. | Afra sold.
body_text:
As we chime in the Year of the Tiger, Bangladesh has come roaring back to the fore, displaying the most aggressive levels on show and in the process, even securing a deal or two.

Chattogram Buyers are getting increasingly hungry, with plots due to be filled and L/C limits to satisfy. As such, so some of the buying that is going on, occasionally surges above what is the reality on the ground.

Local steel plate prices (firming nearly USD 10/Ton this week) have certainly added to the flair of an increased local desire to bid on tonnage, boosting Cash Buyer eagerness on the prices they were eager to table this week.

One of the tanker sales for the week saw the 2003 Korean built and controlled by BULL of Indonesia Aframax unit PETROGARUDA (19,105 LDT) committed for a fantastic USD 650/LT LDT.

headline: SPRING IN STEP!
highlights: Holidays ending. | Markets firing. | Cash Buyer hunger. | Steel surge. | Tankers sold.
body_text:
Both, Pakistan and Bangladesh, have been at the forefront of this recent resurgence, with an improved India (that is still unable to compete on any regular / non-HKC / non-specialist tonnage) and a relatively stable Turkey that has defied explanation for the most part with its remarkably firm / stable levels (especially in light of the collapsing Lira) and even a noteworthy improvement in import steel registering this week.

Sub-continent prices have managed to surge past USD 650/LT LDT on certain select units once again - such is the hunger of Cash Buyers and sub-continent Recyclers alike - just to secure a piece of the dwindling shortage of tonnage at present.

Steel plate prices across the board have been a key driver to the spectacular showings of late, as construction / infrastructure projects ramp up once again, with the worst of Convid-19 and its associated lockdowns and restrictions, seemingly easing of late.

Regrettably, the number of the comparatively less dangerous Omicron cases are on the rise globally even though the combination of vaccines and boosters appear to be (temporarily?) keeping the worst of it at bay – at least until news of another mutation invariably surfaces.

On the sales front, there was news of one 2002 built VLCC and another large LDT Aframax tanker sale to report this week, as opportunistic Owners returning from holidays seek to cash in at these admittedly fantastic levels, amidst continuing poor tanker charter rates.

headline: BUDGET AID!
body_text:
India unfortunately remains stranded on the side-lines for yet another week, such has been the energy displayed by the rampant Bangladesh and Pakistan markets over the past couple of weeks or so.

The Indian budget was also announced this week and there is reportedly no material impact on the domestic ship recycling sector, rather, a positive impact is anticipated as government spending has reportedly been increased on infrastructure and defence.

The Rupee too has firmed marginally, trading in the mid Rs. 74 against the U.S. Dollar, whilst local steel plate prices have increased by nearly USD 11/Ton over the course of the week, leaving the Alang market positively poised as the industry heads into February.

headline: VA VA VOOM!
highlights: Stunning sale. | Sign of things to come?
body_text:
A stunning week in Pakistan led to some increasingly speculative offerings on various vessels this week, and even saw one VLCC reportedly concluded at well above market levels.

The Polemis controlled 2002 built NEW INSPIRATION (40,737 LDT) was finalised for an extraordinary price in the region of USD 660/LT LDT, gas free for hot works clean for delivery Gadani – as one over exuberant Cash Buyer seems ready to speculate on further upward movements in price, as this level is certainly not reflective of today’s prices.

With demand remaining rife across much of Gadani, the hope is that this particular sale may spur owners into introduce / conclude more vessels into the red hot sub-continent recycling markets in the weeks / months to come.

headline: ON THE RISE?
body_text:
Although the Turkish market has been sailing through a period of sluggishness (despite having some of the strongest levels on offer for tonnage), market demand remains steady and levels remain firm.

Despite the Turkish Lira coasting through some record lows (currently in the mid TRY 13.5X against the U.S. Dollar at the time of writing), import and local steel prices have remained relatively steady, delivering the necessary confidence to local Recyclers to maintain their current levels.

In fact, import steel has reportedly improved by a whopping USD 20/Ton this week and such an improvement on the back of stable prices is certain to bring further increases in local offerings.

Is USD 400/Ton the new frontier for Turkey?

Certainly, seems a possibility given that the Winter months are currently restricting movements of most undertow units through EU waters and with no major market tonnage being introduced for sale or any noteworthy sales to report, Aliaga Buyers are dwindling through previous deliveries at local plots and an eagerness to compete certainly appears evident, especially for post Q1 deliveries.

headline: HAVING TO COMPETE!
highlights: Pak competes. | Demand good.
body_text:
Bangladesh has started to see some fierce competition from Pakistan this week, with rumours that levels on the VLCC NEW INSPIRATION (that was committed last week) were seeing similar levels in both markets, resulting in the deal becoming a potential candidate for either destination.

With this in mind, it was no surprise to see Berge sell their latest Capesize Bulker, the BERGE AORAKI (21,285 LDT) at a rather firm USD 640/LDT, basis a Bangladesh delivery and for strictly HKC green recycling to a local SoC certified yard.

Steel prices, though weaker this week by about USD 11/Ton, still remain impressively perched at some very high overall levels, keeping local demand and prices elevated, as Chattogram Recyclers hustle to try and secure some of the few vessels that are available.

Local port position certainly highlights the glaring shortage of tonnage, as only 1 fresh vessel reportedly arrived the Chattogram waterfront this week.

highlights: Firm pricing. | LC issues. | Turkey Firms. | Tanker Supply. | Cape sold.
body_text:
Demand remains rampant and capacity at yards remains open for any available tonnage (market or otherwise), leading to bidding wars on any of the marginal number of choice units hitting the recycling markets.

L/Cs are of continuing concern across the sub-continent destinations, and it is becoming increasingly important / urgent for industry players to have additional bank checks and margins must be placed with the opening banks to ensure L/Cs are opened and released in a timely manner. Therefore, the right selection of Cash / End Buyers’ is an essential part of ensuring a smooth and successful delivery, especially at these record levels of today.

On the Western end of things, the Turkish market seems as though levels here too are looking to take off as import and local steel prices further firmed this week and the Lira sails through its newfound stability in the mid TRY 13s against the U.S. Dollar.

The supply of vessels has seen mostly tankers (often as young as 2003 - and younger at times) being sold for recycling this year. However, we are also likely to see Capesize Bulkers (one was sold this week) with charter rates having cooled off significantly over the previous few weeks, despite bouncing back towards the end of this week.

Vessels (Dry Bulk or Tankers) with surveys due and BWTS due to be installed, are likely to make up a majority of the supply for the remainder of the year, as owners look to take advantage of these fantastic prices, well over USD 600/LDT.

headline: FRUSTRATIONS ABOUND!
body_text:
India has even lost a favoured HKC vessel to the one SoC certified yard in Bangladesh, such has been the exuberantly competitive form of neighbouring sub-continent markets this week.

There had been several specialist non-ferrous units concluded into India at the start of the year, but even this variety in the supply of tonnage has iced up over the last couple of weeks, whilst Alang Buyers become frustrated at the painful lack of tonnage once again.

Ironically however, despite both fundamentals registering declines this week, both demand and prices continue to buoy around the same region as last week.

The India Rupee depreciated further past the mid Rs. 75 against the U.S. Dollar, whilst local steel prices depreciated by about USD 22/Ton through the course of the week, leaving End Buyers nervous about the market once again.

headline: DECADE LONG HIGHS!
highlights: VL decisions. | Roaring back.
body_text:
It will be interesting to see where the 2002 built VLCC NEW INSPIRATION eventually ends up, with both Bangladesh and Pakistan options seemingly open for the Cash Buyer on the resale front, as both markets are now competing aggressively at some record levels not seen for over a decade.

Of late, the industry has witnessed the Gadani market come roaring back to rival a rampant Bangladesh, with some of the highest levels on offer since 2008.

Numbers on select tonnage are even starting to approach the mid USD 600s/LDT – yet the ongoing shortage of fresh tonnage for sale is leading to some well-above market speculation on those units that are working, so desperate are certain Recyclers to fill their plots.

headline: UPWARD?!
body_text:
The stability in prices and overall performance of the Turkish market has been nothing short of impressive of late.

Prices have managed to remain relatively steady over the course of the last few months and despite the Lira breaching TRY 17 against the U.S. Dollar some time ago, demand and local offerings remain firm on the back of strong import and local steel plate prices.

In fact, this week once again, import steel prices improved by USD 5/Ton and local steel plate prices jumped by about USD 10/Ton. While the Lira dances around its newfound stability around the mid TRY 13s against the U.S. Dollar, a firming in levels seems imminent.

As such, as spring is on the horizon, the Turkish market certainly seems like it’s gearing up to take in its share of tonnage coming out of EU waters.

headline: NO CEILING!
highlights: Leading way. | How high can go?
body_text:
Bangladesh leads the way once again, with some of the best numbers in the sub-continent on any tonnage on offer or those units already in Cash Buyer hands.

With one HKC cape being sold to Bangladesh last week, India secured another HKC only Cape this week at even higher levels (albeit with over 1,000 Tons of bunkers on board) – to show that all markets are viable and are willing to strongly compete on available tonnage, at firm levels once again.

With several vessels being concluded well over USD 650/LT LDT, there is now the (worrying) speculation as to just how high this market can go. Notwithstanding, as long as steel plate prices (that are up another USD 12/Ton this week), the Bangladeshi Taka remains firm, and supply painfully sparse, there (hopefully) seems little to be worried about thus far!

highlights: Big numbers. | Tanker flavor. | Steel firm. | Charter hopes? | China back.
body_text:
We have seen several Capes sold for HKC recycling in the mid USD 600s/LDT in recent weeks, especially as chartering rates in this sector have taken a bit of a dip. Tankers keep being introduced into the recycling markets and several deals have reportedly been concluded at levels in excess of USD 650/LT LDT in Bangladesh, as the Chattogram market heats up to some increasingly unprecedented levels.

Steel prices remain firm across all sub-continent locations and even the Indian market has started to come back into the picture, such is the demand emanating from all markets at present.

Finally, the Turkish market remains impeccably poised to place some record levels of their own, if only the dearth of tonnage wouldn’t have kept the market so exquisitely stranded.

Overall, given some of the numbers on show, it is indeed surprising that not more candidates are being introduced for a recycling sale. Yet, there are likely enough inklings in the wet sector to suggest a turn in sentiments, which may lead even more Owners to hold on to their tonnage for now.

With Chinese production set to ramp up again now that Chinese New Year holidays and the winter Olympics are over, perhaps there is scope for further improvements on price as well.

headline: REBOUND!
body_text:
India has rebounded recently after a few nervy weeks following steel reversals and have even got back into the action, with Alang Recycling reportedly securing a couple of units.

Of course, there seems to be no competing with the rampant Pakistan and Bangladeshi markets at present, so firmly placed to secure tonnage are Buyers at those locations.

As such, rather than competing on standard Tankers and Bulkers, Indian Buyers are having to make do on a diet of specialist units such as fish factories, stainless steel tankers and HKC green vessels only.

On the local fundamentals front, local steel plate prices jumped a massive and nearly USD 20/Ton this week, boosting local sentiments. Even the Indian Rupee has firmed against the U.S. Dollar, to Rs. 74.3X during the course of the week, keeping Alang Buyers eager for tonnage.

headline: COMPETING!
highlights: Rivalling Bangladesh. | Delivery concerns.
body_text:
Pakistan remains closely competitive with the resurgent Bangladeshi market, particularly for those geographically positioned vessels that may be operating or being delivered to Cash Buyers on ‘as is’ basis in the UAE / PG region.

Steel plate prices remain firm and demand is certainly ripe in Gadani, as local Recyclers look to fill plots that have reportedly been vacant for some time.

News about some rough deliveries at the start of the year is creating some disturbance amongst the recycling community and it may be that Sellers / Cash Buyers are looking to deliver their vessels elsewhere for now, rather than risk facing headaches at the final stages of delivery.

headline: FIRM…YET SLOW!
body_text:
The Turkish market traveled through yet another slow week, despite local steel plate prices reportedly registering a minor improvement. Even the Lira, while egregiously weaker, remains stable at its worst.

No reports of fresh arrivals or news of market units working, emanated from Aliaga this week as this has overall been a silent week.

Yet, demand remains firm, prices remain at record highs, and Turkey remains the only viable destination for units opening up in EU waters.

headline: SECURING SALES!
highlights: Big numbers. | Tanker sale.
body_text:
Chattogram leads the way for yet another week, with a stunning showing on available tonnage, as rates push on impressively once again.

Moreover, despite a limited showing of fresh sales, those vessels in Cash Buyer hands are already seeing increasing numbers from Bangladeshi Buyers – in what remains a nervous yet impressive showing from the market leaders.

The sale of one MR tanker was confirmed this week, as the HARMONY (8,356 LDT) was finalised at an impressive USD 650/LT LDT basis an ‘as is’ Colombo delivery.

headline: Sub-continent markets remain firmly poised for another week, particularly in Bangladesh and a now resurgent India.
highlights: Markets firm. | Pakistan quiet. | Steel firms. | Russian shame. | Viable options.
body_text:
Pakistan, as seems to be typical for the market there, has gone quiet over much of the international uncertainty surrounding the possible outcome of the recent Russian invasion of Ukraine.

Bangladeshi Buyers have in turn, ramped up their buying and price offerings, mindful of the fact that some increased oil / gas prices due to the unfolding crisis in Ukraine, in addition to the inevitable sanctions that may starve Ship Recyclers of a supply line of ships for a short time.

Steel scrap prices have improved significantly in Bangladesh and India this week, leaving both markets positively poised going into March, whilst Pakistan slows down and waits to watch the international situation and subsequent market developments.

The Turkish market remains especially poised to suffer from the outcome of the Ukrainian invasion, with the supply of import of steel likely to be affected. Should this happen, we can possibly see import steel (and likely) ship offerings from Turkey firm up for a short period.

Overall, Putin’s disgraceful actions of the Russian invasion of Ukraine has certainly shocked the world over and the raft of justifiable sanctions is likely to have a profound impact on the shipping world – especially when negotiating state owned sanctioned Russian tonnage, which of course will restrict them from heading for recycling shores.

As it stands, despite the ongoing international turmoil, recycling markets keep giving owners a viable end of life option at fantastic decade long high levels, while freight rates too continue to perform admirably at present.

Rank Location Sentiment Dry Bulk USD / LDT

Containers USD / LDT 1 Bangladesh Firm 630 / LDT 640 / LDT 650 / LDT 2 India Firmer 620 / LDT 630 / LDT 640 / LDT 3 Pakistan Firm 610 / LDT 620 / LDT 630 / LDT 4 Turkey Firm 360 / LDT 380 / LDT 390 / LDT

headline: BACK IN BIZ!
body_text:
Indian steel plate prices surged back this week as the market improved by about USD 15/LDT, subsequently pushing them ahead of a dormant Pakistan.

Indeed, many geographically positioned vessels that were initially thought of as Pakistani candidates, are now being offered to India at much higher asking prices, given this week’s jump in local offerings!

However, Bangladesh is still so far ahead that (particularly) larger LDT vessels are being suitably diverted to Bangladesh, even if delivery remains W.C. India or in UAE / PG region, given the delta in levels over a Chattogram delivery.

headline: RETREAT!
highlights: Quiet. | Confused & nervous.
body_text:
Gadani Recyclers unfortunately decided to remain silent on any available tonnage this week, just as they had the opportunity to secure a few well-positioned units at resurgent and firm levels.

As a result, most of these recently working vessels have now been diverted to a resurgent India or (better yet) Bangladesh, and Pakistan has been left empty-handed once again, in a market which isn’t already seeing many potential candidates for recycling.

The reason for the currently restricted offerings is that confused and nervy buyers are concerned with the international situation unfolding in Ukraine and how it would affect the price of import scrap - without taking actual fundamentals and market conditions into consideration.

headline: QUEIT, YET AGAIN!
body_text:
Despite the conflict in the Black Sea, the Turkish market remained precariously steady this week. Most domestic Recyclers are suspecting a shortage in import steel coming up in the coming week(s), thereby, artificially pushing prices up.

Even the Lira briefly spiked past TRY 14.50 against the U.S Dollar this week, as global markets rattled to the news of Putin’s invasion.

While the Turkish market was slow moving for the last couple of weeks, with the uncertainty and possible volatility that may be forthcoming, we don’t expect much movement from Aliaga in the coming week(s).

headline: LEADING THE WAY!
highlights: Missing cape. | No 700s.
body_text:
Bangladesh leads the way for another week but has started to miss out on vessels to competing markets, and this week (surprisingly), it was India on a favoured large LDT Cape for HKC recycling only.

Steel plate prices have been on an upward trajectory once again and this week alone, levels jumped nearly USD 42/Ton, leading to some of the best recycling offers we have seen since the highs of 2008.

We have not reached USD 700/LDT on standard vessels just quite yet, with mid USD 600s/LDT being seen for the time being, on the slimmer array of vessels that are working firm for sale - something which is contributing to a rampant demand in all sub-continent markets.

highlights: Firm showing. | Steel rise. | Bangla leads. | Commodities cruise. | Supply cools.
body_text:
Except China, local steel plate prices have made some impressive gains across the board in the top recycling international destinations this week, especially in India and Bangladesh. As a result, Alang Buyers have managed to secure the show stopping sale of the week, with a Capesize Bulker being committed for strictly HKC recycling and that too at levels competitive with those from Bangladesh.

Even in Turkey, both import and local steel plate prices have made improvements this week, with levels for all types of tonnage now firmly poised past the USD 400/Ton barrier – a first in memorable history.

Meanwhile, Chattogram continues to lead the way with some of the best rates witnessed in the sub-continent since the shipping boom of 2008, during which, the world saw recycling prices exceed USD 800/LDT. However, there seems little danger of that feat being repeated once again (at least for now).

Commodity prices have also surged during this bleak time of conflict and the cost to operate / deliver a vessel for recycling has also risen exponentially, primarily due to soaring oil prices that are now positioned well above USD 100 / barrel (at the time of writing).

The supply of vessels may cool off going into the second quarter of the year due to rising Tanker rates and continuing firm Dry Bulk income - unless those vessels that have SS / DD due imminently and BWTS installations required, that may make them uneconomical to continue trading.

headline: PUSHING ON!
body_text:
The Indian market pushed on even further this week, as steel plate prices made some remarkable gains - firming by about USD 46/Ton within this week alone - whist the Indian Rupee (that is now reflecting the global currency volatility) is trading in the high Rs. 76s against the U.S. Dollar.

Indeed, Alang Buyers managed to secure the showstopping sale of the week as Berge Bulk of Singapore sold their second Capesize Bulker this year, for full range HKC recycling. The heavier ice classed and large LDT BERGE ARCTIC (27,461 LDT) was finalised for a whopping USD 660/LDT, on a delivered basis.

As it therefore stands, India seems there to compete on any and all market vessels available - not just specialist non-ferrous units and HKC only vessels (as was previously the case).

headline: RECOVERING APPETITE?
highlights: Too little too late. | Missing out.
body_text:
Pakistan may be starting to regain some appetite and confidence this week, but it seems to be too little too late, especially as the other markets have pushed well beyond Gadani’s offerings and vessels have already been diverted to competing shores.

Gadani Buyers did have decent possibilities to secure some of the geographically positioned candidates, but the ongoing confusion and nerves have (re)surfaced once the Russian invasion of Ukraine transpired.

As such, it seems as though Pakistani Buyers will (once again) be missing out on a majority of the tonnage on offer in the foreseeable future, given the stunning form and confidence / demand from neighbouring competitors at present.

headline: BALTIC BLUES!
body_text:
This week again, the focus of the Turkish market remains the unfolding crisis in Ukraine. While certainly beneficial to the Turkish recycling market, the volatility of this recent improvement certainly remains of concern given that levels for all types of vessels have now firmly jumped across USD 400/Ton.

Steel fundamentals remain firm as both import and local steel plate prices recorded further improvements this week. On the other hand, like India, the Turkish Lira weakened past TRY 14.1X against the U.S. Dollar in light of the unfolding crisis.

Certainly, this market seem poised for a further improvement since the crisis in the Baltic seems far from over at this juncture. As such, Turkey is certainly a market to watch out for in the near future.

headline: LEADING LIGHTS!
highlights: Surging on. | LC limits?
body_text:
Bangladesh leads the way once again, as steel prices surged upwards by nearly USD 65/Ton this week and vessel prices (as a result) pushed on towards the USD 700/LDT mark, in what have been nothing short of impressive gains from the market leaders.

Notwithstanding (and despite multiple enquiries), there has yet to be a sale to take place at these new levels as there does seem to be a growing reticence from Chattogram Buyers to secure ships at the peak of the market, perhaps anticipating likely falls ahead.

There is also a question mark on whether L/Cs can (will?) be opened by various banks at these new peaks, with certain Recyclers being required to place increased securities with the banks, in order to get those limits.

highlights: Further boost. | Reaching records. | India corrects. | Pakistan moves. | Turkish fire. | First sale?
body_text:
These are comfortably (and certainly) the highest numbers we have seen since the historical highs of 2008, when over USD 800/LDT was surpassed and the recent universal skyrocketing steel plate prices across the recycling board (even in China) are carrying the weight of these recent prices.

The chief movement is coming from a rampant Bangladeshi market where steel prices continue to surge upwards (some of the most noteworthy increases of late), in line with soaring commodities in general, as the Russian invasion of Ukraine intensifies into an uncertain future.

Even in India, after two weeks of spectacular gains and despite registering further gains this week, steel prices had a minor correction during the course of the week, raising the guard of local recyclers who have been observing the rate of the recent climb. It may however be that prices continue their upward trajectory in Alang next week again, only to mirror global commodity prices moving upwards / forward.

Pakistan has also started to also improve once again, having missed several geographically positioned vessels that have since been diverted to competing shores.

On the Far end, the Turkish market, like the Bangladeshi market, recorded some impressive gains in local steel plate prices this week, pushing vessel prices into unchartered territory, and certainly worthy of exploiting on quick deliveries.

It remains to be seen just where the first transactions on market tonnage will be concluded at or above USD 700/LDT, as End Buyers do seem somewhat nervous to transact at these new decade long highs.

headline: STEEL TURN!
body_text:
Despite some worrying reversals towards the end of the week, local steel plate prices surged even further this week, jumping nearly USD 35/Ton – clearly a by-product of the global crisis that has affected all of the major recycling destination.

Consequently, this has led to increasing nerves from End Buyers and a reticence to offer on any units that are currently on the bidding tables, whilst they are increasingly adopt a wait-and-watch attitude towards further market developments.

Coupled with an Indian Rupee that has increasingly depreciated (briefly past Rs. 77) this week, ending at nearly 76.5X against the U.S. Dollar, a lot of the recent Indian lustre has been taken out of the market.

As a result, many of the market units (which were being discussed for an India delivery), now seem to be candidates for competing locations, as even Pakistan comes back into the picture this week.

headline: WARMING UP!
highlights: Back to buy? | Few candidates.
body_text:
Despite some recent nerves by Gadani Buyers, the Pakistani recycling market seems to be warming up once again, thanks to surging steel / commodity prices because of the ongoing crisis in Ukraine.

While not as impressive as Bangladesh, local steel plate prices reportedly jumped nearly USD 46/Ton this week – certainly impressive unto itself.

It would seem as though Recyclers in both Pakistan and India are just about on par at the moment (in terms of levels being offered), although there is a fundamental lack of candidates available for negotiation in order to test this pricing theory.

There are currently no signs of Gadani coming close to (or perhaps breaching) the USD 700/LDT threshold being (nearly) breached in Bangladesh, but at least there are some positive signs for this market after a period on the side-lines.

headline: FIRING ON!
body_text:
The ongoing crisis in the Black Sea is further pushing fundamentals into seemingly unchartered territory, as local offerings on tonnage make a noteworthy jump to get ever closer to the USD 500/Ton mark – certainly a first for this market.

Not only did local steel plate prices jump a remarkable USD 60/Ton this week, even import steel improved an additional USD 15/ton. Moreover, in keeping with the global competition and further displaying effects of the Ukrainian crisis, the currency continues to weaken, virtually sniffing the TRY 15.X mark against the U.S. Dollar.

The length of uncertainty surrounding the Baltic crisis remains uncertain, the conflict is invariably pushing scrap vessel prices back to the highs of 2008 (and the markets certainly remember how that roller coaster ended).

How this pricing strategy ends for Ship Owners depends on how promptly they are able to get their vessels into Aliaga and make best of the current incredible (for Turkey) pricing on offer.

headline: RESISTANCE!
highlights: Unwilling. | Bounceback?
body_text:
There is certainly some resistance from Bangladeshi Recyclers to dip back into the market at these extraordinarily firm numbers, even after this week’s decline in local steel plate prices (to the tune of about USD 17/Ton).

Much of the talk recently has surrounded levels exceeding USD 700/LDT, but it would appear very few Recyclers are willing to seriously engage in discussions at these incredible numbers, given this week’s cooling on commodity prices.

India has bounced back from its precipitous fall in steel prices early in the week, so it may be that Chattogram Buyers respond equally firmly, especially given the ongoing sparsity of candidates.

For now however, the market remains rather muted, fearful of potential falls further ahead.

highlights: Peaked? | Cooling prices. | Still firm. | Short dip? | Stability needed.
body_text:
The unfolding crisis in Ukraine certainly has affected global oil and gas prices and those countries that regularly purchase their reserves from Russia (such as India) are now having to hammer out new plans to sustain their local economies, especially given the bevy of sanctions currently in place.

Yet, these are decade long highs that we are witnessing at present, and not since the heady days of 2008 have vessel prices been so firm. As a result, most owners are witnessing values on their end-of-life ships at least double over the past year or so.

Notwithstanding, chartering markets, particularly in the dry and container sectors, continue to perform admirably and certain routes on tankers have once again started to pick up, which is increasingly depriving hungry Recyclers of tonnage and is keeping prices (artificially?) firm. Furthermore, despite this latest dip of about USD 20 – USD 30 / LDT, commodity prices remain firm and there certainly is scope for improvement once again, given that the end of the Ukraine crisis seems far from over at this juncture.

The Indian Rupee, despite firming marginally this week, has suffered some noteworthy currency reversals of late, compounding some of the drastic steel falls seen over the last 2 - 3 weeks. Finally, in the West End, steel fundamentals (both import and local steel plate) recorded depreciations of their own, with the Lira further aggravating the situation this week.

Overall, it may perhaps take a week or two of stability before we understand where the new reality on prices actually is, as the coveted USD 700/LDT level (and above) still appears somewhat illusory for the most part and on most standard units.

headline: YO YO!
body_text:
After the precipitous drop in steel plate prices early in the week (where levels fell nearly USD 65/LDT) coupled with a recent currency depreciation (to the tune of about 4% percent), the Indian market appeared to be in the doldrums this time last week.

However, steel prices clawed back much of that lost ground over this past week, up by over USD 45/Ton by the time the week ended, eliminating at least half of the recent losses and regain some of the local confidence.

End Buyers are still somewhat cagey about negotiating at levels in the mid (and higher) USD 600s/LDT, however they may be left with no alternative in order to fill plots and satisfy their L/C limits.

The concern remains that should the Ukraine crisis be a prolonged one, India (who purchases a healthy chunk of its oil from Russia), may find it hard to sustain regular imports, especially in the wake of the recent crippling sanctions. It is feared that this in effect, may have long term economic implications for the Indian economy, whereby inflation may subsequently hit hard with the rising gas prices and especially if the Indian government is unable to sustain the sale of gas at current levels.

On the sales front, one specialist unit was concluded to Alang buyers this week as the Poland built, (locally favored - due to the prevalence of non-ferrous on board) fish factory SVEABORG (5,015 LDT) was committed for an excellent USD 795/LT LDT.

headline: RELUCTANT!
highlights: Quieter. | Not stepping up.
body_text:
Pakistani Buyers remain somewhat quiet, despite recently coming back into the picture to compete with India (and even Bangladesh on a couple of units) once again.

There does seem to be some reluctance to acquire tonnage at these higher rates after another stunning surge in prices across the sub-continent market at the start of this year, but if Gadani Recyclers wish to compete and continue to secure tonnage, they are left with no other options.

The lack of local market (and even seemingly private) fixtures has made its presence known, with the lack of any fresh arrivals at Gadani’s waterfront this week and the only unit at local anchorage, finding its final resting place at a local yard.

As such, it has been another quiet week in Gadani, with end Buyers struggling to step up and get their heads around these higher numbers on show.

headline: RE-ADJUSTING?
body_text:
Just like in the subcontinent markets, local steel plate prices in Turkey went through a comparatively milder re-adjustment period this week. Not only did import steel decline by about USD 15 / Ton, but local steel plate prices also saw a minor correction – to the tune of about USD 10/Ton this week.

Notwithstanding, the far firmer levels on offer from Recyclers on regular tonnage remain steady and Owners in European waters looking for sub-continent levels from 2 years ago will not be disappointed in concluding a quick sale (or two).

With the ongoing conflict in the Black Sea, local Recyclers remain conscious about the jump in levels and that prices could come rolling down with the end of the fighting. While that remains to be seen how long it will take, levels remain beyond impressive for now and certainly worth a quick fixture.

headline: BOUNCEBACK?
highlights: Sliding. | Mills back buying.
body_text:
The Bangladeshi slide has inadvertently brought India back into the picture of late, and the two markets are now competing on tonnage, with India being a preference for those owners with geographically positioned units, such is the high price of fuel at the moment.

Steel prices have tumbled by nearly USD 50/LDT, leaving Bangladeshi demand softening and a genuine lack of local interest emerging at these new highs that were approaching USD 700/LDT (and excess).

Notwithstanding, despite steel mills not actively buying at these higher overall numbers, they are still helping keep the industry active by acquiring steel that was secured at lower levels. Though all of this may start to change if prices maintain / improve again and local Recyclers refuse to sell ship’s steel for a loss.

highlights: Challenging. | India gains. | Commodities firm. | China Covid woe. | Bangla mills.
body_text:
India has managed to regain over half of the falls seen over the previous few weeks, but the market overall does remain extremely volatile.

Commodity prices and volatile currencies show few signs of cooling off any time soon, as the Russian invasion of Ukraine enters its second month and thus far shows no signs of abating. The Covid situation in China too may be a growing cause for concern as various cities (including the economic hub of Shanghai) enter a fresh series of lockdowns, while the rest of the world is just starting to open again.

The fact that there is very little natural immunity or a fully workable vaccine coverage (that hasn’t already begun to wane) mean that China could be faced with another challenging period, both socially & economically and we can only hope that future virus mutations and inevitable closures do not become a part of everyday life once again.

While mills in Bangladesh had recently stopped buying steel at these higher overall levels approaching USD 700/LDT, they have however, slowly started to acquire small portions of inventory just to stay open and this will surely lead to greater confidence in purchasing larger amounts in due course, in iorder to bring Chattogram prices back up again.

Finally, the Turkish market sails through an uneventful week, with no changes or fresh arrivals reported.

headline: BACK IN BIZ!
body_text:
India has come surging back into the picture this week and is now competitive with a Bangladeshi market that is currently enduring a brief lull due to softening steel plate prices there.

On the flip side, steel prices gained further ground in Alang (despite ending the week a marginal USD 4/Ton lower) whilst much of the volatile currency depreciation seems to be settling too, with the Indian Rupee firming from Rs. 76.5X, closer to Rs. 76.10 against the U.S. Dollar.

It will be interesting to see if India manages to secure any larger LDT market vessels, having primarily secured specialist, non-ferrous and HKC only unit this year, whilst much of the larger LDT Tankers and Bulkers have found their way to Pakistani or Bangladeshi shores.

headline: HALF ASLEEP!
highlights: Not competitive | Nervous.
body_text:
Pakistani Buyers appear invisible at the moment, as they are not even competitive with a resurgent India or worse, a weakening Bangladesh at the moment.

Even geographically positioned units have been ignoring a softer and far more reluctant Pakistani market and have sailed off on even longer voyages across to Bangladesh (especially at the start of this year, so diverse and volatile have pricing differentials between sub-continent locations been of late).

Yet, with the ongoing Russian incursion into Ukraine and the subsequent volatility in steel fundamentals, Gadani Recyclers remain nervous to offer at these higher prices and they are worried about just how far local fundamentals and subsequent sub-continent pricing on units eventually climb to.

This worry has lead to the Gadani market reporting no fresh arrivals at the waterfront this week, a first in quite a while for this market.

headline: SETTLED.
body_text:
After weeks of firming fundamentals, improving plate prices and a semi-weakening dollar, the Turkish market finally spent a week in relative modesty, with no major changes reported in domestic steel fundamentals (import or local plate prices) or even the currency, that has expectedly weakened with the ongoing crisis in the Baltic, declining past the TRY 14.80 mark against the U.S. Dollar this week.

There is not much to report from Aliaga with minimal local activity being reported, logical, given the lack of available market tonnage. There were also no fresh arrivals even reported this week.

Overall, a silent, yet firm period in Turkey prevails and with the Ukraine invasion in full swing, it is even expected to stay this way in the coming weeks.

headline: PLUMMET FROM SUMMIT!
highlights: Rough weeks. | Sales lacking.
body_text:
Bangladesh has endured a rough few weeks, with steel plate prices declining from their previous highs and, local steel mills (as a result) have cooled their interest in buying re- rollable product.

Meanwhile, as most ships are now being diverted towards India and Pakistan (given the increasing gulf in prices), Bangladeshi mills will have to improve their levels in the coming week(s), in order to secure any inventory as there is likely to be a shortage of supply in the weeks ahead, so low are offers on units from Chattogram Buyers at present.

On the flip side, local anchorage remained busy with 7 fresh arrivals this week alone, which should hold over local Recyclers for the coming weeks as these units are digested and local offerings start to react to the competition and domestic fundamentals.

Consequently, there have been no market sales to report into Bangladesh over the past week and local Buyers will have to up their game in order to secure any available vessels moving forward.

headline: Both Pakistani and (especially) Indian markets have come surging back this week, to lead the way over a lackluster Bangladesh that has virtually dropped out of contention of late.
highlights: India and Pak back. | Improving steel. | Losses made up. | Bangla out. | Some reluctance.
body_text:
Firming steel plate prices in India have been the key driving factor behind this, and it still seems inevitable that the USD 700/LDT mark could be breached into these two markets, on upcoming sales in the near future (as long as these fundamentals hold).

Pakistan has been on the sidelines of late, but appear to have woken up this week, in the face of some serious and sustained competition from a resurgent India and a Bangladeshi market that’s begun to slip in the rankings.

Most of the losses on Indian steel plate prices have been made up over the last 3 - 4 weeks and the Alang market finishes this week in a rare position i.e. leading the market rankings ahead of all their sub-continent competitors, especially the usually pole-positioned Bangladesh.

Bangladeshi steel plate prices have been falling in recent weeks, and despite firming nearly USD 24/Ton by mid-week, the industry has seen them plummet from the summit to the bottom of the (sub-continent) rankings as their plate prices declined almost the same amount by the time the week ended.

Furthermore, such a pricing reversal certainly sees them positioned uncompetitively on any market candidates for the time being – even on geographically positioned units in the Far East, which are now heading towards Indian and Pakistani shores.

Finally, in the West, the Turkish market remains unchanged, firmly priced and positioned, with minimal tonnage to compete on.

Overall, there has been some hesitancy to dip in at some of these historical highs approaching USD 700/LDT, across all sub-continent markets. However, due to continually impressive and improving steel prices that seem to have been performing well on the back of the ongoing Ukraine crisis, it’s a wonder how long these numbers will stay around.

headline: TURNAROUND!
body_text:
The scrap steel market in India has clawed back most of the losses sustained over the last three weeks, placing Alang as the number one ranked ship recycling destination in the Indian sub-continent – the first in a while, especially given Bangladesh’s US$ / LT supremacy of late!

Even conventional units now look destined for India – including large LDT Suezmax / Aframax Tankers and Capesize Bulkers that are normally heading towards Pakistan or Bangladesh instead – so impressive has been the turnaround from Alang in recent weeks.

The Indian Rupee also remains settled in the high Rs. 75s against the U.S. Dollar after some worrying depreciations earlier in the year, and this should give Alang Buyers further encouragement moving forward – especially in the near term.

However, the Ukraine crisis does stand to affect the Indian market in the long term, especially since both Iran and Russia are suppliers of oil to the Indian economy and with American sanctions targeting both nations, it is only a matter of time until the Indian Government can figure out how to continue to procure cost-effective oil for the masses and keep the wheels of the Indian economy in motion.

headline: STARTING TO COMPETE!
highlights: Political turmoil. | Missing out.
body_text:
Despite the political turmoil in Pakistan and question marks over the future of Prime Minister Imran Khan, vessel prices from Gadani have come back to become competitive with a soaring India and even firm past a recently roaring Bangladeshi market.

The domestic political uncertainty and the Ukraine crisis has led to Gadani Recyclers finding excuses not to compete of late, even though local steel prices remained firmly positioned. This has, of course, been a classic performance issue with the Pakistani market whereby local Recyclers have historically followed a rampant India vs. taking pricing cues from their own fundamentals.

Consequently this week, even though Gadani Buyers have lost out to Alang Buyers on much of the working market tonnage or those units in Cash Buyer hands, there is hope moving into the second quarter of the year that local Buyers will snag their share of favored tonnage.

headline: QUIET.
body_text:
It has been another relatively inactive week in Turkey, with not much to report on market negotiations or local fixtures. Local steel plate price remains stable whilst import steel dips by about USD 5/Ton.

As the conflict in the Baltic rages on, Turkish Buyers remain ever so attentive on local fundamentals, especially the Lira, that is once again continuing its descend towards TRY 15.0 against the U.S. Dollar.

Meanwhile, as the Indian and Pakistani markets head towards the hotly anticipated USD 700/LDT mark, Turkish Recyclers certainly have their work cut out for them, in trying to tempt Sellers of non-EU units into delivering their units to Aliaga’s shores.

For now, the Turkish market can remain content knowing that virtually all recycling units sailing out of EU waters have a designated spot on a Turkish yard.

headline: BREATHER!
highlights: Ramadan softer. | Demand low.
body_text:
As the traditionally softer month of Ramadan descends across Bangladesh, there have been very few market moves to speak of, into a decidedly softer Chattogram.

Local steel mills are refusing to buy ship’s steel at these incredibly higher levels, even though steel plate prices do seem to be holding up at some impressive prices. As such, it increasingly seems as though this latest slump in the Bangladeshi ship recycling sector is being largely sentiment driven.

Many local Recyclers have already filled their plots with much of the large LDT tonnage that was concluded earlier in the year. It therefore may be a few more weeks before price and demand pick up again after Ramadan holidays and once more of the tonnage is consumed locally.

highlights: Impressive week. | High sales. | Bangla out. | Pak upheaval. | India firm. | Turkey quiet.
body_text:
The Bangladeshi market is the only sub-continent destination that remains mute, despite steel prices there having flatlined (at impressive high’s) through much of this week. Yet, Chattogram Recyclers are refusing to buy at these high levels, even though evidence suggest these numbers are here to stay for at least the next month (or so)!

Much of the high-priced inventory concluded during the first quarter has ended up going to Bangladeshi shores, including a healthy collection of the large LDT VLCCs, VLOCs, Capes and Aframax tankers. As such, many Bangladeshi Buyers have already filled their plots with tonnage and are likely enjoying something of a Ramadan breather (especially with domestic activity having tempered of late).

Meanwhile, Pakistan has been beset by some major political upheaval of late, with Prime Minister Imran Khan being ousted from office (after a vote of no confidence) and his replacement is yet to be fully decided. Moreover, even the Pakistani Rupee has faced some volatility this week, raising eyebrows and caution. It is therefore unsurprising that the focus of Gadani recyclers has been elsewhere, despite two high-priced headline sales this week (that are seemingly set for a Pakistan redelivery).

In the absence of a hot Bangladeshi market, India has been securing much of the market tonnage over the last few weeks - not only HKC and specialist tonnage, but also some larger LDT tanker and offshore vessels finding their way to Alang.

Finally, the Turkish market, whilst still stable at historical highs, remains drudged with not much to report in terms of sale and purchase activity.

Rank Location Sentiment Dry Bulk USD / LDT

headline: STAYING STRONG!
body_text:
Steel plate prices have somewhat cooled in India this week, with levels having dropped over USD 15/Ton. Hence, the two market sales of the week appear to be heading towards Pakistani shores - and at extremely strong levels to boot.

Prices from India remain firm and perhaps the best placed in the sub-continent, despite strong competition from an emerging Gadani this week. Overall, however, it has been a quieter week in terms of sales to Alang Recyclers.

On the local fundamentals front, the currency continues to trade in the high Rs. 75s against the U.S. Dollar, and demand for any units (even non-HKC / large LDT vessels) remains good, as India continues to lead the market rankings for another week.

headline: EVENTFUL WEEK!
highlights: PM deposed. | Two sales.
body_text:
It has been an eventful week in Pakistan wherein, after a vote of ‘no-confidence’, Imran Khan has been ousted as the Prime Minister, subsequently leaving the country in a state of turmoil and without any immediate successor to step-in and stabilise the seemingly volatile situation.

Despite all this uncertainty surrounding the leadership of the country, bullish Cash Buyers have acquired two vessels with an expected Pakistan re-delivery, at levels above well above USD 700/LDT.

Firstly, the Capesize bulker SUNBEAM (21,018 LDT) was committed at an impressively firm USD 715/LT LDT, whilst the Aframax tanker ION (16,640 LDT) was sold for an equally impressive USD 708/LT LDT.

It would certainly seem as though these Cash Buyers are banking on a Pakistan rally in the wake of Imran Khan’s deposition, as these prices certainly do not represent the reality on the ground just yet.

headline: TURKISH HAZE.
body_text:
Despite record offers on units, weeks of inactivity from Turkey have left many wondering just what is going on with this market. Logically, the gongs of USD 700/LT being breached this week will certainly have a collection of Owners being distracted away from the offerings from Aliaga.

All whilst the Lira continues to trade in the high TRY 14.7X against the U.S. Dollar and steel plate prices report no noteworthy changes in both import and local levels, all while still trading at record levels.

Even though there is news of a single cruise liner arriving the local waterfront this week, the ongoing dearth of tonnage can only be equated to most units departing EU waters these days belonging to Owners who are continuing to capitalize on the currently high charter rates.

As such, the level of tonnage remaining available for Aliaga Recyclers remains slim.

headline: MARGINALISED!
highlights: Unable to secure. | Forced to acquire.
body_text:
Ramadan holidays have seen Bangladeshi Buyers marginalised for another week, as both India and Pakistan push on to secure most of the working inventory (market or private units in Cash Buyer hands).

Local steel plate prices, though volatile, remain firmly poised overall. Yet, domestic steel mills are resisting to buy at these higher levels, which is seeing product fail to shift from local recycling yards and subsequently creating a backlog of inventory & slowdown in cutting.

The general feeling is that steel mills may be eventually compelled to acquire at these present rates post-Ramadan, even though high as though they may be, a thorough lack of viable options leaves much to be desired.

highlights: Holidays descend. | Rates firm. | Supply sparse. | Firm charters. | Optimism. | Party retreat?
body_text:
Levels remain firm in Pakistan and India whilst Bangladesh remains somewhat muted, with domestic steel mills still refusing to engage local yards in negotiations at these higher overall levels, as Bangladeshi steel plate prices start to reflect some of the steel volatility from India.

Notwithstanding, it is expected that the Bangladeshi market will likely come back into the fray once again, especially after a month or so on the sidelines as steel prices (though volatile) remain strongly placed and this has perhaps been a period of consolidation over the traditionally softer month of Ramadan.

Away from the sub-continent waters, the Turkish markets remain muted, with declines in local and import steel, resulting in a quieter and (like the sub-continent markets) a silent week.

Overall, the supply of tonnage also remains rather sparse, with fewer wet (large LDT) units to speak of recently, given that charter rates have picked up significantly on select routes. Dry and Container sectors have also been performing rather well and this has led to an overall decline in firm and workable candidates for most of the year thus far – despite some repeat record numbers at decade-long highs above USD 700/LDT.

As such, the recycling markets remain on a firm footing overall and as the second quarter of the year gets well underway, there certainly seems as though there is still more positivity and optimism moving forward, primarily on account of continually strong showings on commodity prices and a decent demand / capacity to acquire across sub-continent locations. The Ukraine crisis certainly has its place in adding to this recent volatility in fundamentals and it’s certainly only a matter of time before this party retreats to more realistic levels.

headline: ENCOURAGED!
body_text:
The Indian market put on another strong showing this week – perhaps even encouraged by a slower working period from competing sub-continent markets on account of Ramadan holidays and the recent political upheaval in Pakistan.

Sales have taken place into Alang from existing Cash Buyer inventories, as steel plate prices, though softer mid-week, did end the week higher (about USD 5/Ton). Finally, the currency has regrettably continued to degrade, falling deeper into Rs. 76s against the U.S. Dollar, as the Ukrainian conflict shows little signs of abating – given Russia’s recently renewed aggression on the East.

Alang Recyclers are now competing on standard vessels once again, even large LDT Aframax and Suezmax tankers, not just specialist non-ferrous units, reefers, offshore tonnage, and HKC sales only.

headline: CAPTURING HEADLINES!
highlights: Sales ignite. | Political turmoil.
body_text:
Pakistan has been on fire of late and this week, a couple of sales captured the imagination of those Owners seeking levels on their units starting with a “7”, as the Capesize bulker SUNBEAM (21,018 LDT) was committed at an impressive USD 715/LT LDT, whilst the Aframax tanker ION (16,640 LDT) also fetched an equally firm USD 708/LT LDT.

Both of these sales above USD 700/LDT by optimistic Cash Buyers have yet to find End Buyers at the required levels in Gadani. However, with local steel plate prices firmly planted at record highs and a firm local demand still persevering in Gadani, the Pakistani market has managed to find itself at pole position in the market rankings.

The recent political upheaval in the country has certainly consumed most of the domestic headlines in Pakistan, with Prime Minister Imran Khan being ousted after a vote of no confidence, and his successor yet to be formally installed.

The currency too has been a recently developing source of concern for the domestic recycling community as the Pakistani Rupee (which has been historically stable against the U.S. Dollar) suddenly spiked for a brief period. This caused increasing concern amongst local Recyclers (who are already skittish about the Ukrainian crisis) about where their fundamentals might eventually lead them.

headline: SHUFLLE TRUFFLE.
body_text:
While the industry has been muscle reacting to the ongoing volatility of the Turkish Lira against the U.S. Dollar, steel fundamentals (both import and local) have managed to display impressive gains and even maintain them for the most part.

This week, however, import steel declined by about USD 10/Ton whilst local steel plate prices plummeted by an eye-popping USD 25/Ton – all while the Lira continues to float around the TRY 14.6X mark as the week ended.

Demand remains firm, local offerings remain at record-highs, and as the weather continues to warm, demand remains firm as local Recyclers remain on the lookout for tonnage.

headline: DOWN AND DIRE!
highlights: Subdued. | Diverted.
body_text:
It was another subdued week in a reluctant Bangladesh, with few firm offers or even enquiries (for tonnage) emanating from this market, where sky-high sentiments during the early part of Q1 2022 have ended up rapidly plummeting as the year progresses on.

Logically, the ongoing month of Ramadan has kept the focus of domestic Recyclers on religious celebrations, even though domestic steel plate prices remain volatile and have even declined by an additional USD 7/Ton this week, stranding Bangladesh as the lowest placed of all sub-continent markets.

As a result, it was hardly a surprise to see no market fixtures into Bangladesh for another week, with most of the available tonnage being diverted to the better placed Pakistani / Indian markets.

headline: As holidays descended across much of the sub-continent over the last week, activity and sales  logically slowed as the recycling industry enjoyed a bit of a breather.
highlights: Holiday lull. | Bangla out. | Pushing 700. | Freight firm. | Losing tonnage.
body_text:
Certainly, the recently ebullient Bangladeshi market has fallen out of contention over this past month, as domestic sentiments and pricing endured a sustained dip, despite having led the industry for much of this year.

Instead, it is the rampant Pakistani and Indian markets that continue to lead the way and continue to pay the most impressive numbers close to (and even above) USD 700/LDT (in some cases).

Having missed out on much of the market tonnage to Bangladesh over the last few months, capacity at local yards remains healthy in both Alang and Gadani. As such, eager Recyclers are snapping up the paucity of available units at increasingly firm numbers.

Indeed, freight markets remain so impressively poised that a bit of a lull has descended over the industry of late (in terms of fresh market sales). Tanker rates across certain routes have also started to fly again and coupled with an admirably performing container and dry bulk sector, recycling markets are being deprived of most of the firm and workable age-appropriate tonnage.

Regrettably, on the ‘right’ of the globe, contradicting the aggression of the sub-continent markets, is Turkey that continues to struggle through a surprising week of declines, with steel plate prices and vessel offerings plummeting towards the low USD 400s/MT.

headline: TOP GEAR!
body_text:
As the top paying market of the moment, Alang buyers are seeing much of the tonnage that was previously destined for competing sub-continent destinations, finally being diverted towards Indian shores.

It has certainly been some time since Alang sat atop the market rankings and this recent resurgence seems well deserved, given the (stunning) surge in domestic steel plate price over the last few weeks.

Surprisingly though, some worrying currency deprecations (have left the Indian Rupee straggling in the mid Rs. 76s against the U.S. Dollar) and alarming steel falls during early Q1 had put the Indian market well out of the competitive space.

Notwithstanding, there remain a number of vessels of all types and sizes from existing Cash Buyer inventories that were working firm into India (even previously unfavoured higher LDT market units), as activity ramps into top gear in this market.

headline: HOT ON THE HEELS!
highlights: Impressive feat. | Price push.
body_text:
Following hot on the heels of India, is the similarly firm Pakistani market that has been on fire of late – an impressive feat given the recent political turmoil & ousting of Prime Minister Imran Khan, in addition to the succumbing of the Pakistani Rupee against the U.S. Dollar – hitting an 18 year-low of PKR 187.50 against the U.S. Dollar as the week ended.

Despite these troubling declines in the Pakistani Rupee, there is the feeling locally that the Gadani market may push on further after Ramadan / Eid holidays, and once the new PM / cabinet has settled in, we hope this market continues to perform admirably.

Especially since local steel plate prices have been performing admirably of late and even registered a firming of nearly USD 46/Ton this week alone – resulting in demand and local sentiments remaining firmly poised.

As it stands, even well positioned vessels for Gadani are being diverted to the slightly better paying India (in some cases), and it may take a greater push on levels in order for Pakistani Recyclers to continue to get their fair share of tonnage moving forward.

headline: WIGGLING OUT?
body_text:
The Turkish market seems to have gone through a bit of a noteworthy dither this week with import steel declining by about USD 30/Ton and prices on units declining about USD 50/MT over the span of a little over a week.

The declining levels almost immediately brought about a sense of instant reservation amongst the Turkish recycling community, given that the this market is witnessing record prices amidst record (Turkish) delcines.

As a result, the Turkish market went nearly silent this week, other than accounting for a couple of high-priced deliveries that seem to have reportedly made their way to Aliaga anchorage this week.

headline: OUT OF PICTURE!
highlights: Severely weakened. | Forward prognosis firm.
body_text:
The Bangladeshi market remained out of the picture for the most part this week, not only as the country celebrated Eid holidays, but the severely weakened sentiments also lead to the utterly unworkable levels at present, as local offerings are no longer competitive even with the traditionally weaker Indian and Pakistani markets.

The currency has suffered some worrying depreciations over the past week, as steel prices have cooled off as well over the month of Ramadan. However, the overall prognosis for Chattogram remains positive / firm in the months ahead.

There also remains a general lack of supply of locally flavoured large LDT units and this may lead to some overly speculative purchases on any available tonnage once the Chattogram market resumes post Eid-holidays.

This week however, as quiet as this market was while Local Recyclers celebrated Eid, so was Chattogram’s anchorage as not a single fresh unit arrived the waterfront this week.

highlights: Sentiments down. | Wait and watch. | 700s gone. | Forwards firm. | Limited supply. | Below USD 400/MT.
body_text:
Most End Users now want to wait-and watch-market developments before offering anew on vessels at far lower levels that seem more in line with the realistic USD 650s/LDT than the struggling USD 700s/LDT most in the industry were gunning for earlier on select units.

There has certainly been some increasing and noteworthy reticence from sub-continent Recyclers about having to dip into levels at or above USD 700/LDT. So, there is perhaps some justification for watching-and-waiting if units can be secured at these currently lower levels.

Notwithstanding, despite this most recent volatility, fundamentals (including steel plate prices, which are at record highs of their own) overall remain firm across the sub-continent markets and the expectation is that appetite and sentiments will likely firm up once Eid holidays conclude from next week onwards, especially before the onset of June / monsoon season.

There has been some worrying currency depreciations in all recycling destinations (India, Pakistan, Bangladesh and even Turkey) over the past few weeks and this week, the currencies depreciated across the board, despite capacity remaining firm to take the paucity of units that are available.

Since supply is so limited at present (with all Dry Bulk and Container markets firm & Tanker charter rates starting to pick up again), recycling prices could possibly return to previous highs going into the traditionally quieter summer / monsoon season.

Finally, at the far end, the Turkish market continues to gradually degrade, as fundamentals and prices both recorded further declines this week, as levels finally fall below USD 400/MT for dry units.

headline: STEEL SLIDE!
body_text:
Indian steel plate prices have continued their dramatic volatility this week as well, as levels declined by over USD 25/Ton, only to recover marginally before the week ended.

As such, most Alang Recyclers remain reluctant to dive into fresh negotiations / new purchases and some are even hesitant to offer at all, especially at these incredibly high overall levels being sought by the few Owners who are introducing the occasional unit into the recycling markets.

Rising inflation rates and a currency that has depreciated significantly against the U.S. Dollar during Q1 are some of the fundamentals fuelling a great portion of the negativity in the Indian recycling market, along with shaky fundamentals over the past few weeks.

With the Ukrainian conflict still ongoing, India’s inflation will remain of concern going forward as Russia is one of India’s primary sources of oil and the current sanctions are making it harder for the Indian Government to acquire the same for domestic consumption, giving rise to the recent volatility / domestic inflation.

There is always some extreme volatility from week-to-week in Alang, but the status of India as the top paying recycling destination after the conclusion of Eid holidays may not be so secure after all.

headline: WOEFUL WEEK!
highlights: Need to perform. | Empty handed.
body_text:
With a political coup and a dramatically depreciating currency still fresh in memory, it has been a rather woeful week in Pakistan – both in terms of fetching fresh firm offers and also getting Gadani Recyclers to honour those deals that have already been committed locally.

At times like these, Recyclers need to take responsibility, rather than use every market movement as an excuse to fret and walk away from existing commitments. A reliable Cash Buyer counterpart is the only other element in the transaction that can help ensure a smooth performing deal.

As Eid holidays conclude and the traditionally firmer Bangladesh gets back to buying, it is hard to foresee any of the dwindling supply of recycling candidates ending up in Pakistani hands (especially at this time).

headline: TUMBLING STEADILY!
body_text:
The Turkish market continues its steady decline as levels have dropped nearly USD 80/MT in a matter of a few weeks.

Declining steel plate prices (both import and steel) and a weakening Lira (that has now fallen increasingly closer to the dreadful TRY 15.0 mark against the U.S. Dollar) that have been the primary driving forces behind local offerings.

The market has remained relatively quiet and most Recyclers are looking for tonnage basis later deliveries in the summer. As such, a permeating demand certainly seems to be present.

Just how this market will react moving past Eid remains to be seen. Yet, levels remain at record highs even today.

headline: EMERGING?
highlights: Inert. | Afra sale.
body_text:
As Bangladesh emerges from a reserved Holy month of Ramadan, pricing and sentiments remain as inert as they were pre-holidays.

There are those in the industry who expect Chattogram to come roaring back at some stage this year, especially as fundamentals have not actually declined comparatively as much over the past month and local steel plate prices have been flatlining for some time now.

Notwithstanding (and based on present circumstances), it may be a hot second before that transpires.

On the sales dront, one sale did register this week as the Aframax Tanker MASCOT 8 (16,616 LDT) managed to fetch (given the current market conditions) a healthy USD 640/LT LDT basis an ‘as is’ Singapore delivery, in ‘gas free for hot works’ condition, and an additional 250 Tons of bunkers onboard, adding to the noteworthy price on show.

Although this vessel could easily end up in competing markets, given that they are currently higher on their offerings.

headline: It has been a woeful week across all of the major ship recycling markets, with some tumultuous  declines leading to minimal interest and offers on any available tonnage.
highlights: Woeful week. | Softer summer. | Currency woe. | Steel slide. | Turkish plummet. | Heading down.
body_text:
It increasingly seems as though it may be a much softer summer given prevailing sentiments, especially as prices ease back towards the (still impressive) USD 650s/LDT mark.

Most of the deals concluded at USD 700/LDT (or above) were always seen as precariously positioned, and it remains to be seen whether End Buyers will be happy to dip back into the buying at these comparatively lower levels, given the global state of depreciating currencies and declining steel fundamentals.

The currencies in Pakistan, India, and even Turkey, remain much cause for concern to those domestic markets – especially as they continue to gradually trudge towards (or have already passed) record highs agains the U.S. Dollar.

Steel plate prices have also suffered severely in Turkey & India with India down by almost USD 45/LDT over the course of the last couple of weeks and Turkey down by about USD 120/Ton, as these markets continue their beleaguered run week after week, leaving End Buyers at these locations extremely reticent to offer on fresh tonnage.

Turkey remains the worst placed with a USD 90/MT plummet in levels post-Eid. Even (ex- market leaders) Bangladesh remain on the sidelines post-Eid and there is little hope of receiving any serious offers any time soon from either market who appear down and out.

In keeping with global stock markets this past week, all major global recycling markets remain decidedly nervy and seem only to be heading down.
