headline: CONSISTENT!
body_text:
India remains the most consistent of the sub-continent markets in terms of levels and firm offers. Prices seem to have settled into the mid USD 500s/LDT (lower than competing markets), but at least Ship Owners / Cash Buyers can be assured of payments (L/C transactions) and End Buyer performances, where both Pakistan and Bangladesh have been faltering of late.

As such, for Ship Owners & Cash Buyers alike, Alang remains the safest delivery location in the sub-continent, even if they (Sellers & Cash Buyers) must accept a slightly discounted price.

Notwithstanding, prices in the mid-to-high USD 500/LDT are still some impressive numbers to beat, considering not too long ago, the markets had tumbled down to the mid USD 200s/LT.

The currency continues to (thankfully) buoy just south of Rs. 80 against the U.S. Dollar, after some significant depreciations earlier this year. However, the ever-present volatility of local steel plate prices continues by the week as levels fell by about USD 14/Ton.

If Owners / Cash Buyers are therefore looking for a safe yet marginally unprofitable / hassle free deliveries, India remains the safest location to bank on.

headline: FLOOD AFFECTED
highlights: Under water. | Worst timing.
body_text:
Much of the focus has turned away from ship recycling this week, with some terrible monsoon flooding taking hundreds if not thousands of lives, subsequently leaving a lot of the country under water.

International aid has been sought to help in the hardest hit areas, with millions affected and displaced from their homes.

Making matters worse for the industry, the recent political coup that ousted PM Imran Khan, economic woes with a constantly Pakistani Rupee that is sitting at a devastating PKR 220 against the U.S. Dollar and local steel plate prices that too have fallen USD 20/Ton this week, these floods have come at the worst possible time for the beleaguered country.

headline: SENTIMENTS SLAUGHTERED!
body_text:
Despite registering no negative movements in import and local steel plate prices this week, and the Lira dangling precipitously at nearly TRY 18.2 against the U.S. Dollar, Aliaga Buyers are simply not interested in engaging in any negotiations at this time.

The destructive dearth of tonnage has done no favours to the local sentiment, which are still reeling from the record drop in vessel prices that have crashed by nearly 50% and that too not long ago.

Understandably, despite dwindling tonnage at local yards, the level of caution remains high, especially as the Russian-Ukrainian conflict in the Black Sea could affect the domestic economy even further.

headline: DEMAND GROWS!
highlights: Difficult summer. | Steel fall.
body_text:
Despite a growing demand in Bangladesh and a gradually emptying port report, it has been a difficult summer in terms of getting hold of new candidates, especially at some of the lower levels currently making their rounds on units, in addition to the ongoing L/C restrictions set in place by the Central Bank for any financial transaction valued above USD 2 – USD 3 million that were recently introduced.

There was news of one VLCC sale last week that is currently expected to be a Bangladeshi candidate, although the unit may well go to Pakistan or even India, given the inability of Bangladeshi Ship Recyclers to perform on these high Dollar value / large LDT transactions – including the various Capesize bulkers that are currently working for a recycling sale.

Local steel plate prices are now on a downward spiral as levels have fallen another USD 32/Ton this week alone. As such, many End Buyers are content to sit and just wait-and- watch market developments before offering afresh on any tonnage (if available).

headline: Activity and availability of sales candidates seem to be finally starting to increase as we enter  the month of September and the fourth (and final) quarter of the year.
highlights: Candidates coming. | Dry bulk dip. | Economies on edge. | Pak flooding. | Bangla L/Cs.
body_text:
Dry bulk (and particularly Capesize bulker) rates have declined noticeably of late, and this is seeing an increasing number of enquiries on dry units starting to come forth for a potential sale for recycling. This increase couldn’t have come at a better time as local demand for tonnage has been gradually ramping up again, after an extremely quiet summer / flooded monsoon.

Of course, after the collapse of the Sri Lankan economy earlier this year, difficulties persist in the sub-continent markets as both Pakistan and Bangladesh have been teetering perilously close to the brink as well.

Pakistan has been beset by catastrophic flooding over the past week, with thousands of people losing their lives and millions displaced. In fact, some international media have been reporting that nearly one-third of the country is currently underwater. As such, calls for urgent humanitarian aid have reached the international community this week, with the situation becoming increasingly dire.

Bangladesh is still struggling with L/Cs with any transaction valued at over USD 2 – USD 3 million needing Central bank approval, which is ensuring that most large LDT / higher value candidates are being diverted to competing markets and even the lower placed India, as Cash Buyers and Ship Owners both do not want to run the risk of getting stuck there, especially when levels have already fallen so much.

India remains the most resilient market and is now becoming the go to destination (albeit at lower prices) for shipowners wishing to get their vessels delivered comparatively hassle and headache free, be it at a lower price.

Finally, the Turkish market remains marginally changed from last week, as import steel and the Turkish Lira both report decreases during the week, all while local sentiments remain in the doldrums.

Rank Location Sentiment Dry Bulk USD / LDT

headline: NEED TO COMPETE!
body_text:
With Pakistan and Bangladesh both itching to return to the bidding tables and secure tonnage to fill their emptying plots, India may have to up their price offers in order to stay relevant and in contention.

Currently, Alang is unquestionably the most reliable market of the moment, due to the difficulties on L/Cs in Bangladesh and the expectedly questionable performance problems we have seen from the Pakistani market for much of this year.

Like the Bangladeshi market, Indian steel plate prices declined (marginally in comparison) about USD 8/Ton this week, whilst the Indian Rupee continues to teeter just shy of the Rs. 80 mark against the U.S. Dollar, in some continually worrying signs for the currency.

As such, even though comparatively stable, the Indian market remains the best option for tonnage, especially large LDT units valued at over USD 3 Million.

headline: DEVASTATING FLOODS
highlights: Third underwater. | Far from minds.
body_text:
The devastating floods that have affected Pakistan this week has seen as much as a third of the country left under water.

Millions of people have been displaced, thousands of lives have been lost, and some urgent international aid will be needed and will likely result in years of rebuilding.

As such, ship recycling is far from the minds of most in the country and any of the small supply of candidates currently working are likely to end up in competing markets, given the loss of confidence in the domestic ship recycling sector.

headline: STAGNATING!
body_text:
There’s only so many different ways that we can describe the stagnating state of the Turkish market, whereby fundamentals seem waveringly ‘settled’ at their current levels and local sentiment is entirely too disinterested in offering on any of the rare unit (market / private) being proposed for sale.

Local steel plate prices remained steady through the week but import steel prices have reportedly fallen by about USD 10/Ton this week. The Turkish Lira too has been buoying around the TRY 18.2X mark against the U.S. Dollar, keeping the current Aliaga sentiment buried where it currently remains.

As such, unlike the silver lining that is currently forming over sub-continent markets, the outlook for the Turkish market, unfortunately, isn’t as positive as Q4 gets underway.

headline: KEEN TO SECURE!
highlights: Emptying. | Restrictions ease?
body_text:
Having seen minimal vessels head to Chattogram shores over the last few months, Bangladeshi Buyers have been increasingly eager to secure tonnage.

Very few Local Recyclers are able to get permissions to open L/Cs on larger U.S. Dollar value / large LDT vessels as Central Bank restrictions on non-essential purchases to save up on the country’s foreign currency reserves have become very strict of late, affecting the domestic ship-recycling sector drastically.

However, there are signs that these restrictions could be eased before the end of the year (especially) if the economic situation in the country stabilises and there are certain Buyers who are now willing to open Usance L/Cs, since it seems that the worst of the currency depreciation appears to be over as the Taka steadied at a BDT 95 against the U.S. Dollar for the entire week.

Local steel plate prices, however, are an entirely different story as domestic steel fell by nearly USD 21/Ton this week, keeping local expectations and sentiments in check.

highlights: Several sales. | Unsteady. | India volatile. | Dry bulk lull. | Still firm.
body_text:
All of the major Ship Recycling destinations are still poised rather precariously, and Pakistan has seen some further depreciations on the currency towards the end of this week, whilst the country continues to battle floods, shortage of essentials, and the increasing spread of water- borne diseases, as thousands have perished in the floodwaters. Bangladesh too remains somewhat tentative, with limits on higher dollar value L/Cs still in place, local steel plate prices that took a noteworthy dive this week, and a Taka that seems to have found its stable place this week.

India has experienced (marginally less) volatile moves on steel across the week and remains the safest destination to deliver at present. Following an incredibly quiet 3 - 4 months of inactivity, there are signs of demand gearing up across sub-continent locations as most plots lie nearly dormant. Lastly, the Turkish market faces its own dithers this week, with further declines on fundamentals that are burying sentiments even further into the rut.

Overall, chartering markets have deprived recycling destinations of most tonnage, but Dry Bulk has recently started to cool off (particularly the Capesize Bulker sector), whilst Containers are also showing signs of softening, all while Tanker rates continue to shoot onwards and upwards.

It should hopefully be a busier finish to the year, as Owners look to capitalize on these still firm levels, despite the USD +100/LDT fall we have seen since the peaks of earlier this year. Rates in and around USD 550 – USD 600/LDT are still incredibly firm, given the lows we had witnessed of USD 250/LDT or so, during the early stages of the Covid pandemic.

headline: UP THEIR GAME!
body_text:
The volatility on Indian steel continues on a daily basis – often up and down by as much as USD 10 – USD 20/LDT and this week was no different, as domestic steel ended the week down by another USD 8/Ton.

End Buyers seem to have become used to this however, as with the currency, which has not yet firmly breached the dangerous level of Rs. 80 against the U.S. Dollar, but has firmed down towards the Rs. 79.7X mark.

With competing markets like Bangladesh starting to wake up from a sustained summer slumber, Indian Recyclers will certainly need to up their game if they want to secure any of the growing supply of candidates heading into Q4.

headline: FLOODS DOMINATE
highlights: Still critical. | Suezmax sold.
body_text:
The terrible floods that have beset Pakistan over the last few weeks continue to dominate the headlines, with thousands having died and millions more displaced from their homes. As being reported, nearly a third of the country has been submerged underwater with mounting troubles of delivering essential supplies, medicines, and the growing spread of water-borne diseases.

It certainly is a difficult time for Pakistan in general.

Yet, there are those in Gadani who remain determined to get back to the business of buying ships once again as one Suezmax tanker CHEVAL BLEU (21,675 LDT) was reportedly committed for an impressively strong USD 615/LT LDT basis a Pakistan re-delivery.

Having experienced some shocking and blatant renegotiations over the previous few months, Cash Buyers and Owners will certainly need to see a show of strength and some good performances on any upcoming deals before tonnage starts trickling back to Gadani with any real confidence.

headline: FESTERING!
body_text:
The situation keeps getting worse for the festering Turkish market that has continued to decline since a few months now. Local steel plate prices have reportedly dropped by about USD 20/Ton and import steel has dropped by about USD 30/Ton, essentially burying local sentiments even further.

Even the Lira has blown past the TRY 18.20 mark against the U.S. Dollar, leaving local sentiments so far down, that there remains virtually no interest from Aliaga Buyers to bid on the non-existent tonnage that is coming their way.

Having declined nearly USD 250/MT from the heady days in late spring / early summer, it seems Q4 (and likely even heading into 2023) will be a quiet time for the Turkish market.

headline: TAKA TUMULT!
highlights: Historically stable. | Taka plummets to BDT | 106.6X
body_text:
Historically, the Bangladeshi government tightly controlled the availability of U.S. Dollars in the country, in order to regulate the exchange rate between the Bangladeshi Taka and the U.S. Dollar. This resulted in the BDT being far more a stable currency over time, than its competing sub-continent neighbours.

This week, however, the Bangladeshi Central Bank finally released the U.S. Dollar rates to be set by the free markets as opposed to governmental controls, resulting in the official U.S. Dollar bank rates against the Taka to sharply plummet from region BDT 95 to BDT 106.6X within a matter of days – a drop well in excess of 10%.

This is a pivotal moment in Bangladesh’s recycling history i.e. releasing local Recyclers of the security of a key fundamental in pricing ships, that will now be just another critical item for local Buyers to strongly consider on future negotiations.

Meanwhile, as local recycling yards are at the emptiest they have been for some time now, there are signs of a lingering demand amongst local Recyclers who are looking to fill those empty spaces and get back to business.

However, local frustrations of not being able to open L/Cs and beach vessels due to the recent government mandate on limiting Central Bank approvals on any L/Cs over USD 2 – USD 3 million, runs deep amongst the domestic ship recycling fraternity and is severely limiting the top paying market from making a decent comeback on some of the recent units on offer.

We can only hope for less drastic of a re-adjustment on the effects of the government’s decision, where prices will re-adapt sooner (rather than later) and that should hopefully affect the stability of this market in the near future.

headline: CURRENCY CAUTION!
highlights: PKR and BDT | ‘Wait-and-watch’. | India steady. | Supply increase? | Busier end.
body_text:
Both locations reportedly experienced a sharp decline in their domestic currencies within the week, leading to more confusion & caution in the sub-continent and this could take a week (or more) of a ‘watch-and-wait’ attitude to see where post-currency-crash vessel pricing will eventually land.

It was the Indian market that remained the only (sub-continent) recycling destination where demand and fundamentals remained ironically stable through the course of the week, despite the ongoing (domestic) plate price volatility that has beset itself as an enduring reality.

West end of things, the Turkish market suffered another decline in local plate prices this week, ensuring local sentiment remains disinterested & depressed and would seemingly remain so, for some time ahead.

On the supply side, even as dry bulk charter levels cool off, the industry has still not witnessed a deluge of dry units being introduced for recycling, despite a collection of 90s built units that are still operating on various trades and this is where much of the supply is expected to come from as we head into the fourth quarter of the year.

There is also the expectation that containers will return for recycling at some stage, as charter rates have also come off from some of the historical highs seen over this latest bull run.

As such, the question as to whether it may be as busy an end to the year is up in the air, at least until pricing chart below eventually re-adjusts to the new realities on the ground.

headline: NUMBER 1?
body_text:
As Pakistani and Bangladeshi currencies plummeted this week, we can certainly expect their vessel offerings to negatively re-adjust moving forward and this could inadvertently slide India into the top spot, should the competing market declines be sufficient (drastic?) enough.

This certainly sounds optimistic for future sub-continent deliveries given that India has been the one notable performer whilst its neighbouring competitors continue to struggle with L/C restrictions, currency depreciations, sliding steel prices and subsequent performance issues at the waterfront.

Meanwhile, the excruciatingly dismal supply of tonnage leaves much to be desired for, despite where various markets levels stand today.

On the local fundamentals front, the Indian Rupee suffered some declines, weakening from Rs. 79.2X back to Rs. 79.6X against the U.S. Dollar this week while local steel plate prices jumped around, eventually ending the week just USD 1/Ton over last.

As such, the coming week(s) may be a surprise for the Indian Recyclers.

headline: ONE STEP FORWARD, TWO BEHIND?
highlights: PKR plummets | Sentiment deteriorates?
body_text:
Like the Bangladeshi Taka (that depreciated over 10% this week), the Pakistani Rupee depreciated tragically by over PKR 10, ending the week at PKR 236.6X. In fact, the PKR has been gradually disintegrating over the last month, to the point it has depreciated by well over 10% within this time.

Local steel plate prices aren’t helping the domestic recycling sector as they danced in sync with the currency, declining by nearly USD 17/Ton this week.

Logically, and as has historically been the case with Gadani Recyclers, local sentiments tend to be rather fragile and are naturally going to deteriorate moving forward, just how far down remains the question.

Domestic flooding also continues to be a problem & the recent effects on domestic fundamentals have only exacerbated an already tenuous situation in Gadani.

The recent decline in the PKR also calls into question the recent fixture of a Suezmax tanker to Gadani Buyers (at impressive levels over USD 600/LDT last week) as to whether the deal will eventually be ‘safely’ concluded, given Gadani Buyers questionable performances during the recent collapse.

As such, it seems as thought the Pakistani market may have taken one step forward and two steps back this week.

headline: MORE OF THE SAME!
body_text:
With local steel plate prices that have declined marginally by about USD 5/Ton, an import steel price that continues to languish USD 20/Ton lower since a couple of weeks, and a Lira that is jumping around a record TRY 18.2X against the U.S. Dollar, the ongoing situation remains a grim reminder to just how quiet Turkey has been since its USD 250/MT decline in vessel prices (and will likely continue to be).

Sentiments remain weak, Aliaga Recyclers remain disinterested in the non-existent number of units being proposed, and activity as a result, is as expected.

It seems increasingly possible that the Turkish market could be out of commission, not only for the 4th quarter this year, but also well into 2023.

headline: FRUSTRATION BUILDS!
highlights: L/Cs restricted. | Needing to fill plots.
body_text:
Frustration appears to be building in Bangladesh, with the recently imposed L/C restrictions that are still in place (any L/C over USD 2 – USD 3 million still needs an unlikely Central State Bank permission to open) and demand has been building steadily for some months now, all while a healthy number of local yards lie virtually empty of tonnage.

The Bangladeshi Taka has been on a worrying path of decline (as with the Pakistani Rupee) and declining steel prices have only exaggerated its ongoings this week. While the Bangladeshi Taka did firm up from BDT 106.6X to BDT 101.90 against the U.S. Dollar – still, a record-low for the Taka – local steel plate prices declined by USD 5/Ton this week.

With many local Buyers needing to fill their yards in order to keep them open and keep their businesses running, Bangladesh is still hoping to lead the way for any new purchases (assuming of course they can get the relevant banking permissions in place, in addition to a decent supply of tonnage).

On the sales front, a Handymax bulker was fixed from Indonesian owners as the 1990 built LUMOSO KARUNIA (7,987 LDT) fetched an impressive USD 592/LT LDT basis an ‘as is’ Singapore delivery. Given the proximity to the closest Recycling location, Bangladesh seems the inevitable choice for the concerned Cash Buyer.

headline: PLATES PLUNGE!
highlights: Doubts arise. | Demand stagnates. | Idle plots. | Tanker turnaround. | Prices steady.
body_text:
Couple of weeks ago, we saw currencies plummet in Pakistan and Bangladesh to the point, a wait-and-watch attitude encompassed both markets – at least until the first sale to a local Recycler establishes the new baseline for a type of unit in that market.

This week, it was local steel plate prices across the sub-continent board that declined to varying degrees, subsequently adding even more pressure on a potential ship-recycling resurgence for Q4.

Mixed in with the fact that there are still, very few candidates that have headed to sub-continent shores over the previous two quarters and sub-continent markets have – as a result - witnessed a gradual buildup of demand over this time, especially as plots and port reports empty out to eerily quiet levels (especially in Pakistan, which has not seen a fresh arrival at the waterfront for nearly 2 months now).

We have not seen recycling markets as dormant for many a year, as all freight sectors push on and Ship Owners are opting to continue trading, rather than getting rid of their older assets.

As Dry Bulk and Container rates continue to cool off, it may be that we see a few more vessels from these sectors before the year is out. Tankers too have seen a remarkable turnaround of late, with VLCCs finally seeing some positivity after years in the doldrums. The main supply of tankers that we have seen come for recycling over the last few years is therefore likely to dry up for the foreseeable future.

Prices remain stationed at or just below the USD 600/LDT threshold, although there are still difficulties in getting vessels sold / delivered into Pakistan (due to a constantly depreciating currency) and in Bangladesh, due to tough government imposed L/C restrictions that are still in place there for any large US$ value transactions.

headline: FEARING FALLS!
body_text:
The Indian market has been severely deprived of tonnage of late – with very few specialist or HKC green units being introduced for sale, all while competing markets in both Pakistan and Bangladesh are seeming to pay up on any available (smaller) LDT units, despite the L/C, currency, and steel plate price madness that is affecting business in those countries.

The INR has finally breached the psychologically damaging level of Rs. 80 against the U.S. Dollar, ending the week at a terrifying Rs. 81.2X, subsequently joining the declining ranks of its sub-continent neighbours.

Even local steel plate prices declined a further USD 18/Ton, leaving end Buyers nervous about the future of the local market once again, especially after a frightful year of depreciations and declines.

Notwithstanding, as with other sub-continent markets, candidates have been few-and-far between and any units that do become available are often subject to end Buyer speculation at and beyond comfort / breakeven levels.

headline: FUNDAMENTALS FLUSHED!
highlights: Unchecked depreciation. | Focus elsewhere.
body_text:
The Pakistani Rupee continues to deteriorate day-by-day, hitting disastrous new lows as the catastrophic depreciation in the currency shows no signs of abating any time soon. This week, the Pakistani Rupee plummeted to PKR 239.5X – an all-time record-low for the PKR.

Even local steel plate prices added further suffocation to the local mindset as they plummeted USD 27/Ton during the week – a rather noteworthy drop at a time the country is battling floods, a currency crisis, and plate price declines.

As such, most Buyers in Gadani remain in a wait-and-watch mode, fearful of committing any sort of price on available units (particularly large LDT / higher US$ value), as the value of that deal could very well be completely different, at the time of delivery whilst at Gadani’s waterfront.

Performance and reliability have therefore been an issue in Pakistan of late and most Ship Owners and Cash Buyers have been avoiding Gadani as a viable destination, particularly after the terrible flooding that has put a third of the country underwater, resulting in domestic focus being diverted elsewhere for the time being.

headline: QUIET Q4?!
body_text:
The Turkish market remains in the doldrums as fundamentals continue their ‘doozy’ downward spiral. Local steel plate prices remain extremely weak and the Turkish Lira continues to create new records by the week.

In fact, this week alone, steel plate prices remain unchanged and at their miserable lows since last week, whilst the Lira continues to languish at record lows, wobbling around the TRY 18.2X mark against the U.S. Dollar.

Lack of availability of tonnage, weak pricing, and poor fundamentals are all converging into a mindset that is ruining any potentially positive outcomes for this market, unless fundamentals improve.

As advised last week, we believe Q4 will be a restricted time for Aliaga.

headline: BACK DOWN!
highlights: Retreat. | Tough LCs.
body_text:
Despite what seemed to be a brief revival for the country’s domestic ship-recycling sector, Bangladeshi Recyclers have retreated their offers once again, forcing Cash Buyers with any tonnage to sell to Chattogram, to now look to trade, hold / lay-up, or even sell to competing locations.

Many of the offers emanating on the paucity of available vessels are now surfacing below USD 600/LDT as Chattogram Buyers sense a bargain or two. Unfortunately, the number of workable units at these reduced rates remain few and far between.

The ongoing restrictions on large U.S.$ value L/Cs remain tight across the country. As such, End Buyers need to have their credit facilities and banks in line, in order to adhere to the necessary government approvals on Site L/Cs.

highlights: Sentiments slip. | Pakistan woes. | Bangla struggles. | Supply improves. | Price lull.
body_text:
The Pakistani Rupee has breached historical lows and despite the odd flash of appreciation, has given Gadani Buyers extreme discomfort over the course of a torturous year of monumental declines.

Bangladesh, likewise, has suffered a currency calamity of its own, coupled with declining steel plate prices and increased limits on establishing fresh L/Cs due to a dire shortage of U.S. Dollars in the country, most Chattogram Buyers are holding back or simply unable / unwilling to offer at all on any of the freshly proposed units.

India has lost about USD 80/LDT on steel prices over the last several weeks and despite gaining a marginal USD 5/Ton this week, remains under pressure as the lowest placed of all sub- continent markets once again. The Indian Rupee has also crossed the psychologically worrying Rs. 80 mark, leaving Alang Buyers as worriedly cautious as their competitors.

Finally, the Turkish market remains depressed and unchanged for yet another week, as there are no units available to this market and at these current levels, most Owners / Cash Buyers wouldn’t commit their units to Aliaga Buyers anyways.

The supply of tonnage in the sub-continent had started to marginally improve but remains relatively strained as all freight sectors continue to perform, leaving demo markets starved of vessels once again. Prices therefore remain stranded below USD 600/LDT for another week with little chance of crossing that psychological barrier any time soon. The tendency indeed seems to suggest that levels will cool off again (perhaps down to the low USD 550s/LDT) in worrying signs for the recycling markets once again.

headline: TORRID TIME!
body_text:
Despite firming a marginal USD 5/Ton this week, the Indian ship recycling sector overall has endured a torrid time of late, with noteworthy declines in steel plate prices of about USD 80/Ton over recent weeks, and this has left Alang Buyers spooked & reluctant to offer anew on any units being proposed.

The currency too has suffered as the Indian Rupee nearly breached Rs. 81.90 (rapidly coming up on Rs. 82) against the U.S. Dollar, retreating back to the mid Rs. 81s, in further worrying performances of a key fundamental for Alang Buyers.

With a diminished supply of tonnage and price levels trailing its competing neighbours, India remains mostly out of the market. Moreover, with all port reports emptying up, it could be a while before local Recyclers are able to snag a few units, fill up their plots again, and business is ‘back to normal’.

headline: BELEAGUERED GADANI!
highlights: Markets suffer. | No sales to report.
body_text:
After continued and devastating currency depreciations, in addition to a political coup that rattled domestic fundamentals and resulted in ship prices collapsing by over USD 100/Ton, the recent catastrophic & destructive flooding was just another source of tragedy for a nation that has suffered terribly this year.

The Pakistani Rupee has firmed marginally from PKR 236 to about PKR 228, while local steel plate prices remained flat through the course of the week.

As a result, very few sales have taken place recently and domestic recycling plots in Gadani are eerily quiet after several quarters of almost complete inertia. In fact, after a couple of months of no local deliveries, Gadani’s waterfront was finally greeted by a small LDT tug this week.

Despite India falling to levels lower than Pakistan and Bangladesh also starting to cool off this week, there appears to be no sign of Pakistan securing any vessels any time soon, even though demand is starting to ramp up in the sub-continent once again.

headline: AIRPLANE MODE!
body_text:
The Turkish market seems to have entered into Airplane mode, with no change in the plummeted import and local steel plate prices, a Lira that has further collapsed towards the mid TRY 18s against the U.S. Dollar, an utter lack of tonnage, and a local sentiment that is simply unwilling to place their bets on any tonnage being proposed, especially until fundamentals display even a glimmer of stability.

As such, lack of sales and lack of any local activity is sure to see yards temporarily close, as we head deeper into Q4.

headline: EMPTY HANDED!
highlights: Eerie silence. | Losing out.
body_text:
An eerie silence has descended across the Bangladeshi market this week, with no reasonable or even firm offers to speak of, on any of the available units on offer as end Buyers prefer to wait-and-watch the market movements to see if there are further falls ahead.

Of late, targeting prices anywhere near USD 600/Ton seems to be a challenge unto itself and it may be a case of the local market seeing how truly starved of tonnage they are, before any sort of demand / hunger resumes – and hopefully at some more aggressive levels.

Unfortunately, fundamentals remain shaky and provide even less impetus for local Recyclers to be aggressive, especially as the Bangladeshi Taka weakened towards BDT 103 against the U.S. Dollar.

Moreover, Chattogram port report was a surprise this week, with a couple of large LDT vessels showing up, including a VLCC. Similar to a couple of stranded large LDT units at the waterfront, it remains to be seen just how these deliveries will be concluded.

Overall, the Chattogram market is in danger of losing out to a re-emerging Gadani altogether, and it is certainly isn’t too long before the most trustworthy and performing Indian market makes a return to form, leaving Bangladesh empty-handed once again.

headline: Sub-continent markets appear to have disappeared back into the ether for another week, as  trading markets rebound and candidates for recycling start to dissipate.
highlights: Into the ether. | Deteriorating. | Hard to gauge. | Frustrating. | Lower LDT.
body_text:
In recent weeks, volatile steel plate prices, a constantly deteriorating currency and starved U.S. Dollar credit lines across India, Pakistan and Bangladesh have all led to a near total halt on buying at anywhere near respectable levels.

As such, it is hard to gauge where prices really stand today, with so few Buyers either having the capabilities to open an L/C & perform on any sizeable vessel, and furthermore, the lack of any sort of confidence to offer and maintain any firm levels.

Even in Turkey, the situation remains unrelentingly gloomy, with little to no movement in any positive direction, all while local sentiments remain depressed on the back of a Lira that has been scraping to record-lows by the week and plate prices that remain in the dumps.

Overall, it has been a frustrating period of time for Cash Buyers with any tonnage to sell and it is becoming increasingly fraught to get vessels delivered into a beleaguered recycling market.

The rebound on VLCCs has also just come at the right time, and to see Suezmax and Aframax tankers flying and even a rebound on Cape rates of late has seen most larger LDT vessels bypass the beaches once again as they have yet another chance at squeezing out a few more voyages.

There are also very few small(er) LDT vessels on the buffet and as such, it increasingly looks as though it will be as quiet an end to the year as it has been for the last two quarters. Certainly, it is time again for the recycling markets to get their affairs in order, ahead of an anticipated higher influx of vessels next year.

headline: BARREN & IDLE!
body_text:
The Indian market appears to be degrading even further as both a plummeting currency and steel plate prices declined during the week.

The INR has become the greatest source of concern for Alang Buyers as the currency breached Rs. 82.50 against the U.S. Dollar, in what will clearly be the most stinging reason for Alang Buyers to be ultra-conservative on their bids in the near future.

Even local steel plate prices have been dithering and declined nearly USD 10/Ton during this time.

As such, India remains at the bottom of the market rankings and is presently lacking any sort of confidence to offer anew on the small supply of vessels currently available, which is clearly evident by the virtually non-existent number of fresh arrivals at Alang’s waterfront.

As we move towards the end of the year, it certainly seems that there is little hope for Alang to improve, unless the markets find their footing and the volume of tonnage increases.

headline: GLIMMER OF HOPE!
highlights: Currency appreciates. | Advantage.
body_text:
There has been a glimmer of hope in Pakistan this past week, as the currency appreciated by over 2% (towards the PKR 221 mark against the U.S. Dollar), finally giving End Buyers a little bit of encouragement moving forward – especially after what has been a dramatically silent Q3 for this market.

The local sale of a Suezmax tanker at levels close to USD 600/LT has further encouraged End Buyers to get back into the swing at reasonable numbers, and it does seem that there is a growing demand emerging from this market.

Pakistan also holds an advantage over Bangladesh in less stringent L/C requirements from the government & even L/C opening banks (despite the dire depreciations on the currency) and as such, it could be that we see a greater number of large LDT vessels heading to Gadani shores before the year is out.

headline: SUSPENDED!
body_text:
The situation in Turkey seems to be mirroring India, with both key fundamentals down in the dumps. The Lira remains of grave concern to local Buyers as it straddles a record- breaking TRY 18.60 against the U.S. Dollar.

Local and import steel prices, though marginally firmer this week, still remain so low that Aliaga Buyers feel suffocated in offering anywhere near firm levels.

The severity of the lack of tonnage isn’t helping this market any and as such, we can only hope for a firmer 2023.

headline: NOT SERIOUS!
highlights: Lacking in sales. | Quiet year end.
body_text:
Despite being presented with a few potential candidates, Bangladesh Recyclers feel as if they have the prerogative to pick-and-choose all from an absolutely shoddy number of vessels on offer!

With a lack of any serious offers and what appears to be a nervy / tentative demand, Cash Buyers are therefore diverting their vessels away from Chattogram or put their respective units back into trading lanes.

Fundamentals remain shaky as the BDT gradually declines by the week, losing another 5% as it approaches BDT 105 against the U.S. Dollar.

Although steel plate prices did jump USD 20/Ton, the level they have fallen to over recent weeks has kept the pressure on local frustrations and the willingness of Chattogram Recyclers to engage in discussions.

As it therefore stands, we expect a very quiet end to the year for Bangladesh, with minimal sales and / or negotiations, thanks to the currently enforced L/C limits and opportunistic / non-serious offers being tossed around.

highlights: Withdrawing. | No sales. | Currency chaos. | Idle yards. | Bleak outlook.
body_text:
Consequently, there have been no market sales for another week, especially as freight markets continue to impress across all sectors and recycling markets remain unchanged, depressed, and starved of tonnage all at once.

Constant currency depreciations have been the chief culprit and there seems to be a lack of confidence to import vessels, with banks being much stricter on sanctioning precious U.S. Dollar Letters for Letter of Credit (L/Cs) for vessels for recycling.

Most yards in India, Pakistan Bangladesh, and even Turkey, are therefore lying idle and will be expected to remain that way (likely) for the rest of the year, with sentiments and levels so depressed across the board.

Demand for new vessels is firming, but at completely unworkable numbers for Owners and Cash Buyers alike, especially given the decent earnings that the majority of these ships continue to make.

As such, for another week, the outlook across all sub-continent markets stays glum and gloomy, with little meaningful activity to talk of and deteriorating sentiments & pricing afflicting the industry.

headline: SPOOKED!
body_text:
India remains stranded as the lowest sub-continent destination for another week, but there are few firm candidates available to work on in order to test that theory, as yards across the sub-continent (especially Indian and Pakistan) continue to dry out.

Even offshore, specialist, and HKC vessels have been lacking of late and with such a dearth in supply, perhaps End Buyers will have to consider temporarily shuttering their plots, rather than leaving them operative and paying local labour, in the absence of any tonnage to work on.

The Indian Rupee continues to fluctuate, as it jumps between Rs. 82.60 to Rs. 82.26 against the U.S. Dollar, whilst local steel plate prices have also endured further falls this week, leaving End Buyers spooked and on edge.

headline: ENCOURAGEMENT!
highlights: Currency gains. | Looking up, finally.
body_text:
With a currency that has started to give some encouragement as it appreciates by the week (not surprising, given how far it has fallen), Pakistan is perhaps the market that has seen the most improvement and re-assurance of late.

It will hardly be a feat to challenge an altogether dormant Bangladesh, but any larger LDT tonnage now available seems like it could be heading for Gadani shores.

Notwithstanding, the shortage of tonnage only seems to exacerbate an already dwindled situation. Evidence of which presents itself with the fact that there no new arrivals in Gadani this week.

Overall, after a catastrophic year that has seen currency collapse, flooding and even a political coup, there seems to be some a positive news for Pakistani Recyclers as we enter the final chapter of the year for the ship recycling industry and Pakistan as a whole.

headline: QUIET!
body_text:
The Turkish market went through a silent and unchanged state since last week.

The only movement critical to the domestic ship recycling sector that is recording any movements (and not in the right direction) is the Turkish Lira, which finds itself hovering just north of TRY 18.50 against the U.S. Dollar.

No market tonnage, weak fundamentals, pricing that has fallen USD 250/MT and sentiments in the doldrums, has left Turkey in a prolonged quietened state.

headline: DULL & DEPRIVED!
highlights: FSU sale. | LC woes.
body_text:
The sale of one previously concluded FSU from a Cash Buyer’s inventory registered at a decent USD 600/LDT basis a Chattogram delivery. However, the unit has been concluded to one of the few local Buyers who can open an L/C with their bank (even on larger units).

Demand and open Buyers remain otherwise dull and even for smaller LDT units, there is not the appetite one would come to expect from a market that has been deprived of meaningful tonnage for most of the last few quarters.

The currency, though marginally firmer this week, remains in a perilous state. Coupled with the ongoing L/C bank restrictions from government banks and local steel plate prices that dipped another USD 5/Ton this week, is resulting in very few sales locally - albeit from a minimal stock of available vessels, which now seem to be diverted elsewhere

headline: PROGNOSIS BLEAK!
highlights: TW gathering. | Topics discussed. | Minimal activity. | Prices subdued. | Hoping for more.
body_text:
The big topics of the day were discussed, including various green and ESG measures being introduced to secure the sustainable future of recycling of older seafaring assets.

Of course, there has been minimal activity to speak of in terms of sales, as we usually see one or two (market / private) deals being concluded and rates rising during the TW conference, but the event this year seemed to be an occasion for people to catch up, rather than conclude business, especially after the recent years fractured by Covid-19.

Sub-continent markets remain subdued and deprived of tonnage as freight markets continue to fly. Depreciating currencies remain the chief concern (as do fragile steel plate prices), with rates well below USD 600/LDT and likely to move further down.

Turkey too, remains in a depressed state with levels that remain suspended USD 250/MT below its recent spring peak, as its own currency and steel plate prices remain buried, along with the sentiments that too remain diminished.

While the recent buildup seemed to suggest a greater level of activity come Q4 2022, this remains far from reality at this time as there is surprisingly little demand, due to strained banking / L/C limits and disconnected / high asking prices from Owners, leaving most plots in the sub-continent stranded in idle.

The prognosis is therefore not good heading into the final months of the year, and all will be hoping for some increased positivity and ability to buy once the expected increase of tonnage starts to come in from next year.

headline: DOLDRUMS!
body_text:
As the lowest placed sub-continent destination, Alang has seen very few firm candidates to work on in recent times – including locally favoured specialist units, offshore assets and HKC green vessels.

Pakistan and Bangladesh have been able to offer significantly higher on the trickle of tonnage available, and it is therefore likely to be a slow end to the year for Alang Buyers, after a record low influx of tonnage heads to the beaches there – evident from the weekly port reports coming out of Alang.

The Indian Rupee continues to create local tumult as it briefly breached Rs. 83 against the U.S. Dollar mid-week, only to settle at Rs. 82.60 – yet a record breaking (and worrying) level.

Local steel plate prices too haven’t been too cooperative either, as volatility ensues, despite ending the week USD 5/LDT over the previous week, leaving the local market unwilling to compete.

headline: STILL SHAKEN!
highlights: Good gathering. | Starved.
body_text:
After an altogether quieter year that was full of tragedy for a beleaguered Pakistan, it was encouraging to see many Recyclers taking a break from the silence of their domestic market and make their way across to the Tradewinds Ship Recycling forum in Dubai this week.

As such, there were no market sales to a still Pakistani market (after catastrophic flooding and a currency collapse that is wavering once again), yet, there are signs that Gadani Buyers may be willing to step up and secure tonnage once again in the months ahead.

Unfortunately, open and eligible candidates do remain starved from the market and it may take a further fall in freight rates going into next year before activity starts to pick up significantly again.

headline: UNCHANGED!
body_text:
No change in the Turkish market since last week.

The Lira continues to dance between TRY 18.5X – 18.6X, no change in steel plate prices that crashed nearly 3 weeks ago, no market tonnage being offered, and finally, no motivation from local Buyers to be competitive or even offer on any of the private vessels being reportedly offered into Aliaga.

The central Government has also lowered interest rates once again, hoping to revive an economy that is overall weaker.

The situation in the Black Sea has not helped market sentiments either with looming fears of nuclear war in the region and as such, Turkey remains a silent player in the industry.

headline: PICKY!
highlights: Turning noses up. | Diverting.
body_text:
Bangladeshi End Buyers have started to turn their noses up at tonnage or tend to offer completely unworkable / below market levels on the absolutely minimal array of vessels currently available for recycling.

Bank restrictions have of course become exponentially tighter over recent times and this is leading to a dampened demand and a reduced number of capable & performing End Buyers.

Notwithstanding, the overall lack of appetite on standard / dry vessel vessels (mostly Bulkers) has become quite alarming. Many vessels have been put back into trading lanes or diverted to other markets, so out of sorts is Bangladesh at present (and has been for much of this year).

Fundamentals also remain quirky as local steel plate prices fell about USD 15/Ton while the Bangladeshi Taka firmed back from BDT 104.X to BDT 100 against the U.S. Dollar – a nearly 4% readjustment after having fallen nearly the same amount just a couple of weeks ago.

Certainly not the ideal scenario for a destination that has remained the market leader for some time now.

headline: TWO TIER MARKET!
highlights: Sparse. | Fundamentals low. | Specialist only. | Mid 550s/LDT. | Persistent inertia.
body_text:
Fundamentals, which remain the primary driving factors of the ongoing volatility, remain precariously poised across all locations, with steel prices volatile / down and currencies still struggling to find stable footing.

As a result, a sort of two tier market has emerged, one where Cash Buyers, Brokers and Owners expect the market to be at a certain level, and another where Local Recyclers seem to be intentionally positioning prices well below asking levels, and both are about USD 50/LDT apart at this time.

Only on select and favored tonnage, like Russian built tankers or smaller LDT specialized units in decent condition are welcomed with acceptable numbers from the markets, particularly from a picky Bangladesh.

Standard Handy, Panamax Bulk Carriers, and Capes are seeing prices in the mid USD 550s/LDT (if at all), as the number of End Buyers with the ability to establish workable L/Cs across the sub-continent continues to dwindle.

Diwali holidays in India have afforded the market there a break, but the persistent inertia evident in Pakistan and Bangladesh has become a prolonged malaise and is not giving Cash Buyers any confidence to offer on any of the small number of candidates available for recycling, instead preferring the far more bullish trading sector as a viable alternative.

headline: DIWALI DELIGHT!
body_text:
Diwali holidays, the traditional festival of lights, have proved to be a rare spot of celebration for a beleaguered and reluctant Indian market this week.

Very few sales have taken place to Alang Buyers over the last two quarters (as evidenced by the record low arrivals at Alang’s waterfront), as port reports lay virtually (and painfully) empty.

While local steel plate prices posted a marginal USD 3/Ton improvement this week, it is the Indian Rupee that registered some noteworthy gains, briefly firming into Rs. 81.9 before settling back towards a still firmer Rs. 82.30 against the U.S. Dollar - as another mute week passes in India.

headline: FALTERING!
highlights: Glum. | Long road to recovery.
body_text:
As Pakistani fundamentals continue to falter, the outlook in Pakistan remains similarly bleak to other sub-continent locations, while Gadani Buyers continue to talk down levels.

There have been one or two candidates purportedly discussed for a potential sale. However, not having seen anywhere near satisfactory offers on the units, both vessels have been reportedly withdrawn and returned to the trading lanes.

On the fundamentals front, local steel plate prices declined nearly USD 25/Ton, while the Pakistani Rupee gradually weakened past PKR 222 against the U.S. Dollar this week.

As such, there certainly seem increasing signs of a silent end to 2022 and probably early ’03.

headline: MORE OF THE SAME!
body_text:
The Turkish market remains suspended in animation, with an ironic degree of stability via unchanged fundamentals, prices, and local sentiments.

Local steel plate prices have remained depressed, yet unchanged for several weeks now. The Lira continues to bob around the TRY 18.5X mark whilst market supply remains abysmal, and local Buyers remain utterly disinterested in trying to present offers that they know will not be entertained as Aliaga remain less than half of what sub-continent markets currently have on offer.

As such, this remains quite the quiet spell that Turkey is currently going through.

headline: SINKING LIKE A STONE!
highlights: Woeful. | No deal.
body_text:
Bangladesh has sunk to the bottom of the sub-continent rankings this week, with a woeful display on any of the few (and mostly smaller LDT) tonnage.

In some cases, we have seen Chattogram Buyers present opportunistic offers that are about USD 100/LDT lower than last week’s offerings – something that has seen Owners and Cash Buyers immediately withdraw their vessels, unwilling to even entertain discussions at such absurdly low and unrealistically numbers.

Fundamentals remain one of the key driving factors as the Bangladeshi Taka remains around the BDT 100 mark against the U.S. Dollar, whilst local steel plate prices seem to have declined marginally this week.

With financing from local banks increasingly hard to come by, it is therefore set to be an extremely quiet and frustrating end to the year in Bangladesh.

highlights: Too low. | Not serious. | Unworkable LCs. | Drying up. | Economic woes.
body_text:
It has become increasingly difficult to obtain any firm or serious offers from any recycling market, as currencies continue to suffer across all recycling destinations and steel endures further volatile moves this week.

Workable L/Cs are of chief concern in Bangladesh where End Buyers are struggling to obtain any sort of financing from local banks, amidst strict and ongoing governmental regulations on precious foreign currency reserves in the country.

On the rare occasion when an End Buyer is able to open a workable L/C in Bangladesh (mostly on smaller LDT tonnage), the numbers offered are so pitifully low, it’s nearly instantaneous to see tonnage withdrawn and re-directed towards competing markets.

We have even seen Local Recyclers attempting to fix deals with Cash Buyers and Owners, subject to them obtaining approval from their financing banks within 3-4 days, which of course is never going to work and will see Bangladesh deprived of any meaningful tonnage until the end of the year - or at least until some sort of stability is seen.

Finally, at the far end, after holding on and displaying some sort of stability (even though it’s in the dumps), things couldn’t get worse for Aliaga Buyers as steel prices took a small tumble this week and the Lira gradually slips further.

Overall, the economic situation across the recycling destinations remains precarious, with currencies weakening by the day and a shortage of U.S. Dollars in those countries, governments and banks are failing to sanction suitable financing for a ship recycling that they do not see as imperative under the current climate.

headline: NO NEED FOR PANIC!
body_text:
As the most resilient economy in the sub-continent, there is hope that India can lead ship recycling markets out of the current slump, or at least show them the way through some sort of stability during these trying times.

On the fundamentals front, steel plate prices have recently come off by nearly USD 21/LDT and the currency continues to trade at a worrying level over Rs. 82 against the U.S. Dollar.

Notwithstanding, tonnage supply remains so low and yards so empty, that there seems to be no need for panic just yet as the excruciating shortage of supply seems to keep Indian prices propped up.

Unfortunately, two ships with cheap scrap cargo have arrived Kandla and these billets are being offered at heavily discounted prices, which is part of the reason behind the present negative sentiments being experienced in Alang.

headline: CONSTANTLY PERPLEXED!
highlights: Following decline. | Troubling.
body_text:
Pakistan has followed the recent decline from competing sub-continent markets and is failing to offer anywhere near serious or competitive or even firm numbers on the absolute paucity of units available for recycling.

Freight markets are still performing well and therefore Gadani buyers do not need to be confused about what to offer, as they are unlikely to receive any serious candidates for the remainder of the year (particularly with their recent performance and L/C issues) and so they may as well wait for some stability to return before returning to market.

Gadani remains a market constantly perplexed, and that situation is unlikely to change at all any time soon, whilst fundamentals and the overall economic situation in the country continues to be so troubling.

Local steel plate prices declined by about USD 10/Ton and even the Pakistani Rupee is slipping back down as it passes PKR 221 against the U.S. Dollar this week. It increasingly seems as though this will be a quiet end to the year even for the Pakistani market.

headline: SLIPPING!
body_text:
Although the Turkish market had found a degree of stability, despite being in the doldrums, both import and local steel plate prices provided another stinger as they declined by about USD 10/Ton this week.

The Lira also weakened marginally this week as it ended the week just north of 18.60 against the U.S. Dollar.

This does not bode well for the Turkish market and is only facing an increased suffocation and disinterest from Aliaga Recyclers to offer on tonnage.

Seems just like the sub-continent markets, we expect little from the Turkish market until 2023.

headline: NON-ENTITY!
highlights: LC woes. | Quiet end.
body_text:
Chattogram remains a non-entity of a recycling destination, with most End Buyers unable to offer on vessels due to currently imposed L/C restrictions. Moreover, those that do have private financing available for vessel purchases, are mostly preferring to wait- and-watch in case of further market falls, rather than commit on an eventually un- affordable unit.

Even the smallest L/Cs of USD one million (and lower) are reportedly finding it challenging to get approval these days. As such, there is very little point in even testing Bangladeshi Buyers with tonnage, so dire are sentiments and permissions at present.

There was no steel plate trading this week, but the Bangladeshi Taka weakened past BDT 103 against the U.S. Dollar, reminding Bangladeshi Recyclers just how volatile the currency is anymore.

Accordingly, it is sure to be a quiet end to the year for a subdued Bangladeshi market, with minimal vessels also incoming in port reports – as confirmed by this week’s performance, where no new vessels arrived the waterfront.

highlights: Decline. | Concerns. | No approvals. | Steel turn. | Low USD 500s/LDT.
body_text:
Reliability and workable L/Cs remain a key concern for Cash Buyers and Ship Owners alike, with Bangladesh all but limiting new arrivals as the Central State bank refuses to sanction any fresh financing for ship recycling endeavors.

Reportedly, only essentials (such as food, fuel, and fertilizers) are able to procure Central State bank approval in Bangladesh, especially for the valuable reserves of U.S. Dollars that are budgeted for domestic expenses. This means that only a small number of Bangladeshi Buyers who have access to private funds are able to secure vessels for recycling at the moment.

Meanwhile, steel plate prices have been falling (more than firming) across the sub-continent markets and currencies have also depreciated astonishingly across all locations to record / historical lows and this is not giving Recyclers any confidence to offer up firm or even workable levels with any sort of certainty.

India remains perhaps the most reliable and performing of all markets, even though prices have come off significantly in Alang, and any available offers are tentative at best, coming in at the low USD 500s/LDT, levels that are now becoming an unfortunate reality of ship recycling today.

Pakistan is similarly low, with End Buyers (for the most part) keeping their eyes on competing markets before offering generally unworkable and depressed numbers.

Finally, after last week’s dip in plate prices, Turkey remains suspended in ‘airplane mode’ with an additional dip in plate prices this week, and no activity reportedly taking place in Aliaga this week.

headline: HEADACHES!
body_text:
Over recent times, the Indian Rupee has been the leading cause of headaches as the currency depreciated worryingly over Rs. 82 against the U.S. Dollar, only to have firmed up to Rs. 80.4X this week.

There have been very few sales to report (so worrying are prices) and obtaining any sort of reasonably firm offer has become a challenge unto itself, especially as fundamentals remain so shaky.

There has even been talk of numbers below USD 500/LDT (the first time we have seen talk of prices in the USD 400s/LDT for some time now) on less favoured, poor condition units - something that has steered Cash Buyers & Owners away from recycling markets at present, especially whilst freight rates remain decent across the board.

headline: DISINTERESTED & DEPRESSED!
highlights: Lacking confidence. | Few vessels.
body_text:
Pakistan is a market lacking confidence at present, and that has shown with an almost total absence of firm offers this week.

Gadani’s Performance has been in question for much of this year and this is also leading most Cash Buyers to avoid the Pakistani market given the opportunity, even for lower levels from competing markets.

Fundamentals remain depressed and shaky as the Pakistani Rupee treads around PKR 260 against the U.S. Dollar, while local plate prices took in a tiny correction this week.

Adding to the local depression is a remarkable lack of candidates to work on, so it isn’t surprising to see that all sub-continent markets remain so disinterested and depressed at present.

headline: ON IT GOES!
body_text:
After last week’s drop in import and local steel plate prices to the tune of USD 10/MT, the trend continued as both (import and local steel) reportedly registered an additional USD 10/MT drop this week as well.

Even the Lira continues to wobble and weaken by the week (down to TRY 18.6X against the U.S. Dollar), in what has been a catastrophic plummet by nearly 80% (from TRY 10) over the span of the last 12 months.

Mixed in with the ongoing utter lack of available tonnage, it’s only a matter of time until yards start shutting down altogether and Aliaga becomes the only destination for large LDT EUSRR tonnage.

headline: STARVED!
highlights: Unable to perform. | Steel slide.
body_text:
Bangladesh is a country that is currently starved of U.S. Dollars and as a consequence, starved of tonnage as well. The Central State Bank is reportedly not approving any L/Cs at present, even for purchases of USD one million.

As a result, no vessels are heading towards Chattogram for recycling at present.

Port reports are emptying out and other than a tiny unit that arrived the waterfront this week, there is essentially no fresh recycling tonnage arriving Bangladeshi shores. While demand should be firming given the current circumstances, there is very little End Buyers can do without having their finances in place, in order to secure tonnage.

Steel plate prices have also been volatile with nearly no movement over the last couple of weeks (at the new lows). Even the currency has been fluctuating wildly, jumping between BDT 102 to BDT 106 throughout the week, which is providing no incentive domestic Buyers to come forward with any sort of firm levels in the market.

No trading has even taken place this week on steel products, such is the dire market situation and currency crisis in Bangladesh at present.

highlights: Markets down. | Further fall. | LC issues. | Back to trading. | Seeking buyers.
body_text:
In fact, prices have deteriorated even further this week at all sub-continent locations and receiving indications / offers – even in the USD 400s/LDT on small LDT units - is gradually becoming a reality.

As such, any Ship Owner expecting some of the better levels (even from last week) will have to readjust their expectations much lower, in order to bring any sort of firm offer to the table.

L/Cs are continually proving to be extremely difficult to get approved these days, especially in Bangladesh, where the government is not sanctioning any fresh L/Cs for vessels, leading to a virtual standstill of the industry there.

Indeed, we have seen multiple vessels enter the market and turn straight back around for trading (even at the reduced dry bulk and container levels of today), having either not found a Buyer with a ready L/C or having suffered embarrassingly low offers.

The price ideas mentioned below are simply illusory, as the key thing today is finding a firm End Buyer at a reasonable level and with a workable L/C, which is turning out to be the most challenging of issues facing Cash Buyers at present.

Overall, it is expected to be a dark and bleak winter for a withering ship recycling industry, especially after the decade long high in prices above USD 700/LDT whilst business boomed during the early part of this year.

headline: UNCERTAIN!
body_text:
As the main performing market (without the L/C issues that Bangladesh and Pakistan have been facing of late), India is still suffering much uncertainty over where prices should realistically stand today.

Volatility in fundamentals remain in place as steel plate prices have come crashing down by nearly USD 27/Ton this week and the currency, though stable, is still standing at a worrying Rs 81.6X against the U.S. Dollar.

End Buyers and steel traders in the country have thus taken to purchasing steel imports (one vessel laden with steel cargo arrived Kandla a few weeks ago) at much lower levels than current ship recycling prices.

As it stands, Alang Recyclers have entered into a wait-and-watch mode, anticipating and fearing further falls ahead, even expecting to see new a normal into the USD 400s/LDT by the end of the year.

headline: TWO MINDS!
highlights: Holding off. | Performance issues.
body_text:
Pakistan Buyers remain in two minds – whether to go for the paucity of tonnage available in the market, or whether to hold off anticipating further market declines ahead – especially as U.S. 400/Ton prices start to emanate from India and the Pakistani market has been historically mirroring India’s offerings.

Rates have come down into the low USD 500s/LDT – in tandem with competing markets. Yet, obtaining any firm and serious numbers from tentative End Buyers is proving to be a real challenge once again.

While local steel plate prices have declined a marginal USD 5/Ton this week, it was the Pakistani Rupee that has Gadani Recyclers on caution again as the PKR declined past PKR 223 against the U.S. Dollar.

Performance issues are also at the forefront of Cash Buyer minds after some terrible stories in the form of blatant renegotiations seen at the waterfront earlier this year on arriving vessels.

Note: In last week’s edition, there was a typo in the reporting of the Pakistani Rupee against the U.S. Dollar. The correct value was PKR 220.60 against the U.S. Dollar. We apologize for any inconvenience this may have caused.

headline: DEAD!
body_text:
After consecutive weeks of declines in an already languishing import and local steel plate price, the market has seemingly continued its dormant performance this week, with no market sales or even news of market tonnage being proposed to local Buyers.

Aliaga yards remain empty, plate prices dead, the Lira is still buoying around the 18.6X mark, and with no units on offer, there is a deathly quiet emanating from this Aliaga.

As the sub-continent markets continue to falter, Turkey seems to be stealing a book from them – especially in terms of overall performance. Pricewise, it does not seem as though Turkish levels will plummet further on fresh tonnage, given how disastrously their levels have already fallen within the year.

Certainly, seems like a quiet winter ahead.

headline: HANDCUFFED!
highlights: Inert. | No sense talking.
body_text:
Bangladesh remains largely inert with domestic Recyclers unable to acquire any fresh units, due to ongoing L/C restrictions imposed by the Central Bank, and End Buyers are compelled into a silence, handcuffed by their inability to acquire and spend U.S. Dollars.

Port reports are virtually empty as Chattogram Recyclers realise they are going to lose out on a majority of the market tonnage, to competing recycling destinations and as such, they are maintaining a quieter profile.

Volatility of domestic fundamentals aren’t being too supportive of the local mindset either, as the Bangladeshi Taka firmed nearly 6% this week, improving from BDT 106 to just over BDT 101, while local steel plate prices fell by USD 30/Ton.

Notwithstanding, until the economic / LC situation in Bangladesh stabilises, there is very little sense in talking new purchases with end buyers since most are unable to perform and the very few who can open an L/C are just throwing silly, well below market opportunistic numbers.

highlights: No impact. | Cape sold. | Bangla out. | Supply low. | Uncertain realities.
body_text:
In the midst of this surge, there was one Capesize Bulker sold for HKC / strictly green recycling into India, and it is hoped that some stability on prices will be found in the week(s) ahead.

Notwithstanding, sub-continent steel plate prices have plummeted greatly this week (especially in India and Bangladesh), further adding to the ongoing stresses that have become routine in the sub-continent markets.

Bangladesh remains on the sidelines with no new L/Cs being issued by the Central Bank and only a handful of private banks / local Buyers able to open L/Cs on (primarily) small(er) LDT units.

It remains a very cautious and tentative market across the board, with most Ship recyclers deeply embedded in a wait-and-watch mode, expecting prices to fall below USD 500/LDT and currently reluctant to dip into the market on fresh purchases until a some sort of a sustained period of stability is witnessed.

Mercifully, the supply of tonnage remains low, despite dry bulk and container rates having cooled off considerably in the fourth quarter of this year. Owners have made decent money on their trading vessels this year and it seems they would rather hold and continue trading at these lower rates, rather than face the uncertain recycling realities of today.

As such, it is not expected to be a frantic end to the year across sub-continent markets, but rather a trickle of candidates may arrive to the few keen and capable recyclers who are open to acquire ahead of an anticipated busier 2023.

headline: TURBULENT!
body_text:
India has endured a largely turbulent and rollercoaster week, with the announcement of a reduction in steel and iron duties by the government (initially introduced in April of this year) seeing steel prices reportedly shoot up by Rs. 4,000 rupees in a single day, only to see the remainder of the week beset by daily dramatic falls to wipe out those gains.

In fact, by the time the week ended, local steel plate prices actually declined by USD 51/Ton overall, while the INR continues to trade in the high Rs. 81 against the U.S. Dollar – leaving this market devoid of much tonnage.

As such, there has been very little material change in prices and sentiments despite this encouraging news on duties.

On the sales front, one overly bullish Cash Buyer has speculated on the news on steel duties by purchasing Berge Bulk’s Capesize bulker for strictly HKC recycling, as the BERGE APO (20,668 LDT) managed to fetch a decent USD 523/LT LDT.

headline: SIDELINED!
highlights: Absent from buying. | HKC needs.
body_text:
Pakistan has largely remained on the sidelines for another week, watching on as local steel prices first rose then collapsed in India, and even observing a muted Bangladesh that is unable to acquire any fresh vessels.

There isn’t a large number of prospective units to work on for an increasingly hungry set of End Buyers, but since they hope to position levels well below market realities, they are unlikely to secure vessels any time soon.

Ensuring this, are shaky fundamentals and weakening prices from competing neighbors that will only encourage Gadani Recyclers to offer low. Steel plates fell by about USD 10/Ton and the currency remains in the PKR 223 region against the U.S. Dollar – certainly one of the record lows.

Furthermore, with vessels now being sold for HKC recycling only (including another Capesize bulker this week to India), unless end buyers significantly upgrade their yards with class approved HKC certification, then they may miss out again on the majority of vessels sold next year and beyond.

headline: UNCHANGED!
body_text:
Marginal improvement in import steel (to the tune of USD 10/MT), currency that is languishing in the TRY 18.6X against the U.S. Dollar, uncertainty with the conflict in the Black Sea, and primarily HKC based EUSRR Recycling candidates being welcomed at any offer level, the Turkish market has all but disappeared from the bidding tables.

Overall, it as been a quiet week and is expected to remain a quiet end to the year for Aliaga.

headline: GRAVE CONCERNS!
highlights: Lacking dollars. | Waving goodbye.
body_text:
The lack of financing in Bangladesh remains of grave concern, with most End Buyers unable to receive the relevant L/C approvals from the government, in order to buy fresh units.

An injection of U.S. Dollars into the country (as a result of an impending IMF loan to the country) may ease the ongoing liquidity crisis, but nobody in the industry is expecting a quick fix if this happens.

On the local fundamentals front, the Bangladeshi Taka continues to jostle around the BDT 100.4 mark, while local steel plate prices recorded no movements this week.

Chattogram Buyers have therefore spent another week watching the slim pickings of vessels head to competing markets, as clearly evident by local port position this week, with only one small LDT tanker having reportedly arrived the waterfront this week.

highlights: Ambling. | 200/LDT decline. | No finance. | Pak tentative. | Muted end to year.
body_text:
Prices have of course come off by about USD 200/LDT in the sub-continent markets since the stunning peaks witnessed over USD 700/LDT just earlier this year – for reference, on a standard Capesize Bulker, that is over USD 4 million lost on the residual value alone!

Bangladesh still remains largely absent on the buying front with a majority of Buyers unable to get central bank financing to open fresh Letters of Credit. There is also talk of the shortage of U.S. Dollars in the country easing once the they can agree to an IMF loan, but we are unlikely to see any clarity on this until early next year (at best). As such, Chattogram seems like it would be unavailable for the remainder of this year.

After the collapse of the currency and the government, Pakistan has yet to fully find their feet again and most End Buyers are extremely tentative and reticent in their offerings, leaving the market mostly a nonevent.

This really leaves only India as a viable sub-continent destination, which itself has endured turbulent times as the currency has once again depreciated into the high Rs. 81 against the U.S. Dollar, while local steel prices gained ground after last week’s volatile plummet, especially after the recent reduction in export duties on steel products.

Turkey on the far end remains lost, with levels of its own having plummeted about USD 250/MT and fundamentals still hampering any sort of recovery, amidst a pinching shortage of any tonnage.

It is therefore likely to be a bleak and muted end to the year, with some desperately needed stability on currencies, finance limits and steel plate prices, in order to bring nervous end buyers back to the table.
