headline: LOOKING UP!
body_text:
After last week’s plummet in steel plate prices, India has had a more positive week this week, as steel prices have come rebounding back to recover in excess of USD 26/Ton.

At first, it was curious to see steel plate prices improve after the announcement two weeks ago that export duties on iron and steel products would be reduced, only to see most of those gains lost over the subsequent week.

Even the Rupee continues to jostle in the Rs. 81.X against the U.S. Dollar, leaving the local market with a seeming sense of (newfound) stability – despite the record lows seen on the currency.

As such, local port position has been the most drastically empty it has been in a while, with no new vessels arriving this week and the last of the tonnage from earlier weeks, finally being delivered to Alang Buyers.

Should no fresh tonnage arrive next week, it would likely one of the few times that India’s port position would be completely empty.

headline: YET TO FIND FEET!
highlights: Sentiments shattered. | Focus away.
body_text:
Pakistani Buyers have yet to really find their feet, with sentiments shattered after the excessive losses suffered on ship prices so far this year.

Of course, the political and financial situation in the country remains similarly bleak, so it is perhaps of little surprise to see Gadani Buyers extremely reluctant to make anywhere near sensible or realistic offers for the few vessels being proposed for recycling.

Local steel plate prices have declined about USD 15/Ton this week, as the currency continues to languish in the mid PKR 223 against the U.S. Dollar.

As such, the focus has therefore fallen mostly on India, with Bangladesh also out of the picture due to the dire lack of financing available in the country, and all will be hoping for some greater stability and demand across the board in the sub-continent to fill empty plots again in the new year.

headline: MEDLEY OF NOTHING!
body_text:
The Turkish market continues its unremitting trudge through its ongoing recycling saga, as Aliaga yards remain deprived of meaningful (market) tonnage. While in passing, news and rumours of local beachings of off market small LDT units would surface, even those have virtually vanished over the recent months.

On the local fundamentals front, import steel improved marginally again by USD 10/MT this week, while the Lira seems to have entered a state of stasis as it jiggles around the mid TRY 18.6X against the U.S. Dollar.

With trading markets still performing well, it remains to be seen how long this lack of tonnage can keep this market moving further.

headline: WISHING ON A LOAN!
highlights: Frustrated. | Seeking funding.
body_text:
Frustrations abound in Bangladesh at present due to a lack of financing and a growing demand whilst many plots lie essentially dormant, following a completely inert previous six months of the year.

The usually fevered buying we have become accustomed to in Chattogram has completely subsided on the back of Central Bank limits prohibiting even USD 1 million purchases these days.

The currency and steel plate also continue to toy with the local psyche as the Taka bounced around a record 104 against the U.S. Dollar and steel plates fell about USD 8/Ton this week.

As such, if the increasingly anticipated IMF loan comes, it will be a major input of funding that will transform the presently dull and lifeless Bangladeshi ship recycling market.

highlights: Positivity. | Several sales. | Bangla struggles. | India emerging. | More busy?
body_text:
On the back of this seemingly positive note, one or two market sales of note even materialized this week and it does seem as though prices have bottomed out and sentiments have flatlined after losing a rather rattling USD 200/LDT, seen from the peaks witnessed earlier this year.

Bangladesh continues to struggle with L/C financing limits, but the IMF loan is reportedly in the works of being approved and with most yards currently lying empty, we expect demand and consequently prices to come back, especially once some liquidity is injected back into the domestic market.

Pakistan remains utterly tentative on new purchases, so significant have the falls been so far this year on both the currency and steel prices.

On the West End, Turkey remains buoyant at its terrible lows, with marginal (at best) improvements in fundamentals being the only news emanating from this market anymore.

As such, the market of the moment continues to be India and despite a few of HKC units also working, nearly all Cash Buyer ‘as is’ sales are being presently finalized with an Alang resale in mind.

It still remains a mystery whether it may be a slightly busier end to the year than many had been anticipating, especially with further sales likely to take place to a more settled and confident Indian sub-continent recycling market.

Once the currency situation starts to stabilize in Pakistan and funds start to become more readily available in Bangladesh, then we really could see prices push on.

headline: BACK TO BUYING!
body_text:
India remains the most stable market for another week, as a handful of sales start to take place after a mostly bleak summer / monsoon (and perhaps year overall) that has seen record low ships head to Alang.

Of course, prices have fallen significantly since the market witnessed levels in excess of USD 700 / LDT seen earlier this year, but some signs of stability and a floor being reached are encouraging end Buyers to finally dip back into the buying again.

One smaller, decent sized container unit was committed this week as the SSL CHENNAI (4,039 LDT) managed to fetch a firm USD 560/LT LDT ‘as is’ Colombo, indicating a price in the region of USD 585/LT LDT in India needs to be considered once delivery costs are accounted for.

Overall, fundamentals too (though volatile) seemed to be less shaky this week as the Rupee continues to buoy around the mid Rs. 82 against the U.S. Dollar and steel plate prices, though declining towards mid-week actually firmed by about USD 5/Ton by the time the week ended.

headline: YET TO SETTLE!
highlights: Frustrated attempts. | Stasis.
body_text:
Gadani continues to be frustrated in their attempts to purchase fresh tonnage, especially against the more confident and settled Indian market that is trumping them for a majority of the (marginal) number of vessels being introduced for recycling.

Mostly lowball / unworkable levels and even terms are emanating from Pakistan – showing the current mindset of a market that is still in a state of turmoil and confusion and with good reason.

The Pakistani Rupee continues to gradually weaken by the week as it treads past PKR 224 and steel plate prices essentially flatlined through the week.

As such, it is hardly surprising that Pakistan is still in such a state of stasis, as the ongoing political instability and dithering fundamentals in the country display very few signs of a sustained stability on the horizon.

headline: DRIFTING!
body_text:
Turkey continues to drift through the year, with no noteworthy activity to report since Aliaga Buyers broke all price records (in memory) when offers close to USD 500/MT were seen earlier in the year.

Regrettably, the short-lived spike in prices has vanished just as quickly, losing over half the value of recycling units that will head to Aliaga shores at present. As it stands, market units are virtually non-existent and even the occasional rumour of a private sale or small LDT unit arriving Aliaga anchorage have all but disappeared.

EUSRR requirements, domestic fundamentals, and a resulting vessel price have all colluded to make any market sale into Turkey an irrational competition against the Indian sub-continent.

On the fundamentals front, even though steel plate prices have marginally improved by about USD 10/MT this week, the Lira continues to degrade into the high TRY 18.6 against the U.S. Dollar – certainly a record low.

As such, Aliaga recyclers seem to be drifting through time, waiting for fundamentals and prices to improve so that the market can at least get to a competitive enough level where the voyage to the sub-continent makes less sense than delivering into Turkey.

headline: BANKING WOES!
highlights: Side-lined. | No loan.
body_text:
Bangladesh remains side-lined for yet another week, with minimal activity to report while the Central bank refuses to issue fresh L/Cs for purchases of recycling units.

Marred by plate prices that remain unchanged at their weaker levels and a Taka that continues to wiggle around the BDT 104 mark against the U.S. Dollar, local Recyclers are simply unable to compete or even complete deliveries.

As such, the industry focus has shifted towards a competing Pakistani and Indian market, who are now absorbing much of an increasing flow of tonnage for scrap.

Finally, despite talks of an IMF loan injecting some liquidity into the market, it is likely to be an extremely quiet end to 2022 in Chattogram, especially whilst these economic and banking woes endure without any sort of resolution.

highlights: Lackluster. | Tonnage flow. | Covid exit. | Stocks plunge. | Bleak end.
body_text:
On the far end, Turkey continues its dead drift through the recycling stream as rumors surface about discussions with Aliaga Buyers regarding 2023 deliveries, in addition a degree of stability in its fundamentals noticed over the last couple of weeks.

Overall, tonnage flow has started to increase as well – particularly in the container sector, which has come off significantly since the impressive peaks seen over the last two years. Tankers too, continue to trade profitably whilst dry bulk markets (and Capes in particular) endure volatile weeks of fluctuations.

Meanwhile, China’s relaxation of Covid restrictions is expected to bring some positivity back into the markets post New Year, as the world slowly gets back to normal after almost three years of varying degrees of Covid restrictions.

On the global front, stock markets have plunged this week off the back of announcements of further rate hikes, in order to try and ease some of the soaring global inflation, as recession fears in the EU, U.K., and the U.S. loom ever larger.

As such, for recycling markets, it is a slightly bleak and glum end to the year, with prices, economies, fundamentals, and sentiments showing no signs of stabilizing just yet, and thus, Sellers and Cash Buyers remain in a state of limbo when considering the sale of older assets.

headline: OPPORTUNE TIME!
body_text:
Much of the recent focus of ship sales has fallen on Indian Buyers over these past few weeks, especially with Bangladesh out of the game thanks to their ongoing L/C restrictions and a Pakistani market that is still undecided and confused on whether or even how much to offer on the odd locally (less preferred) units.

Indian prices have fallen considerably since the peaks seen earlier this year above USD 700/LDT, so it could be deemed as a good time to dip back into the buying at these lower overall levels, especially as an increasing number of Owners and Cash Buyer get accustomed to the current prices.

On the sales front and following the fixture of a similar container SSL CHENNAI last week, another small LDT container was committed this week as the VENUS C (4,394 LDT) fetched a decent USD 525/LT LDT basis an ‘as is’ Singapore delivery with 150 Tons of bunkers included in the sale at no extra cost to Buyers.

Finally, despite several beachings this week, fundamentals remain unsteady as local steel prices have fallen by nearly USD 25/LDT and the Rupee continues to waver in the mid Rs. 82 against the U.S. Dollar, leaving India behind their Pakistani competitors for the first time in several months.

headline: FINALLY POSITIVE!
highlights: Buyers enquire. | Matter of time.
body_text:
The Pakistani market has finally enjoyed its first positive week for some time, with several Buyers enquiring on available units.

The next step is to see a few deals performed smoothly, especially after some of the shocking renegotiations and non-performances witnessed from Gadani earlier in the year. End users need to try and bring some confidence back to Cash Buyers and Owners, in order for them to reroute towards Gadani shores once again.

On the local fundamentals front, local steel plate prices jumped about USD 16/Ton as the currency continues to gradually weaken, nearly grazing past PKR 225 against the U.S. Dollar this week.

As such, it is surely only a matter of time before some deals are confirmed into Gadani, despite a plethora of container candidates that are looking likely to be sold into HKC only yards in India.

headline: END IN SIGHT?
body_text:
After what has been nearly 2 quarters of no positive movement and fundamentals that have crashed early in the summer, there finally seems to be an end in sight as the markets start to adapt to the lower prices on show from Aliaga, on the back of news about prospective deliveries for a 2023 arrival.

That is certainly good news given that the Lira though abysmally weaker, is still hanging around the recent lows of TRY 18.6X against the U.S. Dollar, while import and local steel plate prices have been relatively stable for the last couple weeks.

As such, we can only hope for an increased participation from Aliaga come January (and beyond).

headline: DE-FANGED!
highlights: Out of buying. | Tough limits.
body_text:
Bangladesh remains mostly out of the buying for another week, as L/C limits and lack of financing from the Central bank has essentially stripped away End Buyer capabilities when securing new vessels.

It was of course a stunning first-half of the year in Bangladesh with some of the highest sales for years taking place above USD 700/LDT and for all types and sizes as well – Capes, Aframax tankers, and even VLCCs.

However, in addition to the financial handcuffs that local Recyclers are currently in, fundamentals are still struggling and that is further hampering local sentiments. The Bangladeshi Taka closed at BDT 105.5X against the U.S. Dollar, while local steel plate prices reportedly flatlined through the week at its current lows.

While the currency collapses under the weight of the free markets, the government introduced tougher limits on its precious U.S. Dollar reserves spending – allowing only fuel, food, and fertilisers, and thereby de-fanging the domestic ship recycling sector for the time being.

Hopefully 2023 will find Chattogram Buyers back in the fray once the Central Bank eases its restrictions.

headline: As sub-continent markets veer through the last couple of weeks towards the end of the year,  we can look back and reflect on what has been an extremely turbulent 2022.
highlights: Reflecting. | Decade peaks. | Low supply. | Charter highs. | Hitting limits.
body_text:
Prices reached decade long peaks above USD 700/LDT in the first quarter of the year before crashing back down by about USD 200/LDT, with certain trades seeing below the USD 500/LDT barrier and even into the high USD 400s/LDT on certain occasions.

On the West End, the situation was no different in Turkey, where levels too hit a record USD 500/Ton for a brief period, only to plummet about half in value (about USD 250/MT) in a rather short period, and has remained on the sidelines ever since.

Steel plate prices and especially the relevant currencies have all seen record lows against the U.S. Dollar, shattering records by the month during the summer period.

We have also seen decade lows in the supply of tonnage, with almost all freight sectors performing strongly this year, as we finally seen a much-anticipated rebound on tankers following a number of years in the doldrums.

Dry Bulk and Containers have also had outstanding years, with minimal scrapping seen in both sectors during the first half of the year. As such, moving into 2023, we do expect to see more vessels enter the market for recycling from each of these sectors, especially as freight rates have cooled off considerably towards the end of this year.

There are also a number of vessels trading right up to their limits (in terms of surveys) and due to older age profiles and reduced earnings, Owners are unlikely to pass further surveys and may well scrap with recycling rates still looking relatively firm (USD 350/LDT being the historical average). A reduction in the fleet size amidst relatively low newbuilding deliveries for 2023 should help charter rates recover and for various earning cycles to start again.

headline: YEAR END LULL!
body_text:
A number of sales have taken place into India of late, as this is the one performing market across the sub-continent that Owners and Cash Buyers can together rely on.

Prices have recently cooled off, however as steel prices have continued to dither through the week and display their ongoing volatility, while the Indian Rupee continues to struggle close to historical highs of Rs. 83 against the U.S. Dollar.

As such, many Alang Buyers remain reticent to dip back into the buying, perhaps fearing further falls ahead, as there is something of a lull going into the final weeks of the year.

headline: BOTTOMED OUT?
highlights: Sales register. | Economic fears.
body_text:
Having concluded a number of sales after a period on the sidelines, it appears that some confidence has returned to the Pakistani market, as End Buyers are satisfied to get back to the bidding tables, in the belief that the market has perhaps bottomed out and 2023 will help recycling markets overall.

Pakistan is not beset with the L/C difficulties that Bangladesh is, but there is significant turmoil in the country – both politically and economically - as the Pakistani Rupee now passes the PKR 225.5X against the U.S. Dollar.

Indeed, there have even been fears that Pakistan or Bangladesh may go the way of the recently collapsed Sri Lankan economy, and much uncertainty and fear has seeped into both markets at the end of this year as a result.

headline: 2023 HOPES!
body_text:
As with the expectation for the trading markets to slow down next year, there are increasing rumours from the Aliaga market of an increasing number of units being potentially worked basis a 2023 delivery.

Key fundamentals remain steady (as they have been for most of December) as both import and local steel plate prices have reportedly been steady with no noteworthy change as while the Turkish Lira seems to have found its new playfield around the TRY 18.6X mark against the U.S. Dollar.

With the year about to turn over and an overall holiday mood already set in, Aliaga Buyers are optimistic about a better 2023.

headline: DORMANT!
highlights: Plots empty. | No life.
body_text:
No market sales of any significance have reportedly taken place into Bangladesh over the last few months of 2022, and the outlook indeed remains somewhat bleak unless a swift and steady injection of cash can be made to free up funds for acquiring new units.

The heavily anticipated IMF loan may bring some stability early next year, but it is still uncertain to what extent this will help prop up the market again, given that fundamentals here are still shaky.

The Bangladeshi Taka briefly skipped past 105 against the U.S. Dollar, only to end the week at BDT 102.30. Even local steel plate prices, which remained flat for most of the week, did find the opportunity to fall back about USD 8/Ton before the end of the week.

With an increase of vessels set to potentially hit the market (particularly in the dry bulk and container sectors) next year, this would be a good time to kickstart a presently dormant industry back to life.

highlights: Year closing. | Sentiments down. | Bangla woes. | Price plunge. | Empty ports.
body_text:
While Bangladesh has been the main proponent of such concern – given the ongoing financial crisis that has resulted in the Bangladeshi government restricting the sanctioning of new Letters of Credit (L/Cs) for even the smallest purchases of USD 1 million and below – this week, the Pakistani government threw its hat in the ring as well, restricting a bevy of L/Cs being sanctioned on recent local purchases.

Only very few Bangladeshi buyers with private financing and Usance L/Cs are able to acquire new units, but even so, many end users seem content to take a break and watch market developments before committing afresh, with prices so uncertain.

The picture in India remains slightly rosier, even though levels have cooled off some USD 200/LDT since the peaks of over USD 700/LDT seen earlier this year. On the far end, Turkey spent another slow week devoid of tonnage, but reported marginal improvements in import and local steel – without much fanfare.

Overall, it seems many end buyers are likely still cautious, given the sustained ferocity of the falls, and having filled their plots with more expensive units at the start of the year, are now troubled as to when to buy anew to even out those losses.

Port reports have been a testament to the fact that there have been very few arrivals over the last 6 months and only now that tonnage flow is starting to increase are we seeing some movement in those markets that are able to import new vessels at some increasingly bullish numbers.

headline: PAYBACK!
body_text:
Many HKC sales (particularly from blue chip container owners) have been focused on Alang yards of late, who are finally seeing the fruits of their HKC dedication and investments into improving yards and safety standards that are finally bearing fruit.

None of the recent array of vessels sold can go to Pakistan or even the few HKC approved yards in Bangladesh, and this is of great advantage to an Alang market that is struggling on prices at the moment and the fundamentals aren’t doing much to help either.

Volatility of local steel prices continues to play with the local mindset as levels dropped by about USD 10/Ton, only to have climbed USD 15/Ton by the weekend. Even the currency continues to trade in the high Rs. 82s against the U.S. Dollar, leaving End Buyers reluctant to even pitch in on an increasing number of new sales at firm and workable market numbers.

headline: HOPE...SHATTERED?!
highlights: Top priced. | Worst over?
body_text:
Gadani remains the top priced market as we close out the year and End Buyers have finally been able to commit to fill idle plots with a variety of mostly dry bulk sales, or at least attempted to as this week, news finally broke that Pakistan’s central bank is not opening any fresh L/Cs for local recyclers – which is catastrophic to the industry, especially as vessels now start to arrive the local waterfront.

Several capes and Panamax bulkers have been sold to local Buyers who finally seemed keen to make the most of a market that has slid into the New Year and with levels in the low 500s/LDT (down about USD 200/LDT from the highs earlier in the year).

Like with global markets, fundamentals here remain weak as well as plate prices flatlined this week, whilst the Pakistani Rupee continues to deteriorate by the week against the U.S. Dollar as it passes PKR 225.50

As such, while we had hoped Pakistan would look on with renewed hope towards 2023, perhaps the worst woes of 2022 are not entirely behind them.

headline: 2023 HOPES?
body_text:
Just as the Pakistani market felt like it would have made it across the New Year with fresh sales and optimism to back, but have sadly taken 3 steps back, the Turkish market seems to be in a similar position.

Although local steel plate prices have finally made some improvements this week, a case of “too little too late” seems to have permeated in Aliaga as well, as no real movement in prices has been noted for some months now. Even the Lira – like the PKR – is dangling at its lowest against the U.S. Dollar (around TRY 18.6).

As such, we can only hope this market makes a return to form so that at least EU based tonnage can find a home at a yard in Turkey.

headline: TURNING AWAY!
highlights: No influx. | Virtual closure.
body_text:
The influx of cash expected from a pending IMF loan has yet to materialise in Bangladesh, which means we are faced with a status quo in terms of governments failing to issue Letters of Credit (L/Cs) on fresh recycling units.

As such, it has been an extremely quiet end to 2022 for new vessels in Chattogram. Even some vessels that have arrived recently have reportedly been turned away and may have to head to alternative recycling locations.

The USD 1 million limitation on fresh L/Cs has resulted in a bevy of local Recyclers resorting to snagging small LDT units, just to keep their yards pre-occupied for the time- being and this this is evident in Chattogram’s port report this week, with a healthy number of small LDT vessels having arrived the local anchorage this week.

Fundamentals heading into 2023 aren’t too promising either, with the Taka nearly hitting BDT 104 against the U.S. Dollar, whilst local steel plate prices fell a marginal USD 5/MT as the week ended.

Overall, unless Cash Buyers can find a rare End Buyer with either private financing or willing to open a Usance L/C in Bangladesh, this is a market worth avoiding for now – especially where transactions of larger LDT units is concerned!

headline: MISSING IN ACTION!
highlights: Lowest supply. | Freight flys. | Starved. | LC woes. | Price hold.
body_text:
All freight / dry sectors started to fly simultaneously at various points during 2022 and even the wet / tanker markets started rallying thereafter, and with stunning results. However, Container and Dry Bulk markets finally started to cool off towards the end of the year, and it is from these segments that we can anticipate seeing a majority of the recycling tonnage in 2023.

Compared to previous years, a much smaller number of vessels have been beached in India during 2022, and it is a similar story in Pakistan, Bangladesh, and even Turkey, where local Recyclers have been likewise starved of tonnage.

The financial situation in Pakistan as well as Bangladesh has started to become a real cause of concern to the industry, with governments in both countries now unwilling to sanction fresh L/Cs from their precious (and dwindling) U.S. Dollar reserves.

For the time being, the only sub-continent market of any reliability remains India, and whilst the supply of vessels remains mercifully low, prices are managing to hold up somewhat in Alang, while the number of small LDT arrivals at Chattogram’s waterfront has started to pick up in 2023.

Unsurprisingly, 2023 seemed to have kicked off well in Turkey as well, as steel plate prices (both import and local steel) have reported noteworthy gains over the last couple of weeks, resulting in post-New Year prices jumping by nearly USD 40/MT, finally breaching USD 300/MT – certainly an impressive return to form.

Overall, in order for levels to maintain their present buoyancy (bearing in mind the decade average on scrap prices of around USD 350/LDT), we will need each market to be firing on all cylinders this year to absorb the expected influx of vessels that will surely be seen.

headline: STEADY AS SHE GOES!
body_text:
India has been the steadiest of all recycling markets, with another strong showing from local Buyers on any units being proposed. Alang has resumed their position at the top of the recycling market rankings, especially following a woeful week in Pakistan on L/C approvals / financing.

Several Capes and even a Panamax container have reportedly been committed to local Buyers in recent weeks as Alang Recyclers finally get their appetite back, following a year that saw a decade low volume of LDT beached locally.

Fundamentals remain shaky as ever as the Rupee continues to wobble around the Rs. 82.7X mark, whilst local fundamentals dropped and gain ground again, ending the week with an overall USD 5/Ton improvement.

With more tonnage expected for recycling this year (including HKC / green recycling only units) coupled with the fact that Sellers and Cash Buyers are finally accepting the current pricing realities of the market (as evidenced by recent sales into India), it is therefore expected to be a far more dynamic market in Alang for 2023.

headline: WORRYING WEEK!
highlights: LC restrictions. | Financial uncertainty.
body_text:
It has been a worrying week in Pakistan at the start of the year, with the government suddenly placing restrictions on fresh L/Cs, leaving several end Buyers and Cash Buyers in a lurch on recently committed units, especially the few that are already at Gadani’s waterfront awaiting beaching.

Various vessels have had to be diverted from Gadani towards Alang shores, leaving Gadani Buyers empty handed once again, after what has been a dire 2022 of declines, political instability, currency chaos, and severe renegotiations that resulted into industry players avoiding this market for much of the year.

On the local fundamentals front, plate prices seemed to not trade as they flatlined for the week, while the PKR continues to slip into the abyss at it approaches PKR 227 against the U.S. Dollar.

Therefore, as with Bangladesh, until the financial situation resolves itself in Pakistan and L/Cs can be opened and released in a timely manner, most Owners and Cash Buyers are once again seeking to avoid the market for the time being.

headline: 2023 SIGNS!!!
body_text:
Despite the Turkish Lira dancing around a record TRY 18.8X against the U.S. Dollar, the Turkish market seems to be the only market that started 2023 with a bang as local steel plate prices climbed over USD 40/MT and nearly USD 25/Ton on local steel plate prices, all in a manner of a couple of weeks.

Given this market’s comparatively stable steel fundamentals and weeks of improvements have resulted in vessel prices jumping too, and for the first time since the collapse of summer 2022, have levels finally hit USD 300/MT once again.

With sub-continent levels still slipping to find their footing and with this most recent jump in prices from Turkey, it stands to be seen just how much more tonnage starts heading to Aliaga shores once again.

For now, however, this market seems like it is gearing up once again for a busy 2023.

headline: BANKING ON IMF!
highlights: Lacking LCs. | Bereft.
body_text:
Following another week of inability to open L/Cs, Bangladesh remains a market bereft of confidence, ideas, and tonnage.

Sentiments remain dull as even though end Buyers want to offer afresh on tonnage, they simply cannot under the present circumstances (restrictions).

Local steel plate prices continue to flatline, indicating bare minimum trading activity on the back of non-existent tonnage at local yards. The Bangladeshi Taka too continues to fluctuate violently between BDT 102 and BDT 106, currently having ended the week at BDT 104 against the U.S. Dollar.

As such, much will depend on the progress of the ongoing expectation that the IMF loan would likely inject some much-needed U.S. Dollars into the country, so that business and industry can resume as normal.

headline: FEARING FINANCING!
highlights: Recovery due? | Few LCs. | India focus. | Awaiting loan. | Buyers keen.
body_text:
Financing remains of chief concern in both Bangladesh and Pakistan, with very few end users capable of opening fresh L/Cs on the import of vessels, although some are getting on by with private financing, which usually means and usance (rather than sight) L/Cs or higher interest rates.

The focus therefore falls on India for another week, on the few vessels that are available from larger Container Owners. Most of these are for HKC recycling only, and as such, would be heading to Alang anyway, regardless of the L/C concerns elsewhere.

With the Chinese New Year only about a week or so away, there is perhaps a shortage of candidates as owners wait to see if freight rates improve after China returns, particularly with its Zero-Covid policy having been recently abandoned and world economies continue to try getting back to normal.

If the mooted IMF loan to Bangladesh can finally be negotiated to ease the financial crisis there, we may see further competition from a traditionally bullish Chattogram market. Buyers in Pakistan are similarly keen to buy, but without L/C financing, it is currently very hard for Cash Buyers to get paid at present, so this is another wait-and-watch scenario for this market for now.

On the far end, Turkey continues to impress as plate prices improve and despite a continually weakening Lira, local prices continue to firm up, perhaps thanks to some of the Turkey only candidates that are rumored to be working basis an early Spring delivery.

headline: MARKET OF MOMENT!
body_text:
As the go to market of the moment, Alang Buyers have been increasingly enquiring on the number of container vessels in the market that are largely for HKC green recycling.

Even for those units not intended for green recycling, given India’s financial reserves and ability to open fresh L/Cs, it may be the only destination in the sub-continent that will invariably be the final destination for recycling candidates in the foreseeable future.

On the fundamentals front, steel prices have improved over the course of the week by about USD 8/Ton, whilst the Rupee has gained some much-needed ground to finish trading in the mid Rs. 81s against the U.S. Dollar, having previously been nearly sniffing Rs. 83.

As such, most of the market activity and sales will be focussed on India for the time being, at least until Pakistan and Bangladesh sort their respective financial situations out.

headline: STUNNED!
highlights: LC inability. | Alternatives.
body_text:
The Pakistani market has been stunned by the sudden inability of domestic Recyclers to open fresh L/Cs, after restrictions were recently imposed by the state bank on spending their precious foreign currency reserves of U.S. Dollars on ships for recycling.

Several deals have therefore entered troubled waters, having previously been concluded at decent levels - the highest the sub-continent was offering just before the Christmas break.

Gadani Buyers are therefore trying to open Usance L/Cs or use private financing, rather than going through government state banks to get LCs opened and get their vessels delivered.

On the local fundamentals front, the Pakistani Rupee has been gradually decaying as it passed PKR 228 against the U.S. Dollar, only further adding to the ongoing restrictions to preserve domestic U.S. Dollar reserves.

The only impressive event that bolstered the local sentiment are local steel plate prices that skyrocketed by nearly USD 58/Ton within the week, adding to the local sentiment to figure out financing in order to ride this wave out.

headline: JUMP!!!
body_text:
The Turkish market appears to be traversing through its own private resurgence as local steel plate prices firmed another USD 7/Ton whilst offers on units jumped another USD 20/Ton this week.

All this despite import steel falling about USD 5/Ton and the Lira (like the Pakistani Rupee) slowly deteriorates towards TRY 19 against the U.S. Dollar.

Rumours of several units being talked basis an early Spring delivery have been making their rounds and given the ongoing famine of recycling tonnage, perhaps local Buyers are trying to get a jump on the market in the hopes that construction projects will resume at pace during the warmer months and plate prices will only continue to firm.

For now, Turkey is increasingly the market to consider for units coming in from the West, especially as the price gap with the Indian sub-continent continues to minimize.

headline: ABOVE & BEYOND!
highlights: Frustrations. | Pushing on.
body_text:
Prices are improving in Bangladesh; however, frustrations persist over the ongoing inability to open L/Cs and import vessels onto their emptying yards.

Now that market levels appear to be firmer, End Buyers are currently looking at alternate methods of securing financing, including either privately financed L/Cs or Usance L/Cs, but with little success so far.

Fundamentals wise, Bangladesh is doing better than before. Although local steel plate prices did drop marginally this week, it was the newfound stability in currency exchange at region BDT 105 that has helped in gradually driving prices and demand up.

Indian levels too have pushed on for another week, meaning Chattogram Buyers have to now go above and beyond their nearest competitors to give nervous Cash Buyers and Owners the confidence to head back to an underfunded and underperforming market again.

highlights: Positivity. | India sales. | Other methods. | Barren plots. | CNY holidays.
body_text:
In fact, a number of sales have reportedly even taken place at increasingly firm numbers, giving Ship Owners a greater sense of confidence to offer their recycling candidates up for sale, especially after an altogether bleak 2 quarters.

Financing problems persist in both Bangladesh and Pakistan, but End Buyers in both locations are endeavoring to find alternate solutions (rarely successful at this stage) to open L/Cs (including private financing not going through government banks, foreign currency L/Cs and even usance L/Cs), now that markets seem to be stabilizing and even firming up again.

Plots across most locations remain fairly barren after one of the slowest years (in terms of recycling volumes) in decades and as such, demand for new units is ramping up across all markets and as prices increase, so too do the number of available candidates for sale after a relative dearth at the end of last year.

Even in Turkey, despite a drop in steel plates and a currency that has been relatively unchanged for the last couple of weeks, prices have held their ground amidst growing news of units being talked about basis a Spring delivery.

Overall, the supply of vessels is mostly coming from the container sector (with another sold this week) and an increasing number of HKC green sales – thus putting the deal focus squarely on Alang for another week. Moreover, as dry bulk charter rates weaken and we enter a period of relative inactivity due to Chinese New Year holidays, we do expect to see even more dry candidates heading the recycling path in the weeks / months ahead.

headline: ATOP THE RANKINGS!
body_text:
Indian prices and demand remain atop the sub-continent ship recycling rankings, and Alang is still the preferred destination for Owners & Cash Buyers due to their L/C and performance issues in competing Bangladesh and Pakistan.

As a result, several sales have reportedly taken place into India this week, as tonnage flow increases heading into the quieter week (or two) of Chinese New Year holidays.

Firstly, the fish factory PIONER NIKOLAEV (3,899 LDT) managed to fetch a decent USD 630/LT LDT, thanks to these vessels having a greater prevalence of non-ferrous resulting in the premium price on the unit.

Subsequently, a favoured container unit (with heavy propeller and bunkers for voyage) SSL KOCHI (8,362 LDT) received an equally firm price in the region of USD 580/LT LDT basis an ‘as is’ Colombo delivery.

Indian fundamentals were promising this week, with the Indian Rupee improving sharply from Rs. 83 to Rs. 80.9 against the U.S. Dollar. Even local steel plate prices firmed during the early part of the week, only to decline and still end the week on positive note.

Overall, and has historically been the case, first quarter improvements have been a tradition of sorts and it’s only a matter of time till further positivity creeps in as the year progresses.

headline: CUT ADRIFT!
highlights: Rooted. | LC failures.
body_text:
Pakistan stays rooted in the sub-continent rankings this week and Gadani Buyers remain at risk of being swept adrift with their lowly levels and fading ability to open L/Cs and take delivery of units.

Almost all Cash Buyers are steering well clear of the Gadani market at present, on account of the recent performance issues where vessels that were committed are now finding reasons to fail, citing local inability to open fresh L/Cs and it is clear that Pakistan needs some more time to sort their affairs out before getting back to the buying.

The chief issue (as with Bangladesh) is that all new L/Cs & financing for ships has to go through the central state government bank, which is refusing to approve new purchases as it stands, due to the dire shortage of U.S. dollars in the country and constantly depreciating Pakistani Rupee that is now approaching PKR 230 against the U.S. Dollar.

As such, Pakistan seems like it will be out of the fray for the time-being, especially as most of the recent tonnage seems to be heading for HKC recycling anyways.

headline: JUMPY?!
body_text:
After a couple of weeks of stable fundamentals and prices that jumped by about USD 50/Ton, Aliaga Buyers were greeted with a surprising drop in import steel (by about USD 15/Ton) and even local steel prices (by about USD 5/Ton). Even the Lira, though slightly weaker than last week, has stabilized a touch over recent weeks.

Notwithstanding, the economics of a practically still cash flow is pushing local Recyclers to offer firmer on the few units that are reportedly being discussed for a recycling sale – so barren has the local landscape been through much of 2022.

For now, there is still no news of a fixture, but the tantalizing possibility of sales being concluded into Turkey is much more a reality today than 2 weeks ago.

headline: FEW REALISED!
highlights: Improving. | Sales elsewhere.
body_text:
Sentiments and prices have certainly improved in Bangladesh over these past few weeks, yet there have been very few sales recorded into Chattogram due to the ongoing finance and / LC issues.

Buyers are still trying their hardest to open Usance L/Cs or provide private financing, rather than going through government banks who are currently refusing to open any non-essential L/Cs.

As a result, a majority of the tonnage being proposed for sale has been focussed on India for the time being - not only HKC green sales, but also favoured containers, which are currently receiving the best prices of any market.

Finally, on the domestic fundamentals front, steel plate prices improved by about USD 7/Ton, whilst the Bangladeshi Taka seems to have settled at the BDT 105 region, further boosting the local mindset and willingness to bid on tonnage, even though most options are limited due to ongoing financial hurdles.

As such, it certainly seems to be a conflicting time ahead for the Bangladeshi market.

highlights: Holiday mood. | Container sales. | Tankers out. | Price bounce. | L/C hopes.
body_text:
A larger number of container vessels have so far been sold for recycling at the start of the year, and we are beginning to see signs that older dry bulk vessels with surveys due may follow suit in the near future as well.

Additionally, following a glut of tanker vessels concluded for recycling at the beginning of 2022, this is the one segment that is still flying and it wouldn’t be entirely unsurprising to see any meaningful recycling take place from this particular sector any time soon.

Prices and demand have also started to bounce back across Indian sub-continent markets (except Pakistan) and Turkey, although whether Pakistan and / or Bangladesh can open LC/s to import units remains an ongoing question of serious concern.

Meanwhile, after a year of sustained instability and turmoil in 2022, currencies (except in Pakistan) have finally started to settle at their current lows and there is growing optimism (certainly in Bangladesh) that talks regarding an IMF loan may bring some much needed liquidity into the country so that end buyers can open L/Cs and import tonnage once again.

Finally, steel plate prices in India, Bangladesh and Turkey were on a slightly upward trajectory this week other than Pakistan, where plate prices and the Pakistani Rupee recorded one of the worst plummets in recent memory.

headline: READY TO FIRE!
body_text:
After several sales over recent weeks at increasingly firmer levels, it has been an altogether quieter week in Alang due to various holidays, including the 74th Republic Day of India and the Chinese New Year.

On the local fundamentals front, the Indian Rupee has been trading at far steadier levels in the mid Rs. 81 against the U.S. Dollar – having previously seen hovering close to Rs. 83, whilst steel plate prices, though ever volatile, have managed to maintain their levels over the course of the week.

Indian Buyers therefore seem primed for a busier year, given the growing number of empty plots after a very slow 2022; indicating a demand that is gearing up again, leading to improved sentiments and pricing.

headline: OUT OF IT!
highlights: Frustrated. | Currency woe.
body_text:
Frustratingly for Gadani Recyclers, having offered the lowest (sub-continent) prices in addition to their recent inability to open fresh L/Cs, has unsurprisingly stranded the Pakistani market at the bottom of the sub-continent rankings, leaving local Buyers unable to import any new vessels.

Further hampering their ability to offer firm on units has been the Pakistani Rupee that has depreciated an alarming (nearly) 9% in a single day, wrapping up the week at over PKR 262 against the U.S. Dollar – a historic record for the PKR.

Pakistani steel plate prices also recorded a noteworthy decline, plunging nearly USD 64/Ton during the course of the week, leaving nearly all Gadani Recyclers on the sidelines as they sit by and watch other markets push on to acquire tonnage.

As such, until the currency, plate prices and L/C issues settle, it appears as though Pakistan will remain out of the buying for the foreseeable future.

headline: JUMPY…AGAIN?!
body_text:
After last week’s surprising drop in import steel by about USD 15/Ton and local steel prices by about USD 5/Ton, this week, both import and local steel plate prices rebounded by USD 20/Ton and USD 5/Ton respectively.

Even the Lira, seems to have stabilized a touch over recent weeks, winding down the week at TRY 18.80 against the U.S. Dollar.

Meanwhile, as per news from local sources, demand does remain strong and negotiations on units basis Spring deliveries are still ongoing, however there has been no confirmation of any fixtures into Aliaga of late.

Notwithstanding, given the recent firming of levels by over USD 50/MT, we can certainly expect news of fixtures and / or arrivals at Aliaga anchorage in coming week(s).

headline: HAMPERED!
highlights: LC issues. | Tonnage elsewhere.
body_text:
As much as domestic recyclers desire to acquire fresh units, the lack of L/C financing is severely hampering local efforts.

Indeed, a Capesize bulker was committed basis an ‘as is’ Singapore delivery and has all the hallmarks of a Bangladeshi resale. However, the ongoing restrictions on financing mean that any substantially sized vessels are unlikely to end up here for the time being.

Similarly, there are also a number of mostly container vessels working for only HKC recycling into India, which rules Bangladesh out on that tonnage as well.

Fundamentals are steady for the time being as local steel plate prices have been unchanged for the duration of the week (likely due to minimal steel trading on account of the dearth of tonnage recently delivered into Chattogram), in addition to the Bangladeshi Taka that weakened marginally past BDT 106.50.

It would certainly be interesting to see how the Bangladeshi market will perform in the coming weeks, given that there are increasing rumours of the Bangladeshi government being a few steps closer to concluding the IMF loan and hopefully return this market into the fray.

highlights: Encouraging. | Cape sale. | Demand increase. | IMF talks. | Warship tragedy.
body_text:
Now that the Chinese New Year holidays have concluded, the expected bounce in freight markets has yet to materialize, so an increased number of dry bulk and container units (in particular) have come under serious negotiations for recycling.

Even global currencies are starting to settle against the U.S. Dollar and steel plate prices have found a relatively steady place, as demand and a firm buying interest is increasing across all markets, even for Pakistan and Bangladesh, where it is often not feasible to do deals there due to the ongoing L/C restrictions.

Talks on the much-needed IMF loans are still ongoing in each country, to bring back some essential liquidity and U.S. Dollars needed to establish fresh Letters of Credit so that domestic recyclers can start to import vessels / steel once again.

In Bangladesh, there are certain / select end buyers who can open L/Cs with private financing (away from the government bank restrictions) or with Usance L/Cs, but this still provides only limited options to Cash Buyers / Owners with vessels to sell.

Finally, Turkey too continues its stable streak with firming steel prices and a currency that’s found a new plateau to rest on, resulting in vessel prices firming an additional USD 10/MT this week.

In other news, the Brazilian government owned warship Sao Paolo has tragically and unnecessarily been scuttled off the coast of Brazil with a plethora of hazardous materials on board, all while NGOs and outside observers (with no real knowledge of ship recycling) keep putting pressure on various countries (including Turkey) to deny entry of vessels for recycling.

headline: ABLE TO ACQUIRE!
body_text:
India has been the chief market of most industry players attention of late, as they continue to secure any of the admittedly small number of recycling units available so far for the year (primarily capes and containers), whilst competing Bangladesh and Pakistan continue to suffer on account of their L/C limitations.

There was one more Capesize bulker sale this week as the Chinese controlled SAMC INTEGRITY (24,181 LDT) was committed at a decent USD 518/LDT basis an ‘as is’ Singapore delivery and with bunkers included in the sale – as India remains the most likely destination.

The currency continues to trade in the low-to-mid Rs. 82 against the U.S. Dollar, whilst steel prices have fluctuated a bare minimal amount for the week but remain in overall positive territory.

headline: LITTLE POINT!
highlights: Not competitive. | Steel firm.
body_text:
Pakistan remains far from competitive at the moment, with the lowest numbers across the sub-continent and the most uncertain / unstable destination for L/C financing.

As such, many of the recent sales here have failed – only to be resold elsewhere at higher / more improved numbers, as Cash Buyers or Owners are not even checking with the Gadani market, so precarious is the situation here at present.

Steel plate prices have declined as well (about USD 12/Ton this week) and the currency plummets further past PKR 276 against the U.S. Dollar, as Gadani Recyclers continue to witness increasingly deteriorating fundamentals across the country of late and until there is stability and banks allow local Recyclers to establish fresh L/Cs once again, there is little to discuss where Pakistan is concerned.

headline: FURTHER ON!
body_text:
On the back of firming import steel prices and a currency that has found fair footing around TRY 18.80 against the U.S. Dollar, the Turkish market has pushed on further with vessel prices finding themselves improving an additional USD 10/MT this week.

While there is still no information on market tonnage being actively worked on, local associates continue to advise that a few yards are in talks for some private units basis a Spring delivery.

As such, as the dry bulk markets face possible decline, Turkey may finally be in a position to snag some units.

headline: TALKS CONTINUE!
highlights: Much talk, little action. | IMF loan.
body_text:
Amidst a renewed demand and improving fundamentals, discussions on new deals continue at pace in Bangladesh, but recyclers with the ability to perform on workable L/Cs to pay for vessels, remain few and far between.

As such, the number of locally realised deals is remarkably low as most firm tonnage continues to head towards Indian shores since the start of the year, where Sellers are assured of performances and timely payments.

Negotiations continue on the much-anticipated IMF loan, which should bring some much-needed U.S. Dollars into the country – yet, in the grand scheme of events, this will only amount to about USD 2 - 3 billion when in reality, much more is needed to ease the current liquidity crisis.

On the local fundamentals front, steel plate prices firmed an impressive USD 25/Ton, possibly on the back of some steel being offloaded from recent deliveries that is boosting local resale levels. Even the Bangladeshi Taka firmed back towards the BDT 103.50 mark, in further positive developments for the local market.

highlights: Increased flow. | India focus. | Liquidity woes. | No tankers. | 2023 positive.
body_text:
Of course, India continues to remain the primary focus due to their far more stable market conditions and ability to finance new L/Cs regardless of vessel size.

Bangladesh and Pakistan continue to struggle with liquidity issues amidst a dire lack of U.S. Dollars in each country, despite continued hope that ongoing negotiations with regards to their respective IMF loans may bring some sort of relief to their respective ship recycling sectors (and more).

Lastly, the Aliaga market was understandably quiet after massive earthquakes rocked the Turkey and Syria this week that resulted in the tragic passing of over 10,000 souls.

Overall, the main supply of tonnage continues to arrive from the feeder container sector (few Panamax containers have yet to arrive), whilst there is also an increase in the flow of dry bulk vessels, as charter rates sink to fresh lows - especially after the Chinese New Year Holidays.

There seems to be little chance of seeing tankers this year, especially as charter markets push on to new highs – something which is long overdue, following the bloodletting witnessed in this particular sector over the last few years.

2023 has commenced in an overall positive fashion for the international ship recycling markets, with an increased flow of deals and a positive market with a healthy demand across nearly all locations – and it would seem that as soon as L/C issues are sorted in both Pakistan and Bangladesh, the industry can be sure of a busy and vibrant year ahead.

headline: TEMPORARY SHOCKS!
body_text:
Despite having one of the slowest year (2022) for ship recycling in decades, falls of about USD 12/Ton on local steel plate prices in India (this week alone), and the most recent scandal surrounding the potential collapse of the Adani empire, demand in Alang remains rife for new vessels.

As the currency continues to trade in the mid Rs. 82 against the U.S. Dollar and while few expect any significant long-lasting effects from the Adani affair, this temporary shock to sentiments is expected to recover as the weeks roll on.

Several container (in particular) candidates for green recycling continue to be discussed, but there were few sales realised for the week, with an uptick in activity expected in the weeks ahead.

One sale was concluded after protracted discussions as the Navy Support vessel (converted from container with 2,200 Tons permanent ballast on board) BUNGA MAS ENAM (4,750 LDT) was concluded at a decent USD 320/LT LDT basis an ‘as is’ under tow Malaysia delivery and for guaranteed HKC recycling in Alang.

headline: LACKING BITE!
highlights: Lowest placed. | Trying best on LCs.
body_text:
As the lowest placed and least reliable ship-recycling market across the sub-continent, there has been little to cheer in Gadani of late, especially while the current inertia is expected to suffer for some time to come.

Until the U.S. Dollar credit / liquidity crisis is resolved in the country, there seems little that Gadani Buyers can do and there is little hope of fresh deals being concluded into this market any time soon.

On the local fundamentals front, domestic steel plate prices jumped nearly USD 60/Ton this week, however, the weakening Pakistani Rupee may have something to do with the change in levels as the Rupee briefly dipped past PKR 276, only to end the week at levels just north of PKR 271.

Overall, Gadani Recyclers are certainly trying to do their best to open usance L/Cs or obtain private financing / alternate means of opening L/Cs through Middle East and (especially) Dubai based banks / intermediaries in particular. Notwithstanding, whilst prices remain so off, business, and new transactions will expectedly remain muted.

headline: EARTHQUAKE!
body_text:
Turkey and Syria were jolted by what seems like a once in a century earthquake that has resulted in the untimely passing of over 10,000 souls (some putting the number past 20,000).

As a result, the market remained relatively quiet and unchanged since last week with local steel plate prices stranded on even keel and the Lira gradually weaker, yet buoying around the last TRY 18s against the U.S. Dollar.

This market is far firmer than it was a few weeks ago and we do not expect any long terms absence from Aliaga Buyers.

headline: RESURGENT!
highlights: Highest for a year. | Stunning sales.
body_text:
Having secured some hugely priced sales – not seen since this time last year, Bangladesh has enjoyed a stunning resurgence to finish atop of the price rankings this week!

The most notable sale of the week concerned that of the Sinokor controlled container XIUMEI SHANGHAI (7,276 LDT), which was fixed for an astonishing USD 640/LT LDT. Despite having a decent sized propeller, bow thruster, and about 300 Tons of bunkers included in the sale – this fixture still appears to be one well above the market and it will be interesting to see how the resale progresses!

The Panamax bulker VADI (10,085 LDT) was also finalised from Turkish owners for a decent USD 575/LDT – with about 300 Tons bunkers and a spare propeller contributing to the firmer price on show.

On the fundamentals front, despite a firming demand and local fixtures, fundamentals have in fact traded in the opposite direction (i.e., deflated) this week as the Bangladeshi Taka drops towards BDT 106 against the U.S. Dollar. Even local steel plate prices dropped a healthy USD 41/Ton, as an increasing number of vessels arrives the waterfront over the last couple of weeks.

highlights: Sales add up. | Bangla ways. | Demand builds. | India in hunt. | Firing on.
body_text:
Despite the ongoing discussions about an IMF loan in the amount of about USD 2 - 3 billion, end buyers have been working to find alternate ways to pay for vessels for some time now and without the troublesome central bank approval, which is denying the disbursements of U.S. Dollars for everything but essential items.

Demand has seems hotter in both Pakistan and Bangladesh this week, where they have been unable to import vessels for most of this year and it is good to see several deals being concluded off late, and at firming numbers to match.

India remains on the hunt for tonnage but has failed to keep up with a resurgent Bangladesh this week and will have to raise their respective game up once again, just to keep in contention to secure any available vessels.

Finally, Turkey records a small drop in import steel prices whilst levels for ships hold firm for the past month now and still no news of any market fixtures coming forth.

As the industry heads into March, the supply of tonnage has started to increase as dry (particularly Capesize bulker) rates suffer, and containers likewise show few signs of picking up just yet.

As such, after a year of reduced supply and tumbling prices, we can finally see the recycling markets starting to resume fire again, and we should expect further impressive sales and pricing in the weeks ahead.

headline: PICKING UP!
body_text:
As the second placed sub-continent market, India continues to pick up tonnage by virtue of workable L/Cs and a more reliable performance from local Recyclers, along with an increased flow of vessels that are headed for HKC green recycling.

Such was the case again this week, as the LNG carrier SEAPEK ARCTIC (23,667 LDT), was concluded for a massive USD 15 million basis an ‘as is’ Malaysia sale and for select yards & for strictly HKC recycling only.

Another container was also committed this week as the OEL SHRAVAN (7,281 LDT) fetched a decent USD 587/LT LDT basis an ‘as is’ Colombo, in the second sale from these owners this year.

Meanwhile, domestic fundamentals continue to support the local mindset as the Rupee continues to bobble around the mid Rs. 82s against the U.S. Dollar, while Indian steel plate prices firmed up another USD 10/Ton this week, keeping Bangladeshi Buyers on their toes for prospective competitive units.

headline: LOOKING ON!
highlights: Envious. | Lacking LC approval.
body_text:
Pakistan has only been able to look on enviously as competing markets have surged past and been able to acquire some decent tonnage at firming rates this week.

The main problem in Pakistan has been unworkable L/Cs and a lack of state / government bank approvals for end buyers to open fresh L/Cs and import vessels for recycling.

Adding to the state of affairs has been a steel plate price that has been unchanged this week (likely due to the utter absence of tonnage at the waterfront), in addition to a Pakistani Rupee, though marginally firmer since last week, is sitting disheveled at nearly PKR 264 – not a particularly pleasant state for domestic fundamentals.

Finally, even deals that had been previously concluded into Gadani have since failed to deliver as L/C opening banks have rejected fresh L/Cs due to the severe shortage of U.S. Dollars in the country, and as such it has been another bleak and miserable week for Pakistani ship recycling.

headline: SILENT WEEK!
body_text:
After the devastating earthquake in Turkey and Syria that has reportedly resulted in the untimely passing of over 20,000 souls, it was a relatively quiet week in Aliaga with not much activity being reported.

Steel plate prices did drop by about USD 10/Ton this week (likely on the back of diminished business dealings) as the Turkish Lira continues to buoy around a slightly weaker TRY 18.8X against the U.S. Dollar.

With not much dry tonnage being a candidate for Aliaga based recycling and sub- continent levels that are still twice as much as those from Turkey, it seems private blue- chip tonnage are the only units that seem likely to be Turkish candidates (if at all), for some time.

headline: SOARING BACK!
highlights: Story of past weeks. | Container sold.
body_text:
The story over the last few weeks has revolved around the stunning Bangladeshi resurgence, securing several impressive sales over USD 600/LDT, and finding ways to open L/Cs and import vessels once again.

The ongoing IMF loan discussions are expected to bring in about USD 2 - 3 billion of foreign capital into the country, but these discussions have yet to be concluded and as such, end buyers have been busy finding alternate means of financing and have apparently been successful on select vessels through non-governmental banks.

On the local fundamentals front, local steel plate prices flatlined through the week once again, whilst the Taka breached past BDT 106.50 against the U.S. Dollar this week – all while sales and deliveries continues at pace into Bangladesh.

Finally, another sale managed to rack up this week, with a likely resale into Bangladesh, as the smaller 1984 built Tanto of Indonesia controlled container TANTO SENTOSA (2,726 LDT) managed to fetch a rather healthy USD 490/LT LDT basis an ‘as is’ Malaysia delivery – especially considering the smaller size of the vessel.

highlights: Bangla flies. | Over 600. | India bubbling. | L/C magic. | Pakistan inert.
body_text:
Indeed, we have once again seen levels over USD 600/LDT in Bangladesh for the first time since the same time last year, and competing markets are increasingly struggling to keep up.

India has been trying its best too and has managed to secure a number of HKC green sales this year, but there is no competing with a rampant Chattogram market when they start to fire up, and it is now a case of ensuring L/Cs are in order before committing vessels at decent levels once again.

Of course, not every buyer is able to secure the requisite financing to open L/Cs, especially those that have to go through government/ state banks and are not able to transact government- controlled U.S. Dollar reserves on vessels for recycling.

Therefore, through private financing channels or with usance L/Cs, end buyers in Bangladesh are finding ways to secure much needed tonnage, with yards having virtually emptied over the last 6 - 8 months as the current L/C crisis rumbles on and markets declined from the peaks of over USD 700/LDT seen last year.

Pakistan regrettably remains sidelined for yet another week, neither competitive on price nor are local buyers able to come up with appropriate L/C financing to import vessels for the time being, resulting in a port report that has not welcomed any fresh tonnage for the last two weeks.

Finally, the Turkish market continues to firm up as both import and steel plate prices registered improvements this week, vessel prices climb another USD 20/Ton, and private sales have reportedly registered into this market.

headline: DUTY EXEMPTIONS!
body_text:
Despite the firm performance of the Alang market for a majority of this year, local buyers have been struggling to keep up with the recently strong showing emanating from Bangladesh over these past few weeks and have lost several choice / quality units as a result.

There was however a boon for Indian buyers this week as news that customs duty and GST leviable on vessels for recycling, amounting to 2.5% on the value of imported vessel will be exempted.

While this should see prices push on in the coming weeks, just how competitive Indian buyers will be as compared to a rampant Bangladesh remains to be seen, especially while fundamentals remained relatively steady through the course of this week.

headline: EXCLUDED!
highlights: Not workable. | Little point.
body_text:
Gadani recyclers have largely been excluded from the buying and offerings for most of this year, whilst they remain suspended without being to establish workable L/Cs, all while prices remain far from being competitive with their sub-continent neighbors.

Indeed, with Bangladesh pushing on so far on, Pakistan could find themselves almost USD 100/LDT off the pace, if and when they eventually get back to any sort of sensible / performance on the buying!

As it stands however, state banks are unwilling and unable to sanction fresh U.S. Dollar L/Cs, so there remains a moot point of discussing new vessels into Gadani, regardless of the continued uncompetitive pricing.

There maybe some hope on the frontline however as the PKR continues to firm, dropping just below the PKR 260 market against the U.S. Dollar, all while domestic steel plate prices (like the Bangladeshi market) flatlined for all of the week.

headline: SPRING JUMP?
body_text:
The Turkish market has reportedly jumped once again this week, as both import and steel plate prices registered improvements. The TRY also continues to trade around the 18.8X mark and there have even been rumours of local fixtures this week into Turkey.

Of course, the momentum of positivity continues as the local market remains eager to take on fresh tonnage (especially after almost a year on the absolute side-lines), as local levels also jumped by about USD 20/MT.

As most deals being concluded are direct to end buyers, hence there is not much market talk on prospective units, however, we should have further news once the units arrive locally.

headline: GRABBING HEADLINES!
highlights: Bagging deals. | LNG sold.
body_text:
Bangladesh continues to steal the headlines for another week, with a couple of showstopping larger LDT purchases, casting off the negativity that had engulfed this market for much of last year.

Demand has steadily grown as Chattogram Buyers have struggled with L/C financing on fresh purchases, but recent efforts by local Recyclers to obtain alternate / private means of financing and switching to Usance L/Cs is finally starting to pay dividends with more units being concluded of late.

First up, the Sinokor controlled LNG ADRIATIC ENERGY (32,204 LDT) was concluded for USD 22 million (with 3,760 Tons of aluminium reportedly on board) in the latest LNG sale for recycling this year, whilst the Capesize bulker AGIA TRIAS (22,132 LDT) was fixed from Greek Owners at a decent USD 578/LT LDT basis an ‘as is’ Singapore delivery with sufficient bunkers for the voyage.

On the local fundamentals front, local steel plate prices also had an impressive showing this week as levels jumped nearly USD 56/Ton while the Taka depreciated past BDT 106 several times this week, finally ending the week at said level.

highlights: Strong showing. | Sales register. | Dry improves. | India moves. | Bangla leads.
body_text:
Indeed, several sales market (and reportedly even private units) have also been concluded for the week, including another large LDT LNG (rich in non-ferrous) and another Capesize Bulker.

However, it has been a good week for dry charter rates (Capes in particular) with some healthy gains posted to alleviate some of the doom and gloom witnessed over the last few weeks. Recycling markets can therefore rest easy that the hitherto expected deluge of tonnage is unlikely to materialize any time soon.

Overaged containers and dry bulk units are still the most likely to head for recycling, amidst a healthy outlook in the tanker / wet sector at last, but the recent bullishness displayed in freight sectors has overall put a bit of a dampener on the expected output of supply.

On the local markets front, India has done away with the GST tax on the import of ships for recycling, in order to improve margins for End Buyers by about 2.5% and this has already started to reflect in the local markets that are showing greater positivity this week.

Bangladesh has been the main proponent of the surging markets for the week, with prices pushing on and sentiments soaring as demand has built up after a fairly inactive 6 - 8 months. This is in contrast to a glum Pakistani market, where L/C approvals are struggling even more than Bangladesh, whereas the Bangladeshi market is starting to ease up somewhat on L/Cs for select Buyers with private banking means for financing on fresh vessels.

At the far end, the Turkish market spent a week of inactivity, with steady plate prices (import and local), strong offerings, and still no confirmation on local fixtures.

headline: MISSING OUT!
body_text:
India has missed out once again on market tonnage to a surging Bangladeshi market for yet another week – even on a favoured LNG - rich in non-ferrous and aluminium - which tends to find a home in Alang more often than not!

This is all despite news that customs duty and GST leviable on vessels for recycling, amounting to 2.5% on the value of imported vessels, will be exempted.

Despite this recent financial benefit, end Buyers could not turn that to their advantage, and despite some lower priced green HKC sales this year, it looks set to be a struggle for Alang Buyers in the immediate future, all while prices remain stranded so far from Bangladesh.

Fundamentally, India has finally seen a stronger showing on the Rupee, which has appreciated to Rs. 81.66 (down from nearly Rs. 83) against the U.S. Dollar, while steel plate prices firmed a marginal USD 4/Ton this week.

headline: AVOIDING!
highlights: Miles off. | Stability needed.
body_text:
Pakistan is off once again, miles away from the lower priced Indian market and as such, there is simply no chance of Gadani Buyers being able to compete with a soaring Bangladeshi market as well!

Overall, Gadani Buyers are still struggling to achieve the requisite L/C approvals to import vessels, and once again have had performance issues on various deliveries where things have not gone smoothly, with some vessels even rumored to being diverted prior arrival Gadani.

Fundamentally, the Pakistani Rupee is worse off after briefly firming to about PKR 261, it depreciated to a record PKR 285.2X, finally ending the week PKR 275.8X against the U.S. Dollar. Making matters worse, a likely lack of local trading of ship’s steel has resulted in steel plate prices flatlining through the week, given the lack of any fresh arrivals over several weeks now.

It is therefore of little surprise that Owners and Cash Buyers are avoiding the Pakistani market for the time being, at least until some sort of stability and confidence in the buying can be seen.

headline: UNCHANGED!
body_text:
It has been a quiet week in Turkey this week, with not much activity to report. There has still not been any confirmation of local sales to Aliaga Buyers this week, and no further news of further discussions on fresh units either.

There has also been no reported change in import and local steel plate prices, neither has the Turkish Lira changed must beyond the TRY 18.8X levels it has been sailing through, over the last few weeks.

As such, the much anticipated ‘Spring fever’ has barely materialized, although with the market still steady, we can expect improvements moving forward.

headline: TAKING TONNAGE!
highlights: Activity excites. | LC solutions.
body_text:
After a raft of recent sales – including a Sinokor LNG and several high-priced Capes & Containers, it was a slightly slower paced week in terms of activity this time around, although sentiments and pricing remain extremely positive in Bangladesh.

Indeed, offers on select vessels are in excess of USD 600/LDT for the first time in almost a year, and this has encouraged several owners to cash in on their vintage tonnage.

The question of workable L/Cs (Letters of Credit) still remains a sensitive one, but the IMF discussions on loans, which is set to inject billions into the country and ease liquidity issues, is still ongoing.

Notwithstanding, end Buyers have managed to secure alternate means of financing (including personal / private source of funds and Usance L/Cs) to ensure Cash Buyers get paid on their incoming tonnage.

On the fundamentals front, the Taka remains steady just shy of BDT 106 against the U.S. Dollar, whilst local steel plate prices seem to have flatlined for much of the week.

Finally, in further local developments, reportedly two more Chattogram recycling yards have obtained class NK HKC certification – a testament to the hard work and desire to improve and upgrade standards locally that has led us to this impressive feat.

headline: Recycling markets remain firmly poised for another week, following a stunning resurgence by  the Bangladeshi market (in particular) that leaves them atop the price rankings board.
highlights: Bangla surge. | Over 600/LDT. | No tankers. | Decent sales. | India lags.
body_text:
Indeed, levels close to and even over USD 600/LDT are now being regularly presented on various vessels and this is inducing more Ship Owners to sell their vessels, especially as freight rates in the dry bulk and container sectors are failing to improve sufficiently for Owners to keep holding onto their aging tonnage.

Cape rates have come back this past week, leaving question marks over whether the larger LDT dry units will hit recycling markets any time soon. Overall, container and dry bulk chartering levels are still sufficiently down from the previous few restorative years.

Tankers are pretty much assured not to come for recycling anytime soon - especially as wet tonnage continues to earn impressively high numbers after the last few years of bloodletting and pain.

On the local markets front, after an extremely barren 8 months or so in Bangladesh, it is good to see the market there back firing on all cylinders and some excellent numbers have been seen in recent weeks, particularly on various LNGS, Capes, and Containers.

India lags a rampant Bangladesh by some ways but is still competitive on the raft of green HKC vessels that continue to be made available, and sentiments are indeed firming again in Alang off the back of a repeal in import duty on floating assets for recycling.

Pakistan is stranded far from any meaningful activity – both struggling with L/Cs and competitive pricing, so there is little sense talking vessels into a marginalized Gadani at present.

Finally, the Turkish market has reported a softening of import steel rates as the Lira plummets to a new record low approaching TRY 19.X against the U.S. Dollar.
