headline: KEEN TO COMPETE!
body_text:
As the second placed recycling destination, it was unsurprising to see a quieter week in Alang as Bangladeshi recyclers continue to steal the limelight with the best priced deals.

The Indian Rupee is trading in the low Rs. 82s against the U.S. Dollar and local steel plate prices (though marginally stronger this week) seem to have settled after a volatile period, with extreme fluctuations seen by the day, often fraying end user nerves / shredding confidence.

India remains in the hunt for any available vessels – particularly favoured containers or HKC green sales, of which there have been several already this year after one of the lowest years for recycling volumes during 2022.

headline: UNABLE & UNWILLING!
highlights: Dour. | Well off.
body_text:
Another dour week of inaction has passed in Gadani and there seems little hope of any serious activity taking place on offers or sales, all whilst fundamentals remain in the shambles they currently are.

For starters, Pakistani Buyers are unable to open L/Cs to import vessels and until there is greater liquidity / willingness to sanction financing on ships for recycling, it would be premature to expect any sales taking place into Gadani.

Furthermore, prices remain well off from what Bangladesh and even India are paying, so Pakistan is both unable and unwilling to acquire tonnage for recycling at present. This is also evident via local port reports, where it has been about a month since any fresh units have arrived the local waterfront.

Adding fuel to the local fire are domestic fundamentals, with local steel declining about USD 15/Ton and the Pakistani Rupee performing even worse than before, as it stands at the doorstep of PKR 280 against the U.S. Dollar.

As such, local confidence remains in shambles as fundamentals are simply not helping the Gadani ship recycling community.

headline: STATUS QUO!
body_text:
Minimal activity to report from the Turkish market this week as there is still no news of fixtures (market of private) that are emanating from Aliaga.

Local steel plate prices reportedly declined by about USD 15/Ton this week, while the Turkish Lira, like the Pakistani Rupee, is creating record lows against the U.S. Dollar as it approaches TRY 19.0.

With sub-continent levels pushing on further into the USD 600s/LDT and the gap widening from Turkish offers, it may be interesting to see how many Owners will go the Aliaga way and be willing to settle for half the residual value of their vintage units.

headline: FOCUS FALLS!
highlights: Impressive sales. | L/C solutions.
body_text:
Over the past few weeks, much of the recent focus has fallen on a rampant Bangladeshi market and some impressive sales have taken place before steel prices started to show signs of reversals / flatlining in recent days.

However, this should not put too much of a dampener on local prices, with demand still ripe and End Buyers eagerly looking to fill plots that have remained largely empty for the last half a year (at least).

Many of the ongoing L/C issues appear to be easing up gradually, particularly for the larger appetite Buyers who are able to arrange private financing on various vessels, and this is where the majority of recent sales have ended up.

Finally, whilst local steel plate prices did flatline for the much of the week, the Bangladeshi Taka approached BDT 106.75 before settling in the low BDT 106 against the U.S. Dollar for the week.

highlights: Steel pressure. | Charter turn. | Supply slows. | L/Cs ease. | IMF hopes.
body_text:
An improvement in Container and Dry Bulk charter rates has reduced the flow of candidates for recycling over the last couple of weeks and so much of the firming local demand may still go unrealized for some time.

Indeed, there has only been a trickle of vessels for sale in this last week, and so only a few Owners appear to have cashed in at these higher rates, perhaps at the peak of the market.

As such, given the diminishing supply and firming demand, prices continue to impress, particularly in a Bangladeshi market that has essentially been starved of tonnage over the last 6 - 8 months due to persistent L/C issues. Alternate methods of financing have been established (including usance L/Cs and private financing solutions) to secure some of the recent tonnage for Chattogram Buyers.

Yet, the current preference amongst local Recyclers (given the ongoing L/C restrictions) remains in trying to acquire smaller LDT tonnage, rather than the costlier large LDT vessels that may not get L/C approval – so dire is the shortage of U.S. Dollars in the country at present.

Talks over ongoing IMF loans continue in both Pakistan and Bangladesh, and once that is finalized, we should see some greater liquidity on L/Cs and the ability for all Recyclers in these markets to secure larger LDT vessels at firmer levels.

Finally, Turkey at the far end remains healthy and steady, with no changes reported in steel and still no reports on the mysterious negotiations that were reportedly taking place over recent weeks.

headline: OFF PACE!
body_text:
Declining steel plate prices (by nearly USD 12/Ton) and a depreciating currency (that saw the Indian Rupee approach Rs. 83 before settling in the mid Rs. 82 against the U.S. Dollar) have seen the jitters return to Indian Buyers and they have fallen some ways off the pace from the leading Chattogram market.

When Alang was the highest placed market in January, several HKC green vessels were introduced for sale and Alang Recyclers successfully secured several units, given their sub- continent monopoly on the number of HKC certified yards.

However, this appears to have slowed in the last month as the supply of green vessels has slowed down.

Moreover, three Bangladeshi yards are now HKC accredited to offer up some healthy competition on green tonnage, which further places increased competition and opportunities for Owners and Cash Buyers alike.

Overall, it has been a rather quiet week in Alang, stretching over onto the waterfront as well, where only one fresh arrival has been reported this week.

headline: GENERAL INABILITY!
highlights: Willing but unable. | Little point.
body_text:
There remains an ongoing willingness from Gadani Buyers to acquire tonnage, however, a general inability to do so permeates through the domestic ship recycling industry, given the ongoing L/C restrictions that remain in place and the overall lack of liquidity in the country.

There are also severe political distractions still across the country (including the ongoing arrest saga of former PM Imran Khan), whilst prices remain nowhere near their Indian and Bangladeshi counterparts.

Like Bangladesh, as local steel plate prices continue to flatline and lament, the Pakistani Rupee keeps shifting farther into oblivion as it remains suspended above PKR 280 against the U.S. Dollar.

On the waterfront, even though a vessel arrived Gadani last week week, it remains an isolated case as Pakistan has been entirely devoid of meaningful tonnage for over a month now.

As such, there is little point discussing the paucity of market units currently into Gadani, and it may be some time before we see them back in the picture with a stable currency and permission from the central state bank to spend precious U.S. Dollars on available vessels.

headline: SILENT!!
body_text:
Another week of silence and minimal activity has been reported from the Turkish market for yet another week.

While local steel plate prices (both import and local) remained reportedly stable throughout the week, the Turkish Lira has been on an entirely different trajectory as it blew past TRY 19 against the U.S. Dollar (an all-time record low).

On the sales front, there is still no news of any local fixtures and Aliaga’s waterfront reportedly remains silent as well.

As such, as levels from the sub-continent continue to firm and so does demand, it only becomes harder for Owners to consider Turkey, and for Turkish Buyers to compete with sub-continent levels.

headline: DOWN A TOUCH!
highlights: Concluding sales. | Need to up prices.
body_text:
As the leading market of the ship recycling industry, much of the sales activity has been focused into Bangladesh of late, and some tempting sales have taken place on some choice tonnage over the last few weeks.

However, much of that demand appears to have died down a hair this week, off the back of declining steel plate prices (that fell about USD 25/Ton), and the second category of Buyers are at lower levels. Even the Bangladeshi Taka weakened slightly, ending the week at BDT 106.50 against the U.S. Dollar.

Overall, the trouble for the market is that the supply of vessels has also eased up, so those hoping to still get their hands-on tonnage will have to up their prices just to secure.

headline: Sub-continent markets appear to be more tentatively poised this week, with a cooling demand  and lower levels that are increasingly reflective of domestic steel prices and have likely peaked.
highlights: Price cool. | Market peak? | Above 600/LDT. | Supply slows. | L/C hopes.
body_text:
Several sales were concluded at impressive numbers over the space of one or (maximum) two weeks before prices started to decline again by about USD 20/LDT, returning to the relative normalities of recent times.

That being said, prices are still trading above USD 600/LDT in Bangladesh and are not too far from that in India, with only Pakistan (and even Turkey) lagging significantly behind and out of the reckoning for another week.

As far as Turkey goes, other than the weekly fluctuation in steel plate prices and the Lira depreciating, not a whole lot has changed with this market that has been deprived of tonnage for a while now.

Overall, the supply of tonnage also seems to have slowed, which is encouraging for Cash Buyers with existing inventories in order to get their desired levels and not distracted by the supposed deluge of tonnage that many ship recyclers have been fearing will greet their shores.

Indeed, container charter rates have picked up from their lows seen earlier this year and so too have dry bulk levels enjoyed a rise in rates, which will see vessels from these two sectors arrive at a slower overall pace over the immediate future.

This will (hopefully) allow both Bangladeshi and Pakistani markets to sort out their chronic L/C financing issues, with it still taking much longer in order to open L/Cs and obtain bank approvals (often if going through state central government banks no approvals are forthcoming at all for the time being).

headline: CANNOT REST ON LAURELS!
body_text:
India remains slightly behind Bangladesh in their bidding on the dwindling supply of ships for recycling and need to be aware of resting on their laurels to avoid missing out on their usually guaranteed supply of HKC green tonnage.

This is because three yards in Bangladesh have obtained NK HKC certification with more seeking to upgrade their facilities similarly. As such, it may be that the advantage India currently holds could start to be increasingly challenged.

On the domestic fundamentals front, local steel plate prices firmed by about USD 10/Ton while the Indian Rupee still floats around the low Rs. 82 against the U.S. Dollar, providing some much-needed positivity to the local psyche.

Notwithstanding Bangladesh’s recent yard certification, certain owners still prefer an HKC sale into India only, but as more yards in the sub-continent are approved, those top level facilities will need to keep pushing themselves and achieving higher standards to keep the top, dark green candidates with them, especially as several container owners have fixed their units for select top yards in India so far this year – including one more private Panamax sized container only this week.

headline: SOME WAYS BACK!
highlights: Inert and unable. | Plots empty out.
body_text:
Pakistan remains some ways back from their Indian and Bangladeshi counterparts, and has largely been unable to perform on any vessels this year due to their lowest prices in the sub-continent, in addition to L/C restrictions, amidst an ongoing currency crisis and liquidity crunch across the country.

Of course, political uncertainty continues to reign, and it is unlikely we will see any serious sales taking place into Pakistan, with so much uncertainty and turmoil gripping much of the nation.

With little to no recycled material moving to domestic steel mills, local steel plate prices flatlined through the week as no material was being traded. Even the Pakistani Rupee collapsed to its lowest yet this week as the PKR hit 283.2X during the week.

Even as plots empty out and demand once again rises, prices being offered up are so far off their sub-continent competitors that there is little sense in even discussing units into Aliaga.

However, the fact that most in the industry are still distracted by the higher prices from neighboring competitors is that levels in the USD 500s/LDT are still historically impressive.

headline: UNCHANGED!
body_text:
As a recycling destination, even though levels are still nearly half of what they are in Bangladesh, the Turkish market has displayed an impressive degree of stability. Although import steel prices fell by about USD 10/Ton, local steel plate prices have remained relatively steady through the week.

Even the Turkish Lira, that has been depreciating steadily against the U.S. Dollar, has ended the week at TRY 19.0X.

There is still no confirmation on local fixtures and domestic yards have remained empty for much of the last few quarters.

Overall, little has changed in the Turkish market and the industry is still awaiting local fixtures into Aliaga.

headline: BACKLOG!
highlights: Seeking approvals. | Demand ripe.
body_text:
After a number of deals concluded over the last month or so, there has been a backlog of sales seeking Central Bank approval for the opening of fresh L/Cs in Bangladesh this week and this is leading to local delays in getting vessels cleared and paid for beaching.

As such, there has been a slowdown in sales activity whilst local Buyers struggle to sort their delivery and L/C / payment issues out, and rates remain slightly softer than the peaks they touched several weeks ago, especially due to weaker steel plate prices that have declined about USD 28/Ton.

Adding downward pressure to the local sentiment was the Bangladeshi Taka that further declined past a record BDT 107.10 against the U.S. Dollar.

Notwithstanding the above, demand remains ripe (to an extent) and local Buyers are still there to fill empty plots, as long as L/C issues are sorted. As a reminder to our readers, current prices are still at historical highs, at or above USD 600/LDT on choice units.

highlights: Quiet week. | Holiday season. | Markets stable. | L/C delays. | Expect a wait.
body_text:
With Container & Dry Bulk rates firming once again, the number of firm sales candidates also appears to have dried up and this is leaving keen recyclers empty handed for yet another week.

While there have been a plethora of sales at the start of the year, particularly in the Capesize Bulker and Container sectors, the supply has surprisingly slowed so much of late, it nearly seems like it has timed itself in sync with declining sub-continent prices.

Steel plate prices had also found themselves going through a phase of incredible volatility but seem to have stabilized (comparatively) more since, and there is still interest from the Indian and Bangladeshi markets to acquire at the present overall levels, which are hovering close to or even well above USD 600/LDT on choice units.

L/Cs remain the chief concern in Bangladesh amidst a chronic lack of liquidity in the country, and several L/Cs are left waiting for Central Bank approval, which is inevitably leading to local delays on boardings, payments, and beachings.

Owners are therefore reminded that it is not exactly business as usual (especially in Pakistan and Bangladesh to an extent), despite several sales taking place there recently.

Finally, at the far end, Turkey remains unchanged with its weekly (and marginal) fluctuations in import and local steel plate prices, as does the Lira continue on its seemingly unrelenting decline against the U.S. Dollar.

headline: HOLIDAY ADVANTAGE!
body_text:
After some worrying reversals in recent weeks and despite steel plate prices in India jumping nearly USD 10/Ton by mid-week and ending the week only USD 2/Ton above last week, Buyers in Alang seemed willing to challenge Bangladesh once again, even on the small number of recycling units that are coming to the market.

Not only is this because of the diminished number of units that are in the market for sale, but the natural side effect of it is also being felt at Alang (and Chattogram’s) waterfronts as port positions over the last couple of weeks have barely seen any fresh arrivals.

Moreover, even the Indian Rupee stayed firm in the low Rs. 82s against the U.S. Dollar.

On the sales front, there are still a couple of HKC green sales that are reportedly heading to India (despite the addition of two more NK approved yards in Chattogram last week), but even those container Owners selling for green recycling are now seeing trading interests on their vintage tonnage, pop up again due to improving charter rates.

Finally, as Ramadan holidays descend across the Indian sub-continent, India may be able to secure some much-needed tonnage (with many plots still deserted) in the next few weeks ahead.

headline: FAR FROM COMPETITIVE!
highlights: Inabilities. | Holiday reflection.
body_text:
Despite Pakistan remaining far from being competitive with their Indian sub-continent counterparts, their chief concern is still their crippling inability to get L/Cs approved by the Central Government Bank for any new vessels.

Adding to their frustrations have been (a) the Pakistani Rupee that is now trading at a record PKR 283.60 against the U.S. Dollar, (b) steel plate prices that have flatlined once again due to lack of trading, and (c) even with the minimal supply of tonnage, most units will not be heading towards Gadani shores as domestic recyclers are unable to offer competitively.

As such, Gadani remains an inert market for ship recycling for another week, and there are few signs that this market will get back to being competitive any time soon.

Therefore, as Ramadan holidays commence, it is perhaps an appropriate time to reflect on just how a turbulent a period it has been for Pakistan as a country, and hopefully post holidays, there can be some real and workable progress to get Gadani back in action once again.

headline: EAGER, YET STUCK!
body_text:
Even though import and local steel plate prices registered improvements of about USD 10/Ton this week and local offerings are still strong (on the back of an excruciatingly diminished supply resulting in Recyclers holding their prices), Aliaga yards continue to suffer.

The Lira has also been dwindling, breaking records with each passing week that has resulted in the Lira now floating around the mid TRY 19.1X mark against the U.S. Dollar.

With the recent rumours of local fixtures still being unconfirmed and no further information of market units being proposed to Turkish yards, it remains clearly evident that this market is officially stuck until Ramadan is concluded.

headline: FACING DELAYS!
highlights: Added time. | Still positive.
body_text:
Several vessels have faced delays upon arrival in Chattogram, due to the added time it is now taking to get Central Bank Approval to get L/Cs open, particularly on the larger LDT units.

As a result, tides are now being missed, with Cash Buyers and Owners left frustrated at these ongoing delays. It is therefore recommended for Owners / Cash Buyers of arriving tonnage to be prepared to wait additional times when delivering vessels into Bangladesh.

Fundamentals remain weak, yet steady, as the Bangladeshi Taka firms towards BDT 106 against the U.S. Dollar, while local steel plate prices flatline on the back of virtually no new arrivals / deliveries through March.

This week however, a series of arrivals does indicate there may be some movement in the markets and more units may be introduced going forward, given how painfully absent any tonnage has been of late.

headline: With holidays underway across much of the world, it has been a far quieter week in terms of  sales & activity, whilst sentiments and pricing remain further muted as a result.
highlights: Muted activity. | LC delays. | Precarious. | Demand ripe. | Pick up.
body_text:
Several vessels have arrived in Bangladesh for delivery this week despite it taking much longer these days to get the L/Cs in order. As such, to have smooth boardings & beachings, it is therefore recommended to maintain at least five days prior arrival, in order to allow for local Buyers L/Cs to open, release, and be credited to Owners / Cash Buyers before vessels can beach.

Particularly in Bangladesh, the situation remains somewhat precarious in obtaining Central Bank Approval on the particularly higher value assets, so drastic remains the ongoing liquidity problem in the country.

In Pakistan, it has been nearly impossible to open any L/Cs and neither Owners nor Cash Buyers are considering Gadani as a viable destination, especially in the new future.

Finally, Turkey continues its dreary drudge through the year, week after week, with not much change to report other than local steel plate prices that have been fluctuating within a margin and a determined Lira that is steadily deteriorating against the U.S. Dollar.

Overall, pursuant to the conclusion of Chinese New Year holidays, there was an improvement in both Dry Bulk and Containers for trading / charter, and this has led to a dearth in vessels being proposed for recycling and arriving at most waterfronts, as port reports remained virtually empty across the sub-continent & Turkey through most of March.

Notwithstanding, recycling prices remain relatively steady / strong, as do local sentiments, which are expected to pick up further after the holidays this month, as demand increases and fundamentals stabilizes in the form of steel prices and most local currencies.

headline: READY AND WAITING!
body_text:
Amidst a ‘less-than-often’ phase of stability for local fundamentals overall, both local steel plate prices and the Indian Rupee sailed through the week on an even-to-positive scale.

Not only did local steel plate prices diminish by less than USD 1/Ton this week, but the Rupee also continued to gradually firm past Rs. 82, down to Rs. 81.8X against the U.S. Dollar as the week ended.

Meanwhile, India also remains the leading market for (especially) HKC green vessels, despite the addition of more class NK yards in Bangladesh, yet the container sector has seen an uptick in chartering levels leading to many vessels being withdrawn from recycling sales.

As fundamentals remain firm, we should get some greater clarity on market conditions, pricing, and demand overall, after the various bank holidays are over from next week onwards.

headline: CHRONIC ISSUES!
highlights: Uncompetitive. | Little point.
body_text:
Chronic financing abilities persist for yet another week in Pakistan, and there is little getting over the fact that levels remain far from competitive, and banks remain far from willing to open L/Cs on any available vessels.

Even the unit arrived a few weeks ago is languishing at the waterfront, with rumors that the vessel is still awaiting opening of an L/C.

As such, the Gadani market remains non-event, particularly with the month of Ramadan ongoing and demand down as a result.

Like Bangladesh, local steel plate prices flatlined through much of the week, while the Pakistani Rupee ended the week at a massive PKR 286 against the U.S. Dollar.

Until Pakistan can sort out its liquidity issues and find ways to pay Owners / Cash Buyers alike on arriving vessels, and until levels improve in line with both India and Bangladesh, there remains little point discussing vessels into Pakistan for the time being.

headline: NO CHANGE!
body_text:
Turkey, like India, remains steadily fluctuating in its fundamentals, although in the opposite direction.

The Turkish Lira has been gradually weakening against the U.S. Dollar as it sails past TRY 19.25 as the week ended. Even local steel plate prices dropped by about USD 10/Ton while import steel fell by about USD 5/Ton, which seem more along the lines of weekly fluctuations than anything more serious.

With the world of ship recycling starved of tonnage, Aliaga was no different as Turkish Recyclers continue to starve for tonnage, the much-awaited Spring rejuvenation has yet to arrive, much to local Buyers dismay.

headline: STRESSES AND STRAINS!
highlights: Difficult deliveries. | Various sales.
body_text:
A difficult week on deliveries and L/C approvals has descended across the Bangladeshi ship recycling sector, despite several new well priced sales being concluded and even large LDT units greeting the waterfront through the course of the week – all this bearing in mind the ongoing financing hurdles faced on the large LDT transactions.

Adding caution to the ongoing situation are local fundamentals, whereby local steel plate prices flatlined again through the course of the week, while the Bangladeshi Taka continues to volley in the early BDT 106 against the U.S. Dollar.

As such, the sales of the week certainly raised an eyebrow, given that the General Cargo vessel ATLANTIC RAY (2,461 LDT), built in Turkey, with a steel propeller, eventually managed to obtain a fantastic USD 620/LT LDT – showing that smaller LDT units are very much the flavour of the moment. This was also the case with the LPG APOLLO PACIFIC (2,188 LDT), sold from Vietnamese owners for a very firm USD 655/LT LDT.

Finally, the handy Logger Bulker OCEAN GREAT (6,311 LDT) from Chinese Sellers was committed for a decent USD 575/LT LDT.

Time will tell whether central bank permission on these various transactions (as well as Cash Buyer inventories) will get approval, especially while the strained financial situation in Bangladesh continues to show few signs of abating just yet.

highlights: Relative gloom. | Ramadan ongoing. | Falling steel. | Busy start. | Supply slows.
body_text:
The ongoing month of Ramadan has also led to much softer sentiments across the board, as ongoing religious festivities are observed, and business takes a backseat for the time being. Volatile steel plate prices have not helped the current situation brewing at the various recycling destinations either, and this has seen most end users of fresh tonnage abstain from buying, choosing instead to wait and watch developments and how the market opens post Ramadan, before offering afresh on any new vessels being proposed.

The primary problem for recyclers at all the major locations is the ongoing and noticeably painful shortage in the supply of vessels for recycling, as freight markets in Dry Bulk and Containers have shown some renewed positivity of late.

As such, after a decade long low supply and activity, last year even though it seemed as though it would been an overall busy and bullish start to 2023 for the major recycling markets. However, things seem to be easing off even before May arrives and the customary cooling of performance in the sub-continent markets due to the oncoming Monsoon season will only further aggravate the present situation – despite the state of supply and the current (and plenty of) availability of space at dormant plots.

Making matters worse, with both Bangladesh and Pakistan markets still requiring lengthy central state bank approval processes to open new L/Cs, it is certainly going to be a painful process to get vessels delivered (in time) moving forward, and patience / extra waiting times will certainly be required from those Owners / Cash Buyers seeking to deliver units moving forward. Lastly, the Turkish market echoes virtually identical sentiments and fundamentals as the sub-continent markets, including the Lira, which continues to relapsefurther every week.

headline: DELUGE TO TRICKLE!
body_text:
As the charter market picks up in this previously beleaguered sector, India has seen the marginal number of its favoured HKC container candidates snatched away from their grasp over the last few weeks.

The above, coupled with the overall supply of vessels that has started to slow, as recycling prices continue cool off and what was once a deluge at the turn of the year has eventually turned into a trickle of tonnage, and it may be a quieter second quarter to the year if the current trends persist in Alang, especially as the monsoon season gradually rears its head over the horizon.

Pricewise, India does remain second placed to Bangladesh, although there is the greater comfort factor of comparatively more reliable and prompter performance on L/Cs, giving Owners and Cash Buyers more incentive to head towards Alang on any available ships, despite the cheaper rates.

Fundamentals-wise, local steel plate prices declined a marginal USD 5/Ton, while the Indian Rupee continues to slide around the Rs. 81.8X mark against the U.S. Dollar.

headline: OUT OF CONVERSATION!
highlights: Uncertain. | Bleak outlook.
body_text:
Pakistan is out of the conversation regarding negotiations on any vessels for recycling, so low and so unreliable / uncertain are Local Buyers on price and workable L/Cs at present – and have been for a couple of months now.

The Pakistani Rupee has certainly endured a torrid and unprecedented collapse over the last year at least, and this has left most Buyers incapable of performing with yards closing and the government stepping in to work with the central bank on approvals on the expenditure on any precious US dollar reserves in the country.

Notwithstanding, despite local steel plate prices flatlining (like the Bangladeshi market) through the week – the Pakistani Rupee firmed to the early PKR 284 against the U.S Dollar.

As such, local port reports remain bleak, as does the outlook in Pakistan for the remainder of the next quarter (if not the rest of the year), unless financing issues can be resolved, and some stability can be brought back to the currency and local fundamentals in the country.

headline: GLOBAL SYMPTOMS!
body_text:
Like all of the major ship recycling destinations, Turkey continues to suffer through the ongoing shortage of supply. Tonnage is painful to come by and the easing fundamentals is making harder for Aliaga Recyclers to maintain their historically impressive levels for much longer.

Both import and local steel plate prices have fallen by about USD 5/Ton this week as the Lira continues to gradually sink against the U.S. Dollar approaching TRY 19.40.

It does seem as though the rumours of local fixtures were just that, and as though the Turkish market is similar to the Pakistani market, with a declining currency, absence of tonnage, and a market that may well start weakening in the near future, it is going to be a tough summer for the Turkish market.

headline: ONGOING HEADACHE!
highlights: Delays. | Performance key.
body_text:
After several tides of ongoing delayed deliveries, the end of the Holy month of Ramadan and Eid holidays see the overall ship recycling market at a softer level than when the month started.

It will be interesting to see whether prices show some resilience and start to bounce back at the conclusion of Eid Celebrations, or if levels remain static on the back of a demand that continues to make its rounds.

Certainly, demand remains ripe, with many Buyers keen to import fresh vessels at these current overall levels. However, the question on whether L/C approvals and subsequent performances are forthcoming remains, especially as we move into the summer / monsoon months, amidst tighter U.S. Dollar restrictions.

Fundamentals wise, the situation remains no different locally as local steel plate prices continue to flatline for several weeks now, all while the Bangladeshi Taka continues to waddle around the early BDT 106s against the U.S. Dollar.

highlights: Decline evident. | Steel fall. | Strained approvals. | Deals struggling. | Patience required.
body_text:
Steel plate prices continue to dither across all markets (including Turkey) over the past month or so, leaving the various recycling destinations far more precariously poised than they were during the bullish start of the year.

The key hurdle for Bangladeshi Recyclers (amidst the ongoing liquidity crunch in the country) is working with the Central Bank in getting fresh L/Cs approved, with all but essential items (food, fuel, and fertilizers) receiving approvals instead. As such, several of the higher priced deals that had been concluded into Bangladesh over the past few months, are only now starting to deliver after delays on arrival, as the industry overall is starting to witness how increasingly difficult it might just be to obtain L/C approvals on upcoming deliveries.

As such, it is highly recommended for Owners with any incoming vessels into Bangladesh, to either re-position their units towards competing markets (i.e., India at lower levels but a far more assured performance) or to ensure that a minimum of five days between arrival, tendering NOR, and payment release is provided by End Buyers to ensure they can open L/Cs, have funds arranged for, and then have their end of the transaction wrapped up in time for beaching.

Meanwhile, Pakistan remains in a rut, invisible to the Ship Recycling Community, whilst Turkey continues to sail through week after week, with nearly the same result.

These are certainly not the markets of old we are operating in any longer, and some more time & patience will be required moving forward, in delivering the larger LDT vessels. The end of the Holy month of Ramadan from next week should also bring some greater clarity and desire / demand to buy.

headline: ENDURING MARKET!
body_text:
India remains the enduring market for those seeking a more assured and reliable performance, even at Alang’s comparatively lower levels. A majority of HKC green tonnage and specialist units continue to head towards Indian shores, despite three yards now being Class NK approved in Bangladesh.

Such was the case with another MSC container this week, as MSC continue their clear out of older tonnage, with the Danish built Panamax container MSC PILAR (23,740 LDT) that fetched a decent USD 544/LT LDT, considering the limited yards for a standard HKC Class NK resale.

Local steel plate prices declined a marginal USD 8/Ton this week, whilst the Indian Rupee continues trading around the early Rs. 82 against the U.S. Dollar, giving End Buyers some more confidence towards acquiring vessels moving forward, especially at these more settled rates.

headline: LITTLE CHANCE!
highlights: Unlikely to return. | Quieter outlook.
body_text:
As Eid holidays descend and the Holy month of Ramadan concludes, there is little expectation that the Pakistani ship recycling market will return to the bidding tables after the holidays.

Pakistani prices still remain some ways off their Indian sub-continent competitors and there is little confidence that Gadani Buyers can get approvals from domestic banks for the opening of fresh L/Cs and thereby incurring the expenditure of precious and dwindling U.S. Dollar reserves on vessels for recycling, rather than on more pressing domestic needs at the moment.

This is clearly evident from the fact that only 1 vessel has arrived Gadani over the last 6 weeks and that unit too is facing L/C related issues and is unable to beach.

Even local fundamentals have done little to help the brewing situation as the Pakistani Rupee dangles dangerously over the PKR 280 level against the U.S. Dollar, while local steel plate prices, like in Bangladesh, have flatlined for several weeks now, given the near-zero tons of plate that is moving from Gadani yards.

As such, it is expected again to be a quieter few months in Pakistan with minimal activity, at the very least until the financial situation and currency can be stabilized / resolved.

headline: DROP EXPECTED?
body_text:
The much-anticipated 2023 Spring boost in recycling activity has failed to materialize in Aliaga to date. Making matters worse, the ongoing & painful shortage of tonnage mixed in with the shaky fundamentals, are all conspiring to make the prevailing situation that much worse.

The Lira continues to weaken against the U.S. Dollar as it briefly approaches TRY 19.41 against the U.S. Dollar, while import steel dropped another USD 15/Ton (north of $40/Ton over the last few weeks), local steel plate prices were unchanged but are expected to follow suit post-Ramadan.

Meanwhile, Ramadan Celebrations during the week have also left local Recyclers distracted from the ongoing pain, thanks to the lack of any meaningful activity.

Overall, as Turkish vessel prices manage to hold their ground (uncertain for just how much longer) and sub-continent levels stay steady, the inevitable widening of the margin between Turkey and the sub-continent markets will only make things worse for Turkish Buyers as summer comes around.

headline: LARGELY ABSENT!
highlights: Ongoing hols. | Focus Alang.
body_text:
Bangladesh has been largely absent from the buying over the last few weeks due to ongoing Ramadan and Eid holidays.

Levels have declined by about USD 50/LDT since their peaks seen earlier this year, leaving levels well below the ongoing expectation of Owners and Cash Buyers alike.

Fundamentals do remain shaky as steel plate trading came to a complete halt while the markets remained off during Ramadan, coupled with a Taka that weakened past BDT 107.2X, ending the week at BDT 106.40 against the U.S. Dollar.

Finally, despite the inclusion of several new yards in Bangladesh on the class NK HKC list, the supply of vessels into Chattogram has dwindled of late as the focus has instead redirected towards Alang where several HKC deals were concluded this week.

highlights: India benefits. | Holidays end. | Rate decline. | Two tide budget. | Pakistan out.
body_text:
As the holiday period concludes, ever optimistic industry players are still hopeful that they may see an increase in the number of recycling candidates, as demand in Bangladesh, India, and even Turkey, ramps up again.

Notwithstanding, rates have taken somewhat of a battering off the back of declining steel plate prices & volatile currencies, and as stated in last week’s edition of the GMS WEEKLY, it is becoming increasingly difficulty to get vessels delivered into Bangladesh and Pakistan, with all parties waiting on Central Bank approvals for Letters of Credit (L/Cs) to open.

Indeed, Sellers and Cash Buyers should budget for at least two tides to get vessels delivered, particularly for larger LDT & large U.S. Dollar value vessels, where these approvals are taking longer than expected to come through.

On the other end of the sub-continent, Pakistan remains largely absent from the buying due to unworkable bank limits / restrictions on the expenditure of dwindling U.S. Dollar reserves, in addition to uncompetitive pricing on units that has subsequently placed them a long way at the bottom of the sub-continent demo rankings.

At the far end, Turkey remains worse on the fundamentals front of than last week, as their dithering numbers place an incredible downward pressure on vessel prices.

Overall, due to an uptick in both dry bulk and container charter rates at the start of this year, there has been a relative slowdown in the number of available recycling candidates. However, we have witnessed a slight increase in the inflow of (HKC) tonnage over these last couple of weeks as markets level off, and India has been the chief beneficiary of this over these units.

Rank Location Sentiment Dry Bulk USD / LDT

headline: DEALS DONE!
body_text:
As tonnage flow increases after various holidays have concluded across the globe, several deals were concluded into India this week.

MSC has concluded yet another unit for resale to a limited number of HKC yards as the MSC LUCIA (8,911 LDT) was committed for a decent USD 530/LT LDT. Additionally, the Chinese built MR tanker MARITIME LIRA (12,235 LDT) managed to fetch USD 515/LT LDT basis a recycling resale restricted to 10 local yards only, in addition to strict monitoring – further highlighting an increased commitment of Vessel Owners towards responsible recycling.

On the domestic fundamentals front, local steel plate prices fell another (marginal) USD 5/Ton, while the Indian Rupee further firmed and has been trading in the high Rs. 81s against the U.S. Dollar, as demand and rates slowly improve for the week, inching India closer to Bangladesh.

Unfortunately, Alang’s waterfront has been subject to the effects of the lack of tonnage through the previous weeks, as not a single new vessel arrived local anchorage during the course of the week.

headline: MILES OFF!
highlights: No action. | Price low.
body_text:
Despite the conclusion of Eid holidays and with it, the end of the Holy month of Ramadan, there has been little change to the status quo in Pakistan whilst Gadani Recyclers remain miles from the action.

As it stands, the Pakistani Central Bank remains even less likely than the Bangladeshi Central Bank to approve any forthcoming L/C openings, due to the ongoing and dire lack of U.S. Dollar reserves in the country.

This has further reflected dreadfully at the waterfront as no new vessels have arrived in Pakistan since March 03rd and the only vessel that has, remains stranded outside.

Even fundamentals remain precarious as the Pakistani Rupee is still traversing in excess of PKR 283 against the U.S. Dollar, all while local steel plate prices continue to flatline, week after week in Pakistan.

As a result of the ongoing volatility, vessel prices remain some ways off even India, and it therefore remains unlikely that any deals can or will be concluded into Gadani in the foreseeable future.

headline: DEGRADING?
body_text:
The Turkish market has been gradually slipping (from a fundamentals perspective), week after week.

Local steel plate prices fell by about USD 10/Ton whilst import steel declined by about USD 15/Ton, all while the Lira continues its unending drag down quicksand lane passing TRY 19.40 against the U.S. Dollar – as an overall downward trajectory registers in Turkey for several weeks in a row now.

Meanwhile, the omnipresent problem of the shortage of tonnage has not spared the Turkish market either, as the bitter absence of vessels has kept local Buyers hungry / desperate enough to have maintained their vessel prices despite key fundamentals degrading on a weekly basis.

Overall, it certainly feels as though an inevitable degrading of this market is forthcoming, especially if the absence of tonnage continues.

headline: BREATHER!
highlights: Quieter week. | Missing sales.
body_text:
It has been a quieter overall week in Bangladesh in terms of sales and activity, with End Buyers offering even lower levels on tonnage, but with little success in securing any units thus far.

It is clear that prices have come off significantly since the peaks witnessed earlier this year, however, Cash Buyers and Vessel Owners have yet to share the currently brewing sentiment / appetite in negotiating at such discounted rates on offer from Chattogram Buyers.

As such, for yet another week, India has continued to secure a bulk of the recent fixtures, with several more interesting HKC sales being concluded to the market there, much to the chagrin of the few Bangladeshi Buyers who have recently obtained Class NK HKC certification for their respective recycling yards.

Finally, domestic fundamentals remain shaky as the Taka continues to buoy around the mid BDT 106.5X against the U.S. Dollar, while local steel plate prices find themselves absent from trading altogether (for the second consecutive week).

highlights: Further decline. | Working firm. | Freight ok. | Correction evident. | Pakistan apart.
body_text:
To further compound the presently bearish ship recycling sentiments, local steel plate prices have further weakened at key destinations and LME steel futures show few signs of any sort of recovery in the immediate future.

That being said, several vessels have been working firm over the past few weeks and sales have been taking place. However, these are primarily HKC intended units being committed into India, even at these gradually deteriorating rates.

Moreover, due to a recent uptick in freight rates, fewer than expected Containers and Dry Bulk units have been introduced into the markets for recycling and this is giving the ship recycling industry, an opportunity to draw breath and find true bottom, before reoffering at these new (lower) realities.

The overall correction appears to be between USD 50 – USD 60/LDT since the peaks seen earlier this year. Due to such turbulence, it may be that End Buyers wish to wait and watch market developments before getting back into the buying once again.

Bangladesh & India remain the two most active / competing markets for the time being, as Pakistan remains a non-entity for over two months now, completely out of the market action due to unworkable L/Cs, uncompetitive pricing, and a precarious financial and political outlook (especially in the near future).

Finally, the Turkish market continues to deteriorate (as predicted last week), with weakening steel plate prices and a currency that seems likely to breach TRY 19.50 against the U.S. Dollar next week. As a result, Aliaga’s recycling prices have (negatively) re-adjusted by USD 10/MT.

headline: PRECARIOUS!
body_text:
Despite the precarious nature of recent falls in Alang, news of several deals from last week has surfaced as sales of an FPSO and a General Cargo vessel reportedly registered at decent levels.

Firstly, the General Cargo vessel KUMUL ARROW (10,998 LDT) from Gearbulk managed to fetch an above market USD 560/LT LDT for class NK certified HKC recycling only. The gantry crane and bowthruster likely adding value and justifying the price on show.

Subsequently, the FPSO FERAN VAZ (41,716 LDT) was committed for a decent USD 260/LT LDT basis an ‘as is’ under tow delivery from Gabon, for HKC green recycling in India only. The sale included a whopping 4,000 CBM of cargo residues on board for tank cleaning, in order to make the vessel gas free for hot works clean for recycling.

Meanwhile, after some hefty price declines of over USD 20/LDT in one week alone, most End Buyers are maintaining radio silence, rather than offering firm numbers, perhaps fearful of further falls ahead – and justifiably so.

Even though the Indian Rupee continues to gain ground against the U.S. Dollar as it wraps up the week at levels in the region Rs. 81.6X, local steel plate prices are the ones that have been declining steadily (for several weeks now) as levels reportedly fell another USD 18/Ton during the course of this week.

headline: INACTIVE AND INERT!
highlights: Missing in action. | Off the pace.
body_text:
Pakistan is miles off being competitive with their sub-continent counterparts and, as a result, has spent another week inactive & inert, missing out on all of the recent market negotiations and fixtures.

The ongoing domestic political turmoil and financial crises that have crippled the country show few signs of abating just yet, as local steel plate prices flatlined over the last few weeks. Additionally, the Pakistani Rupee, which has yet to stabilize to any meaningful degree, continues to trade in the mid PKR 283 against the U.S. Dollar.

Crippling L/C restrictions have also kept negotiations at bay and the only vessel idling at Gadani’s anchorage that was reportedly awaiting L/C approval, has finally sailed away this week leaving not only Pakistan’s waterfront after two months, but also a country devoid of any tonnage for the same duration.

As such, it is perhaps unsurprising to see Gadani Buyers so off the pace and unable to acquire fresh units, and until some confidence starts to flow back into this market, there is little sense in discussing any fresh deals into Pakistan.

headline: DROP!
body_text:
The much-anticipated decline from last week finally materialized this week as, on the back of import steel plate prices that dropped in excess of USD 20/Ton and local steel plate prices fell about USD 15/Ton, Aliaga Buyers rolled back their vessel prices by about USD 10/MT this week.

While on the one hand, the lack of tonnage would indicate that the drop in levels is not a big loss for the local market considering there are no vessels to bid on, on the other hand, declining levels may not tempt Vessel Owners to consider Turkish levels or even Turkey as a viable destination – especially when you consider that sub-continent market levels are nearly twice those from Turkey.

Will the traditional summer / monsoon months in the sub-continent come to the aid of Turkish Recyclers, remains to be seen. For now, however, Turkey seems to have no reprieve from the shortage of supply.

headline: REAWAKENING!
highlights: Greater demand. | Budget looms.
body_text:
It has been a quieter few months in Bangladesh as prices have suffered declines of about USD 50 – USD 60/LDT, while the Holy month of Ramadan brought with it some reduced demand and appetite to buy.

However, upon the conclusion of various holidays, some greater demand to acquire has started to emerge and several deals have been concluded over the last couple of weeks, and that too at some impressive levels.

Evidence of these fixtures can be witnessed at the waterfront as Chattogram’s anchorage has been comparatively busy over the last couple of weeks, taking deliveries of all types and sizes of vessels.

Meanwhile, despite a looming budget in early June, we do expect some more deals to be concluded into a reawakening Bangladesh – especially pre-monsoon, albeit at slower overall rates due to the time taken to establish L/Cs and negotiate rates with the Central Bank.

Moreover, fundamentals remain shaky as after weeks of flatlining / no trading, local steel plate prices finally roared back into existence as trading started early in the week and that too at relatively meeker levels. Even the Bangladeshi Taka weakened against the U.S. Dollar, trading over BDT 107.30 as the week ended.

As such, an interesting summer certainly lies ahead for the Bangladeshi market that seems to be gearing up to negotiate on available units.

highlights: Reached bottom? | Post slumber. | Candidates trickle. | Bangla budget. | Demand ripe.
body_text:
However, as the week came to an end, global currencies seemed to suffer against the U.S. Dollar in unison, as all of the major ship recycling destinations faced some declines (especially in Pakistan), leaving sentiments under pressure. This, even though local steel prices started leveling out after weeks of flatlining and even declining by about USD 25/LDT in India over the course of the month, while Bangladesh likewise deteriorated during April where Buyers finally emerged eager to negotiate post-Eid.

As we head into these traditionally quieter summer / monsoon months, the number of available candidates remains low and by some accounts, seems to have slowed even further this week, as charter markets for the previously beleaguered Dry Bulk and Container sectors continue to display a greater stability to keep vessels trading.

Pakistan expectedly remains out of the picture as political and economic uncertainty continues to wreck the country with this most recent arrest of Ex-Prime Minister Imran Khan and impending domestic unrest, in addition to the Pakistani Rupee that has further depreciated to record lows against the U.S. Dollar, leaving End Buyers reeling once again.

There is also the upcoming Bangladeshi budget in early June to be aware of, as many End Buyers are choosing to wait-and-watch the results of the budget before offering firm on tonnage once again, even though there are few expectations of any significant changes to be made for the ship recycling sector.

Finally, the Turkish market remains suspended in nowhere land, leading to absolute silence.

As prices therefore stabilize across sub-continent markets and demand seems as though it is ramping up again after the various holidays, we can only hope that a trickle of vessels we are so far seeing starts to increase and empty plots start to fill up again.

Rank Location Sentiment Dry Bulk USD / LDT

headline: STABILITY SEEN!
highlights: And understandably so.
body_text:
After some sharp declines in prices and fundamentals over recent weeks, the Indian market has finally started to stabilise post-Eid and some greater demand and interest to acquire had begun to emerge again from hungry and emptying End Buyer yards.

As such, several interesting deals had indeed been concluded for a very limited number of HKC recycling yards over recent weeks, including an FPSO, several Containers, and even an MR Tanker.

Since then, it has been a quieter time as both Cash Buyers and Owners seem to remain spooked by some of the more pronounced recent falls and are preferring to wait for some stability to return to the market, before offering any available tonnage again.

Even though local steel plate prices jumped by about USD 12/Ton, this increase followed on from weeks of reportedly regular declines. Moreover, even though the Indian Rupee seemed to be firming against the U.S. Dollar as it entered the high Rs. 81.7X, it closed the week shooting past Rs. 82.20 as the week ended.

Even Alang’s waterfront is showing signs of the diminished trading as barely any fresh arrivals / beachings were reported this week.

Next week will certainly be an interesting one, now that we see further inquiries incoming.

headline: DECLINES AND FALLS!
highlights: Shocking week. | Currency chaos.
body_text:
Another shocking week of declines and falls left Recyclers in Pakistan sidelined once again and unable to compete on any of the tonnage that is currently in the market for sale.

The political and economic turmoil that has beset the country for the better part of almost two years, shows few signs of abating as Ex-Prime Minister Imran Khan was arrested this week and the subsequent unrest brewing amongst his supporters has resulted in the government ordering the army into the streets, so as to maintain peace, law, and order.

Moreover, like the other markets, there is another calamity brewing on the fundamentals side as the Pakistani Rupee approaches PKR 300 against the U.S. Dollar as it closed the week at PKR 295.50, leaving End Buyers utterly spooked, keeping them away from the bidding tables and out of the market for the most part.

Local steel plate prices also continue to flatline as there remains no trading of ship’s steel due to the deathly shortage of product and lack of any deliveries since March.

As such, Pakistani problems seem as though they are here to stay for the time being.

headline: WEAK!
body_text:
After last week’s noteworthy decline in local and import steel plate prices in addition to the Lira’s drop, this week was no different as plate prices fluctuated marginally. However, it is the Lira that is sending shockwaves through the domestic ship recycling sector as it briefly passed TRY 19.65 against the U.S. Dollar.

Will TRY 20.0 be the big barrier to breach in the coming weeks remains to be seen.

For now, with a total lack of tonnage greeted with a seemingly firming sub-continent market where prices are moving further away, Turkey certainly seems stuck in neverland – especially in the immediate future.

headline: BUDGET DUE!
highlights: Some recovery. | HKC discussions.
body_text:
Bangladesh has enjoyed something of a resurgence over the last couple of weeks, as prices picked up a touch amidst the crushing slowdown in the supply of tonnage and steel plate prices that recovered some of the lost ground from previous months.

As a result, on the back of firming demand, two older Chinese Bulker sales reportedly managed to register this week as the TIAN HE SHUN (7,450 LDT) and the XIANG JIANG 6 (7,290 LDT) were both concluded at a modest USD 560/LT LDT, as choice tonnage heads to India (including containers, offshore units, and even LNGs in recent weeks) for strictly HKC green recycling.

The Bangladeshi budget date has been set for June 1st and few changes are expected to impact the domestic ship recycling sector However, it is always worth keeping an eye out for any surprises, and several End Buyers are preferring to wait until after the budget passes, before offering on the marginal number of units currently on offer.

Fundamentals too remain shaky as the Taka stays in a weakened state at BDT 107.2X against the U.S. Dollar, while local steel plate prices had a minor correction of about USD 10/Ton this week.

High level meetings are also scheduled to take place at the end of this week in Bangladesh, in order to ratify the Hong Kong convention, and we will update further on the progress / decisions made next week.

highlights: Tonnage lull. | Decline spooks. | HKC sales. | Bangla upgrades. | Ratifying HKC?
body_text:
Some of the recent market declines of about USD 50 – USD 60/LDT and struggles on L/Cs in the Bangladeshi and Pakistani markets (in particular) may have spooked Sellers and Cash Buyers alike, and for those that were willing to sell above USD 600/LDT, they may now be unwilling to enter the market as they are being greeted by new lower realities in the USD 500s/LDT.

Sales have therefore been at a premium in recent times, although several older bulkers were committed and one 1977 built LNG carrier was confirmed this week basis an ‘as is’ Labuan delivery for an HKC resale only.

Increasingly, most high-profile Sellers are looking to sell for HKC recycling only, and the bulk of the major container owners such as Maersk, MSC, Wan Hai, and Evergreen have committed vessels this year for strict HKC recycling into India.

It is certainly encouraging that certain yards in Bangladesh – three now in total – have managed to obtain class NK HKC certification and have made major upgrades to their facilities in order to encourage other yards to improve likewise.

Discussions will be taking place this coming week in Bangladesh, in order to ratify the Hong Kong convention and we will certainly be keeping a close watch on events to see what finally transpires, and the impact it will have on the industry moving forward.

Finally, while Pakistan remains in the dumps with no new fixtures or fresh arrivals at the waterfront, the Turkish market, though weaker, is distracted with the ongoing Presidential elections in the country.

headline: BACK IN THE PICTURE?!
body_text:
Steel plate prices have lost a lot of ground over the course of the last few weeks and despite levels even climbing by about USD 10/Ton, reversed by the same amount by the time the week ended.

Notwithstanding, local sentiments and eagerness to buy has put India back in the picture on any working tonnage – especially competing with Bangladesh and securing most of the HKC green units in the market.

One such high profile unit (following a recent FPSO sale and ongoing negotiations for another), saw the larger LDT 1977 built GANDRIA (29,500 LDT) concluded for an impressive USD 15,500,000 lumpsum, basis an ‘as is’ Labuan delivery, for HKC green recycling only. The higher content of Nickel and nonferrous along with the HKC requirements mean that these units will usually end up in Alang over Chattogram.

Meanwhile, fundamentals seem to have been on edge this week as the currency has been weakening and is currently trading in the Rs. 82.8Xs against the U.S. Dollar - some of the highest levels seen against the U.S. Dollar, as India looks to cool soaring inflation that is currently being witnessed across much of the world as well.

headline: TURMOIL!
highlights: Arrest scandal. | No more triumvirate.
body_text:
Turmoil continues to plague Pakistan, with the recent arrest of former PM Imran Khan capturing much of the headlines, along with turbulent and worrying currency devaluations that often sees this economy teetering on the brink of collapse.

As such, Gadani is not a viable market for ship recycling at present and Buyers are simply avoiding all negotiations / purchases, especially with so much uncertainty across the country.

On the fundamentals front, not only have local steel plate prices flatlined through the course of the week again, the Pakistani Rupee, though marginally stronger than last week, is still at a precipitous PKR 285.6X against the U.S. Dollar.

Therefore, the usual sub-continent triumvirate is now down to two markets, and it may be some time before Pakistan comes back into viable buying again, given the present state of their economy.

headline: POLITICS!
body_text:
Turkey is going through a politically active time as well, whereby the Presidential campaign is in a dead-heat between President Erdogan and his challenger. With the elections now heading into a run-off (to be decided by the end of next week), the overall sentiments are still weak / cautious.

As the Lira sinks further towards a record breaking TRY 20 against the U.S. Dollar, both import and local steel plate prices did register a degree of stability this week as neither reported any noteworthy change.

Overall, as the sub-continent markets (India and Bangladesh in particular) remain nearly double that of Turkey, the shortage of available units is also keeping Turkish prices steady, though for how much longer, is certainly on anyone’s mind.

headline: WAKING UP!
highlights: HKC talks. | 1st June budget.
body_text:
Over previous weeks, several (market and private) sales have taken place into Bangladesh, as this market appears to finally turn a corner post Ramadan and Eid holidays.

Moreover, just this week, Japan Shipowners' Association (JSA) sent its delegates to Bangladesh, along with representatives from four major Japanese shipping companies as Bangladesh’s regulatory bodies have expressed their commitment to ratify HKC recycling processes and requested Japan's assistance in the further development of a Treatment Storage Disposal Facility (TSDF).

The Japanese delegation also visited multiple ship recycling facilities in Chattogram and had constructive dialogues with members of Bangladesh Ship Breakers and Recyclers Association (BSBRA), with emphasis on increasing the number of HKC compliant yards.

As a result of this visit, Chattogram’s ship recycling industry has been re-categorized from ‘Red’ to ‘Orange’ code on the environmental outlook, which will assure further investments in yard infrastructures.

On the sales front, no fresh market sales registered for the week, as the supply of tonnage remains abysmal, especially as we enter the usually quieter monsoon season – when much of the seasonal labour returns home.

As fundamentals continue to jiggle as the weeks go by where the Bangladeshi Taka still trades in excess of BDT 107.10 against the U.S. Dollar and local steel plate prices flatline through the week once again, all eyes will be on the upcoming budget of June 1st next week – whereby even though few changes are expected to impact the ship recycling sector – many Buyers are being cautious in the event of unexpected changes.

highlights: Price levels. | Budget due. | Ratifying talks. | Next steps. | Pakistan done.
body_text:
There is also the impending budget on June 1st in Bangladesh and many End Buyers are waiting to see if any new changes / taxes are imposed on the domestic ship recycling sector before offering afresh on tonnage.

However, the general consensus on the upcoming budget is that no changes are expected and that it may actually be positive on the overall business outlook in Bangladesh, amidst a growing demand for steel and raw materials due to various upcoming construction and infrastructure projects that are due in the summer months.

Additionally, the recent meeting in Bangladesh on whether to ratify the Hong Kong convention produced some interesting discussions and outcomes, with the country amending its ship recycling standard from ‘Red’ to ‘Orange’, on the environmental outlook for the country. The next step is for flags to ratify the convention before it can be entered into force, in what could be a landmark ruling in Bangladesh – the first sub-continent country to be actively doing so.

Meanwhile, after a recent wobble in prices, India too has steadied and there is now an emerging demand as Buyers in Alang have missed out on a majority of the non-HKC (and reportedly, even some HKC) tonnage to the firmer Chattogram market.

Pakistan remains on the sidelines, with political and economic chaos rendering this market virtually redundant and there is no realistic hope of the situation stabilizing any time soon.

Finally, Turkey remains suspended in no-man’s land, as the situation remains unchanged from last week and the election results awaiting to be announced.

headline: MISSING OUT (ON HKC)!
body_text:
India has recently missed out on some HKC sales, with Bangladesh securing tonnage to some of the newly approved Class NK HKC facilities (three now in total).

Prices in India are a touch lower than Bangladesh and as many of the recent fixtures are coming in from the Far East, a lower delivery cost to Bangladesh (vs. India) helps ease some of the expenses as vessels head to Chattogram, especially as evidenced by the number of arrivals in Bangaldesh over recent weeks.

Fundamentals in India remain wobbly too, with steel prices enduring another shaky week – down by about USD 5/Ton - whilst the currency finally settles back down towards Rs. 82.5X against the U.S. Dollar, keeping Alang Recyclers encouraged, despite the dwindling supply of vessels.

headline: UNFULFILLED DREAMS!
highlights: Lacklustre. | Nothing meaningful.
body_text:
Another completely lackluster week sees the Pakistani ship recycling sector devoid of any sales / activity and remains on the sidelines of the sub-continent ship recycling markets. No progress has been likewise made on upgrading facilities (as Bangladeshi Recyclers have been of late) to adhere to HKC standards, something that could easily see the Pakistani market left behind in the long run.

Understandably, the political and economic chaos that continues to beset the country has taken front and center stage, leaving the market in Gadani only able to hopelessly watch on as competing neighbors continues to take in units’ week after week.

It has certainly been some time since any meaningful sales have taken place in Gadani and with port reports and plots virtually empty, there remains capacity and demand to acquire, even though there may not be any realistic hope of fulfilling those yards (and dreams) any time soon.

A lone supply vessel did greet Gadani’s anchorage this week and time will tell whether local banking and L/C processes have improved the chances of tonnage beaching in this market.

headline: STRAPPED!
body_text:
Turkey remains strapped in no-man’s land, with levels nearly half of those from the Indian sub-continent, local steel plate prices that remain weak, and a Lira that is on a mission (and finally succeeded) to pass TRY 20.0, even though it ended the week at TRY 19.95 against the U.S. Dollar. We believe next week would be firm in the 20s, as the Lira has lost more than half its value in the preceding 18 months or so.

No change in supply, no news of local fixtures (market of private), and a country that’s awaiting the result of a crucial election cycle that’s managed to end in a runoff, as President Erdogan faces his challenger.

Just how much longer can Aliaga’s recycling sector trudge on in this state is anyone’s guess. For now, however, the market seems to be struggling on by.

headline: AS YOU WERE!
highlights: Budget news. | Bulker sale.
body_text:
The announcement of the annual Bangladeshi budget has brought few surprises with it that would affect the domestic ship recycling sector, and buying activity is expected (hoped) to resume in the coming weeks, at the previously energetic levels witnessed through early May.

After several busy weeks and tides of activity, many local Buyers and banks had paused, to ensure that the budget wouldn’t bring any surprises with it, especially in the form of new taxes / duties being levied on the domestic ship recycling sector.

Of course, the fine print remains to be studied and we may have some further clarity next week, however, for the moment it appears to be ‘as you were.’

A couple of sales did register for the week as the ZE RUI 1 (7,735 NET LDT) was committed on an ‘as is’ China basis with 150 Tons of fuel included in the sale, at a healthy USD 531/LT NET LDT. Additionally, a Vietnamese controlled bulker GOLDEN SUN (6,179 LDT) also managed to fetch a decent USD 581/LT LDT for its Owners.

On the local fundamentals front, local steel plate prices flatlined once again for the week, while the Bangladeshi Taka volleys between the TRY 107.3 – 107.5 mark against the U.S. Dollar.

Finally, the pre-budget slowdown can also be witnessed at the waterfront, where only one new vessel reportedly arrived local anchorage this week.

highlights: Budget passes. | Expect activity. | Rupee moves. | Capacity good. | Pakistan out.
body_text:
As such, it should be a busier time for sales and activity from next week once business resumes, although we are now entering the traditionally quieter monsoon and summer months when much of the labor starts to return to their hometowns due to the persistent rains, rendering yards far too difficult for cutting/recycling activities.

Meanwhile, India has also seen some positivity return as the Indian Rupee gained some good ground to fall below the Rs. 83 level against the U.S. Dollar, where it had been recently trading.

The supply of tonnage also remains surprisingly scarce, so any vessels that do come to market are perhaps seeing levels above the reality on the ground, as Cash Buyers look to secure first and work end Buyers’ thereafter, hoping to create some competition and obtain firmer levels.

Pakistan remains completely out of the picture for yet another week, with political and economic uncertainty continuing to beset the country and little hope of ship recycling activity resuming any time soon.

Furthermore, despite a busy few tides gone by in Bangladesh and end Buyers starting to get around their L/C hurdles with the Central State Government bank, plot capacity remains healthy in both Bangladesh and India, so there is certainly potential to absorb more incoming tonnage.

Finally, Turkey sails through another week of opposing fundamentals, as President Erdogan cinches a narrow win and secure his position, with his primary aims reportedly being that of battling the rampant domestic inflation.
