headline: GAINING GROUND!
body_text:
This week, some positive moves on the Indian Rupee finally brought some confidence back into a previously lacklustre and stagnant Alang, and one or two fresh sales have reportedly been discussed with End Buyers (primarily for HKC only recycling at Alang).

As stated, having previously breached Rs. 83, the Indian Rupee gained some good ground to fall back into the low Rs. 82.3X range against the U.S. Dollar. Local steel plate prices also registered marginal improvements (about USD 4/Ton) this week, only to keep local sentiments healthy.

Alang anchorage has had a minimal number of units that have arrived and are awaiting beaching this week, as India continues to lose out on tonnage to a firmer Bangladeshi market, especially on ‘as is’ deals that are opening up in the Far East.

The ongoing slowdown in supply is also keeping Alang Buyers cautioned, especially as we head into the quieter monsoon months in addition to many owners still keeping their vessels trading at these reduced charter levels of today (most containers are now finding trading buyers again).

Even Bangladesh is starting to snap up HKC tonnage, to the three NK class yards now in service and as a result, no new market sales were reported into Alang for the week.

headline: ENVIOUS GLANCES!
highlights: Out of picture. | Barren summer.
body_text:
Pakistan is out of the picture once again and for yet another week, as local Buyers can only look on enviously towards the positivity and (even the few odd) sales being reported from their competing Bangladeshi and Indian counterparts.

Perhaps competitor is the wrong use of the term in this scenario, as Pakistan is unable to compete at all on ships for recycling with its sub-continent neighbors and there have been no meaningful sales into this market for quite some time as the local port report lies empty.

In fact, even last week’s small arrival (undertow) ended up sinking at anchorage due to reported flooding in the engine room and as such, local yards have been completely deprived of tonnage for at least two months now.

On the local fundamentals front, the Pakistani Rupee is still hemorrhaging at PKR 285.2X against the U.S. Dollar, while local steel plate prices appear to have entered a self-induced coma, having reportedly flatlined for several weeks.

Finally, the economic and political chaos that has engulfed the country this year shows few signs of abating, so for ship recycling, it will almost certainly be a barren summer (and likely beyond) in Gadani.

headline: ERDOGAN WINS!
body_text:
As President Erdogan finally cinched his victory this week, domestic inflation continues to run amok, and the Lira continues to degrade against the U.S. Dollar without pause or mercy.

While last week, we questioned whether the Lira would finally breach Try 20.0 against the U.S. Dollar, regrettably this week, the Lira has fallen far quicker and is even likely to breach TRY 21 within next week.

As of close of Friday, the Lira ended at TRY 20.92.

Meanwhile, steel fundamentals (import and local) have remained unchanged, as President Erdogan’s priority remains tackling the rampant inflation, thereby firming Turkey’s domestic economy.

No news of sales or even any market units being proposed. As such, Turkey continues to sail through quiet waters.

headline: TURNING (TO) DRY!
highlights: Decent influx. | LC concerns remain.
body_text:
A positive budget with virtually no overall impact or increased duties on the ship recycling sector has been subsequently tempered by the news out of Bangladesh this week, that fresh L/C approvals will be temporised by the Central State government bank, reportedly due to the ongoing shortage of foreign currency / U.S. Dollar reserves in the country.

Consequently, and even though there has been a moderate influx of vessels from the Far East (Chinese Owners in particular), as of now, there are no easy means for Chattogram Buyers to satisfy their demand with fresh sales – given these most recent L/C hurdles.

Of course, much of the older dry bulk tonnage has tended to end up in Chinese hands (as is the case with older container units these days) and as such, it is perhaps only logical that we are starting to see owners from this market shed vessels - especially as these units approach survey times.

Even though in the past, Chattogram Buyers have had more success in negotiating acceptable L/C / MOA levels with the Central Bank in order to import tonnage, these most recent L/C and financing concerns therefore present a new set of hurdles for open and available Recyclers as reportedly, a brewing demand for steel amidst ongoing construction projects across the country is providing enough incentive for local Recyclers to offer afresh on tonnage.

As such, all those concerned locally (and even the industry at large) will be eagerly monitoring discussions with the Central Bank in the week(s) ahead, to see if sales into Bangladesh can resume at pace once again.

highlights: L/C pause. | India well placed. | Lacking supply. | Production slows. | China busy.
body_text:
Indian fundamentals have also improved, having seen some positive moves on the Indian Rupee over the last few weeks, in addition to steel gains that are providing End Buyers with further encouragement and confidence to improve some of their previously lowish levels on offers. This might eventually help those garish Cash Buyers who have been offering above market levels on some of the recent units.

For now, Pakistan remains the only sub-continent destination that is totally out of the picture, and this is due to the ongoing political unrest and economic calamity that has seen its currency lose much of its value over the last few years.

At the West end, Turkey passes through a reflection of last week, with opposing fundamentals and a Lira that’s essentially fallen off the wagon.

In the overall market today, the only thing lacking is a decent supply of tonnage to keep End Buyers busy and their yards occupied, as we head into the summer / holiday season and many ship owners and yard laborers head on holidays during the warmer / monsoon months.

Finally, after a busy first quarter of recycling, a minimal number of tankers have been proposed so far this year as containers seem to have all but vanished from the market, with over 25 container units sold for varying degrees of HKC recycling. Even dry bulk supply has started to dwindle (apart from a busy Far East / China market that is still shedding older units) and so until more tonnage is introduced, we can expect all of the markets to remain sluggish.

Rank Location Sentiment Dry Bulk USD / LDT

headline: APPRECIATION!
body_text:
An appreciation in the Indian Rupee over the past few weeks has given Alang Buyers a source of comfort, especially as all currencies from the major recycling destinations faced depreciations (some notable) against the U.S. Dollar this week.

Indian local steel plate prices also improved by the tune of about USD 13/Ton this week, recovering / regaining a portion of the losses over the previous few weeks.

Sales have been hard to come by into India of late as the container HKC sales that we had seen at the start of the year have all but dried up. Owners have continued to trade or have even sold their units on for further trading, especially as charter rates in this particular sector picks up again.

Plummeting Chinese steel plate prices over recent weeks that led to negatively positioned LME futures (as a result) have remained a lingering cause for caution in the local market.

However, as supply remains starved heading into the summer months, it may not be too much to worry about just yet.

headline: IDLE SUMMER!
highlights: Inert. | Uncertainty reigns.
body_text:
An inert summer ahead seems a certainty for the Pakistani market, that undoubtedly has other things on its mind than ship recycling. Political and economic concerns still reign supreme in the country, and until one (financial) or both of these items can be stabilized, we are unlikely to see any sales take place into a beleaguered Gadani market.

Fundamentally, the Pakistani market remains in a terrible shape, given that local steel plate prices continue to flatline for months on end and the Pakistani Rupee nosedives past PKR 286.75.

Even local anchorage is reflecting the state of current affairs as despite a couple of units having arrived Gadani’s waterfront over the last couple of months, not a single ship has actually beached in Pakistan since the end of January.

As such, even though the local focus still falls on the dwindling supply of ships, L/C concerns – the type that have beset Bangladesh for much of this year – are the key obstacle in importing and getting ships successfully beached at the end of the day.

headline: WEEKLY MIRROR!
body_text:
In alliance with the state of affairs from last week, Turkey sails through a mirror week this week, with local fundamentals travelling in opposite directions.

While import and local steel plate prices remain relatively unchanged from last week, the Lira has depreciated in truly spectacular fashion this week. Only last week was the industry were worried about the Lira breaching TRY 20 against the U.S. Dollar (and it eventually breached TRY 21) , this week, the Lira breezed past TRY 23.50, only to close out the week at a staggering TRY 23.35.

As such, and mixed in with the global shortage in the supply of meaningful tonnage, Turkey seems destined for a quieter summer – especially until their fundamentals are sorted and supply comes around.

headline: HKC PROGRESS!
highlights: Ratifying talks. | Slower on sales.
body_text:
The recent talks to ratify the Hong Kong Convention (HKC) in Bangladesh have been an interesting interlude to a year of progress in Chattogram, which has seen the number of class NK HKC certified yards increase to three, as Bangladesh finally approves the Hong Kong Convention, in some highly encouraging developments this week.

Pursuant to these meetings and based on the impact to the environment, the domestic ship recycling sector has also been decategorized from red to orange, and the next step is to get Marshall Islands flag state to ratify the HKC and enter it into force, alongside 20 other countries that have already done / are doing so.

Meanwhile, it has been a slower week in terms of sales in Bangladesh even though prices and demand remain on a stable footing. It is instead more difficult now to get Central bank approval on fresh L/Cs post-budget, and it may take some time / weeks for things to smooth out again.

Local fundamentals too aren’t doing too hot as the Taka surpassed another record while it temporarily breached BDT 109.25, whilst local steel plate prices flatlined through the week.

With religious holiday expected towards the end of the month and monsoons further chipping away at the pace of local activities, Chattogram seems destined for a slower summer, especially as supply continues to be constricted.

highlights: Big news on HKC! | Post budget sales. | Solid fundamentals. | Not at peaks. | Ageing fleet.
body_text:
Bangladesh levels and L/C approvals have continued to struggle post-budget, and it seems that for the time being, there will be some stricter requirements imposed from the Central Bank for Chattogram Recyclers to secure tonnage. Hence, a lower overall appetite has emanated from this market this week, while much of the demand appears to be satiated for the moment and the markets seem to be taking a breather, especially as the monsoons start settling in.

India is not yet on par with Bangladesh and lacks some of the aggression and demand from local Buyers to acquire, whilst Pakistan is totally out of the buying for reasons that have been well documented for weeks now. Lastly, Turkey seems to be heading Pakistan’s way as their levels are closest to each other from all the major markets and both markets continue to struggle to secure tonnage due to currency, and scarcity issues.

Indian fundamentals remained firm this week as the Rupee appreciated against the U.S. Dollar and amidst continued demand for raw materials, steel plate prices firm. We are not at the peaks seen last year when the USD 700/LDT mark was breached. Notwithstanding, at these historically firm levels into the USD 500s/LDT and even close to USD 600/LDT, we are still 30% above the decade’s average.

Finally, there is still an ageing fleet that needs to be scrapped, but many owners are not yet biting the bullet and choosing to sell while they still have time before surveys and can make charter income today. However, BIMCO has recently estimated that double the amount of tonnage will be recycled over the next 10 years due to incoming regulations and the order book, compared with the previous 10 years.

headline: CATCHING UP AND KEEPING UP!
body_text:
India has spent much of the year trying to catch up and keep up with the Bangladeshi market, and so it was yet another week with another bleak report for the sales board, amidst a critical shortage of tonnage and an increasingly barren port report as well.

In fact, for the first time in a memorable while, local port position lies completely empty this week (mirroring the Pakistani market), as the local market continues to suffer the shortage of tonnage.

India also no longer holds the HKC “Ace” card, nor can it rely on a regular diet of HKC green tonnage, such is the progress Bangladesh has been making as there is a firm commitment in the Bangladeshi ship recycling community, to further upgrade yards and raise the country’s ship recycling HKC standards, to those of India.

Fundamentally, India seems to be the only recycling destination where local steel plate prices firmed this week (by about USD 10/Ton), and the currency has gained decent ground over the previous few weeks, firming to under Rs. 81.87 against the U.S. Dollar, giving end Buyers an added incentive to acquire at firm levels again.

headline: FALLING BEHIND!
highlights: No upgrades. | Has been market.
body_text:
Gadani has not only fallen behind on pricing and L/C capabilities this year, but they have also been unable to make the requisite yard upgrades (thus far), in order to gain HKC certification and keep up with an improving Bangladeshi market and the overall sub- continent as a recycling destination.

As such, the market in Pakistan is seriously falling behind with unworkable L/Cs, banking limits, and uncompetitive pricing, mixed in with political, economic, and financial woes that has left the Gadani market out of consideration.

On the local fundamentals front, the Pakistani Rupee continues to sail into dark territory as it briefly surpassed PKR 287.70, while local steel plate prices have yet to be resuscitated out of their flatlined state.

Overall, some real progress (and some settled political and economic / currency conditions) will need to be seen in the second half of this year, in order to place Pakistan back on the international ship recycling scene.

headline: CURRENCY TRAP!
body_text:
Despite the lack of supply of tonnage or mildly steady steel fundamentals (import steel firmed by about USD 5/Ton) or the upcoming religious holidays that could further slow the pace of the domestic ship recycling market, the Turkish Lira remains the prime issue concerning the Turkish Recycling sector.

Seemingly on its way to TRY 24, the Lira temporarily breached TRY 23.75 early in the week, only to settle in at TRY 23.60 against the U.S. Dollar.

As such, as the Lira continues to weaken, it is only a matter of time until local offers on units start to follow, and Turkey slips away further from the overall industry.

headline: CLAMPDOWN!
highlights: HKC attention. | Foreign currency woes.
body_text:
Of course, much of the attention continues to fall on the recently announced positive news of Bangladesh finally ratifying the Hong Kong Convention – the only other sub- continent recycling destination to do so after India.

The next steps for the convention to finally enter into force is subject to a flag state also ratifying the convention. At this juncture, it is reportedly either Marshall Islands or the Liberian Flag.

In terms of new activity post budget and in addition to the onset of Eid, the government has seemingly clamped down on foreign currency expenditures and reserves as Central bank approvals are once again becoming increasingly hard to come by on fresh acquisitions – something that will significantly hamper intended domestic construction and infrastructure projects.

Although Bangladesh is currently the highest paying recycling destination in the world, its key domestic fundamentals are not performing as well as local and industry players would have preferred.

Not only have local steel plate prices flatlined once again, the Taka too weakened (albeit marginally), as it slipped passed BDT 108.0 against the U.S. Dollar this week.

Certainly, a tough summer ahead Chattogram Recyclers.

highlights: Basking in HKC. | Sentiments down. | Eid onset. | Bangla struggles. | LC difficulties.
body_text:
Earlier this year, we had witnessed severe difficulties in Bangladesh with the government focusing only on essential items for the expenditure of its dwindling U.S. Dollar reserves – reportedly food, fuel, and fertilizers. It appears that post-budget, Chattogram (and the ship recycling market at large) will once again have difficulties in obtaining L/C approvals on incoming vessels and it is likely to be a quieter summer for this market as a result.

As we also tend to see a traditionally quieter summer / monsoon season, it is undoubtedly turning out to be particularly challenging time for Bangladeshi Recyclers this time around, as most end users are already struggling to obtain financing on units and have therefore abstained from the offering for another week.

The onset of Eid holidays and celebrations has also not assisted the current situation as many labourers and office staff head back to hometowns for several weeks (even though Eid holidays end on 1 July) while nearly all of the yards virtually close and activity subsides over the rainy season (especially in Bangladesh and India).

In the far end on the West, Turkish Recyclers turn increasingly frustrated on that Lira that has been in freefall for 18 months now and has weakened by a nearly catastrophic 200% during this time.

As such, the sales board for the overall industry remains bleak for another week and any Owners or Cash Buyers with tonnage to sell have certainly become frustrated with a lack of overall appetite, weak(ish) prices and an willingness to buy from the various recycling destinations.

Rank Location Sentiment Dry Bulk USD / LDT

headline: STALE SENTIMENTS!
body_text:
Being the largest ship recycling destination in the world and compared to all of the other major recycling destinations, India was the only country to record positive fundamentals over the last couple of weeks.

Not only has the Indian Rupee firmed against the U.S. Dollar and is below Rs. 82 (at the time of writing), local steel plate prices have also recorded positive movements and reportedly even firmed by about USD 6/Ton, where both Bangladesh and Pakistan have flatlined once again.

Despite this, Alang sentiments remain muted and rather stale.

Moreover, even though several vessels were reportedly discussed into India for an HKC only resale (including LNGs and containers), unfortunately, all the levels on offer have so far have failed to capture the attention of Ship Owners, resulting in NO confirmed market transactions this week.

As monsoon kicks in and yard laborers and staff both in India and Bangladesh return to their hometowns, India might just have a leg up on Bangladesh, given that Alang Buyers no L/C restrictions and Ship Owners and Cash Buyers would both have to accept a lower pricing from Alang – especially if they have a unit that has passed the point of inevitability and is overdue for a visit to a beach for its eventual retirement.

headline: NON-EVENT!
highlights: Irrelevant. | Failures.
body_text:
The nonevent that is currently the Pakistani ship recycling sector, continued for another quiet week, especially as the advent of Eid holidays further rendered Gadani as an even more inactive destination - silent and uncompetitive since the start of the year.

Not only have Pakistani Recyclers yet to upgrade their ship recycling facilities to mirror the ongoing improvements being made by the Bangladeshi and Indian markets, but political, economic, and financial turmoil across Pakistan has also left any serious offers from this market out of consideration?

Domestic fundamentals also remain as much of a non-event as the ongoing performance of this market, whilst local steel plate prices continue to flatline for weeks on end as not a single vessel has graced a local recycling yard with its presence since end of January - and with no ships steel available for trading, there are no steel rates emerging.

The Pakistani Rupee was this markets only silver lining this week as the Rupee firmed marginally from PKR 287.20 to PKR 286.33.

Overall, port reports and the sales board remain unsurprisingly empty, and we can expect this to likely remain the case for the remainder of this year, until some serious change comes to the country

headline: CURRENCY $CRAP!
body_text:
The Lira seems to have found itself strapped to a roller coaster that has been in freefall for the last 18 months - and is yet to find its bottom.

Last week, the Lira drastically depreciated past TRY 22, ending the week at levels excess TRY 23.5X. This week, the Lira pushed past TRY 25.75 mid-week, only to end the week at levels just above TRY 25.

This spiralling key fundamental has created a shockwave that’s finally managed to shake up local sentiments, which are expectedly fraught.

Moreover, even though local steel plate prices have remained stable through the course of the week, local Recyclers don’t seem to have the appetite to bid on tonnage that in itself has been missing from this market for quite some time. And given that industry players are unable to gauge where levels truly stand today as no market units have been concluded into Turkey, it truly is a testing time for this market.

Devoid of meaningful tonnage and necessary fundamentals (like the Pakistani market), just how far can this market continue to survive at this rate, remains to be seen. For now, with religious Eid Holidays upcoming, hopefully locally Recyclers can find distraction amongst friends and family.

headline: LACKING LIQUIDITY!
highlights: Virtual halt. | Sales unlikely.
body_text:
Eid holidays and a post-budget crackdown on fresh L/Cs have seen local resales come to a virtual standstill in Bangladesh.

This is somewhat disappointing as the market had been doing rather well before the budget and L/Cs now need to be re-approved, in order to satiate some of the improving demand / capacity in local yards.

Moreover, Eid celebrations and local holidays further added to the damper on SNP activities as Chattogram Recyclers were busy with friends and family this week.

On the local fundamentals front, the Bangladeshi Take treads weakly at levels just shy of BDT 108.50, while local steel plate prices flatlined through the week once again, on account of Eid celebrations and a total lack of trading.

As such, until these financing issues ease and prices start to improve, it may be a far quieter summer to what we had been expecting in Chattogram.

highlights: Not biting. | Below expectation. | HKC positives. | Pakistan risks. | India low.
body_text:
Therefore, any price ideas that are still forthcoming remain noticeably below the market and not worth considering at this time and until we see liquidity issues ease in the industry, we are not likely to make much sense out of local markets.

Instead, the industry continues to move ahead with other improvements, such as the historical news from Bangladesh and its recent accession to the Hong Kong Convention, another positive step forward to finally getting the convention enter into force in another market – certainly a big win for the overall industry. In fact, Bangladesh has become the latest country (amongst 20 others) to ratify the convention, and this is indeed an important milestone for the country.

Conversely, Pakistan is at real risk of being left behind, having failed to follow India and Bangladesh in upgrading their facilities to follow HKC guidelines / requirements, atop the ongoing profound economic, political, and financial chaos that is currently afflicting the nation - Gadani really has become virtually redundant as a viable sub-continent recycling destination.

India has endured another steady if unspectacular week, as prices remain muted and well below expectations, mixed in with the lack of tonnage and no fresh arrivals at the waterfront, leaving another week of unfulfilled sales.

On the Western front, Turkey spends a quiet week on holidays, with no real movement locally, as Eid celebrations get underway.

Overall, tonnage flow has, as expected, cooled over the recent month and the industry is certainly hoping on some post-holiday improvement in prices, in order to get the industry moving again.

headline: MORE TENTATIVE!
body_text:
Levels in Alang have declined since the peaks seen earlier this year and the local market landscape shows an overall more tentative scene, with many End Buyers preferring to wait and watch market developments, before committing on new units.

Fundamentals-wise, Indian local steel plate prices went through a flurry of volatility, only to end the week USD 1/Ton over last. The Indian Rupee too suffered a minor setback as it breached Rs. 82 against the U.S. Dollar once again, leaving a curious after taste with end buyers who are now continually talking down the market.

As such, there seems little overall danger of Owners and / or Cash Buyers being tempted by these lower levels, and if charter markets (though more muted since the first quarter of the year) continue to offer a modicum of profit, fleet removal will be delayed.

This is also glaringly evident from the fact that local anchorage has only registered one fresh arrival since last week, as no fresh vessels were reported this week.

headline: NO CHANGE!
highlights: Inert market. | Uncertainties.
body_text:
Ongoing Eid celebrations and holidays in Pakistan have not changed the fact that this has been an inert market since January when the last units were beached locally, unable to compete with Bangladesh or India, and even unable to gather the requisite finances / LCs in order to perform on deals – even small LDT vessels.

Financially, Pakistan is in the doldrums with some international media reporting that its U.S. Dollar foreign reserves are down to USD 2 Billion, which aren’t expected to last more than a few weeks (if that) and as a result, ship-recycling has slipped down the totem pole of Pakistan’s priorities.

Notwithstanding, the silver lining is that the IMF is expected to reportedly redirect some critical financial aid to the country. Yet, how much of that will be allocated to ship-recycling remains to be seen.

Fundamentally, the currency has endured a brutal couple of years, having lost a significant portion of its value as it currently trades north of PKR 286.10 against the U.S. Dollar, while local steel plate prices have flatlined for probably months on end now.

Regrettably, the ongoing domestic coups, constantly changing leadership, and political turmoil has further driven the economic state of the country in an overall mess.

As such, it remains uncertain when Pakistan will get back to the buying, and it seems pointless even discussing vessels with Gadani Recyclers under the current circumstances.

headline: CELEBERATIONS!
body_text:
Given the torrid shortage in the supply of tonnage coupled with weak sentiments, the Turkish recycling community kept distracted with Eid celebrations this week.

Moreover, given the current state of the Turkish Lira, which briefly breached TRY 26 against the U.S. Dollar, only to settle just shy of, by the time the week ended, local sentiments remain the doldrums. Even import and local steel plate prices reported no major changes this week, whilst Eid celebrations took priority.

As such, like the Pakistani market, there seems to be little happening with the Aliaga market, now or even in the near future.

headline: HARDER TO COME BY!
highlights: Approvals struggle. | Little sense.
body_text:
It has been another week of virtually no buying as the shortage of tonnage (post-Eid) rages on and most End Buyers remain away from their offices, either on holiday, or now, once again chasing local banks in order to seek financing on any prospective purchases they may be looking to secure for their emptying yards.

Since the start of the year, it has been a difficult affair to transact units for recycling into Bangladesh due to the first set of L/C limits. However, as limits eased, especially on smaller LDT (less than 10K LT) vessels, Bangladeshi Recyclers gradually started to find a way back to the buying.

Unfortunately, right after the recent budget of June 1st was announced, the government seems to have cracked down on the domestic budget for U.S. Dollar reserves once again and imposed a fresh batch of restrictions on the issuance of fresh L/Cs.

It may therefore take several weeks before domestic recyclers work out how they can buy tonnage and at what workable levels the central bank will approve any L/Cs moving forward.

As such, with L/Cs harder to open and no meaningful tonnage on offer, opportunistic offers have been forthcoming from some domestic Recyclers, especially on the dwindling supply of tonnage being proposed for sale.

While no Ship Owner or Cash Buyer would be willing to sell at such lowly rates, even the industry at large is taking notice and is unwilling to even introduce vessels for a potential Chattogram re-delivery – at least until some sensible offers / L/C stability returns.

highlights: Lacking movement. | Waiting game. | No financing. | Stability needed. | Fundamentals ok.
body_text:
As such, before proposing any further candidates, most Cash Buyers and (especially) Ship Owners have decided to continue to wait and watch the markets for greater stability and a better handle on pricing.

Meanwhile, after a couple of volatile quarters, fundamentals presently seem to have leveled out across the board in the Indian sub-continent and even Turkish recycling markets, where steel plate prices and currencies (except in Pakistan) seem to have found a brief plateau of peace.

Moreover, an ongoing lack of workable Letters of Credit (L/Cs) & financing in Pakistan and even in a post-budget Bangladesh is once again driving prices and demand down as the Central Government Bank in Bangladesh seeks to impose tougher limits on the expenditure of its precious U.S. Dollar reserves.

Overall, amidst the ongoing crippling lack of tonnage, those Owners with units closer to recycling age have been seriously reconsidering placing their vessels back into service and are invariably adding to the growing lack of tonnage.

With monsoon’s being the only silver-lining for the sub-continent markets – in that cutting activities come to a crawl as it is - it certainly seems to be a quieter July (and perhaps even August) headed the industry’s way.

headline: GAINING GROUND!
body_text:
While Indian fundamentals (local steel plate prices and the Indian Rupee) recorded some improvements over the last couple of weeks, this week, a different story played out as steel plate prices registered some volatility to end the week slightly weaker, all while the Indian Rupee took a nosedive past Rs. 82.70, only to end the week at levels north of Rs. 82.50 against the U.S. Dollar.

However, unlike the rest of the sub-continent recycling industry, India has not suffered any L/C or financing issues over the year and this has certainly helped them offer on and even secure vessels on an ongoing basis – including their precious HKC units.

Moreover, even of late, there have been some HKC green sales concluded into Alang – including an LNG and a few MSC containers – and this is starting to compel recycling neighbours to compete and up their offers, if they stand any chance at securing any vessels – especially amidst the ongoing L/C issues in Pakistan and now in Bangladesh.

Finally, we anticipate that the ongoing slowdown in the supply of tonnage will likely continue through the next month (or two), as shipowners head off on summer holidays and it is expected to be quieter (in terms of sale and purchase activity) over these monsoon months.

headline: NO EFFORT!
highlights: Missing out. | Ongoing struggles.
body_text:
Far from competing against any of their sub-continent competitors at present, Pakistani Recyclers cannot even compete amongst themselves for tonnage – so dire and low have Pakistan’s U.S Dollar Reserves been for much of this year, causing the Pakistani Rupee to depreciate uncontrollably.

In fact, over the last couple of weeks, Pakistan was on the verge of running out of all its U.S. Dollar funds until the IMF (in addition to several other nations) stepped in this week and provided a financial U.S. Dollar stimulus package to Pakistan.

While this did not help local steel plate prices, which have remained horizontal for practically most of this year, the Pakistani Rupee did however, immediately receive a boost and firmed up to PKR 277 (from PKR 287) against the U.S. Dollar.

As the shortage of tonnage continues and India takes in its share of regular and HKC tonnage, Pakistani Recyclers have yet to make any efforts at improving their facilities during this downtime, especially so that they maybe in a position to compete even strongly against its sub-continent neighbors.

Of course, the Pakistani economy has struggled significantly as leaders have been ousted while the local currency has also collapsed, and this has seen end buyers and banks retreating from the buying of ships for recycling altogether.

headline: ON PAUSE?
body_text:
Post-Eid, the Turkish market seems to have gone through a bit of a pause, as local fundamentals came together in unison and reported no changes for the week.

Surprising much of the industry was the Lira that reported no further declines as it ended the week at levels just north of TRY 26. Even imported and local steel plate prices have reported virtually no change for the week.

As post Eid-holidays / celebrations continue amidst the ongoing shortage in the availability of tonnage and a Lira that is completely unsupportive of current offers, it remains to be seen just where (USD / MT) or when this market will open for business ‘as usual’.

For now, like the rest of its industry counterparts, it ended a quiet week in Aliaga.

headline: PAUSE!
highlights: Yet to get back. | No local sales.
body_text:
Following the conclusion of Eid holidays, Bangladeshi Buyers are yet to get back to the buying as very few offers at reasonable (or even acceptable) levels have been forthcoming this week.

As such, Ship Owners and Cash Buyers are starting to turn to other markets / India, so inert is the Bangladeshi market at present - and it may be that we see this market on the sidelines over the quieter summer / monsoon months.

The previous problem surrounding Central Bank permissions is continuing to affect the financing of fresh L/Cs once again, whilst fundamentals, especially local steel plate prices have continued to flatline for some time now.

Even the Bangladeshi Taka continues to tread at record-breaking highs against the U.S. Dollar, all while local Recyclers continue to present opportunistic below-market offers on units being proposed.

As a result, infrastructure projects are mostly on hold due to the incessant rains & lack of steel from the mills, and the fact that steel mills have yet to fully reopen / resume business following Eid holidays.

Notwithstanding, on the sales front, as Chinese owners continue their clear out of older tonnage, this week, the General Cargo / Bulk Carrier vessel XIANG HE (9,016 LDT) managed to fetch a decent USD 520/LT LDT basis an ‘as is’ Singapore delivery.

highlights: Frustrations | Flow slows. | Mills yet to resume. | LC woes. | Pak back?
body_text: Rank Location Sentiment Dry Bulk USD / LDT

headline: NOT WORKABLE!
body_text:
Indian levels continue to confound and disappoint the industry as Alang Buyers believe that offering levels below USD 500/LDT will entice Ship Owners and Cash Buyers to part with their vintage tonnage.

Unsurprisingly, few sales have materialized into Alang, and any available tonnage looks set to head to competing markets (with three yards in Bangladesh now class NK HKC certified), including a newly funded Pakistan after news of the IMF loan broke this week.

Fundamentals too remain volatile as local steel plate prices declined by about USD 13/Ton this week, while the Indian Rupee straddles around the Rs. 82s against the U.S. Dollar.

As such, if the current trends persist, we can certainly expect a quieter summer in Alang as End Buyers continue to complain about market conditions and give unworkable & unreasonably opportunistic offers, all when Owners may as well sell elsewhere or continue trading their vessels.

headline: LOAN APPROVED!
highlights: IMF help. | HKC needs.
body_text:
News about the recent USD 3 billion IMF bailout loan has been forthcoming into Pakistan, with USD 1 billion already being received by the country, and this may give the ship recycling industry some hope that Pakistan could get back to some form of buying in the weeks / months ahead – especially if a portion of the funds are allocated to the domestic ship recycling sector.

As such, as soon as commercial banks start sanctioning fresh L/Cs, we may see some deals taking place into a recycling location that has otherwise been starved of tonnage for most of the year, due to the ongoing and dire political & economic circumstances in the country.

Of course, Gadani Recyclers will need to seriously focus on upgrading their facilities and keep up with the ongoing industry changes, especially as the HKC enters into force in Bangladesh, else Pakistan seems destined to miss out on tonnage altogether.

Fundamentals aren’t too supportive either, especially as domestic steel plate prices continue to flatline for months on end and the Pakistani Rupee that recently firmed to PKR 277 against the U.S. Dollar, has stayed there during the course of the week.

As such, and like its competing neighbors, we can certainly expect a quieter summer / monsoon in Pakistan.

headline: GOING DOWN?
body_text:
The Turkish market seems poised to soften moving forward, as not only did local steel plate prices decline by about USD 20/MT, even import steel prices followed suit with a decline of about USD 10/MT of their own.

All while the Turkish Lira glides along and gradually weakens deeper into TRY 26.2X territory against the U.S. Dollar. And this is unravelling whilst the shortage of tonnage continues to deteriorate local sentiments well past Eid holidays.

As such, it’s certainly a reasonable bet that the Turkish recycling market may face a correction in prices in the weeks ahead.

headline: EASING!
highlights: Buyers emerge. | Bulkers sold.
body_text:
A lot of the L/C difficulties post-Eid seem to finally be easing this week as an increasing number of Buyers emerged at the tables to offer on and acquire new units, be it at these lower overall levels of today.

Vessels continue to be proposed from the Chinese market (in particular) and there are several Dry Bulk vessels (Handy and Panamax sizes in particular) backed up and waiting for L/Cs to open so that vessels can arrive locally and eventually beach.

Fresh sales this week saw the Chinese controlled ZHENG HAO and ZHENG JIE (10,613 LDT) committed en bloc, for a decent USD 495/LT LDT basis an ‘as is’ China delivery, in addition to another Bulk Carrier YANG FAN (10,934 LDT) that was committed with various removals, a conversion, and installed cranes, for a decent USD 540/LT LDT basis an ‘as is’ Batam delivery and with sufficient bunkers included on board for the voyage to the sub-continent.

Meanwhile, fundamentals continue to face their share of troubles as the Bangladeshi Taka continues to trade at a record-breaking BDT 108.50 levels against the U.S. Dollar, all while local steel plate prices continue to flatline.

highlights: Price struggle. | Supply increase. | LC moves. | Dry bulk. | Static.
body_text:
The supply of tonnage seems to have increased just slightly over the last couple of weeks (particularly from the Chinese market) and as such, many Owners and Cash Buyers have been left chasing down various recycling destinations amidst weakening prices.

As forecasted a few weeks ago, Pakistan finally seems ready to return into the game and has even overtaken an extremely lackluster Indian market wherefrom, lowball offers of below USD 500/LDT seem to be coming regularly in, with little success for all parties involved. As such, it may take some time to work through the L/C issues in Pakistan, but it is certainly encouraging to see various offers come back close to currently competitive levels.

On the supply side, it has mostly been vessels from the Dry Bulk sector that continue to be introduced to the recycling markets, especially older Panamax and Handy units built in the 90s that are perhaps overdue for retirement from their respective fleets.

Post budget in Bangladesh has certainly been more difficult to get Central Bank approval on fresh L/Cs, but things seem to have eased up a touch this week as local Buyers are emerging once again, just as the tonnage flow is also increasing.

Finally, the Turkish market seems to have taken a turn for the worst, as import and local steel prices, the Currency, and even vessel prices have all taken a tumble during this week, with some vessel indications reportedly coming in even below USD 300/MT.

Overall, it will certainly take some time to absorb many of the unsold vessels not only being freshly proposed into the markets, but also those units in Cash Buyer hands and as such, sentiments and demand may remain somewhat muted for some time – at least until the monsoons start to subside.

Rank Location Sentiment Dry Bulk USD / LDT

headline: ON EDGE!
body_text:
Indian prices have sunk to their lowest levels for quite some time now and there are even opportunistic offers forthcoming from Alang Buyers that are below USD 500/LDT.

These lowball offers are not resulting in much success for Indian Recyclers - even for HKC green tonnage - and with Pakistan coming back into the picture recently, firmer prices will be needed in the near future, in order for domestic Recyclers to secure their share of tonnage.

Domestic fundamentals continue their dance as the Indian Rupee continues trading into the high Rs. 81s against the U.S. Dollar, all while local steel plate prices extended their volatility once again, ending the week only USD 1/Ton above those from last week.

headline: LEAPFROG!
highlights: Enquiries emerge. | Above India.
body_text:
News of the USD 3 billion injection of IMF funding is set to ease the financial crisis that Pakistan has crushingly endured for nearly all of this year, and this has seemed to finally bear some fruit this week as several offers and End Buyers were seen emerging from the abyss and enquiring to buy tonnage once again.

Having been out of the picture for the better part of a year, it will take some working through the ongoing L/C issues with domestic banks, in order to see some form of business normality resume moving forward.

For now, fundamentals continue to deteriorate as the Pakistani Rupee weakened drastically from PKR 277 to nearly PKR 286 this week, all while local steel plate prices remain horizontal for months on end.

Notwithstanding, despite the weakening fundamentals, Pakistani Buyers have jumped above India in the price rankings and are encouragingly within striking distance of competing with Bangladesh once again.

As such, we can only hope a quick small LDT deal or two should help set the local financial gears cranking again, making it smoother for further deals moving forward.

headline: DECLINE CONFIRMED!
body_text:
Last week, imminent fears of an upcoming correction seem to have played out this week as declines in key fundaments (i.e., plate prices and the Turkish Lira) resulted in vessel prices declining by about USD 20/Ton this week.

Not only did import and local steel plate prices decline by about USD 15/Ton and USD 20/Ton respectively, but the Lira also declined further as it approached TRY 27 against the U.S. Dollar – ending the week at TRY 26.95.

Sentiments have gotten worse and on the few units being offered, all levels in the low USD 300/MT (some even reportedly below) came forth this week from nervous Aliaga Buyers.

As such, even though supply may seem better than before, these new lower levels might put off fresh Sellers and Cash Buyers, at least until these prices are finally accepted.

headline: MARKET OF ONE!
highlights: Sale over 600. | Withdrawing.
body_text:
The big news this week surrounded a well-above market sale of a Sinokor container as the SINOKOR TIANJIN (4,672 LDT) managed to fetch an astonishing USD 622/LT LDT on a delivered basis.

The sale included about 250 Tons of bunkers (about USD 10/LT worth) and the favored small LDT unit has likely assisted the Vessel Owners in achieving a big price, as more Buyers could obtain USD / Ton financing on smaller LDT vessels.

Nevertheless, it is certain that it is an above-market sale of one into Chattogram, especially as very few End Buyers are actively pursuing tonnage at sensible levels.

The ongoing incessant rains are hampering domestic construction projects in the country as well as ship-recycling activities, in addition to domestic fundamentals that are jointly degrading local sentiments. Not only have local steel plate prices declined by nearly USD 20/Ton this week, but the Bangladeshi Taka also continues to languish at record-lows against the U.S. Dollar - at nearly BDT 108.50.

As such, Cash Buyers and Vessel Owners are withdrawing sales candidates from this market, or are simply diverting them to other markets, or continuing to trade them while sentiments, demand, ability to perform (amidst ongoing strained financing and Central Bank LC approvals), and pricing remain so low at present.

highlights: Negative. | Monsoon slows. | Container sale. | Pakistan enquires. | India low.
body_text:
Ravaging monsoon rains are the leading cause of the ongoing slowdown in the sub-continent as minimal cutting / recycling activities at yards is taking place and as such, the market is barely moving forward with the minor number of vessels being committed.

There is no question that Cash Buyers and Vessel Owners are unaccepting of some of the opportunistic offers being put out there and as such, we are witnessing something of a standoff on any number of unsold vessels at present.

The one confirmed sale for the week saw a Sinokor controlled container that was committed for an extraordinary price into Bangladesh, but we would like to caution our readers that this is not a true reflection of current market conditions at all, and it increasingly seems to be that just one particularly hot Buyer who was able to arrange L/C limits / bank financing on a favored small LDT unit.

Encouragingly, enquiries have been emerging from Pakistan as well, and it may take one or two confirmed sales and beachings to go through, what would inevitably (and eventually) establish a new direction for Cash Buyers and Gadani Recyclers, for clearing L/Cs & various other payment issues, especially having been out of the game for so long.

India once again slips to the lowest placed of all sub-continent markets and as the supply of green ships and specialist units dries up, Alang Buyers are seeing minimal tonnage and new arrivals, as evident from this week’s local port position, which reported no fresh arrivals.

Finally, the Turkish market remains suspended in no-man’s land (just like the sub-continent markets), with the Lira briefly breaching TRY 27 and no movement reported in steel prices.

headline: LOWLY!
body_text:
India slips once again to become the lowest placed sub-continent destination as Alang Buyers started placing opportunistic numbers – even below USD 500/LDT on occasion on any proposed tonnage, which is subsequently drying up the local market of tonnage.

No new vessels arrived Alang anchorage this week, with only one beaching of a prior arrival from last week. Even an emerging Pakistani market (albeit a market with ongoing LC / financing difficulties) is now ahead of India on pricing.

Fundamentals continue to crisscross in opposite directions as volatile steel plate prices firmed marginally this week, all while the Indian Rupee deteriorated past Rs. 82 against the U.S. Dollar once again.

Accordingly, the only constructive way forward for Alang Buyers will be to raise their game and offer realistic levels, should they wish to secure vessels moving forward.

headline: EMERGING!
highlights: Demand increase. | HKC needs.
body_text:
Pakistan has started to re-enter the game in recent weeks, as enquiries for various working vessels have started to be fielded by Pakistani Recyclers after a year (and then some) of being out of the game.

As domestic financials (and the Pakistani economy overall) have gained a degree of stability amidst the incoming financial bailout from the IMF, we can only hope that funding for the domestic ship recycling sector may eventually get a slice of the incoming pie.

It will certainly take a couple of sales to see how L/C approvals will unravel moving forward and in order to import & beach ships in Gadani once again, all while domestic fundamentals continue to suffer.

The Pakistani Rupee is still in the high PKR 280s against the U.S. Dollar as local steel plate prices remain flat for months on end.

Of course, local Buyers will also need to upgrade their facilities (like India and Bangladesh have been busy doing) up to HKC standards, as the convention is due to be finally entered into force and officially in 2025.

headline: DULL WEEK!
body_text:
Aliaga is now going through a lull after last week’s decline in prices, as these sudden low offers (some reportedly even below USD 300/MT) are probably not going to entice many Ship Owners or even Cash Buyers to successfully complete a sale into Turkey, other than market proposed EUSRR specific units, of which, we have not seen any for a while.

Fundamentals continue to affect local pricing as the Lira remains weakened at record levels, briefly surpassing TRY 27 against the U.S. Dollar, while local steel plate prices reportedly recorded no changes this week, after both import and local steel reported noteworthy declines last week.

Other than the summer heat burning up the nation, everything recycling remains on ice.

headline: UNTENABLE!
highlights: Outlier sales. | Lack of interest.
body_text:
Several sales have reportedly taken place into Bangladesh this week that seemed to belie the overall negativity in this market as present.

Firstly, a favored Polish built container unit SOL STRAITS (7,770 LDT) was fixed to one particularly keen hot Bangladeshi Buyer, for an impressive USD 592/LT LDT (with 250 Tons of bunkers included in the sale).

Additionally, another favored type, RoRo vessel TAI HWA (4,043 LDT) from Taiwan Navigation was committed basis an ‘as is’ Kaohsiung delivery, for a decent USD 460/LT LDT.

However, the overall sentiments and demand in Bangladesh remain dire and these sales are once again outliers and not indicative of the true conditions of this market, especially one that is becoming untenable for most Owners and Cash Buyers to negotiate with.

Fundamentals too remain dire as the Taka nearly breached BDT 109.40 (highest ever) against the U.S. Dollar, only to retreat and end the week at BDT 108.95. Even local steel plate prices depreciated last week and flatlined through this week, further deteriorating local sentiments and confusing local Buyers where local prices should truly stand.

highlights: Not workable. | Unsold. | Bleak. | Troublesome. | L/C concerns.
body_text:
There remain a number of unsold units that are currently being diverted to other destinations from Bangladesh, including India, in additional to a recently re-emerging Pakistani market.

Owners with vessels to sell are being price-shocked into diverting their vessels to another market or withdrawing them from the market entirely, due to a lack of sensible offers that present no encouragement / motivation / interest from Owners (or Cash Buyers) to commit for recycling.

We could therefore be entering a bleaker period of sales and activity through August, especially whilst this standoff in prices persists, and congestion abounds.

Deliveries have started to become troublesome as well, particularly for those units sold at recently higher levels and are now facing the inevitable song-and-dance at the waterfront with unreliable Cash Buyers and painful renegotiations being reported at the waterfront.

As such, it is an extremely frustrating and fraught market at present, with Owners and Cash Buyers alike, who are becoming disillusioned by the falling levels and lack of serious offers. There is only so much chasing down a market that can be endured before some sort of stability is seen, especially once prices level out and the industry finally accepts the levels on the ground.

L/Cs also remain an area of concern in Bangladesh as it has been taking much longer to get L/C approvals over USD 5 million these days, and this is leading to delays in obtaining offers and getting vessels delivered.

headline: SLIPPING!
body_text:
India remains the lowest placed sub-continent market and has once again seen tonnage slip through their hands, despite being the one location that is capable of reliably performing financial / L/C transactions.

Indeed, offers below USD 500/LDT have not been received well by Ship Owners or Cash Buyers and they have either diverted their units to alternative destinations, or even entirely withdraw them from the market.

The biggest question that remains is WHY?

The markets need to stop evaluating every transaction as a lottery win each time – trying to beat the ‘last done’, especially considering the cyclical nature of the industry. Prices at every level are firm, price-shock or not. While remaining in the green is certainly essential for the parties involved, watching the direction of the market when concluding units is just as critical, especially in order to avoid unpleasant surprises at the time of physical delivery and just accept the declining nature of market conditions.

At a time when prices hit the mid USD 200s/LT during the worst of the market, we are presently at levels that are over double those for recycling back in ’08 and certainly a long way from the early USD 100s/LT from only a couple of decades ago.

As such, price amnesia certainly remains a detriment in current times.

The traditionally quieter period over the monsoon and summer months are also upon the industry, so perhaps prices and aggression to acquire may improve from September moving forwards.

For now, with a Rupee that came close to breaching Rs. 83 and local steel plate prices that have moved in the opposite direction (firming by about USD 12/Ton), India is certainly in the crosshairs of confusion this week.

headline: BACK & BIDDING!
highlights: Slowly returning. | LC time.
body_text:
Pakistan has finally started to re-emerge as a viable force after almost a year on the sidelines, unable to conclude any units due to the ongoing financial, economic, and even political woes besetting the country.

Consequently, it seems certain that several deals may need to be concluded into Gadani as vessel Owners and Cash Buyers seek alternate options to a lowballing India and a Bangladesh lacking demand.

Local fundamentals too remain weakened like the rest of the industry, with local steel plate prices flatlining for months on end due to a total lack of domestic steel trading, in addition to the Pakistani Rupee that briefly breached PKR 289, only to retreat to PKR 287 against the U.S. Dollar, by the time the week ended.

As such, it may take some time to work through what are likely to be some L/C delays, but it is certainly encouraging that enquiries are emerging, and the feeling is that it is only a matter of time before deals will start being concluded into Pakistan once again.

headline: SLIPPING FURTHER!
body_text:
Like the Bangladeshi market, the Turkish market seems to be slipping even further as local steel plate prices reportedly declined by about USD 10/MT and the Lira briefly breached TRY 27.20, only to retreat to TRY 26.9X as the week ended.

Such fundamentals are certainly not conducive to maintaining market levels and although Turkish prices seemed far more resilient to declining this year than the years gone last, just how long can Aliaga Buyers maintain their pricing through such unrelentingly negative fundamentals, including a domestic economy that has been set alight due to inflation, remains to be seen.

We can only hope that the ongoing ‘regulations’ for environmentally conscious recycling are also taking into account, the livelihoods of people that are so dependent on this sector and may likely be displaced due to the prevailing rules on recycling.

headline: NO GO!
highlights: Frustrations. | Sales.
body_text:
Despite Owners & Cash Buyers attempts to commit their vessels into Bangladesh, it turned into an extremely frustrating (& failed) exercise that resulted in an inert week in Chattogram, since local Buyers continue to present lowball and opportunistic offers, only to lose out on those units to competing markets.

The weakened state of domestic fundamentals coupled with prevailing economic concerns, all of it mixed with the monsoon rains certainly seem like the key drivers behind the current state of pricing affairs.

For starts as demand for steel intended for national infrastructure projects has slowed significantly amidst the intense monsoon rains this year, local steel plate prices have resumed flatlining on account of a standstill in the trading of ship’s steel with domestic steel mills.

Moreover, the Bangladeshi Taka hit a record BDT 109.38 against the U.S. Dollar this week, further adding to the ongoing hassle that the Bangladeshi ship recycling sector has become today.

Notwithstanding, even though a couple of geographically convenient ‘as is’ dry bulk sales have taken place this week that could see Chattogram Buyers get their hands on these units, the chances that these could handily be redirected to a competing destination remains rather high, given just how disastrously Chattogram Buyers are toying with their local offerings are at present.

At the onset, bulk carrier B H MALLY (9,379 LT) was concluded for a decent USD 465/LDT, basis an ‘as is’ South China delivery and with 200 Tons of bunkers included in the sale. Subsequently, the Handymax bulker AN YUE (7,985 LDT) was committed for an equally firm USD 475/LT LDT basis an ‘as is’ Singapore delivery, also with 200 Tons of fuel onboard.

highlights: Inert week. | Dying appetite. | Weak. | India for LCs. | Withdraw.
body_text: Rank Location Sentiment Dry Bulk USD / LDT

headline: FLACCID!
body_text:
At a time when Indian Recyclers have a real chance to strike out much of the competition and secure most of the meagre amounts of tonnage that is currently on offer, local Buyers have failed to distinguish themselves from the crowd by lowering their prices this week.

Unfortunately, at a time when resilience is the key, the chance to secure vessels seems to be squandered away by Alang Recyclers.

Like Bangladesh, fundaments certainly have their share to add to the current state of affairs as the Indian Rupee once again approaches Rs. 83 against the U.S. Dollar, while local steel plate prices declined by about USD 12 / Ton by the time the week ended.

Should this continue, we may well see previous and even fresh market deals concluded by various Cash Buyers (with an India redelivery in mind), eventually ending up in a competing market with firmer offers, so flaccid are Alang prices at present.

The old sale of Panamax Bulker AGIOS NIKOLAOS (9,743 LDT) surfaced this week as the vessel was previously committed to a Cash Buyer at a decent USD 540/LT LDT basis an ‘as is’ Singapore delivery and a reported India redelivery in mind. The unit remains unsold due to the declining prices and is still idling in Singapore, almost certain to lose money on this transaction.

Additionally, container vessel HENG HUI 2 (14,775 LDT) was likewise concluded for a surprisingly firm USD 550/LDT, basis an ‘as is’ Colombo delivery and with 300 Tons of bunkers included in the sale.

headline: QUESTIONABLE!
highlights: Could secure. | Finance issues.
body_text:
Pakistan has inadvertently found itself in a situation whereby, Gadani Buyers could secure any of the recently committed ‘as is’ units that are currently (or may soon be) on offer, and this most recent declining of Bangladeshi and Indian prices has found the Pakistani market thrust atop the price / market rankings this week, with some unexpectedly firm indications coming forth as well.

Pakistani L/C and financing issues logically remain a big concern for the industry, especially after a dire year of economic and political hurdles in the country, coupled with declining fundamentals that have only further added to the crippling of this market.

On the domestic fundamentals front, not only has the Pakistani Rupee collapsed back to a record PKR 287.2X level against the U.S. Dollar, but local steel plate prices also need to be resuscitated from their months long flatlined demise.

Moreover, Pakistan has had virtually no L/C and finance approvals on vessel purchases for quite some time now and as such, the country remains a precarious destination to consider business dealings with, at least until a couple of sales have been concluded into Gadani and the industry gets acclimatized to doing business here once again.

Notwithstanding, given the incredible lowball offers emanating from Bangladesh and even India at present, Owners and Cash Buyers might as well be giving the Pakistani market a serious second look and as such, it will therefore be interesting to see just which vessels will end up at Gadani’s waterfront.

headline: DEAD QUIET!
body_text:
For the most part, the Turkish market remained reportedly devoid of activity for yet another week as the recently deteriorated vessel prices remained unchanged for the week and the Turkish Lira, though stable, remains depreciated at a historic TRY 27.X against the U.S. Dollar.

The only positive movement for the week (without any positive outcome in return) were steel prices whereby import steel firmed by about USD 10/Ton and local steel prices improved by about USD 6/Ton.

Notwithstanding, despite all the ongoing volatility in fundamentals, there is little this market can do in the face of intense tonnage starvation, which has left this market unable to maintain a pulse.

As such, this market remains dead quiet for now.

headline: EXCESS TONNAGE!
highlights: Bargain deals. | New round of sales.
body_text:
Bangladesh has been the market to struggle with (or perhaps exploit) the excess tonnage over these summer months with some absolutely bargain deals being done to end buyers below USD 500/LDT.

Fundamentals in terms of steel prices actually remain remarkably sturdy, it is just that the constant rains that invariably come at this time of year due to the seasonal monsoons, means that product is not shifting from yards to mills, so there is a backlog of unsold steel material lying idle for the time being (which should start to ease once monsoon ends in mid September onwards).

In terms of sales, the container vessel SOL HIND (7,792 LDT) was fixed for a decent USD 565/LT LDT for a prompt end August delivery (with 200 Ts bunkers), whilst another poor condition Chinese bulker (with questionable crane removal weight), the MINGZHOU 25 (6,729 LDT) was committed at USD 400/LT LDT (‘as is’ Zhoushan), and the smaller MPP JIN YUAN SHENG 9 (3,000 LDT) fetched USD 490/LT LDT.

highlights: Spiralling prices. | Over 100/LDT fall. | India lowest. | Supply still. | Post monsoon up?
body_text:
Indeed we have seen prices decline from over USD 600/LT LDT earlier this year, to seeing several standard (albeit poor condition) dry bulk sales below USD 500/LDT recently.

So a fall of over USD 100/LDT has been realized in recycling markets since the start of the summer and the age old problems persist of strained LCs and lack of financing, meaning there appear to be more vessels than capable end buyers at present – certainly in the more challenging markets of Pakistan and Bangladesh.

India remains a constant market, in terms of end buyers capable of opening LCs, yet prices are once again positioned at the bottom of the pile in the sub continent, with most end users fearful of committing on fresh tonnage such has been the extent and ferocity of recent price falls.

The supply of tonnage – particularly from Far East and China markets – has remained a constant over these summer months (when it is usually quieter), and those cash buyers who have bougbht ‘as is’ tonnage without back to back end users in place have been hardest hit with tumbling levels and a stockpile of seemingly unsellable tonnage.

There is hope however that once monsoon season ends and product starts to shift from yards and mills reopen, that we may see a greater demand at least to acquire once again.
