As we stand on the edge of the final weeks of 2024, compared to the rest of the year, it certainly seems as though there has been more of an uptick in the markets of late, in addition to a far more positive conclusion for ship the recycling sector in the Indian sub-continent, as news of fixtures on the back of firming levels has kept recyclers busy taking deliveries at the various waterfronts over recent weeks. Though the markets are not quite there to breach the coveted USD 500/LDT mark just yet, they have come out of a Q2 – Q3 and even early Q4, when recycling levels were at their lowest this year. Moreover, and pragmatically, rather than attempting to break the next high-priced fixture in the market, ship owners (especially) and even cash buyers need to historically reflect on the fact that these are still very strong prices today.

Meanwhile, unlike the unfolding chess moves from the tanker sector, supply from other sectors is expected to remain steady / likely improve into 2025 and despite trading markets performing impressively as they drive the global fleet to its highest average age it has ever been, increasing newbuild constructions in 2025 should phase out older units faster and ensure a steadier recycling supply. Additionally, despite China’s stimulus announcements promising stronger measures for its economy, Capesize bulkers managed to lose ground even further and all eyes will now be peeled on the Trump’s incoming tariffs that will manifest once he takes office from January 20th, including the tariffs he intends to impose on China, in particular.

headline: RESURGENT TIME.
highlights: Picking up tonnage. | HKC ready. | Keen to buy.
body_text:
As with Chattogram, Alang’s ship recycling sector has welcomed a version of its own resurgence in the final moments of the year and likely into early 2025 as well, as news of even more deals being successfully concluded to Alang ship recyclers as a result of the firming offers – including specialist stainless steel units, containers, oil rigs, tankers, fishing vessels, and HKC only India vessels – have started to increasingly surface over successive recent weeks.

The fact that nearly all recycling yards in Alang essentially have their HKC certification in order, will immensely help India maintain pole-position on a global ship recycling level, to safely absorb much of the world’s environmentally conscious recycling tonnage when it comes for sale in the years ahead, as the Hong Kong Convention finally enters into force from the middle of next year and Bangladeshi and (especially) Pakistani recyclers are not only in the process of still gathering recipes to upgrade their facilities, but they also remain far from receiving any SoC approvals from IACS class-societies thereafter.

Even domestically, India remains the most financially secure destination for global ship recycling on account of a comparatively larger (than other ship recycling destinations worldwide) availability of U.S. Dollar reserves, further bolstering India’s financial stability in a sector that is heavily dependent on it. Moreover, as trade with the U.S. is about to breach a unique milestone and break a record USD 77.5 Billion in 2024, it marks an overall 10.3% rise over the last 30 years of India’s trade with the country.

Notwithstanding the economic stability, key fundamentals driving local mindsets remain shaky as ever amidst a Rupee that has now seen the better part of Rs. 84 throughout the week, even as it spikes to hit a record Rs. 84.99 against the U.S. Dollar and finally end the week an overall 14 basis points weaker at Rs. 84.80. Local steel plate prices weren’t seemingly supportive of the prevailing mindset either and although shaky, managed to end the week at just USD 1/MT below last week, easily chalking it down to market movements.

As the Indian ship recycling sector continues to surf the wakes of a relatively optimistic economy and much in contrast to this week’s local port position – where a healthy collection of units from rigs to reefers are awaiting deliveries – the future supply of tonnage may see hiccups amidst unfolding global tensions, rising average ages of the world’s overall fleets, and the persisting slowdown in the output of newbuildings, all of which would be the final nails in the coffin for ship recyclers worldwide. And the fact that it was only this past January where levels were at USD 600/LDT for containers and today stand almost lower USD 150/LDT, the industry is certainly eager to see global economies firm again to where levels at or above USD 500/Ton become the norm.

headline: SAD REFLECTION!
highlights: Not easy going. | Liquidity issues. | HKC failures.
body_text:
It certainly has not been easygoing for Pakistan’s ship recycling sector this year and second only to 2023, where only 16 vessels were delivered to local recyclers throughout the year, 2024 looks on track to be the second slowest year for the ship recycling in Gadani over the last decade. Logically, supply has also been at its lowest over the same period, but the present can simply not be the reason behind Gadani’s ongoing performance, especially as neighboring India and (especially) Bangladesh continue to dominate the bidding tables and market rankings of late.

The ever-tailing Indian offers mindset aside, Pakistan has been beset with financial / liquidity issues and an unfolding lack of overall confidence in the state of the domestic economy, which has eventually filtered down to perpetually nervy end buyers who have seen their plots lie mostly dormant for a majority of 2024. As inflation continues to create hurdles amidst stalled discussions on IMF’s incoming loan, which itself continues to be delayed on account of pending investigations, the Paksitani government has continually curtailed expenses towards non-essential industries for the time being, including ship recycling, as the country hopes for the incoming bailout package to ease ongoing economic constraints.

As a result of the lack of availability of U.S. Dollars, the Pakistani Rupee, though ending the week only 2 basis points weaker at PKR 278 against the Dollar, certainly rollercoaster-ed its way to this point through the course of the week. Psychologically hurting the local mindset even further are collapsed steel plate prices, which, despite being the highest of all of the major ship recycling nations, is the least traded of all as it continues to flatline at a comparatively stronger USD 654/Ton – nearly USD 200/Ton higher than those from neighboring India and amidst cheaper imports, further highlighting just how weak domestic demand for steel currently is.

With the HKC coming into force a mere 6 months away and Gadani ship recycling yard owners still buying the recipe books for the ‘green’ efforts needed towards upgrading their respective recycling yards, 2025 may end up being just as bad, if not worse for Gadani, especially once the convention comes into force and yards owners will be compelled to make investments in order to continue operation, or shut shop by the time 2026 comes around.

headline: AFLOAT…BARELY!
body_text: As the Lira’s decline against the U.S. Dollar continues uncontested, declining 37 basis points and ending the week at another historic TRY 34.91, import steel plate prices corrected / improved about USD 12/Ton, matching local steel plate prices, which themselves remain constricting low. As local offers stable after declining nearly USD 30/MT over recent weeks, the new lows are going to raise the bar for Aliaga buyers to snag their share of tonnage even more, especially in the face of sub- continent levels that are firming / on the rise again.

headline: RETURN TO FORM?
highlights: Year of upheaval. | Volumes low. | Demand return.
body_text:
The Bangladeshi economy is gradually crutching its way through a recovery phase and local confidence certainly was elevated this week, on the back of the news that a U.S.D. 500 million budget support loan in order to greatly boost domestic reserves at a time the country is in desperate need of financial support and recovery through a year of unrelentingly negative outcomes. The government is expected to sign the agreement within next week, further delivering a message that a characteristic January firming may still be on the charts, at least for Chattogram Choppers.

As reports of construction projects are yet to come forth, news of stalled trading of steel continues to haunt domestic recyclers as demand from steel mills remains stranded on the back of flailing domestic demand. As demand from local ship recycling yards consequently stalls coupled with the lack of available U.S. Dollars for domestic recyclers, has resulted in most of the plots lying empty for a majority of the year.

The lack of ship’s steel trade has also seen local steel plate prices remain stranded at a weak-ish USD 521/Ton, leaving the ceiling of local offerings constricted to how far recyclers are willing to bite into their margins, just to keep their yards operational through a time so many others are still functioning at or below desired levels of output. The U.S. Dollar too continues to dance vigorously around late BDT 119s, managing to stay just above BDT 120 against it, ending the week at a slightly optimistic (compared to last week) BDT 119.47. This is finally starting to see local offering finally take a hit as indications maybe taking a hit. Time will tell.

This reluctance from domestic recyclers handicapped with prices capped at current steel plate levels is once again seeing no news of market or even private sales being committed to Chattogram, resulting in a waterfront that could likely deliver an empty port position next week, as the only activity at the waterfront were deliveries of last week’s arrivals to their respective Choppers and no new arrivals indicated at anchorage for this week.

Notwithstanding, with the economy gradually on the mend and domestic reserves looking to get a healthy boost for the interim (at least carry the economy until the country’s national elections are concluded), domestic sentiments remain eager and recyclers are on the lookout for tonnage, amidst a relative return to form has been seen from this market as we approach the end of this year, despite it being a year of upheaval and concern for the country and in turn for Chattogram’s ship recycling sector. The volumes available for sale have also been at the lowest level in the last decade and yards have been wisely spending their time upgrading their infrastructure facilities during this period of slowdown, so much that class NK have thus far approved 4 facilities in Chattogram in 2024, with more set to follow before the HKC kicks into gear around mid-year.

headline: CHANGE AHEAD!
highlights: Encouraging. | Price cool. | Big year coming. | Elections done. | Bangla turmoil.
body_text:
And although a slightly disappointing local port position earmarks the end of Week 51, it still remains a more encouraging end to the year that has left recycling markets in an overall more bullish mood heading into Q1 2025 – seeking to negotiate on and absorb the incoming flow of tonnage of some seriously aged beauties. Moreover, despite prices cooling from the peaks over USD 600/LDT down to USD 450s/LDT over the last 11 months alone, after weeks of abstaining from the lower levels, both ship owners and cash buyers are finally comfortable / willing to offer vessels back into the market at these now acceptable lower numbers being tabled. While 2025 is gearing up to be a big year from a safe / green recycling regulation stand point, as the Hong Kong Convention is finally set to enter into force and ship recycling yards at all of the major ship recycling destinations will need to be compliant and operate in line with the guidelines of the convention, in order to continue taking in the vast array of vessels that will eventually come available for a recycling sale. India has a majority (if not all) of its ship recycling yards already HKC compliant, and Bangladeshi recyclers are still recovering through their economic meltdown and trying to work towards having most of their yards compliant by June 2025. Pakistan, however, lags far behind with not even a single yard HKC compliant, amidst desperate calls for the upgrade process to now start, in order not to be left too far behind the plate. Finally, Turkey at the far end continues suffering through its fundamentals collapse for over 3 years now.

Overall, as elections will likely come to an end by Q1 2025 in Bangladesh as well, with some stark shifts in regime and power playing out this year, in the USA as well with President Trump winning another 4 years and PM Modi regaining a majority in India in November, the future is certainly a cautionary tale. As supply is expected to gain momentum once the ongoing sanctions are in place and businesses adapt to the post-sanction world once the fallout is known, 2025 may end up being a comparatively resurgent year to 2024, if not besting it.

headline: LACKING TONNAGE!
highlights: Demand good. | Not plain sailing. | Economic woes.
body_text:
Despite India standing in a position to easily take first place on the market rankings on the back of a firming demand, many yards in Alang have partially shut down due to crippling levels of supply and reduction in the overall levels of recycling activity witnessed during the year, for the right vessel(s), the demand from Alang buyers has seen levels being driven into the high USD 400s/LDT and even above, on select, specialist / NF rich units, all in the face of local steel plate prices that remain stranded so far below where local offerings stand today.

Moreover, with an unfavourable election outcome for the pro-business PM Modi, perhaps the biggest shock for the nation this year came from the performance of the Indian Rupee, which saw it lose another 17 basis points, inching its way ever closer to Rs. 85, ending at Rs. 84.96. Of note, the Indian Rupee, like the Bangladeshi Taka, remained volatile throughout the week, even repeatedly spiking briefly to a record Rs. 85.31.

Yet, inflation remains levelled at moderately acceptable levels, leaving the Indian government with an overall optimistic outlook for the near future, especially with the Modi Government garnering additional seats in Congress via a victory in the key state of Maharashtra. This momentum in positivity saw another fixture being concluded to Alang recyclers as the fire damaged / undertow bulker TRUE CONFIDENCE (8,766 LDT) managed to fetch a decent USD 353/Ton with about 650 Tons of IFO and about 180 tons of MGO onboard at the time of arrival.

With the year end approaching rapidly and the festive moods setting across the world, deals might remain fewer than the marginal collective witnessed of late, even though Alang’s local port position remained the busiest in the industry, with only a couple of new arrivals and deliveries reported for the week, and Indian recyclers, with their HKC accreditations in hand, approach Q1 2025 on a better prepared note.

headline: STRUGGLES!
highlights: Falling behind. | Minimal vessels. | Time for action.
body_text:
Pakistan’s struggles continue unabated amidst the nation’s ongoing economic downturn as the shortage of U.S. Dollars has left them not only struggling to negotiate effectively for tonnage at the bidding tables, but they have failed to obtain the necessary funding to arrange for infrastructure upgrade projects at their respective yards, so as to upgrade them and meet the deadline to operate in accordance with the guidelines of the HKC within 2025.

The lack of market sales has corresponded with an empty port position that has remained devoid of any arrivals / deliveries for over 2.5 months now. This is seeing an increasing number of yards and recyclers go quiet over the recent months, as dormancy takes a hold and ongoing operability of the yards once again comes into question.

Whilst still awaiting to clear the queries surrounding the misappropriation of USD 400 Million of previous funding, IMF’s upcoming loan hangs in limbo, as do hopes of this market returning to the bidding tables and that too in form, seems like a fading possibility.

Fundamentals too aren’t dishing out their share of support to the local mindset as not only has the otherwise dormant local steel plate price record a decline to the tune of USD 8/Ton this week, but it has also further put downward pressure on the already disheveled state of local offerings. The Pakistani Rupee too reported minimal movement during the course of the week, as has come to be expected of the nation’s currency.

How will local recyclers manage dip back in and fill plots remains an mystery unto itself, especially as Indian levels continue to firm and domestic pressures push local offerings down, remains to be seen in Q1 2025. For now, let’s hope this market finally starts overhauling facilities once the next tranche of financial aid package gets delivered to the nation, so that Gadani’s’ ship recycling fraternity can fall in line to operate withing the guidelines of the HKC, else the industry risks becoming obsolete.

headline: FROZEN!
body_text:
With the onset of Christmas next week, Turkey seems to have frozen in time with no change reported in import or local steel plate prices, along with local levels or interest in none of the units that are on offer. The Lira however, lost 70 basis points and closed the week at a whopping TRY 35.20 against the U.S. Dollar.

Although news of a recent private sale to one lucky local recycler did make the rounds, it still going to be a grim end to the year for Aliaga.

headline: SLOOOW!
highlights: Year of upheaval. | Volumes low. | Demand return.
body_text:
A truly transformative year for Bangladesh has finally settled in the last two months of this year as end buyers are gradually starting to look toward 2025 with a greater sense of optimism & hope for the country’s ship recycling sector, and the nation overall. After initially resisting the IMF’s assistance, a couple of years ago when the country eventually succumbed to apply for a bailout package, coupled with poor fiscal policies and an oligarchic control of the previous government that resulted in interest rates rising, exports declining, and the government dipping ever deeper into the nation’s reserves to balance out the needs of the populous.

The resulting economic collapse coupled with the implementation of unpopular government plans saw violent outbreaks that saw thousands dead, a Prime Minister flee the country, and weather patterns batter the nation through an incessant monsoon that bought domestic construction projects to a complete halt. However, not all is down the tubes and into the ocean. Bangladesh’s upcoming budget for FY 2025 - 2026 promises greater economic stability and is expected to be about 6.5% higher than the current one. While the budget is concentrating on health and education sectors, notices were surprisingly issued to curtail any major construction projects, at least for the time being.

This is certainly going to hit Chattogram Choppers in the welding torches as the ongoing dithered volume in the trading of ship’s steel has seen demand from Bangladeshi steel mills come to a grinding halt, causing local steel plate prices to collapse in sharp declines throughout the year, to where they have now set the ceiling price for the Bangladeshi ship recycling fraternity. And this week was no different, where steel levels remained dead on the floor at a weakened USD 521/Ton. The collapsing Bangladeshi Taka too has done little to entertain the pricing comfort-zone from this market as the Taka continues to trade at a famished BDT 119.99 against the U.S. Dollar, after briefly spiking to BDT 120.05 mid-week.

The lack of demand of recycled ship’s steel from domestic steel mills continues to hamper demand and the negotiating mindset of local recyclers at the bidding tables, who only welcomed a tiny sub 2K LDT tanker at the nation’s waterfront this week, earmarking the true state of Bangladeshi affairs. As impending sanctions stand to see an influx of wet tonnage from certain regions of the world, most of which will likely end up in India due to L/C values on the large LDT tonnage, but there will be more of those favoured larger LDT dry vessels for recycling sale next year, especially given the performance of the Baltic Dry Exchange of late, and a prolonged absence of juicy units this year on account of consistently impressive freight rates.

As the deadline for compliance with HKC standards gradually nearing and only 4 ship recycling yards in Chattogram have received their NK HKC accreditations, the remaining yards will need to gear up and implement the necessary infrastructure upgrades over the course of this year, as the convention is finally enters into force in 2025.

headline: SEE YOU FOREVER 2024!
highlights: More to be done. | Record low ships. | Price decline. | Further upheaval. | Volatility around.
body_text: 2024 has also marked itself as a year of noteworthy transitions and development across international recycling markets, as a recognition to upgrade facilities and officiate the HKC in the respective Indian sub-continent ship recycling destinations highlights the willingness of these governments to undertake the business of ship recycling, in a broader and internationally accepted standards on safety and environmental safety and 2025 should hopefully see Pakistan and Bangladesh ramp up yard upgrades to HKC standards ahead of its entry into force from the middle of next year. Local steel plate prices have been through the worst of times falling over USD 150/Ton from the highs seen earlier in the year, until the close of this week where both Indian and Pakistani steel plate prices reported further declines whilst Bangladesh and China flatlined this week.

headline: CONSIDERABLE CONSTERNATION!
highlights: Rough year. | Cheap Chinese. | Acceptable levels.
body_text:
Alang, like the rest of the sub-continent ship recycling industry, has endured a tumultuous year of declining prices, economic collapse, political shock, a declining Rupee, and all of it, swimming in a sea of the lowest ship recycling volumes seen in over a decade, resulting in an increasingly Buyers` market that is compelling ship owners and cash buyers to finally accept current day realities on vessel prices. This has increasingly seen Alang’s waterfront get busier over recent weeks, as a healthy chunk of recent introductions into the market seemed to find themselves with navigation charts towards WC India.

Cheap Chinese steel has caused considerable consternation, and the recently renewed alliance of ruling parties India has finally announced upcoming tariffs on incoming steel from China that are expected to range anywhere between 10% - 15%. The imposition of further tariffs would on the one hand, help it compete more effectively with Indian steel thereby driving more business towards Alang’s ship recycling sector. The flip side would not only see Chinese steel demand start to dither, but a possible redistribution of excess and resultingly cheaper inventories may garner further business on the trading front, possibly having a counter-effect on the supply of tonnage for recycling during this time.

Notwithstanding, the steady volatility in steel plate prices have seen levels decline by over USD 150/Ton, bringing down vessel prices by the same amount over the span of 2024. With the sudden new lows of USD 450/Ton being presented on vessels, it has taken some time for the ship owning and cash buying fraternities to finally adjust to the ongoing offerings from ship recyclers and resume negotiations in kind. With tonnage supply set to firm and hungry recyclers worldwide welcoming the potential increase, steel plate price and U.S. Dollar concerns continue to keep local sentiments in check as not only did plate levels drop by a couple of Dollars this week, but even the Rupee ended at a disastrous Rs. 85.40 against the U.S. Dollar.

Local port positions too were left empty this week, with nothing more than deliveries of prior arrivals, and no fresh deliveries this week, resulting in India potentially suffering a possible empty report next week?

Finally, as HKC convention gears up to head into force this year and a majority of yards in Alang already HKC approved, India seems well geared to take on the influx next year.

headline: STRUGGLING WHILE DISINTERESTED!
highlights: Negligible. | Little efforts. | Woefully off.
body_text:
Pakistan, like its subcontinent counterparts, has struggled through a year of economic hardships, a PKR that also collapsed this year, shortage of U.S. Dollars that has practically halted its trading and restricted its availability via lack of available L/Cs for local recyclers who were already being crippled by the ongoing shortage of tonnage and a far more competitive India of late, the nation has struggled through all of 2024 and ending it with the 2nd lowest volume of tonnage recycled over the last decade.

As pending IMF loans and those from Saudi Arabia still hang in the balance, there is little brewing locally to ignite any meaningful discussions with Gadani recycles at the bidding tables, a trend that has been painfully prevalent for a majority of the year and especially Q4 this year, where nearly 3 months of an empty port position highlight the true state of not only Gadani’s ship recycling sector, but even the nation on the whole. And regrettably, this trend is likely expected to continue well into Q1 2025 as economic stability is yet to get back on stable footing.

Fundamentals are doing little to help Gadani ship recyclers especially as the collapse of local steel plate prices continues again for the 2nd week this month and plate fell by another USD 7/Ton down to USD 639/Ton this week, but it was the depreciated Pakistani Rupee that fell 30 basis points to end the week at USD 639/Ton, further ensuring Gadani’s deliberate lack of participation at ongoing tonnage offerings.

Moreover, as Bangladesh and India remain well ahead from Pakistan in terms of demand and pricing, both markets have already made considerable efforts and investments in upgrading their facilities up to HKC standards ahead of its entry into force by mid next year, while Pakistani recyclers are yet to initiate any yard upgrades whatsoever, severely diminishing the ability of local recyclers to prepare for the convention coming into force in the next 6 short months.

As such, questions must be asked surrounding the viability of any serious business for the Gadani ship recycling market, whilst pricing, pending yard infrastructure upgrades, weak fundamentals, and a struggling economy still remain so woefully off the mark.

headline: SILENT YEAR!
body_text:
As week 52 wraps up another year in Aliaga’s ship recycling market, the situation here, like in Aliaga, has been severely affected by its own fundamentals, cheaper steel imports, and a Lira that continues to drop by the week. This week as well, the Lira fell another 23 basis points (surprisingly lower than Pakistan’s), to end the week at TRY 35.30 against the U.S. Dollar.

With bare minimal tonnage offerings, weak import and local steel plate prices, as well as a Lira that has shown no mercy to its citizens, Aliaga, like Gadani, is expected to spend Q1 2025 in a rather dishevelled state.

highlights: Uncharacteristic. | Taka record. | IMF experiment.
body_text:
Although 2024 delivered an uncharacteristically muted year and especially Q4 in Chattogram, any real momentum has failed to take hold under the interim government since July 2024 when the rioting first broke out, resulting in a highly volatile and tumultuous end to the year for the entire nation, which then saw the abdication of former PM Sheikh Hasina, and a disastrous and costly flooding that set the country back economically a great deal, whilst the state of fundamentals continues to hammer away at the purchasing mindset of Chattogram Choppers at the bidding tables. While demand for the right units at the right price and backed by the ability to obtain financing does prevail, these hurdles aside, levels perhaps remain lower than hoped for and a return to prices closer to the elusive USD 500/Ton mark remains out of reach of the #1 market in the world.

And as stated earlier, Bangladesh’s economy has been the prime mover behind the ongoing see- saw in performance at the ship recycling end. To start, the U.S. Dollar suffered an intentionally calamitous decline in the middle of 2024 that saw the Taka teetering in the high BDT 119s against the U.S. Dollar for the rest of the year. And this week was the one to re-write the history books as the Taka spiked to a record BDT 121.90, before retreating and winding the week down at BDT 120.01. Local steel plate prices too have added another mountain to trudge as they have not only remained dead on the floor for months on end (including this week), but they have also only recorded movements that have been on a consistently downward trajectory resulting in levels remaining stagnated at a USD 521/Ton, crippling the ability of local recyclers to offer on vessels approaching the coveted USD 5XX/Ton.

Q1 of 2025 isn’t forecasted to offer as much hope as expected by the nation’s leading economists as they fear that political agendas now seem to occupy much of the ongoing reform efforts that could see a muted start to, if not all of the 2025. Even Bangladesh’s loan experiment with the IMF that eventually saw the drastic and intentional depreciation of the Taka has done more to harm the Bangladeshi economy under the prior administration’s oligarchic collaborations, as the current administration is still trying to curtail and keep domestic inflation in check, while simultaneously attempting to make arrangements on alternative bailout packages and help ease the nation’s precipitating instability.

Notwithstanding the unfolding efforts of local recyclers, at least one sale managed to conclude into Bangladesh as bulker THREE STAR (7,626 LDT) found a spot on Chattogram’s beaches in the immediate future. Yet, Chattogram’s waterfront continues to take a beating as there have been no new arrivals this week and the only thing not earmarking Bangladesh’s first empty port report for 2025 is last week’s arrival that is still idling at anchorage awaiting her turn on the next tide. 2025 isn’t off to the best of starts.

headline: NEW YEAR, NEW CHEER!
highlights: Cautious optimism. | VLCCs sold. | HKC progress. | Price cool. | Supply increase.
body_text: Meanwhile, and as reported in prior editions, news of several large LDT wet units (including those with questionable / sanctioned backgrounds) were seen making the rounds on the back of which, several VLCCs are reported to have been concluded over preceding week, to the few financially capable recyclers in both India and Bangladesh. Although there is a significant disparity in pricing a +40K LDT asset that requires greater financing and ability to endure the fluctuations of the market over longer cutting periods, when compared to the smaller sub-4K LDT units that have been the primary diet through 2024 as stricter L/C and banking limits on larger U.S. Dollar value transactions have become notably tighter to obtain over these last few years. This has exacerbated the crippling effect that recyclers have faced whilst looking to transact and has seen otherwise busy port positions remain drastically empty or with bare minimum units, as further highlighted this week.

headline: BARGAIN BANGERS!
highlights: Low on volumes. | Taking advantage. | Tariffs on steel.
body_text:
Despite being the most aggressive of all ship recycling destinations at the start of 2025, Alang recyclers continue to seek bargains on the marginally few vessels that have been proposed for sale over the festive period - and logically so. As is the case with Bangladesh, Indian fundamentals have suffered in kind as not only did Indian plate prices suffer catastrophic declines across 2024 resulting in the lowest steel prices in the Indian sub-continent, but they also suffered another marginal trip this week, declining another USD 1/Ton and end the week at USD 460.64/Ton. Yet, it was the Indian Rupee that stole the championship for the worst performance as not only did it breach a record Rs. 86 against the U.S. Dollar, it re-adjusted itself by the time the week ended, closing it out at another record Rs. 85.77.

While the naturally nervy mindset of local recyclers has certainly taken a hit over these key declines, the overall pervading optimism towards the nation’s economic reform via India’s upcoming budget for FY 2025 – 2026 that is due on February 1, 2025, remains omnipresent, especially as the business- driven PM Modi’s ruling party gained further seats in the Parliament via India’s regional elections that were concluded in November 2024, further helping Alang recyclers maintain local pricing elevated at or even above local steel plate prices, gradually clawing at Bangladesh’s offer margins.

Economically, the much larger nation has financially outperformed its ship recycling competitors via a consistent performance at the waterfront and ongoing offerings at the bidding tables despite the calamitous state of 2024, which only speaks volumes of the ability of this market to sustain itself no matter what the unfolding situation(s). Alang recyclers have also been able to take advantage on HKC only tonnage and specialist units that have been introduced for ship recycling throughout 2024 and even this week, where tanker RIALTO (9,711 LDT) and another private container was sold to Indian buyers for HKC only recycling. Alang’s port position has also gotten a larger boost than all of its competitors as another 3 vessel / 18K LDT arrived the nation’s waterfront this week.

Overall, despite levels remaining disappointingly lower than expected, ship owners & cash buyers are finally coming to terms with the pervading reality of recycling and India remains the market to go to for consistent and reliable performance. Moreover, as tougher tariffs have been announced on the deluge of comparatively cheaper Chinese steel that has been dumped into the local market at damaging levels below that of existing steel inventories through much of 2024, these tariffs should see further optimism from local buyers at the bidding tables and ongoing activity at Alang’s waterfront, especially if the upcoming budget addresses key areas of economic growth and further help move ship recycling prices further ahead in 2025.

headline: FLICKERS OF LIFE?
highlights: Demand returning. | No sales yet. | Big year ahead?
body_text:
Even though there were flickers of life in the Pakistani market at long last this week and several larger LDT units, including VLCCs, were reportedly proposed for a recycling sale towards the end of December 2024 into Gadani, these proposals have yet to translate into any finalized deals as yet and it does seem as though Gadani buyers are finally making a reasonable attempt at the bidding tables with the turn of the year! Like the rest of the world, exacerbating economic fractures coupled with a torrid devaluing of the Pakistani Rupee to its current state has also seen with it, local steel plate prices gradually slip from the highs of USD 765/Ton to a destitute USD 659.37 (yet highest in the industry) where it ended the week this week. Even the collapsed to a reasonable level PKR fell another 15 basis points against the U.S. Dollar, down to PKR 278.60.

The collapsed state of domestic U.S. Dollar reserves is a great part of the equation that is translating into the ongoing performance of Gadani ship recyclers throughout all of 2024, where local port position eventually ended the 3rd straight month and the year at large, on an empty note. While a pending IMF loan subject to the conclusion of incomplete investigations hangs in the balance, the surprise announcement of the World Bank granting a USD 2 Billion loan package to the Pakistan came to light this week, which should in tur, alleviate short term financing stresses for the various non-critical domestic sectors including ship recycling, where the government has maintained current restrictions on the issuance of U.S. Dollars for domestic consumption via the issuance of large value L/Cs for Gadani’s ship recycling community.

Should the above materialize positively for Pakistan, it will also end up being a big year for Gadani as the pending and urgent need to desperately upgrade Pakistani ship recycling facilities to HKC approved standards and moreover, vetted by IACS societies for approval, may suddenly inject new life into this failing sector. This should help the Gadani gang not only be more competitive at the bidding tables in the near future once the funds have hit, but the overall business of ship recycling should be able to resume normally under the guidelines of the HKC once facilities get accredited in time.

Certainly, looks like Pakistani ship recycler have a lot of work cut out for them in the near future and should all of the above come optimistically to fruition, 2025 might just turn out to be one of the biggest years on record for the Gadani’s ship recycling sector.

headline: TRAILER!
body_text:
With the new year now in tow, January has started off just as tired as 2024 ended for Aliaga’s ship recycling sector, with little to no movement reported on local and imported steel prices. However, it was the Turkish Lira that continues to take centre stage with another reported 38 basis point drop against the U.S. Dollar, wrapping up the week at TRY 35.65.

Aliaga has been so quiet that there has barely been any movements from local recyclers at the bidding tables, resulting in levels remaining paralyzed for another week despite the collapsing Lira. Tonnage supply, which stands to increase globally through 2025 might just provide the parachute this market needs. For now, however, the matter remains very much in status quo as Turkey continues to trail the ship recycling world in currency declines, minimal activity with its weakened offerings, and a sub-continent market that is gearing to go.

headline: VAT WOES
highlights: Cooling. | Unexpected hike. | Falling. | Exuberance.
body_text:
As Bangladesh continues to battle economic uncertainty after one of the worst years in the nation’s history, the situation doesn’t seem to be getting any better as government reserves continue to deplete amidst a dithering recovery under a temporary government that doesn’t seem to have gotten their administrative gears in mesh just yet, as the economy continues to lose traction through its unfolding inflationary disaster. In ongoing attempts to correct this trajectory, the government unexpectedly announced that the National Board of Revenue would be planning a rate hike in the VAT by the middle of the fiscal year, despite widespread concerns that this move will stoke inflation even more and further degrade economic activities – something that could see domestic steel transactions, ship recycling prices, and overall demand from this market start to retreat even more. On the one hand, although the rationale behind such an action is to assist with the interest repayments on the IMF’s upcoming remittances, on the other, yard upgrades, vessel negotiations, and everything near and far related to even affecting the price of steel, will be greatly diminished.

And as the possibility of lower offers on future vessels seems well within the limit of a few weeks from now and the negative sentiment continues to permeate, Bangladesh could soon slip past India and end up closer to Pakistani levels, which themselves are roiled in a similar situation. Yet, Bangladesh somehow seems to be worse off, as key economic factors affecting an imminent return to a recovery path also need to address (at the very least), prevailing political instability, banking sector instability, elevated (and likely to rise again) inflation, high interest rates (especially for local businesses), and the mother of all worries, the seemingly uncontrollable exchange rate volatility.

And still certifying the latter is the ongoing performance of the Bangladeshi Taka that has, for the last 2+ quarters, suffered at the hands of the U.S. Dollar as it ends the week nearly 1% weaker and at a comparatively weaker BDT 120.96, despite having nearly breached BDT 122 once again. Local steel plate prices seem to be the only anchor keeping ship recycler sentiments in check, as despite being flatlined yet again, they remain suspended at a comparatively healthier USD 529.41/Ton. And although this has helped maintain local sentiments steady enough to the where current vessel offers are still the highest in the industry, it has certainly helped bring in another 2 small tankers with a total weight of just about 6.5K LDT at Chattogram’s anchorage. Just how will Biden’s COSCO sanction affect the general inflow of future wet units into Bangladesh, remains to be seen. For now, Chattogram Choppers have managed to avoid a Gadani-gate of an empty port report.

Overall, despite retaining pole position on the market rankings, the Bangladeshi market seems to cool a shade this week, even though a decent number of local sales (reportedly including a VLCC) and several unsold vessels are still trying to find their respective final resting grounds before the customary Chinese New Year slowdown drives things to a screeching halt. And those ship owners and excited cash buyers who were banking on a post-2024 Bangladesh at levels firmer than those currently unraveling, are having their expectations at the bidding tables continue to take a beating, especially as over-aggressive cash buyers with unsold vessels bought at higher rates are now starting to suffer and pay the price for their exuberance.

headline: 2024 STUCK!
highlights: Rupee deterrant. | Tariffs due. | Stuck in 450s.
body_text:
Like Bangladesh, the Indian market continues to strut through an unexpected January 2025 with the poor performance of the Indian Rupee that continues to fluctuate against the strengthening U.S. Dollar and has remained as the primary deterrent keeping Alang recyclers from improving their prices over the last fortnight or so. Especially as it blew industry players expectations out of the water and ended the week at levels approaching Rs. 86.20 – adding another (yet solid) excuse that recyclers have on their itemized list of justifications to present behind their lower offers, despite varying degrees of economically positive news that continue to enter the market.

At the ship recycling outset and unlike Bangladesh and Pakistan, India’s foreign reserves greatly exceed them, which cements India’s ability to not only offer a stable interest rate to domestic recyclers, but also a steady inflow of U.S. Dollars and L/Cs that has already helped nearly all Alang ship yards up to mark for the upcoming HKC rules by the middle of the year, and helped Alang become a destination of less economic concern for incoming deliveries via fewer renegotiations at the waterfront.

And speaking of, just like Chattogram, Alang has not marked an empty port report through all of 2024 and even so far in 2025, where this week, 6 vessels and nearly 58K LDT lies idling or delivered to their respective owners. This tonnage will certainly keep trade with domestic steel mills active, which have been the only ones registering any movements in the sub-continent over recent weeks, ending the week on a downward trajectory and a Rupee short, at USD 459.94/Ton. And although the expectation is that the tariffs intended to curtail the import of damagingly cheaper Chinese steel that continues to collapse week after week causing continued and tremendous pain to steel markets in both India and Pakistan last year (when it consistently undercut local steel inventories), the ongoing dither in Chinese plate levels doesn’t look like it’s done with the Indian sub-continent steel markets just yet.

Whether the ongoing declines in Chinese steel eventually trickle down to the sub-continent markets, remains to be seen.

For now, however, despite the otherwise (and comparatively) strong state of the India economy, vessel prices aren’t displaying any positive signs or movements and perhaps, won’t do so any time soon as they currently lie stubbornly stuck in the mid USD 450s/LDT on most dry vessels, of which, Alang recyclers seem destined to be getting more of. Moreover, with the budget just a fortnight away and expectations of positive news running high, India remains the go to place for all types of tonnages, including those that require SoC certified HKC recycling yards as a final destination.

headline: ECONOMIC FRACTURES!
highlights: Slow moves. | Reluctant to invest. | Stay relevant?
body_text:
Worse of than Bangladesh is the Pakistani market where in addition to having crippling effects on its economy with inflation still high, a near and total lack of available L/Cs has essentially bought the nation’s ship recycling sector to a complete halt for the last 4 months, as Gadani’s anchorage presents another empty position yet again this week. And although Gadani recyclers have been bobbing their heads above the waterline to check the prevailing recycling weather of late, this sector has, for the most part since the advent of Q4 2024, remained underwater.

The fractured state of the nation economy is the key driver behind Pakistan’s ongoing financial distresses. With loans lying in the balance of pending investigations, domestic economists predicting return of inflation into double digits, and the World Bank’s promised aid that is still hanging in the balance as reported in last week’s edition of the GMS WEEKLY, the Gadani gang seem to all be preparing for the upcoming feast, with meals yet waiting to thaw.

As a result of the indecisiveness and the government curtailing the issuance of large U.S. Dollar value L/Cs on non-essential domestic expenses, large Dollar value transactions out of the country have all but halted leaving the Pakistani Rupee as one of the most stable ship recycling nation currencies of all, across 2024. On the back of minimal fluctuations within a PKR 2 limit where it fluctuated and eventually ended every week in 2024, including this week one, where it wound up 35 basis points weaker, at PKR 278.32. Even the lack of domestic trade in ship’s steel has left Pakistani plate prices stranded at the (comparatively) healthiest level of USD 639.37/Ton in the ship recycling industry.

Even if offers / indications seem to be improving ever so slowly in Pakistan (at a snail’s pace and fraught with confusion / nerves), Gadani ship recyclers stand to face another herculean challenge post-June 2025 once the HKC comes into effect, unless they initiate upgrading their yards in time. Given the ongoing reluctancy on part of Gadani recyclers to expend finances and efforts on their yards, which themselves have hardly seen any ships being delivered over the last couple of years and as a result, (likely) see these upgrades as an unwarranted (at this time) and unworthy of investment / upgrades.

Nevertheless, if buyers in Pakistan can display a touch more courage, confidence, and most importantly, stability at the time of taking deliveries of incoming units, perhaps only then can they secure some of the market / private tonnage before the HKC cutoff mid-year and continue to do so thereafter, helping the nation stay relevant in the ship recycling game in the years ahead. Adding hope for the future was this week’s additional announcement that the United Arab Emirates (UAE) would rollover a parked USD 2 Billion, further assisting the Pakistani government maintain their level of U.S. Dollar reserves and providing a silver-lining to the otherwise ailing economy. Q1 looks like it is gearing up to be a tricky January for the country, just like its Indian sub-continent counterparts.

headline: JOLLY!
body_text:
As week 2 of 2025 wraps up in Turkey, they seem to be jolly, celebrating an over-extended Christmas break with virtually nothing to report on local offerings, local deliveries, movements in local and import steel prices, except for the Turkish Lira, which seems determined to head on its pilgrimage of obscurity, as it records another 23 basis point reduction that saw it close the week scratching TRY 34.45 against the U.S. Dollar.

With freight rates set to climb again, the Dollar continually devaluing, and no change in vessel prices to offset the ongoing declines clearly indicates the “on holiday” mode of Aliaga Buyers given that there have been no local fixtures of late, in order to button down where levels truly stand today.

headline: BAGGING BULK!
highlights: VAT reversals. | Panamax influx. | Rates collapse. | Continually controlled.
body_text:
Economic miseries in Bangladesh continue as the nation suffers through ongoing financial fractures that are taking longer than usual to heal. To start with, for Chattogram’s ship recycling sector, local steel plate prices have managed to cement themselves at USD 529.41/Ton for several weeks now, despite competing neighbors (including China’s) steel plate prices reported improvements this week. However, it is the Bangladeshi Taka that remains the true star of domestic misery, not only for the Bangladeshi government, but also for Chattogram Choppers who remain battling higher lending rates and a domestic currency that continues to collapse against the U.S. Dollar, recording another whopping 1.22% decline through the course of the week, ending it past BDT 121.65.

Making matters worse was the announcement by the National Board of Revenue on a reported VAT increase in the middle of the fiscal year that saw strong protests led against the government, which then led them to revise VAT rates for certain sectors, in the latest show of indecisiveness an the interim administration that continues to haphazardly manage the nation’s economic needs. Indeed, domestic unrest seems to be on the rise once again after the previous violent insurgency saw former PM Sheikh Hasina flee the nation. Now, the interim government is failing to achieve anything of substance in order to stimulate the economy via pending infrastructure projects that remain on hold due to the lack of dithered domestic reserves – at least until the upcoming FY 2025 – 2026 budget is announced in the second quarter of this year. In the interim, this likely won’t afford the necessary funding to the remaining ship recyclers who are looking to upgrade their yards and satisfy the incoming HKC regulations, which go into effect around the same time.

Meanwhile, as the supply of tonnage – particularly Panamax bulkers and LNGs - have increased since the start of the year, two sales were confirmed to Bangladeshi recyclers this week and at levels even lower than those from last, as the new realities on pricing now start to show. This doesn’t even include at least 4 - 5 other previous private deals (including the private sale of a VLCC). As such, this week’s fixtures started off with Chinese Sellers fixing OCEAN PEACE (10,847 LDT) at USD 455/LT LDT, before the next lower priced sale of the RONG YUAN (9,165 LDT) took place, only managing to fetch USD 450/LT LDT, as increasing regional sellers look to offload units before Chinese New Year holidays ensue.

Consequently, local port position avoided an empty port report for a second time with a healthy dose of arrival in excess of 48K LDT, most of them promptly delivered to their respective recyclers without much fanfare and despite a falling market. As the nation desperately awaits financial aid, outgoing IMF interest repayments stand to take a massive bite out of the proceeds, in effect, keeping the re-distribution of funds at continually controlled rates, likely maintaining the status quo into February.

headline: TUMBLING DICE!
highlights: Worrying reversals. | Depreciation pie. | Supply drive. | Bangla decline. | Looking bleak.
body_text: Yet, along with the jilted state of global economies, ship recycling destinations suffered worrying reversals in vessel prices of late, primarily on the back of weaker currencies, depressed sentiments, and overall declining steel plate prices which, for the first time in a long time, firmed across the board except in Turkey and Bangladesh (who still remains atop the market rankings). As the supply of vessels starts to increase after 2024 was awarded the lowest year for recycling volumes in over a decade, the exit of overaged vessels from operating fleets has been consistently delayed due to the incredible performance of freight markets through the first 3 Quarters of 2024. Given that most of these units are likely starting to come off charter with the turn of the year, a raft of 90s built drybulk (mostly Panamax) vessels were suddenly up for sale at the same time, primarily from Chinese ship owners looking to tie up pre–Chinese New Year holiday loose ends, and this increase in supply has set a damaging pressure on the sub-continent markets, as demand has remained forcibly in check via the collapsing state of fundamentals. As such, vessel offers are starting to get shaky once again. Bangladesh has been the hardest hit this year, with up to USD 30/LDT wiped off vessel prices over a couple of weeks. And those recyclers who were keen to negotiate and fill dormant plots are now pleasantly booked with cheaper tonnage for the near future. Whilst the supply of vessels has largely been vintage bulkers and even a few LNGs were seen, tankers and containers remain at large and are likely to come at scattered stages across the year. The question of what to do with the raft of elderly / eventually dissolute tankers on Biden’s recent sanctions lists when they eventually show up for sale, remain to be seen. For now, the overall ship recycling outlook looks uncertain once again, especially as ship owners consistently look to achieve the next highest priced sale and ever exuberant cash buyers remain eager to please, driving prices up rather than enjoying the present.

headline: SHADOWBOXING!
highlights: Not ‘at it’. | Sentiments beaten. | Dancing with fragility.
body_text:
Even though Alang buyers have been the keenest of the sub-continent ship recycling bunch at the bidding tables of late, they have been far from ‘at it’ as Alang recyclers have lost out on the bulk of the market tonnage that has been coming in from the Far East, to a geographically better-suited Chattogram, whilst vessel offers from both locations have been retreating on the back of shuttered fundamentals. This has seen Alang sentiments taking a beating this week, despite positive news on tariffs set to finally tax cheaper imported Chinese steel and it is certainly concerning to see such a decline amidst a growing number of vessels being proposed for a recycling sale.

Confidence in fundamentals seems to be at an all-time low amongst Alang recyclers and this does not bode well for India’s shipping recycling sector or the shipping industry at large, especially as an anticipatedly busier 2025 lies ahead, Pakistan still looking to get back into the picture after an extensive period on the sidelines spanning over 4 months now, and both Pakistani and Bangladeshi ship recycling yards needing to get their HKC compliance (infrastructure and yard) upgrades to initiate within January, leaving India uniquely positioned to reclaim pole position and maintain it well into 2026. This is of course unless China amends it ongoing policy and opens up domestic ship recycling for international units once again, redistributing the flow of global recycling tonnage.

For now, however, amidst Indian fundamentals that have certainly seen the better part of south (on local steel plate prices), remain precariously positioned under the present circumstances as not only is the U.S. Dollar hammering the Indian Rupee, which saw it close the week out nearly 50 basis points weaker at INR 86.56, but local steel plate prices are the ones dancing with the fragility of Alang recycler mindsets as steel prices shook violently through the week, closing it out at about the same levels as those from last, albeit marginally higher and in line with international movements.

Yet, compared to its global ship recycling neighbors, India’s economy remains one of the strongest and its primary concerns, unlike its competing ship recycling neighbors, remain the effects of global economies and not internal instabilities, which only cements its standing as the most dependable of ship recycling destinations. Furthermore, helping this market is India’s upcoming budget scheduled on February 1st, where the government is expected to lower import taxes for certain sectors, and this could have a direct or even trickledown effect on the profitability of Alang’s ship recycling yards ahead. Finally, given the fact that all ship recycling yards in Alang are already operating in line with the rules of the HKC and no real upgrades to local facilities are needed, India may inadvertently become the prime mover behind global ship recycling tonnage from Q3 2025.

For now, however, with the way things are going, Alang recyclers seem destined to face competitive struggles to have it all their own way in 2025, especially until the start of Chine New Year holiday and especially once Pakistani recyclers start fixing units once again.

headline: ACTION – MISSING!
highlights: More enquiries. | Chinese sales. | HKC upgrades needed.
body_text:
January has certainly not welcomed Gadani’s ship recycling sector with the improvement in the domestic economy that anyone in the industry was anticipating thus far. The PKR lies in shambles, local steel plate prices in contrast, remain the highest in the industry, yet Pakistani offers on the bidding tables have been at the bottom of the sub-continent market rankings for over 4 months now, reflecting a similar situation at Gadani’s waterfront as recyclers have failed to conclude / import even a single vessel into the nation during this time. And as stated, the economy that has led to the unfolding state of key fundamentals has been driving the flaccid state of interest from the Gadani Gang.

To start, local steel plate prices have not only reported a surprising improvement to the tune of nearly USD 7/Ton this week, but they also closed the week out at nearly USD 644/Ton. Yet, the PKR was ironically the only recycling nation currency to register an improvement of 35 basis points and close the week out at PKR 278.66 against the U.S. Dollar.

Yet, Pakistan’s overall economic situation remains in the dumps as the government is still heavily in debt (with the IMF), is in the process of obtaining fresh loans to the tune of USD 20 Billion (pledged by the world Bank), have only recently obtained an extension on parked amounts (from UAE), and are still in the process of clarifying queries to the tune of about USD 440 Million that were seemingly misappropriated, it remains in a precarious situation for the nation at this time. All of the above has led to a collapsing of key fundamentals that has driven the domestic ship recycling sector to a grinding halt.

Notwithstanding the above, Pakistani recyclers have been slowly (and agonizingly) trying to make a return to the bidding tables of late, with a seemingly greater volume of enquiries emerging even though very little has realized in terms of a confirmed deal that would back up recent spate of enquiries. Moreover, despite vessel offers having declined from Chattogram over the course of the week leaving Pakistan (and India) more competitive, it is the long term future Gadani recyclers need to focus on and urgently start upgrading their facilities to comply with the requirements of HKC, in order to stay relevant, or invite self-irrelevance at the international level altogether, given that the Convention officially enters into force by the middle of the year.

Meanwhile, there remains no news about the state of Pakistan’s FY 2025 – 2026 budget and this could put a serious strain on the ability of the local recyclers to shore up the necessary funding in order to put in necessary infrastructure upgrades needed at this time. As such, Pakistan’s ship recycling community certainly has an uphill challenge for themselves in 2025.

headline: JILTED!
body_text:
Just like Gadani, Aliaga seems to have been jilted by the global economies as this is the only market to consistently record single and dual fundamental collapses with each passing week, including this one where not only did both import and local stee plate prices report declines of about USD 10/MT, but the ever consistent Lira drop continues into the abyss of uncertainty, taking the entire market down with it as it wraps up the week at USD 35.45 against the U.S. Dollar.

Impressively, and surprisingly yet, local offerings have still not dipped below those stated in the market rankings, indicating that no tonnage has even been offered into the Aliaga thus far, where local pundits are able to establish where current prices really stand.

Mercifully for Aliaga recyclers, given that a majority of their recycling facilities are already operating in accordance with EUSRR requirements, the upcoming HKC implementation by the middle of the year should likely be nothing more than a resubmission of documents to confirm ongoing yard operations. Yet, with supply increasing in the sub-continent, vessel owners with units intended for Turkey are still looking at the price differential with the sub-continent on their upcoming units, especially now that larger LDT tonnage is starting to make the rounds at the bidding table.

headline: SHAKY...WHEN STEADY!
highlights: Bangla focus. | Pun intended. | Action over extension. | Expensive and unsold
body_text:
The market leaders (in terms of vessel pricing) also seem to be engorging on a diet of tonnage that is not only of Far Eastern ownership, but one that is also geographically located in the same region as the nation’s ship recycling waterfront reported an impressively loaded destination this week, with over 61K LDT via just 6 ships is at Chattogram’s anchorage. This performance has certainly raised eyebrows given how shaky the nation’s fundamentals remain at this time as not only is the Bangladeshi Taka demolishing records week after week, even ending this one 26 basis points lower and a nose hair shy at BDT 121.99 against the U.S. Dollar, but it was local steel plate prices that although have been dead on the floor at BDT 529.41 / Ton for several weeks and have invariably assisted Bangladeshi ship recyclers maintain the level of their vessel offerings during this time, this is in fact, displaying a deeper and more metastasized state of domestic affairs as steel trade between domestic ship recycling yards and local steel mills is reportedly at a virtual standstill, and it has only been a few weeks that a majority tonnage deprived Chattogram Choppers are now taking deliveries of a batch of vessels and hopefully keep trade of domestic steel rolling (pun intended).

Yet, the stalling of local infrastructure projects, some of which are reportedly bloated in value while others deemed unnecessary altogether and are being re-investigated by the interim government in greater detail, an action that will further delay the nation’s economic revival. As pending loans from internationals States and financial bodies remains hanging in the balance and the economy once against displays signs of slowing, local economists are fearing a negative growth through 2025 as a result of their economic spiral. Meanwhile, in order to stay abreast of the competition and keep the domestic ship recycling industry alive, the Bangladeshi Ministry amped up the pressure on domestic ship recyclers to initiate respective yard upgrades, in order to be prepared for the upcoming HKC deadline by the middle of the year, thereby revoking the ability of those recyclers who have failed to initiate yard upgrades by January 31st, from obtaining No Objection Certificates (NOCs) that would disbar their recycling vessel(s), entry into territorial waters for completion of a recycling delivery. Whilst the initial deadline of December 31st, 2024, was extended to January 31st, 2025, on the back of the BSBRA requesting the Ministry for an extension, the government is now reportedly digging their heels in and demanding action over extension.

Notwithstanding, Bangladesh has remained the focus of much of the sub-continent’s ship recycling activity over the previous week even as local offerings are gradually coming in line with their sub- continent competitors. And it is usually is geographically appropriate units that have been coming in for a recycling sale from the Far east of late and have been shifting the balance of where these units eventually end up. As Panamax bulkers have become the flavor of recent times, LNGs too have been increasingly proposed for a recycling sale, as containers are expected to eventually come down the waterslide later in the year, after a cooling in rates resulting from the re-opening of the Red Sea lanes for regular business in the wake of the Gaza ceasefire has already seen the Baltic Index cool this week. Domestic sentiments and demand, though prevalent and should be driving prices up, are in fact, still on edge as a number of unsold and more expensive, previously acquired units still in cash buyer hands are yet to find firm buying interest from this market.

headline: POWER SHIFT!
highlights: New Order. | Restructuring. | Feeling strain. | Red Sea reopening. | Belly dance.
body_text:
In the meantime, fundamentals continue to remain jittery amidst a likely interest rate cut by the U.S. Feds and the U.S. Dollar continues to shake global ship recycling currencies as some impressive gains against the Dollar were registered while others continue to shatter records, in an Indian sub- continent ship recycling market that continues to feel the strain of an increasing number of candidates for a recycling sale, particularly from Panamax bulkers and now, likely containers in the near future. The imminent easing / reopening of traffic through the Red Sea shipping lanes following the truce in Gaza is likely to be bad news for many container operators who have been raking in 2024s charter highs, and this is certain to eventually see a slew of containers head for recycling after an extraordinary last few years of earnings – although experience tell us that the effects from this should take 3-4 months to filter through to recycling markets, at least with most vessels still on TCs.

Overall, sentiments remain of an eagerness that is shackled by economic uncertainty and despite an increasing supply of tonnage earmarking the present, unraveling indications have simply failed to fuel the expected volume of sales, as disappointed ship owners and cash buyers of expensive inventory reevaluate further moves as the (residual) values on their assets are just not what they were hoping to see in 2025, especially since USD 600/Ton is only a dream from a year ago. Many have been expecting 2025 to gear up to be a busier year than the last two of inertia and inactivity, despite delayed infrastructure developments that remain in the works. As Bangladeshi recyclers now risk NOC bans and prices across sub-continent markets seem unmotivated, it is likely to be just as volatile a year of unpredictable movements / events, which should in turn see prices, sentiment, and demand belly dance week after week.

headline: ON PAR!
highlights: Deals to do. | Rupee depreciation. | Prime movers.
body_text:
Much like the state of the Bangladeshi ship recycling sector with all “get up” and barely any “go”, India remains in a state comparable to its Western counterpart, with fundamentals squeezing local offers down, despite a clear and present demand permeating from the shores of Alang - albeit it at dithered overall levels.

And despite a spate of the recent negotiations at the bidding tables circling around a batch of prospective Bangladeshi candidates that have been opening up in the Far East of late, it was the receding indications on potential units from Alang buyers that saw fewer fixtures into India, as ship owners have barely gotten used to the regular offers well below USD 500/Ton. But to now see fresh indications on units even well below USD 450/Ton (after USD 600/Ton was on these very tables last January) is resulting in ship owners and even cash buyers of recent and expensively acquired units, seemingly holding off until a shade of stability and bounce back in prices is imminent, before a first batch of losses is officially recorded for 2025.

Moreover, unlike their Bangladeshi counterparts, Indian ship recyclers saw a clearly diminished number of arrivals at the nation’s recycling waterfront this week, albeit with one of them driving the total LDT of tonnage at Alang’s port position to well over 51K LDT. But it is the overall diminished number of vessels at Alang’s waterfront that is troublesome, given that Alang is nearly 3 times the size of Chattogram with just 1/3rd the number of vessels at the waterfront in the midst of a tonnage resurgence of late.

Meanwhile, and as stated above, fundamentals have been the prime movers behind Alang’s unfolding sentiments and subsequent vessel offers, in that, despite local steel plate prices registering an improvement in excess of USD 1.50/Ton and clocking the week out at USD 457.71/Ton, these levels remain pinching-ly at, or even above local offers in some cases, resulting in losses right off the bat. While local recyclers have been trying to stay optimistic about the future, especially with India’s budget due for announcement next week, the spate of recent deliveries, lack of interim movement in plates, and the overall dithered state of the Indian Rupee has left much to be desired. Notwithstanding, the Rupee did provide some respite as it recorded a 45-basis point recovery against the U.S. Dollar, winding the week down at Rs. 86.18.

One sale was still concluded with a likely Alang redelivery as the stainless-steel tanker MARTHA OPTION (3,868 LDT) from Indonesian Sellers Waruna, was committed to cash buyers at a firm USD 660/LT LDT basis an ‘as is’ Belawan delivery and about 273 Tons of solid SS316 + 371 Tons of cladded SS on board, contributing to the fantastic price on show.

headline: INCOMPLETE PLATFORM!
highlights: Matter of time. | Fundamentals | unreliable | Trade deficit.
body_text:
Of all of the problems that Pakistan as a nation faces under the present times, perhaps none is as critical as the one that Gadani recyclers will face from July 1st on, once the HKC comes fully into effect by June 30th. As not even a single Gadani ship recycling yard has been ratified to operate in line with the convention thus far (despite some having obtained ISO certificates and proper access to remediation sites), the overall state of domestic ship recycling yards has some catching up to do, not only to compete with regional competitors on future HKC units once the convention is in effect, but also the ability to negotiate on vessels posts June 30th for those ship recyclers who are still not up to the mark with IACS class accreditations as well. This is will certainly curtail a healthy flow of recycling tonnage towards Pakistani waters from Q3 and probably even into Q4. The question remains, what will come of this market same time next year?

For now, Pakistan remains positioned a short ways behind India and unfolding economic affairs in the country leaves the near future for Gadani’s ship recycling community, stranded in despair with nothing optimistic to look forward to, especially as driving fundamentals further compress local ship recycling affairs at a time a marked supply of tonnage has greeted the industry since the start of 2025. As local steel plate prices remain stranded at USD 643.78 / Ton, inadvertently offering the illusion of stability to vessel prices that are realistically much lower, nothing has changed with the Pakistani Rupee either, as it continues to trampoline its way between PKR 277 and PKR 279 against the U.S. Dollar, winding down the week a mere 5 basis points stronger at PKR 278.54.

As the economy remains in tatters, reportedly, the nation’s trade deficit with neighboring countries has surged nearly 45% over the last fiscal year, with signs indicating to a similar performance this year as well. Inflation, like in Bangladesh, is unsteady once again and a slowdown in growth through Q1 and perhaps Q2 (or until some much-needed financial aid hits government banks) can be expected from this market.

Overall, like those in the government working towards improving the economy, groundwork at the domestic ship recycling yards should be the interim focus of Gadani ship recyclers as Gadani’s port position is coming up on 4.5 months of an empty report and with nearly all of January now gone and the convention being a mere 5 months away, reality might be the one to eventually put the brakes on and have Pakistan’s port position fade into (temporary / permanent?) obscurity.

headline: WALKS LIKE A DUCK …
body_text:
… quacks like a duck, it’s probably Aliaga’s ship recycling sector as Turkey has virtually disappeared from the bidding tables for well over a year and a half now. And logically so, given that EU regulations and EUSRR requirements mandate local yards to only secure tonnage primarily from EU ports, resulting in a massive slowdown of arrivals at Aliaga’s waterfront. This was further exacerbated by the fact that the ship recycling price differential between Turkey and the sub- continent markets is, at minimum, USD 200/MT. And with most vessels returning towards Asian waters after discharge, has seen global ship recycling tonnage naturally shift towards sub-continent destinations, further isolating an already limping Aliaga.

Turkey’s economy is another vital part of this equation, especially the Lira, as it trudges on down without any control or compunction, plummeting 57 basis points and closing the week at TRY 35.66 against the U.S. Dollar. Steel plate prices too remained shaky as both import and local steel levels reported minor movements during the week.

Overall, Turkey seems destined to be off the market report, unless further movements can be recorded through the year. And if sub-continent markets get HKC compliant by December 2025, the next year doesn’t seem to be setting itself to be any better for Aliaga recyclers either.

headline: BREATHER!
highlights: Chinese break. | Price dive. | Seeking direction. | Accreditations
body_text:
In the wake of Chinese New Year holidays, Chattogram Choppers seem to have gotten a much- needed breather this week as the recent supply of recycling tonnage has mostly been Panamax bulkers from Chinese / Far Eastern owners since the start of the year, coinciding with ongoing offer declines of up to USD 30/Ton on dry units from the few open and capable buyers. As such, it has been difficult to negotiate tonnage into Chattogram of late, especially as most of the tonnage has even been opening in the Far East and has seen Bangladeshi buyers swallow nearly all of the recycling arrivals (in terms of the number of vessels) this week, certainly the most LDT we have seen arrive any waterfront in a while with nearly 105K LDT either idling or already delivered to their new owners. Yet, the nation’s ship recycling waterfront disguises the true state of local affairs as the ongoing economic instability highlighted by a resurgence of political instability, is pushing once again domestic recyclers into a fresh corner of confusion after a year of tonnage scarcity.

As highlighted last week, the timely effectiveness of the interim government seems to remain in question as not only have some domestic infrastructure projects been entirely rescinded, but those in question are being re-evaluated for over-bloated budgeting practices and is back to the drawing board for this sector for the time being. Moreover, steel trade remains abysmal as fears of incoming tariffs coupled with Chinese New Year Holidays have likely been the reason behind the flatlining performance of steel plate prices, with a side of a large hangover of reigning political affairs. On the political end, ousted PM Sheikh Hasina’s crumbled party is reportedly attempting to regroup and calling for renewed activism, whilst college students, who were the drivers behind the ousting of her regime, are reportedly in talks to create a new political party in order to run in the upcoming elections. As this only spells further delays for the nation’s economic recovery for the rest of the year, the present is unfortunately turning into a troublesome time for ship owners and cash buyers who are misreading the tea leaves amidst a time these markets are performing contrary to historical Q1 norms on the back of rare events.

As local steel plate prices remain dead on the floor at USD 529.41/Ton, the Taka made a marked and rather surprising improvement against the U.S. Dollar, to the tune of 21 basis points as the week ended, closing it at BDT 120.59. This consistent volatility and weakening of the Taka across 2024 (and even of late), has seen prices gradually decline from the highs of USD 600/Ton, down to the mid USD 400s/Ton, with unfolding indications of up to USD 30/LDT lower on tabled tonnage. As such, any dry units currently for sale are only seeing USD 450/LDT depending on condition of the vessel and especially, the availability / interest of an open-end buyer given that many recyclers are now booked with tonnage for the near future. Moreover, with the January 31st deadline to obtain NOCs for incoming recycling tonnage now past, the BSBRA has appealed to the Ministry of Affairs for an extension once again, in order to provide recyclers who have initiated infrastructure upgrades on their yards, to receive time beyond the January 31 cut off and get up to HKC standards well prior to entry into force in June of this year, as most yards are still on their way to obtaining a an SoC backed HKC accreditation. Coupled with the extremely shaky state of fundamentals, February maybe a challenging time for Sellers/Cash Buyers with this market.

headline: SLIPPERY AS A SNAKE!
highlights: Frantic start. | Pressure on. | Mostly dry & LNG. | Tariff time. | Tastes like...
body_text: The Baltic Dry Bulk Index also gained ground as rates across the dry bulk categories displayed signs of positivity / improvement this week, which might still be late for a bulk of the already-aged still- trading units that are being compelled to reconsider their immediate futures. Making matters for inflation and global economies were oil futures that are expected to surge and even reported firming this week as levels approached USD 74/barrel once again, and Week 6 is likely setting itself up to be the pivotal point of global Tariff Wars of 2025. This also seems to be affecting the performance of the U.S. Dollar, which although seems to have made minor improvements against most of the major ship recycling nation currencies by the end of the week, actually started to decline across the board early in the week with the uncertainty of the upcoming Tariffs, which even resulted in flattening steel plate prices at all ship recycling nations, except India where expectedly, they declined.
