The emergence of recycling traffic has also seen a remarkable amount of LDT at both India & Bangladesh this week, and this is not only happening amidst declining vessel offers that have cooled by up to USD 30/LDT over the course of January, but also from the few recyclers (in Bangladesh & Pakistan) who are financially secure enough to even be at the tables and drop an offer.

headline: UNCHANGED!
highlights: No change. | Tariff aims. | Geographic advantage.
body_text:
The Indian budget was announced this week without much fanfare for Alang’s ship recycling sector. Moreover, even though the government has dived nose first into improving the lives of the lower and middle classes via massive tax cuts / breaks in this budget, the only indirect effect to Alang’s ship recycling sector was the announcement of a 3-year plan to distribute intended infrastructure projects, a decision which stands to delay any steel recovery that maybe in store for the nation’s immediate ship recycling needs. Meanwhile, despite the threat of incoming tariffs flatlining plates from the major recycling destinations this week, India was the only one to register a decline to the tune of nearly USD 3/Ton, ending the week at USD 455.75/Ton and just barely above prevailing offers on any dry vessels currently making the rounds. Even the Indian Rupee fell drastically through the week, only to make a minor improvement towards the end of the week and still record an overall decline of 20 basis points to close at Rs. 86.33 against the U.S. Dollar.

The weakening state of local offers coupled with the fact the much of the tonnage across recent weeks has emanated from Far Eastern waters thereby completely circumventing any chance for Pakistani / Indian recyclers from even bidding on these units, has eventually resulted in the first week of 2025 where Alang reported only one large-LDT arrival for the week, along with a couple of deliveries of prior arrivals that saw local anchorage LDT balloon to well over 70K LDT this week – a number not seen at the Indian waterfront in some time.

Notwithstanding, the budget did provide a breadth of far-reaching tax cuts and even complete tax breaks for individuals and families ranging from the lower and middle classes, delivering more cash for consumers through FY 2025 – 2026 along with the expectation that private sector infrastructure investments will likely go up, kickstarting demand for steel as well, which would then help 2025 hold a candle to 2024s performance. Yet, the return and unfolding of this performance remains up for grabs as the fine print of the budget is still being digested.

Finally, as little to no infrastructure upgrades are needed for Alang’s ship recycling yards, there isn’t a need for financial loans by local buyers as most yards have already fulfilled their obligations at obtaining their HKC SoC accreditations and are prepared to take on Q3 with the same fervor as Q2.

Overall, as Trump’s tariffs on Chinese steel will inevitably affect sub-continent markets in some way and despite India also placing their own tariffs on Chinese steel imports, an impending excess of globally available Chinese steel could disrupt sub-continent steel and furthermore, vessel prices from India. As India, Pakistan and Bangladesh are all on a virtually level playing field in terms of price, a vessel’s final discharge location a.k.a. geography seems to be the only determinant factor as to where vessels eventually end up.

headline: CLOSE…BUT NO CIGAR!
highlights: Need to do more. | Largely absent. | Demand slow.
body_text:
Despite offers from the Pakistani ship recycling sector lagging not too far behind their Indian counterparts (perhaps Indian offers declining to be more in line with those from Pakistan?), Gadani ship recyclers need to get a lot more serious, not just to conclude deals but even continue to do business post July 1st, 2025.

To start, not only do they need to take stock of the current economic situation within the country and gauge the immediate direction of the winds in the face of tonnage being offered, but to also bear in mind what is also happening with the competition in the near and far terms, so as to strategically start offering (even above market if needed) on the right unit(s) and get the wheels of Pakistan’s ship recycling sector turning once again. Not to mention, as Bangladeshi ship recyclers pursue extensions with their respective Ministries in order to keep Bangladeshi ship recycling yards open for business post January 31, reportedly, neither the Pakistani government nor Pakistani ship recyclers have undertaken any serious measures to initiate infrastructure upgrades on their yards or even have the possibility of completing them in time for when the HKC comes into effect, further laying barriers in the ability of this nation to represent themselves at the ship recycling tables starting Q3, and as it seems the present / cemetery-like appearance of the shores of Gadani that it is now past 4.5 months of missing tonnage arrivals at the water front, is likely to face another terrible year for ship recycling.

Even the Pakistani government needs to do more, not only to assist Gadani buyers by way of more liquidity and financial instruments being made available to Gadani buyers, but also to the nation overall as Pakistan is hemorrhaging through its financial reserves as a handful of incoming financial aid hangs in the balance. The nation’s fundamentals are doing little to assist local ship recyclers as not only did Pakistani Rupee drop 12 basis points against the U.S. Dollar and close the week at PKR 278.44, but local steel plate prices, the highest in the Indian sub-continent, have also remained flat on the floor for months on end and closed the week at USD 643.78/Ton.

Overall, having been largely absent from the buying for the last two years, a greater degree of confidence and certainty is needed locally, in order for the Gadani Gang to get back into the picture with any sense of normality for 2025. And while the demand for finished products remains slow and low, and the possibility of an influx of even cheaper Chinese steel stands to greet February starting from the 4th (once Trump’s Tariff’s kick in), local plate prices will likely decline and lower the intensity of local offerings to one that would only assure more of the same performance and the likely closure of even more recycling yards.

headline: SPLASH!
body_text:
Turkey’s unrelenting collapse in fundamentals and eventual collapse in vessel pricing that has been teasing the industry for so many weeks, finally made a grand splash this week as local offers declined in sync with sub-continent ship recycling markets and to the tune of USD 30/Ton across the board. And while import and local steel plate prices have marginally remained in the same state since last week, the Turkish Lira’s unfinished dive into the abyss continued unabated, closing the week out at TRY 35.71 against the U.S. Dollar.

Notwithstanding, and like the rest of the industry, even though a surprising uptick in the amount of tonnage being proposed to local recyclers has reportedly gone up this week, it is up to already disappointed ship owners to consider another USD 30/Ton officially wiped off Turkish prices as well, further exasperating the price differential with sub-continent markets and making matters that much harder for Turkish Recyclers.

How many of these ship owners will consider repositioning their vessels with further cargo runs that relocate their units suitable for a sub-continent redelivery, remains to be seen. For now, what will be interesting to note is how many ship owners will actually bite the bitter bullet of falling prices once again.

headline: 2024 AGAIN?
highlights: Lower overall. | Taking tonnage. | Far East buyers. | Square distribution
body_text:
The political situation in Bangladesh is starting to deteriorate once again as currently exiled PM Sheikh Hasina delivered a fiery speech from oversees, calling on all her supporters to re-unite the party her father (the founder of the nation) founded decades ago. This led to a massive unfolding of local riots that then saw several residences and government properties associated with her party, torched in the process as protests unfolded across the nation. This instability is further adding to an already deteriorating situation that the country’s economy is currently afflicted by i.e. minimal progress on construction projects, minimal steel movements being reported, very few breakers able or even displaying interest at the bidding tables, and a spate of deliveries to keep those ready and capable buyers, busy with tonnage and away from offering in the foreseeable future.

Speaking of tonnage, Chattogram’s anchorage remains an impressive sigth with 7 ships and nearly 82K LDT either lying in wait at the waterfront or delivered to their respective owners through the course of the week. And while this will certainly help maintain operations and regular business activity at domestic ship recycling yards, including the resale of recycled ship’s steel to domestic steel mills, the level of offerings remain constricted on the back of stranded local steel plate prices that have refused to move from USD 529.41/Ton for about a quarter now. Further suppressing the ability of local offerings to move in a positive direction is the Bangladeshi Taka, which has been hemorrhaging in value since June 2024 including this week, where it ended nearly 0.5% lower than last and at BDT 121.33 against the U.S. Dollar.

Yet, in the growing face of vessels (from Chinese and Far Eastern owners) gradually steaming off charter, SNP activity with local recyclers continues at pace despite ship owners and cash buyers progressively facing ever decreasing levels, and the hottest and most capable local recyclers book their yards with tonnage leaving the next group of available buyers, positioned at notably lower levels. Approximately TEN Panamax Bulk Carriers have so far been committed into the local market since the start of the year and one would expect deals to continue taking place on these vintage 90s built bulk carriers that have been and continue to ease off charter and as time only progresses. Chattogram choppers have also been keen to take on some of the larger units in play i.e. LNGs, VLCCs, FSUs, and surprisingly even a private Capesize bulker, despite rates in this sector starting to firm up once again.

Overall, as Bangladeshi pricing lies just ahead of Indian levels by a whisker and is, as a result, busy taking in much of the Far Eastern tonnage, India and (even) Pakistan have started to take deliveries of their own as an even keel on pricing squarely distributes geographical tonnage across the sub- continent markets. However, with the HKC coming into effect by the middle of the year and the Ministry of Affairs granting an extension on deadline for domestic yards to initiate yard upgrades to March 31st, an act that has merely extended the inevitable for Chattogram choppers, Q3 will be the determinant factor as to where tonnage will eventually end up.

headline: TARIFFS & PRICES!
highlights: Surprise softening. | Surge in supply. | Slimmer at the | Tariffs yet to tell. | Continually
body_text:
As the Baltic Exchange’s Dry Index reported dry bulk rates stabilizing across January 2025 and even start to climb across the last couple of weeks, the inflow of recycling tonnage at the bidding tables has continued unabated even in the face of declining offers. Even oil prices remain volatile as they close the week out at USD 71/barrel amidst further fears of rising fuel and energy prices and President Trump furthering President Bidens recent sanctions on both Russian and Chinese energy / dark fleets, via a fresh set of sanctions on Iranian tankers and those trading oil with Iran. As global economies react to the unfolding present, the U.S. Dollar continues to dominate the currency race as it registers noteworthy improvements across the ship recycling board, sadly hitting India the hardest this week, given that India is the most viable option for units sailing East out of the Red Sea.

This weakening in ship recycling nation currencies as well flatlining / declining steel plate prices have seen vessel offers continually cooling across the sub-continent markets, which remains no surprise given that the true nature of unfolding reality is yet to fully settle in and be felt, as levels of up to USD 30/LDT across the board were wiped out at a time that is a traditionally stronger period for global ship recycling markets ‘pre’ and now, ‘post’ Chinese New Year, as Chinese / Far Eastern owners are generally the most active in selling their overaged candidates including this year, where dry bulk / Panamax units have also been the flavor of late. While tanker rates continue to soar and owners globally re-positioning their units on the back of rising rates / sanctions, 2025 might be the year of the missing tankers despite a few wet sanctioned units making the recycling rounds. Even as a raft of LNG sales from the Korean market saw several respective units from this sector hit the beach, supply is expected to remain strong for the upcoming quarter(s) and perhaps, even the remainder of the year, all at a time tariffs on Chinese products - including steel – are due to take effect and where this excess and increasingly cheaper steel ends up, could spell disaster for the ship -recycling markets and vessel prices. As riots and violence re-erupts across much of Bangladesh, India’s budget ending up a miss, Pakistan still seeks funding, and Turkey dissolves in the West, post-Chinese New Year state of affairs is keeping the wheels of ship recycling turning, albeit at expectedly lower levels and a persistent demand from all markets.

headline: FIRMLY ROOTED!
highlights: Not improving. | Rupee struggles. | Sanction questions.
body_text:
Despite being the only ship recycling destination to consistently face the wrath of unending volatility in domestic fundamentals (including this week), Alang recyclers have managed to stay towards to the top of the marking rankings since 2024 and even managed to conclude their fair share of tonnage introduced into the markets since the start of the year, despite their firmly rooted offers in the mid USD 400s/LDT that continue to face immense downward pressures and are, as a result, displaying an ongoing reluctance to improve.

Speaking of fundamentals, not only have local steel plate prices been the only ones to consistently register declines whilst some competing neighbors have remained paralyzed by flatlines for months on end, but like the Bangladeshi Taka, the Indian Rupee has also seen its share of declines over the last couple of quarters as it registered the largest ship recycling destination currency decline of the week at nearly 1.6% against the U.S. Dollar, ending it at a historical record of Rs. 87.71.

With the exchange rate now starting to bite down harder, salted in with a less than appreciable FY 2025 - 2026 budget (for Alang’s ship recycling sector), any form of domestic recovery in the domestic economy, the Rupee, or even local steel plate prices seems destined for delays, especially now that pending Trump Tariffs on Chinese products and the possibility of even cheaper Chinese steel coming into the markets in the near future, stands in the way of making any serious recovery in prices through Q1 and even Q2, an improbability.

As reported in last week’s report, ship owners and overly optimistic cash buyers only stand to face the wrath of ongoing market movements as unfolding affairs are doing little to achieve breakeven figures on some of the prior expensive fixtures. Yet, fixtures have continued as Alang recyclers have managed to squirrel away another 6 ships and nearly 75K LDT, a healthy number at Alang given that India’s ship recycling waterfront nearly faced the indignity of an empty anchorage at least twice over the last two Quarters. Of note, included in this week’s arrivals was even a rare passenger vessel, the likes of which have primarily been a Turkish flavor since 2023.

From the mixed number of units, several OFAC listed / sanctioned larger LDT tankers (VLCC and Suezmax size) have arrived and even delivered in Alang recently – calling into question activities of the cash buyers who blatantly skirt international regulations, the actions of which only stand to affect the ability of Indian authorities to permit allowing any questionable units from even arriving locally in the future.

headline: MEANING BUSINESS!
highlights: Back in action. | Upgrades needed. | Lagging behind still.
body_text:
On the eve of the 5th month potentially highlighting an empty port report, the Gadani Gang seems to be leaping back into action over recent weeks via greater inquiries at the bidding tables and have as a result, even managed to secure several smaller LDT vessels and (finally) show that they mean business, especially after an extended period on the sidelines watching competing India rake in all of the recycling excess that has been coming into the market of late. Yet, unlike India, where levels seem to have more of a downward hint than an even one, Gadani offerings have remained entrenched in third place since Q4 2024, further compelling this market down the path of Turkey’s abyssal trench.

Like the rest of the industry, domestic fundamentals remain the prime movers behind the lethargic performance of Pakistan’s ship recycling sector. Local steel plate prices, though strongest in the sub-continent, have remained horizontal for the longest at USD 643.78 / Ton, being suppressed by the influx of cheaper Chinese steel that has devastated ship recycling activity at all domestic yards, and this only stands to potentially get worse as the effects from recently imposed tariffs on China are yet to come through.

Making matters worse for Pakistan’s economy are the numerous financial loans and international aid hanging in the balance and are still to come through, including that from the IMF who are still investigating misappropriation of hundreds of millions of dollars and even send an investigate IMF mission to Pakistan to assess the feasibility of governance, corporate affairs, and the ongoing corruption in the country. Moreover, with the Pakistani army now taking an active interest in the nation’s economy, the shift in the balance of powers and government further stands to deteriorate (if history has been any example). Finally, pending / major infrastructure upgrades at all domestic ship recycling yards needs to be initiated promptly in Gadani and bring ship recycling facilities up to HKC standards by July 1st of this year, or gay of the way of the Dodo.

As such, Pakistani buyers, though eager for tonnage and increasingly on the bidding tables of late, are lagging severely behind the rest of the industry in both current infrastructure capabilities and HKC standards at their respective yards, as some serious catching up needs to be done including that on price levels so that Pakistan can remain a relevant destination heading into 2026.

headline: NOISE!
body_text:
In addition to forever dithering fundamentals, the only new noise emanating from Turkey has been the buzz around recent proposals of fresh units, even though no fixtures have been reported to Aliaga recyclers thus far, and certainly with reason. Like the sub-continent markets, with USD 30/MT being wiped off vessel prices in the matter of a week, ship owners and cash buyers are left evaluating residual value differentials with the Indian sub-continent markets, especially with some of the larger LDT units on offer.

Fundamentals have remained true to their dying causes as both import and local steel plate prices continue do demonstrate their share of volatility, stirred in a with a healthy shot of a lamenting Lira that weakened further by 27 basis points and ended the week, squarely at a record-breaking TRY 36 against the U.S. Dollar.

What more can we expect if the only way for this market has been consistently South.

headline: ROCKY RACCOON!
highlights: Bagging big. | Misleading. | More aid? | Levels lower.
body_text:
Of late, an increasing focus on larger LDT vessels coming out of the Far East has seen Bangladeshi recyclers book a healthy collection of decent-sized units since the start of the year – including an FSU, a Capesize bulker, and even several LNGs tankers that followed a decent number of arrivals at Chattogram’s anchorage across recent weeks including this week, which registered a couple of fresh arrivals and a bevy of deliveries to their respective recyclers. Yet, the ‘busy’ anchorage hid the deceptive illusion of Chattogram’s ship recycling sector that not all is well, even with the nation at large.

At the macro end of things, the economy has spent another dull week with not much movement reported locally, amidst a political scenario that keeps on repeating in dialogue over reforms vs. early elections, in order to speed up a potential recovery. Yet, no apparent resolution on either stands in effect to this date and a specific direction for the nation at this time, remains uncertain. The general law and order situation in the country also remains turbulent given that the interim government remains unable to get a grip on unfolding events and riots (as reported last week) are still ongoing. Even despite Asia Development Bank (ADB) pledging USD 1 Billion in concessional aid to Bangladesh every year for the next 5 years, local economists are calling on the nation to brace for incoming headwinds on the news that the country registered the slowest economic growth as compared to the last 4. While this has previously seen the government curtail expenditures on foreign reserves towards non-critical sectors through 2023 and even 2024, given the unfolding economic crises, could be a foretelling of another financial crisis that is yet to potentially hit in Bangladesh’s ship recycling sector the (near) future, especially in the face of a deadline extension from the Bangladeshi Ministry with when to begin yard infrastructure upgrades from the original January 31st cutoff date by the BSBRA, to March 31st, as work reportedly commences on yards who aim to be fully compliant with the Hong Kong Convention ahead of its entry into force by the end of June 2025 and recyclers face further cuts in financial aid.

At the micro end, as inflation and ship recycling fundamentals remain extremely volatile, not only are local steel plate prices still flatlining, but the Taka made a surprising and desperately needed recovery of 31 basis point against the U.S. Dollar, ending the week at BDT 121.69. While domestic offerings for tonnage remain constricted as a result of previous declines on the Taka into the BDT 120s, sentiments continue on a downward trajectory as most of the aggressive and capable local recyclers are now booked with recent deliveries and the next batch of indications emanating are far below than those of recent fixtures, further pushing ship owners and cash buyers to chase down markets that are clearly in fall. As such, Bangladesh seems to be treading on rocky terrain with a momentary of binging of tonnage in the face of suppressed fundamentals and vessel pricing backed by geography and timing that have somewhat come together and insulate this market from the recent tariffs, even though the fear of the far-reaching effects of these potentially hitting Bangladesh, remains high. And lower recycling indications seen since the start of the year are now permanently snaking their way onto the bidding tables from the next tier of Chattogram Choppers.

highlights: Market uncertainty. | 25 percent tariffs. | Cheap Chinese. | Price fall. | Tonnge lull.
body_text:
Through it all, the knock-on effects of the tit-for-tat trade wars have certainly been felt across the ship recycling markets as well – perennially in India, where despite PM Modi being in America to visit Pres. Trump and ensure no tariffs were in the works to affect India and ensure the smooth and ongoing cooperation between the nations, the 25% tariffs announced on Chinese steel & aluminum products is already seeing destabilizing effects on the recycling markets, and it remains unsure as to where much of this surplus / excess and resultingly cheaper steel will end up, devastating ship recycling prices as a result of.

Speaking of prices, downward pressure on tabled levels has remained unrelenting since the start of the year and the ongoing and intolerable performances of key fundamentals has continued to push levels down ever since USD 600/Ton was achieved back in January 2024. Flatlining steel plate prices across the board including declining levels from India that have fallen in excess of USD 11/Ton over the course of 2 weeks alone, has done little for prevailing offerings. In fact, over the course of last year, both India and Pakistan were rigorously subjected to the import of cheaper Chinese steel imports that kept undercutting local inventories, resulting in sub-continent steel markets collapsing. Although new duties by both governments to curb the ill effects of this cheaper steel via anti- dumping tariffs were introduced, there remains a great deal of nervousness as to how these latest rounds of tit-for-tat tariffs will end up hitting the ship recycling industry.

headline: DOOZIE!
highlights: Fuelled by fear. | Modi in US. | Currency woes.
body_text:
Panic gripped India this week as the U.S. slapped 25% tariffs on Chinese steel & aluminum products – the unfolding fear of which is that, this surplus inventory (some of it already ready for export) is eventually going to make its way to the sub-continent markets where it will more than likely face price adjustments made to undercut sub-continent steel prices just so that Chinese steel owners can offload their excess inventories at increasingly loss making prices despite previously imposed and potentially further incoming punitive duties from the Indian government set to limit this crisis, has clearly done little thus far.

Whilst PM Modi was in the US to meet with President Trump this week in order to discuss this very issue amongst many others, in an attempt to layout potential damage control and aid India’s economy (which is in recovery) amidst growing international pressures that are all but certain to affect sub- continent markets across 2025, as Alang itself struggles to maintain its levels through current times. The present-day worldwide economy is also already facing the domino effect of the tariffs as global steel including Chinese plate prices, continue to flatline at far lower levels than those of Indian steel prices this week. This has seen (and will likely continue to see) Indian steel prices decline in excess of USD 11/Ton over the last couple of weeks, seriously pressuring Alang ship recyclers to reconsider and lower their offerings for future tonnage coming out of the Red Sea, at noticeable lower levels.

The currency has, however, strangely found stability this week as not only did it stall ongoing declines, but it also reversed recent losses by gaining about 1.2% against the U.S. Dollar and ending the week at Rs. 86.60. Although to the outsider, this may seem like a “win” of sorts, the truth is that the Rupee has lost nearly 5% over the last 4 Quarters and as a result, the ongoing decline in prices likely isn’t going to immediately translate into a price jump just yet.

And like Bangladesh, India is the only nation Eastward that is helping maintain a balance in the ongoing re-distribution of global tonnage for recycling as prices remain in the neck of the woods for units intended for an India / Pakistan re-delivery. Yet, given the ongoing price differentials with Pakistani Buyers after nearly 5 months who are still tabling a healthy collection of weak offers on a majority of their ongoing offerings, has helped India consume all but a single unit that has come available for a recycling sale basis both destinations as potentially final ones.

headline: NO TIME LIKE PRESENT…HOPEFULLY!
highlights: Finally converting. | Prices close. | HKC hopes.
body_text:
After an altogether inert few years on the sidelines, some signs of life are finally emanating from the Gadani gang and on the back of their recent effort, a couple of sales have even materialized to local buyers albeit on comparatively smaller LDT tonnage, one of which was even delivered to her new recyclers this week, the only delivery into Pakistan thus far in 2025. And unlike the other markets, Gadani’s anchorage has reported no further arrivals since. Notwithstanding, local offers remain not too far away behind their Indian counterparts, but sufficient enough to matter on the larger LDT units that have invariably headed further West to Alang, as Gadani recycling yards lie virtually dormant following such a prolonged period of inactivity.

But as welcome as this price aggression may seem, it remains a target too low for a majority of ship owners and cash buyers who are looking to offload tonnage as on the broader end of things for local recyclers, the Pakistani government is still struggling to maintain control of their unraveling economic affairs whilst the Pakistani army is essentially aiming to regain control of the government once again. Moreover, in the midst of a potential visit from IMF delegates to investigate corruption and governmental shortcomings in the nation, a turbulent time lies ahead for Pakistan’s domestic ship recycling sector, which is entirely dependent on U.S. Dollar transactions for financial assistance from the central bank, which in itself has been hemorrhaging cash up wards of USD 440 million amidst reported mismanagement. With the incoming IMF team ready to investigate and further lay out a framework to wash out wasteful / unnecessary / potentially illegal access to funds to aid the nation’s economy, how this will affect the nation’s ship recycling industry and / or the ease of with which future access to funds / L/Cs becomes available, remains to be seen.

Fow now, on the back of a reported few private fixtures, we don’t know how much more activity to expect at Gadani’s anchorage as once these recent fixtures and eventual deliveries bottom out, like in Bangladesh, will have likely done its share in satisfying tonnage to tier 1 Gadani buyers and tier 2 of buyers is already and expectedly testing the market with lower offerings, hoping to snag a deal at a time most markets seem destined to be heading South, and more importantly, ship owners and cash buyers start to finally bite at these lower(ing) levels.

Upgrade work does need to begin in earnest in Gadani so as to get domestic ship recycling facilities up to HKC standards ahead of its entry into force in June of this year, and hopefully still remain relevant post July 1st once no non-HKC yard will be permitted to take in tonnage now that the convention has been officially ratified by the Pakistani Ministry. Thankfully, some yards seem to have realized that the hard work must start now in order to remain relevant, and news of some upgrades (in the works) being initiated has come forward.

Ship recycling post June 2025 is going to be a wild ride in Gadani.

headline: BRUNT!
body_text:
The Turkish market seems to have borne the brunt of Trumps recent tariffs as not only did local steel plate prices report volatility again through the week, ending it marginally lower, but the Lira took the icing on the economy’s melting cake as it declined nearly 0.5% against the U.S. Dollar, closing it out at TRY 36.10.

Yet, there was no other news (other than a few private discussions) taking place locally, with no news of fresh arrivals either.

headline: REALIZING REDUCTIONS!
highlights: Coping. | Work underway. | Coping. | Further headwinds.
body_text:
Having endured an impressively active & busy start to the year by absorbing nearly all of the tonnage that has emanated from the Far East, January has certainly helped Chattogram stay busy through recent times, which have certainly been the most trying since 2008. And while external factors remain responsible for the supply of tonnage, massive internal problems still ongoing have left the domestic ship recycling sector in a state of stasis across much of Q3 - Q4 2024; a time that looks like it may be returning once again now that freight rates are firming are on the rise now.

For domestic, and a majority of now satiated ship recycling yards that have been busy taking in a bulk of Far Eastern deliveries, has continued even this week where over 52K LDT and 7 vessels are at anchorage / being delivered to their new owners. Ironically, the rate of recent deliveries seems to outline a budding indicator of the positive movement of recycled ship’s steel from Chattogram ship recycling yards that continue to trade with local steel mills at a level that has flatlined the one of longest in the industry since October 2024, albeit a relatively healthier (than local offers on ships) USD 529.41/Ton. As steel trade resumes amidst domestic infrastructure projects that remain hanging in the balance, the spate of recent deliveries is expected to keep local ship recyclers busy well into Q2 before seeing their return to the bidding tables just prior to Bangladesh’s budget, which is expected around June of 2025. And although this should buy some time for domestic businesses to prepare for the eventual FY 25 – F26 budget, it also afford them the time to initiate yard upgrades in the interim.

Purchasing abilities of local recyclers has left them atop the recycling market rankings as Chattogram Choppers continue to table the best levels and some even higher than prevailing figures, especially if a particular unit of interest comes to the fore. But it has been the Taka that has delivered the most downward pressure on recycling offers as it nearly breached BDT 122 once again this week, only to firm up towards the end of the week and still end it 20 basis points weaker at BDT 121.53. And although personal incoming U.S. Dollar remittances from overseas to families saw a healthy amount added to their national reserves, the economic condition of the nation state remains far from healthy as stresses from the lack of economic reform are eroding profits from local industries and the private sector, and the 6 month report sheet of the interim government has resulted in a growing economic fragility of the future for the country for the rest of 2025.

At the recycling end, this pressure remains tantamount as most yards have yet to initiate upgrades to their facilities to HKC standards after the BSBRA extended the deadline to commence works from January 31st to March 31st and failure to react in time could see even the nation’s ship recycling sector face further headwinds and likely see Bangladesh lose to India for the top spot. For now however, this market continues to bask in glory of dominating the tonnage inflow from the East whilst its price differential with neighboring competitors stands less than the delivery cost further West…primarily on smaller LDT units.

headline: FREIGHT FRUSTRATES!
highlights: Markets deprived. | Panamax surge. | January sales. | Pak back. | Bangla upgrades.
body_text:
Speaking of tariffs, while the ones already implemented have kept the oil markets subdued of late, those tariffs still in the pipeline have pulled the barrel back closer to USD 70/barrel this week, as recent sanctions coupled with growing U.S. oil reserves could continue to see the barrel buoying around the early USD 70s in the near future. Whilst global economies adjust around these unfolding market dynamics, key fundamentals continue to see their shares of volatility given that local steel plate prices are either vacationing / laying horizontal in key markets while registering declines in others, and the U.S. Dollar, which remains of key concern for ship recycling nation currencies, which continue to decline whilst others struggle to re-adjust / likely to lose further ground.

As a result, ship recycling markets offerings have fallen by up to USD 30/LDT over the first month of the year and while further pressures on key drivers seem to have been working in unison to pull recycling offers further down, the lack of tonnage has seemingly found a price floor around USD 450/LDT despite indications far below on certain units are easily forthcoming. Now that workable and firm candidates are drying up, the ever-present hunger to buy might return in the final month of Q1 2025 as we have even seen Pakistan come back into the picture of late, securing a smaller LDT unit after a significant period on the sidelines. But it remains too little too late for a market that has seen just one arrival at the nation’s waterfront since Qct 2024. Moreover, despite Bangladeshi ship recyclers picking up the pace on respective facility and infrastructure upgrades, with the HKC finally entering into force by July of this year and urgent / pending yard upgrades are still needed in Chattogram and especially in Gadani, to ensure compliance with the convention now that a potentially bumper few years of tonnage supply and deal making lie ahead. As Alang buyers note the increasing presence of the Gadani Gang trying to take a bite out of their tonnage buffet at the bidding tables, they remain the epicenter of ship recycling West of Bangladesh with nearly all yards ready to operate post July 1 and business being as usual thereafter. Finally, Turkey continues to dissolve into its economic uncertainty as no meaningful market news has been forthcoming other than the steady descent of the Lira to where it is gradually approaching to half the value of the Indian Rupee. Times are changing.

headline: SHORT SHARP SHOCK!
highlights: Tariff panic – ironic? | Modi moves. | No malaise.
body_text:
Like the rest of the world, India has not been immune to varying crises and tariff shocks that have sent ship recycling economies into a freefall, as Alang recyclers themselves continue to constantly adjusting to the varying degrees of supply amidst disastrous fundamentals despite which, has driven Alang buyers to maintain second place in the market rankings. And through the smorgasbord of the craziness of current time, the nation’s recycling waterfront stands on the edge of an empty port position with just one vessel reported to have arrived anchorage this week, albeit a couple of vessels are currently lying in wait awaiting inward permissions, including a reportedly sanctioned tanker.

At the broader end of things, the Rupee remains the most disastrous of entities for Alang recyclers as it nearly breached INR 87 against the U.S. Dollar, only to settle the week unchanged from last at Rs 86.60. And while local recyclers went into a tailspin over PM Trump’s raft of tariffs introduced last week including a healthy 25% on Chinese steel and aluminum products, Chinese steel plate prices have continued to flatline over the last few weeks and that too at levels far below those from India, resulting in Indian steel plate prices dipping even further this week by a couple of Dollars, totaling a near USD 15/Ton decline over the last 3 weeks. As the only sub-continent destination to face declines in both fundamentals, the pressure on local pricing has been the most imminent at the bidding tables, as Alang buyers conservatively approach available tonnage as it starts to dissipate once again.

While PM Modi was in the U.S. to welcome Trump into his second term in office and discussions pertaining to his administrations Indian outlook were reportedly tabled, pending tariffs still in the pipeline could see some of the highest tariffs in the world on products imported from India, amidst an already reported decline in exports for the first time!

Overall, even though Alang remains competitive (even with Bangladesh for certain units) at the bidding tables and for the time being, an increasingly eager Pakistan and the ongoing downturn in Alang offerings since the start of this year does seem like the present may not merely be a short sharp shock to the system rather than a prolonged malaise that many are now fearing.

headline: IS IT TIME?!
highlights: Not far behind. | Tough last few years. | IMF downgrade. | Frustrations build.
body_text:
The Pakistani market has been and will continue to remain one of the most confusing markets to peg down given that local buyers are clearly not (and truly never have) followed the direction of domestic fundamentals in determining just how to remediate local pricing, choosing instead to follow the direction of offerings from competing neighbors, and this has helped them set a price ceiling is already well below the capacity of what Gadani ship recyclers can table, but what remains in question is their capability given that they are and have been the lowest placed at the bottom of the market rankings while simultaneously struggling to secure any tonnage, as a result of.

To start, when compared to global recycling destinations, the Pakistani Rupee has displayed the greatest stability against the U.S. Dollar as it has stayed between PKR 277 – PKR 280 over the last 4 quarters including this week, where despite losing 22 basis points, it still ended the week at USD 279.48. Simultaneously, local steel plate prices remain the highest in the industry at USD 643.78 although having flatlined the next longest. While this in itself, should more than justify a healthier level of offerings at the bidding tables from the Gadani gang, they have in fact, barely managed to improve their levels in any positive direction over recent quarters.

And although competing (and simultaneously flatlined) Chinese plate prices have stalled at a far more competitive level near USD 300/Ton, this has invariably helped domestic steel mills stay afloat with far cheaper imports. So why then is this market still not re-adjusting to the influx, just to keep the net return on its only delivery of 2025 in the green or even for those that still are / will be in the pipeline? As uncertain as this question remains, Pakistan remains fairly close behind their Indian sub-continent competitors in pricing amidst a return of tonnage scarcity that has seen Gadani’s anchorage return to an empty one.

The domestic economy remains of primary concern and although international remittances by families has helped maintain a degree of equilibrium in the nation’s treasury reserves, the IMF has downgraded Pakistan’s forecast for 2025 citing ongoing governmental irregularities and reported mismanagement of funds, including the fear of the army taking on an larger role in the nation’s governmental and economic affairs, leaving the question just as to when it will be before Pakistan’s ship recycling sector is able to get back in business at the bidding tables vessels with a degree of regularity.

As it has been a tough few years on the sidelines for the Paksitani market, buying minimal vessels and still far from initiating meaningful yard upgrades in order to become HKC compliant ahead of the official HKC entry into force in June this year (meaning non-compliant yards will not be able to import any tonnage from July 1st), frustrations at the bidding tables are starting to build up at losing so many vessels to India and Bangladesh since the start of this year and this fervor could be a good thing for Pakistan moving forward, as long as the Gadani Gang positively uses this momentum.

headline: DUKES OF HAZZARD!
body_text:
Aliaga recyclers have been hemorrhaging the worst of the ship recycling world since 2023 on the back of crashing economic fundamentals, a bevy of ship recycling regulations imposed by the EU, weakening import and local steel plate prices, a Lira that has declined nearly 492% against the U.S. Dollar over the last five years (nearly a 1,355% decline if you go back a decade), a shortage of tonnage over the last 13 months, and save for the heady days of cruise vessels that once lined the shores of Aliaga, a near absence of market fixtures that has reportedly left some local buyers having to temporarily shutter their yards while the bigger names have reportedly survived by negotiating off- market smaller LDT tonnage emanating from regional waters.

And like last week, the Dukes of Hazzard have nothing to report this week as well, as another silent week / month / Quarter comes to an end.

headline: STARK CONTRAST!
highlights: Fewer sales. | Political shakes. | HKC deadline. | Historic shift!
body_text:
As the first week of Ramadan sets in, Bangladesh continues to trudge through a truly confusing time where not only are the highest payers in the industry facing the same music as the rest of the world’s economies that have started reacting to the unfolding tariffs, including ongoing political and economic hurdles of their own. While February ended up in the history books as a rather stark contrast to a far-busier January on the back of fewer sales being confirmed, and an instability in pricing emerging that was absent since the start of this year has bought in a bevy of fixtures through the last batch of acquisitions, which found themselves simultaneously arriving the waterfront this week, with over 105K LDT and 10 vessels (LNGs, Tankers, and Bulkers) that are either lying in wait or were already delivered to their respective new owners on the beach.

Domestic fundamentals continue to test the rigidity of local offerings as not only have plate prices held dead on at about USD 529/Ton, but it has been the Taka which, like the Lira, has lost a far less disastrous in comparison, yet disastrous enough on its own as it has plummeted over 11% in just over the last year alone including this week, where it fell another 20 basis points and ended the week at a calamitous BDT 121.97/Ton. With the budget expected in about 3 months from now, the economic fragility continues as despite seeing a massive collection of arrivals over recent weeks highlighting the ongoing trade of recycled ship’s steel at levels that have helped Bangladesh dominate pole position over the market rankings for several months now.

As the interim political party is also coming under growing pressure, particularly from the increasingly militant student body who ousted former PM Sheikh Hasina and have formed their own party, political (in)stability has trumped (pun intended) economic stability as despite seeing some easing in inflation rates reported across February, it (inflation) remains at a concerned 9.98% as the “to-do list” of the current intermittent administration starts to become rather tenuous across 3 quarters now. Moreover, despite key indicators highlighting a gradual recovery, the nation faces inflationary pressures, slow public spending, diminishing employment opportunities, and an overall sluggish investment climate amidst faltering large U.S. Dollar loans by domestic businesses.

All of this coming to a head and at a time the HKC stands to enter into force by July 1st 2025, earmarking a historic shift in the business of ship recycling and HKC yard upgrades, though delayed, have reportedly commenced at pace in Chattogram on the back of the BSBRA’s recent deadline extension for upgrades to start by March 31st and subsequently obtain relevant SOC certifications from accredited Classes confirming the ability of domestic ship recycling yards to operate post Q2 2025. For now, amidst a sharp decline in the availability of vessels, Ramadan prayers and celebrations, Taka tumbles, and growing pressure on local offerings, Chattogram Choppers may have bought some breathing time until Q2 before the need to engage in discussions from the same tier of buyers resumes again, all while the 2nd batch of hungry buyers are lingering at levels much lower.

headline: DWINDLING…SURGE?!
highlights: Ramadan begins. | Price decline. | Freight surge. | Trade concerns. | Demand good.
body_text:
As tonnage availability has been notably absent at the bidding tables of late, the industry was greeted by the start of the Holy Month of Ramadan this week, which descended across the Indian sub-continent (and Turkish) markets, providing India and Bangladesh some respite from the fiery January sales witnessed since the turn of the year, and all at a time where the recent decline in levels of about USD 30/LDT due to ongoing geopolitical volatility that has perpetuated itself via flatlining and even declining steel prices and ongoing currency depreciations that saw the U.S. Dollar surge against currencies of all ship recycling nations across the board this week.

At the respective ship recycling destinations, as currency and steel starts to hammer harder where ongoing Indian declines were joined by Pakistan for the first time since October 2024, further highlighting the unfolding effects of the tariff wars as news of 25% against Mexico and Canada going into effect on March 4th surfaced this week, including an additional 10% to be levied against China, which will maintain an unappreciable amount of pressure on ongoing vessel offerings. Political crises have once again resurrected themselves in Bangladesh as the law-and-order situation remains of concern there, whilst Pakistan’s treasury continues to hemorrhage cash as fundamentals here declined in unison this week. While India continues to take in questionable tonnage and recyclers here start to feel the pinch of a Rupee that’s gone AWOL, cash buyers are being greeted by Turkish offerings even below USD 280/Ton on units, all amidst a devasted Lira that remains clutching to life support.

Overall, with the Red Sea reopening and freight rates set to potentially cool once charters are set to refresh, ongoing peace talks for both Ukraine and Gaza continue to be hit with a bat as Norway cuts off fuel supplies to U.S. Naval vessels over Trump’s contentious meeting with President Zelenskyy and Israel cuts off all aid into Gaza amidst an unfolding ceasefire standoff that will unquestionably see freight dynamics start to shift once again. And this may lead to an increased supply of units / containers later in the year. Recent alarming news concerning a potential ban on Chinese built / owned tonnage calling U.S. ports also stands to devastate the U.S. economy in turn, eventually sending prices skyrocketing even further as U.S. inflation starts to rise once again and the Feds cancel their recently intended interest rate cut. Nevertheless, demand for units at flimsy levels remains firm across sub-continent markets and it will be interesting to see what levels upcoming sales are concluded at, especially as the supply of tonnage starts to slow once again.

headline: FALLING…FAST & FURIOUS EDITION!
highlights: Price woes. | USD 17/Ton | PM Modi’s efforts. | Over a decade.
body_text:
India’s economy has been earmarking what is today, and what will more than likely be the near future for Alang recyclers as not only are their offerings coming under immense economic pressures, but Indian buyers are also coming under increasing competition from a Pakistani market of late, even though their purchasing prowess seems largely dithered over recent weeks on the back of a growing shortage of tonnage that is similarly affecting India’s ship recycling sector. Yet, like their Bangladeshi counterparts, Alang’s port position has recorded an impressive number of arrivals exceeding 40K LDT via 5 decent size units including tankers, dry units, and even a RoRo.

Additionally, Indian fundamentals are keeping Alang’s offerings at the bidding table in check as not only has the Indian Rupee suffered a devastating week as it lost nearly 1% in value to close the week out at Rs. 87.48 against the U.S. Dollar, but local steel plate prices have not stopped falling over the recent past as they fell another $2/Ton this week, pushing the total decline to over USD 17/Ton over the last month alone and this is making it harder for Alang recyclers to compete with the better placed Bangladesh market as well.

Notwithstanding, some of the key markers affecting India’s economic scorecard have been pointing in the right direction as Q4 2024 ended with an uptick noted on the back of increased government and consumer spending that even drove the country’s economic growth by over 6% during the same time. India’s recent budget providing massive tax cuts for low – median income families / individuals will more than likely maintain the nation’s economic trajectory and even gradually send India’s inflationary numbers South.

But for the nation’s ship recycling sector, none of it seems rosy under the current environment, especially since candidate introductions at the bidding tables have slowed over the past month, economic pressures on vessel prices are growing, and levels are without hesitation, seemingly ready for another adjustment. And despite the best efforts of PM Modi to build firmer ties with President Trump during a recent visit to the White House and maintain bilateral economic relations, sentiments also took a beating and weakened off the back of the tariff volatility that is engulfing much of the world at present.

Nonetheless, any Far Eastern fixtures will continue to wind up in Bangladesh and those vessels coming from the West are now under an increasing threat of heading to Pakistan as Alang offerings are the ones coming under the heaviest fire, unless of course needing HKC only recycling including those post June 30th 2025, for which Alang buyers already excel at and have been well prepared for this moment for nearly a decade now.

headline: MORE COMPETITIVE?
highlights: Confirming deals. | Rockier start. | Time to restart. | Eke out.
body_text:
Even though the Gadani gang stand in 3rd place on the market rankings, their inability to perform at a sustained rate leaves the very question unanswered i.e. just how competitive has Gadani’s ship recycling sector truly been of late? Although Indian levels stand to approach Pakistan’s levels before the reverse takes place, but Pakistan (like the rest of the word) is facing economic wranglings of their own especially after the recent IMF downgrade and billions of dollars in aid and financial loans that remain hanging in the balance.

Notwithstanding the ship recycling act playing out in Q1, of late, Pakistan did become a competitive option rather than the primary destination for any geographically positioned units opening West of Sri Lanka that finally helped even confirme a smaller LDT deal to one hungry recycler whereafter, the market has gone silent again as it wraps up the 2nd consecutive week of an empty anchorage.

And with plots lying largely dormant after an extremely inactive and inert last few years that has seen many recyclers having to partially close shop and divest in alternative business interests, some of the top-tier buyers are still keen to conclude vessels and as such, interest on select units is lingering behind the scenes, albeit at a subdued level, especially after years of lagging behind the competition and registering some of the lowest sales volumes seen into the nation in nearly over a decade. And with the looks of it, 2025 is certainly off to a rocky start.

Meanwhile, in the face of the nation’s depleting reserves by the government are now being greeted by a healthy inflow of personal foreign remittances into the country leading to a stable February that even saw inflation sit at the perfect level of around 3% that is needed for every major economy to perform at, and this should hopefully ease the burden of finances in short time needed for Pakistani recyclers to initiate upgrade yards to HKC standards, given that a serious influx of recycling tonnage expected in the year(s) ahead!

For now, however, as India’s levels are all but certain to see the better part of south in the coming week(s) with their fundamentals written all over the recycling wall, helping Pakistan easily slip into 2nd place and eke out the next healthy batch of units before the next slowdown in the supply starts to hit the markets again, just as they currently are. At the moment however, local steel plate prices fell a massive USD 11/Ton while the Pakistani Rupee itself lost 4 basis points and ended the week at PKR 279.56 against the U.S. Dollar, likely putting their own pressures on Gadani offerings in the interim.

headline: DOWN…AND NEARLY OUT?
body_text: Turkey’s chances at securing tonnage and owners receiving a fair offer in the face of a near USD 200/Ton price differential with the sub-continent markets have left little for Aliaga buyers to nibble on. And on the units that are being proposed to test the waters are being greeted by indications that are permeating even below the current price floor of USD 280/Ton. Fundamentals continue afflict their pricing strategy as well as subdued import and local steel plate prices that continue face weekly jitters, all while the Lira remains in freefall as it collapsed another 20 basis points to end the week at TRY 36.53. Certainly not an even playing field for Aliaga recyclers under the current environment.

headline: FRANTIC AND FANATIC!
highlights: Dwindling. | Price cool. | Far short… | Logger done.
body_text:
It has been a frantic February in Bangladesh as an ongoing collection of deliveries has been taking place over recent weeks, including this one, given that 9 ships and nearly 100K LDT is still at anchorage / being delivered to their respective recyclers, which is helping domestic ship recycling yards maintain a sense of equilibrium in the middle of another resurging crash in the supply of tonnage. Moreover, fanatic members of the newly formed student-led political party continue to take the law into their own hands, rendering the ability of local law enforcement and even the army, meaningless in the wake of violence and rioting that is on the rise once again as Sheikh Hasina continues her attempts at reviving her political party.

This has seen the security apparatus across the country fail to maintain law-and order while the economy itself continues to face unending hurdles under the interim government where despite foreign personal remittances into the country fattening Bangladesh’s treasury reserves across February, interest repayments on the nation’s outstanding debt saw reserves take a notable hit and register a sharp decline this week, mercifully coinciding with the ongoing decline in the supply of tonnage that would’ve otherwise only restricted the ability of those Chattogram Choppers who are / could be in the market for a unit, from securing potential tonnage. The flattened state of local steel plate prices (at USD 529/Ton) has done little to move the pricing needle, especially as the Taka also managed to firm 13 basis points and end the week marginally firmer, at BDT 121.78 against the U.S. Dollar.

Meanwhile, as the economy reports marginal improvements as February 2025 winds up, the rate of economic growth fell far short of expectations as local confidence in the interim government remains low, unemployment (resulting in violence) remains high, shortage of loans and financial aid to domestic businesses remain beyond reach, and commodity inflation (especially food and groceries) were responsible for over 51% of domestic inflation, leaving it at a rather troublesome 9.86% - a less than 1% improvement from the period of Dec 2024 – Jan 2025. Yet, this could provide employment opportunities at recycling yards for unemployed workers, especially as infrastructure and yard upgrades are needed at pace and those recyclers without units on their yards still have the opportune time to make the necessary upgrades and stay prepared post June 26th, 2025.

Overall, in the face of minimal deals being concluded into Chattogram, vessels purchased back in January that are now being delivered to their new owners, should keep activity at domestic yards ongoing and the addition of another smaller LDT Chinese owned handy size logger BC that was concluded this week into Bangladesh, should help stagger the momentum ahead as the poor condition SEA WISE (5,533 LDT) managed to fetch a notably diminished USD 420/LT LDT, even though there is a Gadani option wrapped into this deal (not India).

headline: STATIC NOISE!
highlights: State of stasis. | Geopolitics. | Sales slow. | Pak active? | Turkish sale?
body_text:
Meanwhile, following another quiet week of unremarkable activity, recycling markets are also being drug into the state of economic global stasis as Q1 2025 is proving itself to be somewhat of a turbulent time given that over USD 150/LDT has now been wiped off of vessel highs since Jan 2024 where a container breached the now long-forgotten USD 600/LDT mark, and ongoing economic / trade pressures continue to push vessel prices down while hampering sentiments and aggression from the various ship recycling destinations, despite an omnipresent demand permeating at new lows. And even though all the hints of a price correction are mushrooming from most markets, especially as local steel plate prices continue to react to the unfolding tariffs, the ability of ship recyclers to be aggressive is being curtailed at an increasing rate that continues to affect the global residual values of recycling candidates, when compared to the levels witnessed amidst the recent surge in supply back in January, followed by the ongoing and dithered supply since February. And amidst mounting geopolitical pressures, ship recycling sales have slowed to such an extent that most yards are now either concentrating on recycling their recent deliveries, all while tier-2 recyclers lie dormant in wait to snag a new low-priced deal, helping demand stay afloat even if prices remain slippery.

In Bangladesh, increasing protests and political clashes re-emerge, while Indian recyclers fail to maintain the trajectory of their prices leading to a gradual approach to Pakistani levels, which themselves have (inadvertently) rendered this market a touch more active of late and helped them slip into 2nd place. Turkey at the far-end reported no meaningful change despite a surprising sale surfacing this week. Overall, ship recycling yards keen to continue operations are busy upgrading their facilities ahead of the Hong Kong Convention’s (HKC) entry into force on 26 June 2025 as the changing documentary requirements and new incoming formalities need to be addressed.

headline: FREAKY FEBRUARY!
highlights: Leapfrogged. | Sharp shock. | Historical highs.
body_text:
India has endured a rotten February with declining vessel offers on the back of sentiments being impacted by the ongoing and diminished supply of tonnage that has been drying up rapidly at the bidding tables of late. And as declining offers from India silently help Gadani recyclers dislodge Alang in the market rankings for the #2 spot, the lackluster performance of local buyers continues to deteriorate local sentiments over recent weeks, leaving them at the bottom of the sub-continent ship recycling market rankings. And as forecasted last week, this is expected to get worse for Alang despite the nation’s economy reporting positive movements across 2025, including strengthening U.S. – India bilateral trade ties as governments of both countries reportedly struck oil deals on the back of recent Russian sanctions.

Meanwhile, despite the initial hiccup of the tariffs and PM Modi’s visit to America, the Indian Rupee still collapsed to its lowest levels against the U.S. Dollar over the last two months. And even though ongoing trade has clearly played its part this week, the Indian Rupee, though severely diminished, marked a serious improvement of 43 basis points against the U.S. Dollar that helped it close the week at INR 87.09. Moreover, despite mounting pressures resulting from tariffs on Chinese products that could potentially see another influx of cheaper steel imports into the country in the coming Quarters, local steel plate prices managed to hold their ground and even make a small recovery of USD 2/Ton, which is noteworthy given that steel levels have declined without remission over 4 straight weeks.

This has already seen a minor correction in prices from Alang as anticipated and even though key fundamentals have registered minor improvements this week, there is simply no telling which way these critical elements will move the pricing needled in the coming week(s) and further affect the currently fragile sentiment in Alang. Moreover, even local port position continues to deceive the outsiders’ eyes as 8 vessels and over 76K LDT is currently idling at the nation’s recycling waterfront or have already felt the sands below their hulls.

Finally, in the face of improving internal trade and the nation’s economic recovery seemingly written on the wall - especially after this year’s powerful budget that was designed to help the low-income populous en masse - Alang recyclers are expected to have a tricky end to Q1 and likely even well into Q2, as tonnage scarcity grows, vessel prices face ongoing fundamental pressures, and India loses footing to an otherwise diminished, yet comparatively ‘unchanged’ Pakistani market that seems to be on the road for another possible fixture. Loses footing.

headline: COME BACK?
highlights: Securing lower LDT. | Uncertainty on higher. | USD 22/Ton drop. | June 26th, 2025.
body_text:
Has Pakistan surprisingly come back into the picture this week once again? Clearly (and as predicted in last week’s edition of the GMS Weekly), India’s falling prices have elevated Gadani’s diminished (yet stable) pricing slide into second place on the market rankings, even shifting the focus of potential owners & cash buyers towards the shores of Pakistan, as has been clearly visible from this week’s market fixture into Bangladesh where the vessel surprisingly also has a Gadani redelivery option, not India, highlighting the poorer sentiments that have been emanating from Alang over recent weeks.

And although a Pakistani recycler did manage to conclude a vessel back in January followed by its redelivery into Gadani in early February, the last four weeks have tragically ended on an empty note, leaving hungry local recyclers still scavenging for tonnage. Notwithstanding, India’s ongoing decline could see some market (or even private) tonnage head towards Gadani shores in the coming week(s), especially if the incoming unit is better suited (geographically) for a WC India / Pakistan range redelivery.

Yet, the economic uncertainty (at large) that has permeated the nation and even the nation’s ship recycling sector, which continues affecting the ability of Gadani recyclers to transact large(r) LDT tonnage including some of the big ticket deals that have been making the rounds, especially in the face of strained LC / finance limits with domestic banks that remain in place and continue to detract the abilities of local buyers from securing tonnage despite a semblance of demand (of shifting of industry focus) starting to return to this market once again.

And this comes at a time of weakening fundamentals as not only has the Pakistani Rupee been the only ship recycling destination to lose ground against the U.S. Dollar through an 11 basis point drop that briefly breached the PKR 280 mark and ended the week at PKR 279.82, but local steel plate prices also joined the drop as they fell another USD 11/Ton, ending the week at region USD 629/Ton; a mere USD 100/Ton higher than those currently in Bangladesh and a total USD 22/Ton fall over the last couple of weeks.

Encouragingly, in the face Pakistan’s looming IMF investigations, loan reprieves continue as not only did the UAE government extend the deadline on interest repayments on their loans back in January, but even the Chinese government came through this week providing another year extension on interest repayments that could greatly help the nation’s treasury reserves, which themselves have been elevated by an impressive amount of personal foreign remittances, lowering the nation’s inflationary numbers to the coveted 3% range. While these remittances may not be infused into non-essential sectors at this time, the comparatively lower capital requirements for yard upgrades (as compared to large LDT ship purchases) should make it easier for the Gadani Gang to obtain the funds needed continue the arduous process of upgrading their facilities in line with HKC standards, ahead of the final entry into force by June 26th this year.

headline: TAKE…1!!
body_text:
In what seems like a clear unfolding of “even a broken watch can tell the correct time twice”, Aliaga recyclers seem to have managed to snag in a juicy private unit as the Greek ferry KRITI II (LDT 12,960 MT) was compellingly concluded (due to existing regulations) at about USD 3.6 million, equating to about USD 277.77/MT – easily about USD 175/Ton lower than those from the sub-continent and that too on a unit this size. This also highlights the fact that even though large LDT juicy units are being proposed to local buyers, EUSRR requirements likely affected the resale price into Aliaga given this is even lower than recent offerings as highlighted in the market rankings. A single sale, while not enough to confirm current levels, will likely set the pace for future potential fixtures.

Fundamentals too, continue keep local recyclers on their toes as weekly jitters that saw import steel levels improve by USD 5/Ton, they have still remained volatile and kept local steel plate prices hanging in the balance. The Lira also managed to miraculously firm a mere 5 basis points against the U.S. Dollar as it closed the week out at TRY 36.49 – although this could be a case of rising tides lift all boats.

For now, as tonnage dries up, so do the chances of Turkish buyers at securing tonnage.

headline: BANGING AWAY!
highlights: Above market. | …the only pillar. | Subsidies. | Rusty.
body_text:
As the price & tonnage leaders in the ship recycling sector across a majority of Q1 2025, Bangladesh ship recyclers remain keen to pick up tonnage despite being in an economic and political meltdown that is currently taking the nation a lot longer (than expected) to recover from, especially as there remains very little available at the bidding tables to bid on and this is leading to an accrual of local frustrations even though local anchorage continues to report healthy arrivals of nearly 72K LDT via 7 ships (including another LNG Tanker), that are either idling at the nations waterfront or have already been delivered to their respective recyclers this week. As such, it would not be surprising to see a few above market sales concluded to local buyers in the near future, just to satisfy some of the demand that has been resurfacing of late, as now-aggressive tier 2 recyclers become keen to fill their plots with tonnage at these newly cemented and comfortable levels in the USD 450s/Ton.

Rightly so, given that Bangladeshi steel plate prices continue to be the only pillar supporting local offerings at their current levels, helping local Chop Shops stay atop the market rankings week after week and even be the beneficiaries of virtually all of the tonnage that has been opening up in the Far East over the last 2 quarters, on the back of steel late prices that ended another week flatlined at region USD 529/Ton. Notwithstanding, while the economy and the Bangladeshi Taka are doing their best to suppress local offerings to mirror those of regional competitors, prices may eventually head in the wrong direction as the Taka weakens another 5 basis points to end the week at BDT 121.42 against the U.S. Dollar.

On the domestic economy front, Bangladesh continues to suffer amidst ongoing protests, violence and attacks on law enforcement as unemployment remains high, business slowdowns continue, reduction in domestic exports to both the U.S. and the EU affect the nation’s treasury, slowdown in activity at port terminals due to labor shortages is causing delays and resulting in rising costs of imported goods that are further grinding against domestic inflation, which itself has climbed just 0.5% in February 2025 whilst still at a high 9.32%, oil and energy costs are skyrocketing, and wavering bank deposits due to a growing lack of trust in the interim government continues despite rumors of the upcoming budget granting generous subsidies for the domestic agricultural and manufacturing sectors, in an attempt to jump start the economy and keep the nation’s reserves in check. With the budget still being over a Quarter away and economic pressures still at play, just how Chattogram Choppers will react in the interim remains to be seen.

Finally, local sales continue as another bulker from Chinese owners (their third sale of this year so far) was confirmed as the RUN FU 6 (6,297 LDT) fetched a weakened USD 435/LT LDT with a Pakistan option in hand, as the vessel may well end in Gadani due to her condition and the fact that Bangladeshi recyclers are being far pickier in acquiring rusty units these days.

headline: SPLURGING END?!
highlights: 200K LDT. | Bangla ahead. | “If and when”? | Downtime for HKC. | Tariff moves.
body_text:
It has been a number of weeks since we saw more than one market unit concluded into the sub- continent ship recycling markets as the Baltic’s Dry Bulk Sea Freight Index reported further climbs and registered its highest levels since November 2024, further deviating dry bulk & container freight sectors away from the bidding tables as firming rates push on and are maintaining the backlog of vintage / over aged vessels on the high-seas over the last few years. This will certainly drive global inflation up as logistics gets more expensive and trade wars aggravate an already volatile situation that much worse. Even oil prices continue to see jitters after they declined another 1% in early-week trading and rose back 0.9% by Friday, as oil closed the week out at $67.20 / Ton, all in the face of an ongoing over-supply of oil from OPEC+ countries despite a global easing of energy demands.

On the domestic fundamentals front, there has been a mixed bag of confusing signals emanating from the recycling markets. On the one hand, the U.S. Dollar has suffered a stuttering time as it weakened against some currencies while strengthening against others, and local steel plate prices hammer sentiments down further in both India and Pakistan this week, all while Chinese plate prices finally firm after a long time, which could have a positive affect on sub-continent markets in the long run and sub-continent levels continue to decline as an equilibrium finally settles things down…but that still remains an “if and when” type of situation.

For now, the ongoing downtime via the lack of availability of tonnage is providing recyclers in both Bangladesh and Pakistan the perfect opportunity to upgrade their yards up to HKC standards ahead of its entry into force on June 26th, while a majority (if not all) Alang yards are already HKC accredited with SoC certifications. Turkey at the far end has receded into hibernation in the face of the ongoing lack of tonnage, other than a marginal private proposal this week. Finally, many of Trump’s tariff deadlines have now passed and it will be interesting to see how economies fare now that China too is reacting in kinds. Finally, a number of larger LDT OFAC listed / sanctioned vessels also remain unsold in cash buyer hands amidst fresh sanctions being imposed on vessels currently idling outside Bangladesh, highlighting once again the risks some cash buyers are willing to take and the international laws they are willing to violate, just to make a quick buck!

headline: TWINNING!
highlights: Nemesis. | 4% | Supply low. | Unable to test.
body_text:
Ship recycling markets certainly never fail to deliver their share of surprises given that on the back of declining local offerings (as previously forecasted in prior reports), not only have Alang recyclers managed to dislodge themselves to Pakistan on the market rankings, but Alang’s anchorage has also managed to become the inadvertent twin of Gadani’s waterfront as both destinations reported just one arrival this week, highlighting the relentless pressures on India’s ship recycling sector that continue to hammer away at local sentiments.

At the micro end for the ship recycling markets, their nemesis have been local steel plate prices as well as the U.S. Dollar, both of which have suffered catastrophically of late and even this week, where steel levels fell nearly another Dollar, down to USD 443/Ton and well below the current vessel pricing strategy out of India, and the U.S. Dollar too made a (meaningless) 12 basis point jump this week, but still ending the week at an astronomical level just above Rs. 87 (at the time of writing).

Nevertheless, the Indian economy at large, continues to make gains (compared to the economies of competing ship recycling neighbors), with retail inflation finally slipping below the 4% mark in February and news of upcoming interest rate cuts by the government make the rounds. Moreover, as Chinese steel plate prices start to rise on the back of recently imposed tariffs, this could definitely help Indian steel plate prices in the long run, but just when and how soon, remain the question. Moreover, with tonnage dithering at the bidding tables and firmer Pakistani levels taking a bite out of India’s recycling buffet via a second fixture in as many weeks (with a Pakistan option in hand), is certainly laying out additional hurdles for Indian recyclers leading into Q2.

This has pushed Alang Buyers into a corner where they remain patiently waiting on the sidelines to acquire specialist units (LNGs, stainless steel tankers, offshore vessels) and even HKC tonnage – some of which has made it to Chattogram of late while others (including HKC tonnage) have been entirely amiss in the face of firming freight rates that continue to deprive global ship recycling markets of any serious tonnage over the last couple of months - at least.

While January was certainly a busier month for India’s ship recycling sector, after the recent decline in sub-continent levels amidst tariffs and impeding fundamentals, the ability of Indian buyers to satiate their lingering appetite has been notably abysmal. Adding a salted cherry to the injured state of Alang’s ship recycling sector was the strong reaction to Trump’s announcement on tariffs that would affect Alang, but with no recent fixtures to test the market, it has been another quiet week in India with Holi holidays keeping the local populous distracted on religious holidays.

headline: UNLUCKY, YET LUCKY!
highlights: Unstable economy. | Empty handed. | HKC underway? | Willing to engage.
body_text:
Gadani recyclers have been struggling at the bidding tables since Q3 2024 since when, they have only managed to secure 2 units thus far. Unluckily for Gadani buyers and in contrast to what is happening in India, even though domestic fundamentals have been far more stable here despite both the Pakistani Rupee that firmed 24 basis points to end the week at PKR 279.64 and local steel plate prices that are still plunging into the deep end as they recorded further declines this week, which ironically remain the highest in the industry and that too by a wide margin.

Making matters worse for the economy is the state of the nation’s treasury reserves that are facing a beating despite international personal remittances into the country helping Pakistan’s inflation across February, thanks to the prior mismanagement of funds that has compelled the government to make drastic cutbacks for non-essential sectors - Ship Recycling being one of them.
