This has seen an exacerbating performance of Pakistani recyclers at the bidding tables as the nation struggles to stabilize domestic spending, despite national inflation bouncing around the 3% market. Even the plethora of pending loans / financial aid instruments and extensions on loan repayments being granted by the U.A.E and China, the government seems to be incessantly struggling to keep all sectors of the nation running in sync.

On the flip side and luckily for the Gadani Gang, their relatively stable vessel prices have helped them watch India slide right on by and invariably slip Pakistan into 2nd place on the ship recycling market rankings, in effect, helping them negotiate and even have 2 vessels with delivered locally with another 2 recent fixtures reportedly having navigational charts for Pakistani waters on standby. As such, arrival after a month of silence, Gadani’s waterfront finally reported a fresh as another small LDT bulker greets the nation’s anchorage for recycling.

Notwithstanding, despite Pakistani recyclers making an effort, some even at testy levels, they have ended empty handed for another week as diminishing supply due to improving freight rates (dry bulk in particular) hammers the ship recycling industry overall. Pakistani recyclers have instead been busy trying to structure upgrades to their facilities to HKC standards during these trying times, and several have reportedly started the initial infrastructure work on their yards.

Yet, it seems unlikely that these facilities will be ready to operate before the June 26th deadline and likely even after, as Gadani as a destination has yet to receive HKC and subsequent SoC approvals or even recycle a single vessel under the HKC guidelines. As such, it remains to be seen just how many ship owners will be willing to engage in serious discussions – at least in the interim and until a few smaller LDT units have become the test subjects for the industry overall.

headline: ZZZZZZ?
highlights: Compliance. | Zzzzs seem back for Aliaga.
body_text:
After what seems to have been an exciting fixture that certainly raised pulses across the industry last week, Aliaga has gone quiet again this week as tonnage is non-existent for this community once again and regulations coupled with domestic fundamentals keep Turkey’s pricing in check.

Levels remain subdued and the last fixture was clearly below levels on the market rankings. Yet, given that strict compliance rules that owners have to abide by, have a cost factor attached to them, could justify the lower price on show for this particular fixture. Moreover, despite an odd private unit making the rounds, suppressed local steel plate levels and the Lira continue to place hurdles along Aliaga’s pricing trajectory, having declined other 18 basis points and ending the week at nearly TRY 36.60 against the U.S. Dollar, all while Indian / Pakistani offerings remain nearly USD 150/Ton above.

headline: HOT ASSETS & COOLER TIMES!
highlights: Unwilling. | Ramadan lull. | Jackrabbit. | Forced to face.
body_text:
With two OFAC listed VLCCs currently idling outside Chattogram port limits, it remains to be seen just what the concerned cash buyer intends do with such loaded assets given that both local banks and local authorities are unwilling to permit entry and redelivery of these assets into the country, especially given the U.S. administrations hardline stance against the Iranian regime, including those who (defacto) choose to deal with them. As the ARTEMIS III & ITAUGUA face an uncertain future awaiting at OPL, inner anchorage was whole new song and dance with over 103K LDT via 7 vessels ranging from sub-1.5K LDT to over 42K LDT units that are either awaiting delivery or were delivered to their respective end buyers.

Meanwhile, the internal situation in Bangladesh remains rife with shock as fresh news surfaced locally this week that Bangladeshi army generals were reportedly discussing the possible arrest and overthrow of the current administration, as the country continues to battle ongoing political and economic tumult. If true, this could spell disaster for the nation and its populous as the economy struggles to get unemployment numbers lowered and inflation reigned in, despite several measures reportedly in the works that have yet to see any progress in the development and infrastructure sectors.

Moreover, with Ramadan holidays incoming and the country bracing for an unprecedented 11-day break, there certainly would be no movement in domestic business activities or even local steel plate prices during this time, which remain dead on the floor at about USD 529/Ton for about two Quarters now. On the flip side, the Taka continues to jump around the U.S. Dollar like a jackrabbit as it shuttered through its share of volatility across the week and ended it, 25 basis points weaker at BDT 121.70.

Despite all of that is unfolding in the nation, the ship recycling sector in Bangladesh seems firm, albeit for the right type of unit and it could easily be that we see the odd deal concluded into Chattogram at or even slightly above prevailing rates, just so currently open buyers are able to snag a unit before the traditionally quieter Ramadan holidays commence from the end of this coming week. Moreover, this will be especially challenging for those local recyclers who are yet to initiate the necessary yard upgrades that are due to have started by Match 31st failing which, those yards will not be allowed to operate or receive NOCs on incoming vessels once the market returns from Ramadan holidays in April, in essence, forcing local recyclers to face a cooler time on the sidelines until necessary action has been initiated.

Overall, as demand has seemingly pent up and indications have come up by about USD 10/LDT, Bangladesh remains as the top ranked market in the sub-continent for another week.

highlights: VLs stuck. | Unable to beach. | Flouting rules. | Markets firm. | Backlogged.
body_text:
India is similarly taking a restricted approach on such vessels despite previous few deals having reportedly slipped through the cracks on the back of alternate / non-USD payment arrangements. These could likely also come under the microscope even more given that the U.S. State Department has reportedly sanctioned several entities involved in these sales, including even the Oil Minister of Iran. As the spotlight remains squarely on the ship recycling markets over recent times with several OFAC listed / sanctioned / dark fleet vessels still making the rounds to / from cash buyers who seem unabashedly willing to skirt international regulations for the sake of a quick buck, may soon come under fiery investigations from U.S. authorities under the current Trump administration that want to ensure no escape routes or future transmission of funds to / from such transactions occur.

How the future of recycling the world’s dark fleet unfolds in this post-sanction friendly, trade war rollercoaster world of 2025 remains to be seen. For now, it does seem as though ship recycling markets maybe heading for a firmer Q2 as the slowing supply of candidates following a recent resurgence in freight rates (particularly in the dry bulk sectors with a number of Panamax bulkers sold for recycling in January) may drive demand (and hopefully vessel pricing) due North. And while charter rates jump, oil remains anemic overall as it ended the week at USD 68.30 / barrel, while ship recycling nation currencies (except in India) recorded noteworthy declines against the U.S. Dollar, and respective local steel prices continue to record jitters keeping sentiments in check despite Indian and Pakistan’s economies registering improvements / stability. Bangladesh on the other hand continues to have even more problems with domestic violence than the revival of its economy and Turkey at the far end continues to collapse under the weight of U.S. Dollar in addition to a fresh outpouring of political protests that gripped Istanbul after the arrest of its mayor, the leading opponent against President Erdogan in the upcoming elections.

headline: POISED!
highlights: INR jumps 1%. | HKC formalities. | DASR! | 3 X (< 3K LDT)
body_text:
The Indian market seems increasingly poised to not only take in any geographically positioned tonnage or even those units with a WC India / Pakistan / Bangladesh range redelivery where a recently firmer Bangladeshi market may reject a vessel (on account of its poorer overall condition), but the Indian Rupee also reported a strong 1% increase against the U.S. Dollar closing the week out at Rs. 86.07, as did local steel plate prices record a massive USD 10/Ton jump to USD 453.33/Ton, helping local indications firm up across the week and dislodge Pakistan for the #2 spot on the market rankings.

Yet, growing questions have been surfacing of late over just how cash buyers were able to complete the recent deliveries of several OFAC listed / sanctioned vessels into Alang and how were local banks and authorities able to permit the same, given that U.S. investigations are reportedly underway. Notwithstanding, Alang of course remains ready to take in the full range of HKC units post June 26th, with Bangladesh still lagging some ways behind (in terms of yard approvals), and Pakistan yet to have seriously begun any upgrades to domestic facilities just yet. In fact, the Indian government is taking the incoming deadline seriously enough that based on initial discussions with GMS representative offices in Alang, the DG of Shipping provided several clarifications on the prospective implementation of the Hong Kong Convention (HKC) post June 26, 2025, which are highlighted as follows.

a. There will be an anticipated six-month buffer period of adjustments to the requirements. b. The International Ready for Recycling Certificate (IRRC) and the IHM on incoming vessels

are now mandatory requirements under the new rules. c. The HKC Statement of Compliance (SoC) will be replaced by the Document of Authorization to conduct Ship Recycling (DASR) and all classification societies have been authorized as Recognized Organizations (RO) by the DG of Shipping. This means that if a particular yard has an HKC SoC from IRS Class, then IRS can issue a DASR to the respective yard with the same being applicable to classes NK, LR, and BV respectively. Any Alang yard(s) without an HKC SoC will not receive a DASR and will logically not be permitted to import ships for recycling post June 26th, 2025. With such rapid progress and advances being made in India coupled with firming at the bidding tables, it is clear that Alang might after all be making the early Q2 / pre-monsoon purchasing rush that the industry has been historically acclimated to.

And certainly, just in time, especially with their Bangladeshi counterparts now entering an extended holiday period and prompt incoming deliveries from the Far East in addition to those coming in from the West of Alang will more than likely make a debut at local anchorage, making it a far busier place than that compared to what has unfolded this week i.e., a mere 3 x sub-3K LDT units totalling less than 8K LDT.

headline: EMPTYING AGAIN?!
highlights: Lying dormant. | Price moves. | Performance concerns. | Delays!
body_text:
After nearly a miserable Q1 where Pakistani port reports posted just as many arrivals as the number of months thus far, in the face of increased enquiries / offers emerging from local buyers that helped them briefly move into 2nd place on the market rankings, Gadani anchorage has finally shown promise this week as in addition to last week’s arrival that is still idling at the waterfront, a second sub 9K LDT bulker arrived and was delivered to her new owners this week. While this certainly has boosted local confidence seeing more traffic at Gadani, it has not helped raise local offerings, which remain at lower overall numbers when compared to their Indian & Bangladeshi counterparts and especially as Indian indications have jumped this week as well.

And as forecasted last week, the ever-declining local steel plate prices recorded another USD 3.5/Ton drop this week (totaling the entire decline to just about USD 26/Ton over the last four weeks alone), including the Pakistani Rupee, which fell 13 basis points and clocked the week out, breaching the coveted PKR 280 mark, at a record-breaking PKR 280.06 against the U.S. Dollar. Making matters worse is that not only are Bangladeshi recyclers entering an extend holiday break next week and Gadani recyclers stand to celebrate their upcoming vacations as well, but with Indian levels also on the move and distancing themselves from Gadani offers once again, local recyclers will likely endure a quieter time on the sidelines in the coming week(s).

Moreover, recent U.S. tariffs that have elevated domestic concerns of rising inflation to the extent that the central government has decided to maintain the prevailing interest rate at 12%, the ship recycling future heading into Q2 may not be as historically rosy as this time of the year has been for this market, especially given that issuances of large U.S. Dollar L/Cs to non-critical sectors remain far and few between, and this has very well highlighted by the meagre collection of comparatively small(er) LDT units that have announced their arrivals into Gadani across Q1.

In fact, should this market keep at pace to take in just one arrival every month, they will have the slowest year on record over the last decade, with 2023 being the slowest with just 16 deliveries throughout the entire year. There are also growing concerns over the capacity of end users in Pakistan to perform post June 26th given that they are yet to commence any serious upgrades, as compared to the neighboring competition that already has a leg-up on their ability to perform in a sustained manner once the HKC comes into effect.

As such, Pakistan certainly seems to have directed itself into a tight spot over the next several weeks despite an omnipresent desire to bid on tonnage at the bidding tables, even if they are currently lower than the competition and will likely get lower moving forward, especially if incoming international aid / financial loans fail to arrive in time.

headline: WHIFF OF THE EAST?
highlights: Corruption.
body_text:
This week, Turkey seems to have gotten a whiff of the Easterly winds from Bangladesh as huge protests descended across Istanbul due to the key opposition leader & Mayor of the city (who is entering the upcoming elections against President Erdogan) being reportedly arrested on corruption charges, risking further unrest in an already economically battered Turkey.

While local steel plate prices (both import and local steel) reported no major movements across the week, it was the Turkish Lira that devastated the local ship recycling mindset as not only did it briefly spike to over TRY 40.75 against the U.S. Dollar, but it also still closed the week having declined a whopping 3.57%, at TRY 37.91.

And like the Paksitani market, their local offerings will likely succumb to this economic pressure and fall in the coming week(s), further widening the now increasing gap with sub-continent ship recycling markets.

headline: PRICE HYPE
highlights: Caution urged. | Premiums paid. | Extension likely. | Earthly jitters.
body_text:
In local news, one of the OFAC listed VLCCs currently stuck outside Bangladesh has reportedly made moves to imminently depart Bangladeshi waters for a potential India re-delivery, whilst the other remains stranded outside without a local resale / MoA and subsequently without an NOC (No Objection Certificate) that would otherwise have permitted its entry into local waters. And with little hopes for a local resale at present, given the strong opposition from domestic authorities and banks on beaching prohibited / OFAC listed / sanctioned tonnage, her, and the unfortunate future of other sanctioned ladies like her, remains an unfolding mystery.

Meanwhile, a renewed shortage of viable recycling units for sale in addition to the looming March 31st deadline for local buyers to have initiated yard upgrades whereafter, they will not be permitted to import vessels for recycling upon resumption of normal business hours post-Eid holidays, any units that are currently on offer and are locally favored are seeing premiums above market levels from those recyclers looking to quickly book a unit prior to the deadline, thereby artificially raising the ship-recycling price floor out of Bangladesh this week. And as any potential extension on the deadline to initiate yard upgrades is unlikely to come through at this time, local ship recycling facilities who have not already done so, will urgently need to initiate yard upgrades or fail to align with HKC standards before its entry into force on June 26th of this year, risking falling out of the recycling scene entirely thereafter. This failure to extend is also delivering a lot of confusion in the local market as to the fate of vessels concluded to those recyclers who have not commenced yard upgrades and are still enroute, due to be delivered post-Eid opening. What happens to these deliveries remains to be seen.

And as indications for prompt delivery units that are of local interest seem to have rendered the illusion of a firming market, the reality of Bangladesh’s economy and even local fundamentals has failed to provide the much-needed industry-wide confidence that the interim administration has yet to deliver for nearly a year now. Moreover, even though Eid holidays have calmed the local rioting, they have also seen no movement of local steel from local recycling yards into domestic steel mills, resulting in an expected flatlining in plate prices that have remained in cold layup at about USD 529/Ton for nearly all year, and still managing to keep this market atop the market rankings for over two quarters. Even the Bangladeshi Taka reported marginal movements as it firmed a mere 10 basis points against the U.S. Dollar, ending the week at a still high BDT 121.17.

Finally, the recent earthquake that devastated neighboring Myanmar has set off panic amongst the populous that far-reaching aftershocks may reverberate through the nation in the near future and while this could create a major disruption in services, Chattogram Choppers seem like they more than have their hands full upon their return battling potential earthly jitters and administrative haltings on incoming vessels, all while Gadani’s anchorage remains the busiest of sub-continent destinations at the end of Q1 2025 and HKC upgrades are yet to commence.

headline: CONFUSION!
highlights: OFAC concerns. | Tsunami of Tumult. | Margarita surprise. | Freight deprives. | HKC looms.
body_text:
For now, like 2024, the 2025 tsunami of economic tumult continues to surprise week-after-week with macro fundamentals taking turns to shake up ever-changing sentiments across the board. Oil has started to jitter like the stock markets as despite registering declines through the week (and being low overall), it ended at a ‘higher than last week’ level of USD 69.40/barrel, as oil markets remain cautious on the back of recently announced Iranian and Venezuelan sanctions. On the flip side (and rather surprisingly), charter rates declined this week across the dry bulk board as nearly all sectors (Handies, Panamaxes, Capes, and even Supras) registered falls, dragging the overall Baltic Dry Sea Freight Index down this week, which was followed by a minor uptick in recycling enquiries from sellers at the bidding tables. And while some of the discussions are still ongoing, local anchorages delivered a Margarita Mix of surprises as Pakistan took in more vessels than India this week, despite a clear overall decline in the number of arrivals & deliveries across the sub-continent board.

Zooming into domestic fundamentals of ship recycling markets, steel plate prices played opposite roles in Pakistan and India as while Indian levels recorded an impressive jump, Pakistani levels continue to bleed out as they have declined non-stop over the last month now, all while Bangladeshi and Chinese levels continue to flatline at the bottom of the pool. Even the U.S. Dollar remained undecided against these currencies as it made firm improvements against some, while losing ground against others. Bangladesh seems surprisingly bullish despite ongoing Eid holidays and the end of the Holy Month of Ramadan, likely on the back of a few hungry recyclers, whilst competing India and Pakistan struggled to keep up even though there remains a distinct lack in the availability of units for a recycling sale as we end lucky number Week 13 and head into Q2 of the year. Prices in Bangladesh are slightly higher than USD 450/LT LDT on certain select / favored units (such as tankers and containers) coming in from the Far East and this has left India & Pakistan gravitating towards even smaller geographically positioned units to satisfy their own permeating demand.

Finally, with the HKC June 26th deadline approaching closer and even the deadline within which to begin yard upgrades in Bangladesh by March 31st has not been extended as yet, a healthy number of domestic recyclers will be unable to import vessels post-Eid. Pakistan, meanwhile, is at the very early stages of starting upgrades and needs to do much more work in the months ahead in order to stay relevant, whilst Turkey surfs away into the distance on the back of a receding Lira. Q2? Phew!

headline: DAMPENING!
highlights: Slower & softer. | Losing out. | Tariff fears. | Infra projects.
body_text:
Of late, it has been a slower period for Alang recyclers on account of India’s weakening offerings and Pakistan’s inadvertent passing India into 2nd place on the marking rankings, in addition to minimal sales (apart from the rare few HKC only green vessels for India only redelivery and specialist nonferrous and offshore units), and finally, softening / dampening fundamentals that have decimated local sentiments over the last 6 – 8 weeks.

Fortunately, this week, as both Bangladeshi and Pakistani markets were busy celebrating the end of the month of Ramadan and Pakistani fundamentals were being hammered, Indian plate prices jumped a massive USD 9/Ton this week and are on their way to USD 455/Ton, mercifully (yet barely) above where local recyclers are comfortable that local offerings are just about aligning with domestic fundamentals. Even the Indian Rupee that only recently saw the better part of Rs. 87 against the U.S. Dollar (nearly breaching Rs. 88), has finally been firming once again as it ended the week 55 basis points firmer at Rs. 85.53.

This recent dampening of Indian sentiments that saw Pakistan slide up into 2nd place also saw India drop into 3rd place on the local port position via the number and total LDT at Alang anchorage this week, as a mere 2 ships and 6K LDT are being / have been delivered locally. And while Pakistan has managed to maintain the 2nd spot in the market rankings, it has an aggressive Bangladesh that has been capturing most of the headlines and most of the (geographically viable) market fixtures at some top numbers over the preceding few weeks, all while India and Pakistan start to lag and clearly have some catching up to do, especially in this most recent wake of tonnage delinquency.

Moreover, being the 2nd largest Asian Economy, the effects of Trump’s tariffs are also expected to affect India the most given his recent blanket announcement of 25% tariffs including fresh ones on all imported vehicles and thereby, vehicle parts coming into the United States, of which, India is a supplier of, including being a major pharmaceuticals exporter to the States, which will certainly see India’s economy take a hit through 2025. Oil sanctions too are making a situation for a heavily oil dependant nation such as India, that much more watchful of the U.S. government’s upcoming moves given that the nation’s economy is traversing through recently buoyant times.

Notwithstanding, the positive news on the horizon is that the Indian government continues to make efforts at ensuring that sector specific exports from specific countries (including India) are tariffed in a more structured way so as to ensure smooth ongoing trade with the U.S., thereby keeping currencies stable. Moreover, even though major tax breaks for low – median income individuals and families is already seeing an uptick in India’s consumer spending index, the much-needed and far delayed infrastructure projects that would greatly help local steel plate prices and in effect, the world’s largest ship recycling destination i.e. Alang, become a booming place (from a purchasing standpoint) once again, remains out of the government’s collective minds at the moment.

headline: TINY GAINS!
highlights: Attempting. | Ice cream truck. | HKC!!! | Ahead of India.
body_text:
Despite attempts to get back into the buying at competitive levels in recent times, Pakistan has yet to really transact on a significant portion of any of the market tonnage that has come available since the start of the year. Other than a handful of small LDT / geographically better suited (for a Pakistan re-delivery) units that have been concluded to local buyers with largely dormant plots, a rampant Bangladeshi market remains significantly ahead of a seemingly improving Gadani.

Moreover, Pakistani offerings remain marginally ahead of those from neighboring India where Indian fundamentals marked noteworthy improvements this week, all while local fundamentals continue sinking in a sticky mess that seems to be dragging them down by the week as not only did local steel plate prices fall about USD 4/Ton and end the week at about USD 624 / Ton (a drop that has totaled nearly USD 40/Ton over the last 4 weeks), but even the Pakistani Rupee firmed a mere 5 basis points against the U.S. Dollar as it still ended the week at PKR 280.04, certainly in record-high territory for the currency.

How this will affect Gadani’s purchasing mindset at the bidding tables post-Eid remains to be seen. For now, the Gadani Gang has managed to takeover the ice cream truck as over the last couple of weeks, the industry has seen a vessel arrive locally every week including this one, where a couple of units welcomed the waterfront. Of these, one is a really tiny unit that was likely trading regional waters. Nonetheless, Gadani’s anchorage now has more units and LDT than neighboring Alang, something the industry has not witnessed in a very long time, and this should keep respective Gadani recyclers engaged through a time the number of local units delivered into Pakistan can be counted on one hand – and that too through the span of an entire quarter.

Gadani recyclers have yet to also make any moves towards upgrading the respective recycling infrastructure and ship recycling practices at their yards to HKC standards, in addition to receiving their SOC (Statement of Compliance) Certifications’ from recognized / IACS societies, something that nearly all Alang ship recyclers are fully prepared for and Chattogram Choppers are slowly getting their inertia moving on from static now that those who have yet to initiate upgrades of their own will fail to receive NoCs from April, which will certainly push their pedal further in. What seems certain is that a few (if not a majority) of Pakistani ship recycling yards will face recycling restrictions from the authorities post June 26th, unless by some miracle, speedy action by the Gadani Gang is initiated to get their respective yards ready just in time.

For now, however, as we stand on the precipice of Q2 2025, Pakistani ship recyclers can at least be buoyed by the fact that they are ahead of India in the marking rankings, especially after a miserable showing from Alang over previous weeks (on account of their declining fundamentals), and the Gadani recyclers would certainly take these tiny gains after an altogether forgettable last few years spent largely on the sidelines of the ship recycling industry.

headline: INCOGNITO!
highlights: TRY 40?
body_text:
In the face of a rapidly declining Turkish Lira that has now recorded the largest decline amongst ship-recycling nations across Week 13 of Q1 2025, plummeting over 1.15% to TRY 37.99 against the U.S. Dollar, Aliaga recyclers were left in shock and retreated back to Eid celebrations as the sentiment post-Eid is certainly going to be one of sheer alarm, especially as the Lira is a breath away from TRY 38 and probably on the verge of jumping past TRY 40 within the next month.

And whilst on holiday, even though there has been no trading of local steel plate prices, rumors of a collapse are circulating and only Week 14 / 15 will reveal just how the local market is reacting to the collapsing Lira. Turkey’s inflation, though improving, also remains precarious at nearly 40% (down from the highs of 80% only 3 years ago) and has seen a near collapse in vessel purchases from Aliaga over the same time. Notwithstanding, a smaller LDT sale is rumored to have taken place into Aliaga this week and will only be confirmed next week.

Aliaga has certainly gone incognito…and limping in the dark again.

headline: VOICEMAIL!
highlights: Best placed. | Questions arise. | Deadline to extend? | Dry Week
body_text:
It has been a voicemail week for the Chattogram Choppers as the ship recycling fraternity was collectively celebrating Eid and the end of the Holy month of Ramadan this week, resulting in steel plate prices that have started Q2 2025, flatlined at the bottom of the pool where they have been for about 7 months now. Moreover, even the 2024 experiment by the Bangladeshi government to permit the Taka to be controlled by market forces, saw it decline over 21 basis points / BDT 11 during this time, ended the week at BDT 121.82, likely to pass BDT 122 in the next week(s) as the pending 37% tariff truffle against Bangladesh awaits delivery to its economy.

The key ‘beneficiary’ of these tariffs, which are currently at 20%, will be the Readymade Garments (RMG) sector and is expected to be hit the hardest as they have been, ever since the collapse of the government in June 2024 that resulted in local violence, rioting, and ongoing unemployment. Moreover, despite being the firmest placed sub-continent market atop GMS’s market rankings, local recyclers have started to question what the overall impact on prices further down the line might be, as the markets saw local offers being scaled back by about USD 5 - USD 10/LDT whilst other end buyers decided to take a wait and watch approach entirely.

And despite the supply of tonnage being at concerning levels over the last few weeks and freight rates cooling off this week as well, the expectation that the BSBRA will again extend the HKC deadline to begin yard upgrades from March 31st to a later date remains up in the air as authorities and governmental offices remain closed on the back of ongoing Eid holidays and end buyers are still pressuring authorities for an extension, as they remains keen to fill their plots before the HKC comes into force on June 26th, 2025 and certainly as the immediate future of incoming deliveries hangs in the balance.

Weakening prices and the ongoing diminished supply of viable units also saw a drop in the number of market and private local fixtures, and subsequent arrivals at the local waterfront, where local recyclers reported no fresh arrivals this week, other than a handful of prior deliveries, including vessel ‘THREE STAR’ that had been stranded at anchorage since January of this year.

On the local economic front, the nation recorded the largest ever international personal remittances back into the country to the tune of aver USD 3 Billion, which saw domestic reserves being actively replenished through the volatile uncertainty that is currently affecting the economy and the decisions of the interim administration. And due to the ongoing holidays, there remains little of importance to report from Bangladesh, as Week 14 winds to a halt with nothing of significance to report.

headline: TARIFF TRUFFLE!
highlights: Tariff time. | Reciprocal moves. | Hard liner. | Post-tariff world. | Troubled Waters.
body_text:
The global ship recycling sector also witnessed some interesting activity as not only have local steel plate prices continued to climb in India, but they also fell in China and flatlined in both Bangladesh and Pakistan. On the currencies front, while some reported improvements (India), others declined with Turkey surprising the industry, reporting no change this week. Recycling activity too has somewhat inevitably been picking up in sub-continent markets over these last few weeks as the number of deliveries greatly improved of late, and this week has seen the various waterfronts take a beating with no fresh arrivals in Bangladesh, while India and Pakistan snared just one each. Even Bangladeshi prices that climbed briefly following on a dearth of tonnage, seem to have settled as there is no tonnage to bid on, and Indian & Pakistani recyclers remain cautious & tentative in their offerings on fresh tonnage in light of the recent U.S. sanctions saga, while simultaneously observing markets to see what the overall impact on prices and potential renewed dumping of cheap Chinese steel into the sub-continent could spell for their purchases, before presenting fresh offers on tonnage at numbers that could conceivably be far lower in a post tariff world.

With minimum activity taking place in Bangladesh, Pakistan, and Turkey thanks to Eid celebrations and holidays that have kept most markets closed through this week, the outcome of Bangladeshi restriction on imports remains unresolved on the back of the March 31st deadline for local recyclers within which, infrastructure updates at all domestic ship recycling yards were to commence, leaving the fate of pending deliveries through the upcoming tide(s), an uncertainty. Overall, while we may be witnessing an overreaction to a hardline, exaggerated, and thoughtless action from the highest office in the U.S., rather than collectively forecasting doom and gloom for global trade, a more pragmatic long-term view may be needed to navigate through these troubled waters together.

headline: ALERT ‘N’ ALIVE!
highlights: Most sensitive | Limited supply. | Not dramatic.
body_text:
Despite being the most sensitive of sub-continent markets to unfolding global events and global market turmoil, India the most part, has been for cautiously waiting on the sidelines to see how Trump’s tariff tantrums play out before committing afresh on any of the slim pickings of recycling vessels that are currently floating around the bidding tables.

And despite Trump announcing 26% tariffs on India across the board, the reaction from India has been surprisingly filtered thus far, with no news of retaliatory tariffs or retreating vessel offerings (as yet), especially as domestic fundamentals continue to collectively strengthen through the week. Not only did local steel plate prices climb another USD 9/Ton to over USD 473.56/Ton (pushing local purchases on dry vessels further in the green), but even the Indian Rupee firmed down to Rs. 85.50 (from the highs approaching Rs. 88), providing further confidence to Alang buyers, especially as their Bangladeshi counterparts are pulling back on their offers by up to USD 10/Ton this week and Pakistani recyclers continue to take a bite out of India’s tonnage buffet.

And while most of the market tonnage in recent weeks has filtered through to the far better positioned Bangladeshi market, with India being the one destination that has been left to only taking HKC only limited vessels and specialist units, the recent global market turmoil may still see more vessels arrive for recycling in the near future and a greater supply of vessels are therefore expected to head to India and Pakistan later into Q2. Whether levels hold at prevailing rates remains to be seen, especially as some recyclers are already taking the opportune time to talking down the market, to take stock of unfolding market falls. But the reality is that steel prices and local currencies have not been impacted to such a dramatic overall effect (as yet), to justify a sudden decline in offerings.

Meanwhile, Alang anchorage continues to simmer on the number of its local arrivals with only a small LDT arrival of a supply vessel, as India seems increasingly destined for an empty port position, especially in the face of all of the global craziness unfolding. India’s economy, however, seems to be on the right trajectory especially as the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) announced that it would likely cut interest rates by 25 basis points in the coming week, indicating a greater sense of urgency to induce local spending after the recent tax breaks.

And while this could further assist India’s ship recycling sector on large U.S. Dollar transactions when the time comes, the lack of tonnage at the bidding tables is likely to see this market spend the next week(s) on a quieter note. Quiet.

headline: MINI REVIVAL?
highlights: Smaller LDT deals. | No impact. | Taking seriously. | HKC upgrades?
body_text:
A mini revival of sorts in Pakistan, bought on primarily due to India’s recently diminishing levels that inadvertently thrust the Gadani Gang into 2nd place on the market rankings, has brought the Pakistani market back into the picture of late, with a series of smaller LDT, mostly local Middle Eastern owned, geographically positioned sales to local buyers – and this week was no exception with another fresh arrival and with the most amount of LDT in the Indian sub-continent markets this week, given that 20K LDT is currently delivered or lying in wait at anchorage awaiting delivery.

The overall impact of Pakistan’s recent moves in the sub-continent ship recycling markets has been rather limited so far however, with most of the larger LDT deals of the year (including a cape, several LNGs and larger tankers) ending up either in Bangladesh or neighboring India. However, Pakistani buyers need to really engage on incoming LDT after having spent a prolonged period on the sidelines, in order to sustain this momentum. Notwithstanding, fundamentals are deliberately conspiring to keep local offerings in check, especially as local steel plate prices lie flatlined for the last week at USD 624/Ton (almost USD 40/Ton lower than previous highs), all while the Pakistani Rupee loses another 26 basis points, to end the week at PKR 280.34 against the U.S. Dollar.

The recent tariffs placed across the globe have also not spared the Pakistani economy where Trump announced an additional 29% blanket tariffs on all imports from Pakistan, which could seriously affect Pakistan’s textiles and garments exports (like Bangladesh). And while this could spell disaster for the domestic economy, which is once against in the thralls of rising inflation, Pakistan’s Finance Minister sees a silver lining via opening possible new avenues for negotiating a “balanced economic relationship”, not only with the U.S., but with other nations and economies worldwide. And although this strategy maybe present viable long-term opportunities for the nation, in the short-term, the domestic economic situation will likely dip for the worse.

Notwithstanding, all that is unfolding, it is good to see some recycling transactions finally being concluded to local recyclers, all while yard upgrades are yet to be taken seriously, with several end users reportedly only now starting infrastructure works and investments in order to get up to HKC standards ahead of its entry into force in June of this year. For the rest, it maybe an even longer time on the sidelines until their certifications come through.

Overall, with Raman holidays keeping the local ship recycling community distracted with celebrations, the week ended on a quiet note, just like the rest of its sub-continent neighbors.

headline: JUST LIKE THE REST…
body_text:
Similar to the performances of its sub-continent ship recycling associates, Aliaga recyclers spent the week busy in celebrations with nothing to report from their end this week. No movement in local or import steel plate prices reported, no sales reported, and the biggest surprise of all, no movement reported from the Turkish Lira, which, for the first time in a very long time, reported no change this week. Moreover, being the one ship recycling destination to have faced only 10% of Trump’s tariffs this week, which it is seeking to negotiate further down, the economic hammer from Trump’s recent actions might mercifully not affect this market as bad. But to what extent is that any better from what Turkey has been going through over the last couple of years?

As tonnage availability remains amiss, there remains nothing to report from Turkey, yet again.

headline: EXTENSION EXPECTED.
highlights: Not yet in place. | Ministry at work. | Price woes. | HKC + Tariffs
body_text:
Despite local rumors that the Department of Environment had approved an extension to the March 31st deadline within which, Chattogram yard owners must have initiated the necessary upgrades to ensure their ship recycling facilities are conforming to the standards & requirements of the HKC within June 26th of this year, this does not seem to have been the case as this Department has no jurisdiction over NOC issuances and SRFP extensions, instead only being concerned with annual yard permissions and vessel visits to local ports. In fact, the Ministry of Industries has been occupied with the transfer of responsibilities to the newly formed Ship Recycling Board and it is this department that is expected to grant said extension upon their return from Eid Holidays next week, especially as the fate of several incoming vessels / deliveries for the upcoming tide(s) hang(s) in the balance.

Meanwhile, there has not been much of meaningful economic or political news emanating from the country over the last couple of weeks due to ongoing religious celebrations across the nation, which have reportedly been the longest in the nation’s history. And in keeping in line with religious traditions, record-breaking incoming personal remittances and monetary gifts helped boost the nation’s domestic reserves to well over USD 21 Billion, further facilitating Bangladesh’s foreign exchange and treasury reserves. Similar to India, this will only help ensure domestic recyclers have a steady stream of finance / funding needed to help with purchases (current and future) that are still ongoing, even in the face of a declining supply of recycling tonnage, which is clearly evident from this week’s arrivals where 2 really small units greeted Chattogram’s anchorage.

And with fundamentals and international tariff news keeping local prices in check for the most part, especially as the Trump administration announced 30% tariffs on Bangladesh and reversed course on them days later, resulted in the Bangladeshi Taka strengthening against the U.S. Dollar and ending the week 13 basis points stronger at BDT 121.76. On account of the local holidays, local steel plate prices too have logically remained flatlined (on account of the lack of domestic steel trade) and remained where they have been for a while now (USD 529/Ton). This has delivered a confusing time for Bangladeshi recyclers post Eid holidays – with local indications and demand nosediving on the back of global tariff announcements, before coming surging back up to current levels once the 90-day suspension was announced.

Overall, with deadline extensions expected for yards that have not begun improving their facilities in order to keep operating when the Hong Kong Convention comes into force on June 26th this year, along with the 90 day pause on tariffs that could rear its head up against the local economy from July, will all come wet-wrapped in the midst of a likely crazy monsoon that certainly doesn’t bode for a meaningful Q2 in Bangladesh.

headline: TARIFF TAINTED!
highlights: Volatile week. | Stock surge/plunge. | Tariffs rule. | 90 day pause. | Extension due.
body_text: Although the 90-day suspension seems to have given recyclers some reprieve for the time being, the deadline realistically stands a mere quarter away. In the interim, oil has volleyed like a beach ball in the wind, declining all the way to USD 56/barrel mid-week (lowest levels seen since 2020), before climbing back up to USD 61.50/barrel where it ended the week, and future declines are still expected as OPEC+ countries re-affirmed their decision to increase output despite tit-for-tat trade wars raising global economic uncertainty and rising lack of energy demands abound. Even the U.S. Dollar spiked briefly against all ship recycling nation currencies before settling down with a surprising result, where even the Lira made decent gains against the Dollar. And global trade markets too continued to take a dunk in the tariff pool as freight rates cooled, although they did even out towards the end of the week and report minor gains. What comes of this dip in rates remains to be seen since no fresh tonnage has made its way onto the bidding tables of late. And this has demonstrated itself in plain sight at the respective anchorages this week as India (technically) reports its first ‘empty’ report, while Pakistan impressively takes in the most tonnage in the sub-continent. Through it all, Turkey continues to idle in stand-by, waiting for the opportune moment to set into gear – as long as there is some tonnage to feed into any of the markets at this time.

headline: RESPECTING RELATIONS!
highlights: Seemingly unaffected. | Steel key. | Short window. | Busy Q3?
body_text:
Despite all of the unfolding tariff drama across the world, Alang has been remarkably unaffected for the most part, especially as the Indian government had played it strategically with Trump even before he took office on January 20th, when PM Modi made several visits to the U.S. in order to address future trade between the nations. And although tariffs were initially imposed on India, the 90-day pause in addition to ongoing bilateral discussions between the administrations is likely to yield far greater results for the Indian economy post July, especially given how tenaciously volatile 2025 has already proven itself to be thus far. With January – February flooding the markets with units to a seriously muted supply of tonnage through March – April, which has left India devoid of any fresh arrivals at the waterfront this week, with the only vessel idling outside being an arrival from last week that is still awaiting delivery.

Meanwhile, the Indian Rupee, which has been a bane for local recyclers, continues its predictably volatile dance against the U.S. Dollar as it lost 80 basis points and ended the week at Rs. 86.05, having nearly approached Rs. 87 by mid-week. Even local steel plate prices fell by about USD 6/Ton overall, despite having made a recovery towards the end of the week. This has seen some local concern about what happens to these fundamentals from next week as the U.S. – China tit-for-tat tariff twitter-spat has yet to find a middle ground before imported steel plate prices can find stable footing once again, especially now that Chinese steel plate levels themselves plummeted over USD 15/Ton this week and ended the week at USD 293/Ton, well below their usual playing field of USD 300/Ton.

Logically, elevated local concerns about the potential dumping of cheaper products into India and competing markets due to a flood of cheap Chinese billets and far cheaper Chinese steel, which ship recyclers will have to contend with and this will more than likely drag vessel prices down with them, even though local punitive measures to prevent any undercutting is already in place. For now, despite assertions of a special relationship with the Trump regime, India will likely still be subject to its share of tariffs under new U.S. decrees even though the 90 day pause on activity may give recyclers a short window to import vessels, all while Pakistan continues to take larger slices of the available tonnage pie.

On the HKC front, and unlike their competing neighbours, Alang recyclers are full prepared for the advent of the HKC as local authorities have even gone to the extent of aligning necessary paperwork and formalities on all incoming vessels post June 26th, something that was highlighted in a previous edition of the GMS Weekly (ask us for a copy). On the domestic front, other than the ongoing deliverance of American financial hiccups, not much has changed with India’s economy over the last week as all key figures and trajectories are still pointing in the right direction. Q3 seems like it is gearing up to be one of the busiest times for the Alang market, especially considering how 2025 is playing out so far.

headline: INSULATED?
highlights: Slim pickings. | Smaller LDT. | Eyes locked. | 8,000 points.
body_text:
Despite Pakistan emerging as a viable ship recycling destination once again, the supply has trickled down to slim pickings of vessels on the bidding tables that have primarily been geographically positioned Far Eastern units, which remain better suited heading to a far more bullish Bangladeshi market, as trading markets / freight rates start to favor ship owners all over again - even on vintage / over-aged tonnage. As such, there have only been a handful of mostly regionally owned vessels of smaller LDT units heading to Gadani recyclers, even though demand is there to acquire any larger units that may come available. And with their firmer (than India) prices on show and even firmer indications coming forth this week, it was no surprise to see this market conclude the most tonnage in the sub-continent as local recyclers took in more LDT than neighboring Indian and Bangladeshi anchorages combined.

Local fundamentals, meanwhile, remain in a state of flux as not only have local steel plate prices finally settled (after falling over USD 40/Ton over March) at USD 624/Ton over the last couple of weeks, but the Pakistani Rupee Pakistan also resumes its slow devaluing trudge against the U.S. Dollar after it briefly gained a lot of ground mid-week, yet lost 10 basis points overall and declined to PKR 280.06 as the week ended.

And just like the rest of the world, Pakistan has not been entirely insulated from the now- suspended tariff wars that are largely playing out between the U.S. and China, in an increasingly retaliatory manner. Yet, all eyes will be firmly placed on the next moves from either side, as this unpredictable drama surely has its share of twists and turns yet to come, especially for the Indian sub-continent steel and ship recycling markets, given that Chinese steel plate has already plummeted about USD 15/Ton this week and the fear is that cheaper competitive steel products will imminently flood this market causing steel trade between domestic ship recycling yards and local steel mills to be severely affected and likely result in further declining Paksitani steel values.

In the interim, local recyclers have bigger fish to fry as with pending HKC upgrades from a bulk of domestic ship recycling yards are yet to commence at pace and this will have even greater implications for Gadani ship recyclers in a post Q3 world as not only will local recyclers be barred from importing vessels for recycling, but the tariff wars are also expected to resume, which could affect the nation’s economy moving forward. With monsoons being in full swing at that time and India leading Pakistan on the pricing chart more often than not, a healthy collection of Gadani ship recyclers might have to rapidly make amends in order to continue operating in a post June 26th

Overall, despite the Pakistani stock exchange plunging over 8,000 points on the back of economic hiccups experienced throughout the week, the nation’s financial position remains in decent standing and able to assist local recycling purchases through the interim.

headline: WAIT…WHAT?!?!
highlights: One eye open.
body_text:
The Turkish market really surprised industry players this week as a myriad of fundamentals defied explanation and reacted contrary to how much of the industry reacted to Trumps tariff tantrum this week as on the one hand, both local and import steel plate prices declined by USD 10/ton and USD 20/Ton respectively, but the Turkish Lira amazingly ended the week on a positive note, having firmed 10 basis points against the U.S. Dollar and closing the week out at a still whopping / record breaking TRY 37.94.

The supply of vessels to Aliaga, like the rest of the industry, remains lament-worthy, as does the number of available recyclers who are still operating with one eye open. Mercifully, the 90 day pause on tariffs should help keep local offerings where they are…for now.

headline: EXTENSION EXCITEMENT!
highlights: Not until 27th. | Frantic scramble.
body_text: Yard inspections are reportedly underway this week as the BSBA seeks to grant extensions on the deadline to begin HKC upgrades to facilities from March 31st. However, late (at the time of writing), news from our Bangladeshi offices reported that key personnel within the newly formed Ship Recycling Board are currently traveling overseas on official matters until April 27th, only then will any viable extension be granted. This has left a bunch of local arrivals, stranded outside Bangladesh without their respective No Objection Certificates (NOCs), unable to enter port limits. This will certainly spell trouble for the next batch of incoming vessels within minimum fuel, to be delivered promptly within the subsequent tide, certainly sending some of the incoming ‘as is’ units deeper into the red. It is now a frantic scramble as Chattogram recyclers are rapidly engaging various department heads in coming to a swifter resolution as L/C interest charges too are likely to start as these vessels lay idling awaiting delivery.

headline: EXPLOITING EXTENSIONS!
highlights: 90 day pause. | Knock on effects. | Reciprocal rules. | Tonnage deprived. | Deadline extends?
body_text: The 90-day pause has brought some respite from what was expected to be a busy second half to the year - in terms of a supply of backlogged vintage ships for recycling sale including many 90s built bulkers and containers that have managed to over-extend their respective trading lives. Conversely, on the back of the recently firming freight markets, recycling destinations are being deprived of tonnage once again causing demand and prices to stay steady, especially as we stand before another crazy monsoon a mere 6 weeks away and local fundamentals display their respective shares of volatility. The U.S. Dollar shuffles up the week with its mixed performance against recycling nation currencies, and steel plate prices start to display unfavorable signs all over again. As such, this perhaps is as good a time for non-HKC yards to concentrate on facility upgrades, all while the authorities in Bangladesh are yet to confirm an extension beyond the original March 31st deadline for yards to have begun yard upgrades until June 26th after which, their future operations would be denied. While Pakistani recyclers still have some ways to go with their upgrades, Turkey at the far end has nearly all fundamentals decline as it resumes its journey into the abyss of despair.

headline: BOUNCING BACK!
highlights: Volatility eases. | Financially fixed | Taking advantage? | ‘Pedal to the metal’.
body_text:
Fresh off the 90-day tariff pause announcement for countries worldwide and similar to the market in Bangladesh, India seems to have resumed its form (in part). And although there still remains the spectre of potentially alarming reciprocal moves between China and the U.S., which Alang recyclers are eagerly monitoring, for the time being however, the tariff volatility has certainly eased local sentiments as no immediate knock-on effects have made themselves known thus far. Yet, volatility in key fundamentals continues as despite the INR registering an impressive 75 basis point jump to end the week at Rs. 85.45 against the U.S. Dollar, local steel plate prices declined USD 5/Ton, in the face of improving Chinese plate prices that firmed in the same amount.

Nonetheless, after last week’s maddening economic uncertainty that nearly halted global trade and resulted in Alang offers being immediately reduced or even entirely withdrawn from the bidding tables, prices and demand have subsequently improved on the back of the pause this week, leaving India 2nd on the market rankings once again. And this has immediately presented itself at Alang’s waterfront this week as India was the destination with the most vessels and tonnage idling / delivered to their respective recyclers this week.

And while Indian official are due to meet with the Trump team in the coming weeks, in order to engage in further bilateral trade talks between the nations (especially as India is increasingly becoming a prominent international player in the auto and medicinal exports sectors), the overall economic forecast for the country (as a ship recycling destination) does seem far rosier than its neighbouring competition. Moreover, with well over USD 666 Billion in treasury reserves, Indian ship recyclers are certainly financially well-aided on any upcoming recycling transactions, no matter the shape or size. Retail inflation too has reportedly dipped as low-income individuals and families incumbered by tax burdens are free to spend even more of their disposable income, further bolstering the lower and middle classes, which are the largest in the nation, including the over 100,000 labourers and yard workers at Alang.

And while the nations finances are headed in the right direction, buyers in Alang remain keen to get their hands on any of the slim pickings of vessels that are being paraded on the bidding tables and that too finally at levels above those from Pakistan, which itself is starting to show signs of disarray at the local anchorage. Moreover, as Bangladeshi recyclers put the ‘pedal to the metal’ with upgrades to most of their facilities up to HKC standards, leaving India with a lower advantage in a post July 1st

HKC world, save for the perennial love affair of Alang buyers with specialist / SS / Non-Ferrous / Cruise vessels.

headline: POSITIVELY SINKING!
highlights: Back to bottom. | Sales recorded. | Back to positive. | Engaging time.
body_text:
Despite leading India for a few short weeks and hammering away a collection of purchases and even more impressive number of local deliveries on the back of firming local sentiments and prices, which themselves improved only recently when the global economic situation was far more stable (pre-tariffs), Pakistani recyclers have managed to sink themselves to the bottom of the Indian sub- continent market rankings once again this week. Indeed, several sales were recorded to starving Gadani recyclers who spent a significant time on the sidelines – a diet that primarily included small(er) LDT bulkers and offshore units (such as barges and tugs) from regional owners with geographically conveniently positioned vessels.

In contrast, this week was far less rosy as there have been no fresh arrivals reported and the only two deliveries were arrivals from weeks prior. Moreover, fundamentals aren’t doing that much better either as other than a local steel plate price that’s managed to start flatlining over the last 3 weeks (after plummeting USD 40/Ton in a month) at USD 624/Ton, the Pakistani Rupee itself declined to well above PKR 280 against the U.S. Dollar (below which, it has managed to stay under for the longest time) to close the week out PKR 280.48 (having spiked to nearly Rs. 281.45 during the week). Blending both of the above into a toxic cocktail of a serious shortage of tonnage and a far more aggressive India and even Bangladesh saw Paksitani recyclers positively sinking to the bottom of the board this week.

On the broader domestic front, with Chinese steel plate prices firming towards their baseline USD 300/Ton once again, coupled with the possible redirection of tariff-afflicted cheaper Chinese steel into the local market, could see Pakistani steel plate prices starting to slide in the coming weeks, especially if these tariff wars continue unabated. Moreover, the result of recent tariffs is also seeing a massive sell-off of U.S. Dollars amidst the populous on the back of rising concerns and a loss of confidence in Team Trump, including their ongoing administrative policies that are adversely affecting the lives of hundreds of millions of people worldwide. This could see the U.S. Dollar start to devalue in the coming weeks, especially if the reportedly dramatic sell-off continues at pace.

Finally, an upcoming FY 2025 – 2026 budget in the first week of June, followed by the HKC in July and all of it being delivered in a drowning Monsoon season, is certainly gearing up to be an engaging time for Gadani recyclers, especially as they slip to third on the market rankings against the backdrop of a firming India and even firmer Bangladesh. What is to come of Pakistan over the next quarter remains to be seen. For now, however, as all sub-continent locations look to make the most out of the 90-day tariff pause, it will be interesting to see if Gadani buyers can get their hands on any of the tonnage that comes around in the interim, or will they spend another quarter on the sidelines again?

headline: DOWN THE HATCH!!
highlights: Below USD 300/Ton | Oh, Constantinople!
body_text: As the single market being hammered the worst by the sheer brunt of its economic collapse (to where inflation was over 75% and is still at a massive 38%.10 at the end of March), the Lira having dropped by nearly 450% in the last 5 years, the maddening shortage of recycling tonnage, volatile steel plate prices, ongoing political riots, and (impeding) regulations that have created a chokehold on Aliaga’s ship recycling sector, this week proved to be adding cherries to the cake of Turkish misery as not only did both import and local steel plate prices fall by about USD 12/Ton and USD 10/Ton respectively (having declined USD 20/Ton and USD 10/Ton respectively just the week prior), resulting in local offerings across the board declining by about USD 10/MT and under USD 300/Ton on all units across the board, all at a time that both Indian and Bangladeshi levels on the bidding tables seem to gearing up for slightly firmer offerings. The Turkish Lira too resumed its unimpeded decline against the U.S. Dollar as the Lira itself fell another 35 basis points this week, closing it out at another record-breaking TRY 38.09. The compounding lack of shortage in the availability of tonnage is just the final…

headline: HKC STUCK!
highlights: Inspections ongoing. | Upgrades a must. | Approved / Rejected? | Turbulent.
body_text:
The Bangladeshi ship recycling sector came to a virtual standstill this week given that no fresh No Objection Certificates (NOCs) have been issued for over two weeks now, thereby suspending nearly all active negotiations with local recyclers on potential units currently at the bidding tables, in addition to the likely redirection of incoming units towards India / Pakistan range as only now are Bangladeshi authorities starting to inspect local ship recycling yards to ensure that the level of infrastructure upgrades needed towards attaining an HKC Statement of Compliance (SoC) by its gradually approaching deadline, had been initiated by the respective recyclers ever since the original deadline of January 31st to initiate such upgrades was extended to March 31st, and a 2nd

Before any further extensions will be considered or granted, especially to those facilities that have units idling outside or even on the way, that indeed the necessary infrastructure works have started and permissions on incoming units belonging to these recyclers could (hopefully) be granted allowing these units inside. But with the nation officially having confirmed to abide by the rules of the convention with its entry into force by June 26th, a mere 8 weeks away, the pressure is on the authorities to ensure the nation will deliver as assured and is the reason behind the seeming unwillingness of local authorities to ‘play ball’ with local recyclers. As a result, Chattogram has not reported any fresh arrivals of recycling units into Chattogram this week (on account of those pesky missing NOCs), all while a couple of last week’s arrivals to recently approved SoC yards of which, there are reportedly a total of 7 thus far ,managed to deliver to their respective owners this week.

On the positive side, our Bangladeshi offices reported late Sunday that the Director General of Shipping did visit local ship recycling yards over the weekend and was pleased with the overall upgrades done so far, confirming that NOCs would be issued to certain yards with satisfactory progress. Although how many ship recycling yards with disproportionate degrees of upgrades stand to be given permissions and whether the vessels idling outside do indeed belong to this freshly approved (or yet to be rejected) batch, remains to be seen. On the worst-case scenario, any yard not yet HKC approved will have to wait to import vessels or display substantial progress of updates before they can continue operations and open future L/Cs.

This has put a virtual pause on the domestic ship recycling industry whilst the results from the inspections (potential re-inspections for some) are completed. And with domestic fundamentals performing horrendously – local steel plate prices opening post Eid at USD 478/Ton (a whopping USD 61/Ton collapse from USD 529/Ton) and the Taka losing 10 basis points to close the week out at BDT 121.99 against the U.S. Dollar - the ongoing downtime may be worth the wait to see where these turbulent fundamentals eventually settle. For now, we well see Bangladesh’s standing atop the market rankings come under threat from India, especially if Bangladeshi steel plate prices take another tumble in the coming week(s).

headline: PRECARIOUS!
highlights: Uncertainty reigns. | Momentum shift. | Upgrades apace. | Bangla deliveries? | Turkish collapse.
body_text:
The flip flops from the White House are causing global markets to remain precarious too as freight and oil prices reversed course this week where charter rates jumped 1.5% by close of Friday while oil receded by over 1% ending the week at USD 63/barrel. Flip flops seem to be the theme of the week as OPEC+ countries too are reportedly seeing this week’s version of the future from the White House and advocating for an accelerated output through June, as having met with Pres. Zelenskyy during the revered Pope Francis’s funeral on Saturday, Trump commented that the Russia / Ukraine conflict now seems closer to reaching an agreement. Through it all, Team Trump’s trade stance against China remains firm and as Pres. Xi acknowledges this very fact, it remains a dire time for the rest of us, especially when, if at minimum, auto and medicinal trade, finances, stock markets, school / college and retirement savings are going to be affected moving forward. At the broader end, student & intellectual migration and global tourism will collectively start to degrade, especially when the safety of not only those visiting other countries but even in their home countries, where visitors collectively become victims of political differences, the world may have truly slipped past President Trump’s playful grip this week.

Although some momentum was generated in sub-continent markets over preceding weeks as the 90-day pause on tariffs was announced, ship recycling markets have remained cautiously stalled as the ambiguity around U.S. - China tariffs has maintained volatility on recycling nation steel plate prices & currencies, subsequently keeping vessel offerings & sentiments at the bidding tables, firmly in check. The ongoing restriction on issuing any No Objection Certificates (NOCs) in Bangladesh has also dragged on for another week, leaving Chattogram with no fresh arrivals even though some vessels did manage to find a way to delivery. Pakistan has disappeared into ‘Empty Port Position’ territory all while India’s recently firming prices have helped it have the busiest anchorage of the week with nearly 40K LDT idling at Alang. Lastly, Turkey at the West End looks like its bottom fell entirely out this week as levels across the board (offers and fundamentals) fell sharply.

headline: CONUNDRUM!
highlights: NOC process drags. | Steel volatile. | Out of the fray. | Mystery May.
body_text:
With Bangladesh’s recent involvement at the bidding tables coming to a pause amidst their ongoing, slow-moving yard and NOC approvals and overall extension processes spanning the last two weeks over which, Indian ship recyclers jumped at the opportunity to step up and conclude a majority of the available market tonnage during this interim period. And with several small LDT, prompt delivery units being traded, this week’s anchorage was a display of purchasing prowess blended with geographic convenience as 6 ships and nearly 40K LDT is currently idling at Alang.

However, volatility continues to reign in India as not only did declining (towards the end of the week) local steel plate prices manage to still end USD 1/Ton higher than last, but the Indian Rupee suffered through extreme volatility through the course of the week and ended it 5 basis point lower than last week, at nearly Rs. 85.40 against the U.S. Dollar. Moreover, the ongoing U.S. China tariff uncertainty and overall economic global tensions continue to rear their collective heads in India (and Pakistan) once again, leaving most in the ship recycling industry calling for calm unless (and until) the situation actually deteriorates.

Recent Pakistan-linked terrorist activity that also led to the deaths of several innocents in Northern India is seemingly escalating to a dangerous level between the two nuclear armed nations as India threatens a retaliatory suspension of water services into Pakistan from the Northwest of India, and extremist Pakistani politicians call for blood should India act on its threat. Amidst cancelation of student visas between the countries and other punitive retaliations, India is starting to build up a significant presence of armed forces along the Line of Control (LoC) against the claimed Paksitani border, as the threat of another potential war has certainly seen a recently stabilizing sentiment take a hit again, resulting in an overall decline in aggression to conclude even on a unit of local interest beyond safe margins, despite the overall economic state of the nation being in good standing.

Moreover, as Pakistani purchases retreat into the shadows and Bangladesh is still out of the fray, it is certainly upon Indian recyclers to make the most of this current situation and conclude whatever the market has to offer. What happens in May is a mystery waiting to unravel itself, with looming tariff whiplashes and reacting local fundamentals that could stand to up-end price levels and an overall lack of tonnage at the bidding tables. Ship owners could once again be chasing down the markets again, hoping the slide has ended.

Finally, with monsoons around the corner and local yards being fully certified to HKC standards, Alang recyclers do have it comparatively easier than the regional competition is currently enduring.

headline: TRYING BUT FAILING!
highlights: Not taking chances. | Pressing HKC. | Stark Notifier. | Like Turkey!
body_text:
There have been several opportunities for Pakistani ship recyclers to step into the ever-evolving spiral that has been the ship recycling industry so far this year, in order to secure their share of tonnage with aggression and firmer prices that were certainly higher than those from neighboring India over a recent few weeks. But Gadani buyers have regrettably been unable to secure much of the market tonnage over the past 3 quarters unto their dormant plots, tonnage that eventually ended up in competing Alang including this week, where Gadani expectantly and regrettably returned to an empty port position once again – a phenomenon that plagued local ship recyclers for well over 2 quarters between late 2024 – early 2025.

And like India, Pakistani fundamentals certainly have a fair share of their effect on local sentiments as not only did local steel plate prices fall USD 10/Ton down to USD 624/Ton this week, but the Pakistani Rupee also continues to suffer as it fell dramatically to PKR 282.19 against the U.S. Dollar, only to eventually firm up and still end 16 basis points weaker than last week, at PKR 282.05. Moreover, as Chinese steel plate prices themselves firmed to and above USD 300/Ton this week and the future of tariffs hangs in the balance, should Pakistani steel levels continue to fall and Chinese levels continue to become more competitive, it may not bode well for Gadani ship recyclers as 2025 progresses, as local steel plate prices will come crashing down if there is no supply of steel / raw material from recycled ships and cheaper Chinese imports become more appealing to domestic steel mills.

Moreover, even the domestic economy, though stable, remains a work in progress when compared to a recently firming India. And the possibility that we may see recycling tonnage heading towards Gadani shores in the coming days or even weeks, is now an increasingly diminishing probability. Notwithstanding, the more pressing matter of the moment remains around the pending HKC upgrades at Gadani yards, especially with all of the recently unfolding drama in Bangladesh via suspended entries for recycling units into Chattogram port limits, which should be a stark warning to Pakistani recyclers of what could happen to them in the next 8 weeks, should they fail to follow up with their own yard infrastructure works (that have reportedly barely begun) before the HKC enters into force on June 26th, lest they too face the same NOC hurdles post July 1st and as Bangladeshi recyclers are now going through.

Finally, as tonnage availability (even of regionally available units) increases (looking at you, Alang) monsoon remains a mere 5 weeks away, HKC kicks in a short 3 weeks hereafter, and hesitant ship owners unwilling to initially commit their units into Gadani will likely exacerbate the ability of Gadani buyers to procure tonnage through the last 2 quarters of the year, certainly leaving a bleak 2025 forecast for Pakistan, much like it could be for Turkey.

headline: BOTTOMS…BLOWN!!
highlights: Two-market industry
body_text:
Turkey has endured a crazy 3 weeks whereby import and local steel plate prices have dropped by USD 52/Ton and USD 40/Ton respectively, having each declined a further USD 20/Ton this week as well. Not to be outdone, the Lira took its parachute off and jumped out of the plane, plummeting past a 1.6% decline this week and ending it at nearly TRY 38.50 against the U.S. Dollar.

And despite the 90-day tariff pause kicking into effect, Turkey’s economy seems to be the one major ship recycling destination hit especially hard, with sentiments increasingly battered and Aliaga indications on prospective units dropping another USD 20/MT this week, the overall offer levels on bulkers / dry cargo vessels from Turkey now hitting USD 250/MT – a remarkable drop from only a couple of years ago when recycling vessels were being regularly concluded well into USD 400/MT to Aliaga recyclers.

And with sub-continent levels being steady overall, the now USD 200/Ton price differential will certainly be a hard pill for board members of publicly traded ship owning companies to swallow, should they consider the recycling route on their again beauties, thereby further alienating Turkish recyclers in the process. Like Pakistan, the remainder of the year seems like it might be destined to a two-market industry – shared between India and Bangladesh.

headline: DELAYED…BUT THERE!
highlights: NOCs being issued. | Vessels stuck. | Draught. | Busy times?
body_text:
After over 5 weeks of delayed visits and inspections by governmental authorities that resulted in virtually no inflow of tonnage into Chattogram across April, a breakthrough late on Sunday was finally announced as permissions were given to developed yards, HKC approvals granted, and NOCs (No Objection Certs) started to be issued once again following a pause of well over one month that left the nation on the verge of an empty port position several times including this week, where no new vessels have been reported other than the lonely beaching of a relatively small LDT unit to an already approved yard.

As government bodies intervened to ensure HKC yard upgrades remain on track ahead of the HKC entry into force on June 26th, a plethora of vessels have been stuck outside Chattogram awaiting their respective NOCs forthcoming from the DG of shipping, meaning LCs could not open from banks and vessels could not enter IPL for boardings and subsequent deliveries. As such, any sales or activity over the past month or so has essentially stalled, with many vessels being reportedly diverted to competing sub-continent markets of late.

And if it wasn’t approvals on HKC / pending NOCs, it has been local fundamentals that continue to take a beating (as they have been since the highs of October 2024) where local steel plate prices remain dead on arrival at a lowly USD 478.55/Ton, not too far ahead of the current pricing strategy from Chattogram recyclers. Even the Taka reported a minor improvement towards the end of the week as it gained a mere 4 basis points against the U.S. Dollar to end the week at a still high BDT 121.91. Making matters worse has been the lack of incoming tonnage that has seen local steel trade take a hit over recent weeks and hopefully the breadth of tonnage that is currently idling outside Bangladesh will finally receive their respective permissions and alleviate the recent draught.

On the nation’s economic front, a joint meeting between the IMF and Bangladeshi government is due to take hold this week and address an ongoing deadlock over the release of upcoming payment installments on IMF loans over the issue of liberalizing the exchange rate, which has seen the Taka collapse far beyond last year’s forecasted decline to region BDT 116 and the introduction of a floating point rate, which clearly has failed to accommodate the currently depreciated state of the Taka. Ongoing international remittances from Bangladeshi citizens to family members also increased for the month of April, recording a healthy 34% increase for the nation’s treasury, further alleviating any near (or far reaching) investment and financial hurdles that Bangladesh’s ship recycling sector might face in the interim – at least until the budget it announced in a few weeks.

As yards gear up for the HKC that is now less than 2 months away, a monsoon that is just 4 weeks away, and a suspected healthy collection of deliveries to local recyclers in upcoming weeks will likely see a busier Chattogram ship recycling sector across May, and possibly June.

headline: BUMBLING RIDE!
highlights: Shaky few weeks. | Seeking approvals. | DG satisfaction. | Shutdown. | War.
body_text:
The Baltic Exchange Dry Index too reported increases this week as trade starts to shift around the world and global economies hash out fresh trade agreements without the United States, causing freight rates to report minor improvements this week even though overall trading activity seems to be far lower.
